rules.trigger: Requester asks for electronic-format record that agency holds electronically
rules.legal_concept: Electronic-format availability
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: The agency must make the information available in any electronic format in which it holds the information, and must provide a copy in the requested format if that format is one the agency has used to create copies for its own use or for other agencies.
rules.source_language: (1) The agency shall make the information available in any electronic format in which it holds the information. (2) The agency shall provide a copy of an electronic record in the format requested if the requested format is one that the agency has used to create copies for its own use or for provision to other agencies.
rules.trigger: Requester specifies an electronic format
rules.legal_concept: Format-of-production choice
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: An agency may satisfy a records-posting/production obligation by maintaining the record on its website and directing the requester there, but must promptly provide a copy if the requester cannot access or reproduce the record from the website.
rules.source_language: [Subd. (a)] a public agency may comply by posting the record on its internet website and directing the member of the public to the location on the website; [Subd. (b)] if the requester is unable to access or reproduce the record from the website, the agency shall promptly provide a copy of the public record pursuant to subdivision (a) of Section 7922.530.
rules.trigger: Requested record is available on the agency website
rules.legal_concept: Website-posting production alternative
rules.notes: is_paraphrase=true: WebFetch returned this section in summary form; re-verify verbatim before reliance. Operational fork: website-redirect path vs. direct-copy fallback. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: Any reasonably segregable portion of a record must be made available after deletion of the portions that are exempt by law.
rules.source_language: Any reasonably segregable portion of a record shall be available for inspection by any person requesting the record after deletion of the portions that are exempted by law.
rules.trigger: Record contains both exempt and non-exempt content
rules.legal_concept: Segregability / redact-and-release
rules.notes: Structural redaction step preventing whole-record withholding when segregation is reasonable. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: Fees for copies of records are limited to fees covering the direct costs of duplication, or a statutory fee if one applies.
rules.source_language: Except with respect to public records exempt from disclosure by express provisions of law, each state or local agency, upon a request for a copy of records that reasonably describes an identifiable record or records, shall make the records promptly available to any person upon payment of fees covering direct costs of duplication, or a statutory fee if applicable.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks copies (not mere inspection)
rules.legal_concept: Direct-cost-of-duplication fee limit
rules.notes: Ceiling: the state caps fees at 'direct costs of duplication' (or a separately-authorized statutory fee); the city sets the actual per-copy amount under that ceiling — do not split fixed vs. ceiling into separate concepts. No statewide cents-per-page number exists. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: The cost of duplicating an electronic record is limited to the direct cost of producing a copy of the record in an electronic format.
rules.source_language: The cost of duplication of an electronic record pursuant to paragraph (2) of subdivision (b) of Section 7922.570 shall be limited to the direct cost of producing a copy of a record in an electronic format.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks an electronic-format copy
rules.legal_concept: Direct-cost limit for electronic copies
rules.notes: Ceiling: city sets the actual electronic-duplication charge under the 'direct cost' cap. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: The requester bears the cost of producing a copy (including the cost to construct a record and the cost of programming and computer services) when the electronic record is produced only at regularly scheduled intervals, or when the request requires data compilation, extraction, or programming to produce the record.
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding subdivision (a), the requester shall bear the cost of producing a copy of the record, including the cost to construct a record, and the cost of programming and computer services necessary to produce a copy of the record when either of the following applies: (1) In order to comply with subdivisions (a) and (b) of Section 7922.570, the public agency would be required to produce a copy of an electronic record and the record is one that is produced only at otherwise regularly scheduled intervals. (2) The request would require data compilation, extraction, or programming to produce the record.
rules.trigger: Electronic record is produced only at scheduled intervals, OR request requires data compilation/extraction/programming
rules.legal_concept: Cost-shift for constructed/extracted electronic records
rules.notes: A conditional branch, not a city-set value, so config_home=structural. This is the narrow exception to the direct-cost ceiling in CA-0022. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: For ordinary production of electronic records, an agency may not charge for the ancillary staff time of searching for and redacting/reviewing records; such time is chargeable only within the narrow data-extraction cost-shift of Section 7922.575(b) (i.e., where extraction/programming or interval-only production applies).
rules.source_language: Under section 6253.9, subdivision (b) [now § 7922.575(b)], the cost of 'data compilation, extraction, or programming' recoverable from a requester does not include the ancillary tasks of searching for, or redacting, otherwise-disclosable electronic records; those tasks must be borne by the agency except in the two circumstances the statute specifies.
rules.source_authority: National Lawyers Guild, S.F. Bay Area Chapter v. City of Hayward (2020) 9 Cal.5th 488 (Appellate/Supreme Court Decision)
rules.trigger: Request for electronic records requiring redaction or search time
rules.legal_concept: Scope of recoverable electronic-production costs
rules.notes: is_paraphrase=true and REQUIRES MANUAL LEGAL REVIEW: holding stated from memory of the California Supreme Court opinion; the operative holding language was not opened this pass. Included because it changes fee behavior (bars charging redaction/search time as 'extraction'). Interprets § 7922.575(b) (former § 6253.9(b)). Source Type: Appellate Decision.
rules.effective_status: Current (requires manual verification of quoted holding)

rules.atomic_rule: The agency's duty is to make copies available upon payment of the duplication fees, permitting the agency to condition release of copies on payment.
rules.source_language: ...shall make the records promptly available to any person upon payment of fees covering direct costs of duplication, or a statutory fee if applicable.
rules.trigger: Copies are ready and a duplication fee is owed
rules.legal_concept: Payment as condition of copy release
rules.notes: 'Upon payment' gates release of copies (structural precondition); statute does not authorize an advance-deposit/estimate scheme for ordinary requests. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: A response to a written request that includes a determination denying the request, in whole or in part, must be in writing.
rules.source_language: A response to a written request for inspection or copies of public records that includes a determination that the request is denied, in whole or in part, shall be in writing.
rules.trigger: Written request is denied in whole or in part
rules.legal_concept: Written denial requirement
rules.notes: Written-response duty attaches to WRITTEN requests. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: A notification of denial must set forth the names and titles or positions of each person responsible for the denial.
rules.source_language: The notification of denial shall set forth the names and titles or positions of each person responsible for the denial.
rules.trigger: Agency issues a denial notification
rules.legal_concept: Responsible-person disclosure in denial
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: An agency must justify withholding any record by demonstrating that it is exempt under an express provision of the CPRA, or that on the facts of the particular case the public interest served by nondisclosure clearly outweighs the public interest served by disclosure.
rules.source_language: An agency shall justify withholding any record by demonstrating that the record in question is exempt under express provisions of this division, or that on the facts of the particular case the public interest served by not disclosing the record clearly outweighs the public interest served by disclosure of the record.
rules.trigger: Agency withholds a record or portion
rules.legal_concept: Withholding justification standard (express exemption or public-interest balancing)
rules.notes: The public-interest 'catch-all' balancing test requires human legal review; do not automate the balancing. § 7922.540(c) cross-references this section as the justification each denial must meet. Source Type: Statute.

material_negatives.note: No statutory administrative appeal or AG-review stage exists in the CPRA. Enforcement is exclusively judicial (§ 7923.000). Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists in local ordinance, but the state statute provides none.

No explicit statutory 'deemed denial' / constructive-denial clock (e.g., 'silence for N days = denial'). Failure to meet the 10-day determination duty exposes the agency to judicial enforcement but the statute does not convert silence into an automatic denial with a terminal clock.

No statewide fixed per-page copy rate. The statute caps fees at 'direct costs of duplication' (§ 7922.530(a)); the city supplies the actual value under that ceiling. (Some jurisdictions and courts treat ~$0.10-0.25/page as within direct cost, but that is not a statewide statutory number.)

No statutory required request form, and no requirement that a request be in writing to trigger the access right (inspection may be requested orally). A WRITTEN request is what triggers the written-denial duties of § 7922.540 — but writing is not a precondition to access itself.
No separate mandatory acknowledgment deadline distinct from the 10-day determination. The 10-day determination under § 7922.535(a) is the only intake-side statutory clock.

No statutory advance-deposit or fee-estimate-and-hold scheme for ordinary requests; the statute conditions copy release on 'payment of fees covering direct costs of duplication' (§ 7922.530(a)) but does not authorize a deposit process.

No explicit statutory tolling or pausing of the 10-day determination clock while the agency seeks clarification. The assistance duty (§ 7922.600) exists but carries no attached toll of the § 7922.535 deadline.

No numeric statutory deadline for actual PRODUCTION of records; production is governed by the soft 'promptly' standard (§ 7922.530(a)) and the agency's self-set 'estimated date' (§ 7922.535(a)), not a fixed day-count.

structural_branches.description: Mandatory 10-day determination stage: agency issues a notice stating whether the request seeks disclosable records and the reasons (§ 7922.535(a)).
When records are disclosable, the agency commits to a per-request 'estimated date and time' of availability — a stored commitment the engine tracks, not a fixed value (§ 7922.535(a)).
Optional unusual-circumstances extension branch: written notice from agency head/designee stating reasons and the expected determination date, capped at +14 days (§ 7922.535(b)).
Soft-standard production deadline ('promptly') distinct from the determination clock — engine applies a standard, not a city-entered number (§ 7922.530(a)).
Website-posting production alternative with a direct-copy fallback when the requester cannot access/reproduce from the site (§ 7922.545).
On-premises inspection branch permitting requester no-contact self-copying with their own equipment, subject to reasonable agency limits (§ 7922.530(b)-(c)).
Redact-and-release step: reasonably segregable non-exempt portions must be produced after deleting exempt portions (§ 7922.525(b)).
Conditional fee-shift branch where interval-only production or data compilation/extraction/programming moves construction/programming costs to the requester (§ 7922.575(b)).
Withholding-justification decision requiring either an express exemption or a case-specific public-interest balancing test (the latter needs human legal review) (§ 7922.000).
California's sole review path is judicial: writ of mandate / injunctive / declaratory relief in court — there is no administrative appeal stage (§ 7923.000).

rules.legal_concept: Public records open to inspection by any person
rules.atomic_rule: Any person may inspect any public record at reasonable times, except as otherwise provided in the Act or by law; no requester qualification is imposed.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right of access)
rules.source_language: All public records shall be open for inspection by any person at reasonable times, except as provided in this part 2 or as otherwise provided by law.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule per the universal-access-symmetry instruction. 'Any person' is the eligibility gate; no residency, purpose, or status qualification appears in the operative clause.

rules.legal_concept: No residency requirement to request public records
rules.atomic_rule: CORA imposes no residency or citizenship requirement; the right to inspect runs to 'any person' without geographic qualification.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: The Act extends inspection to 'any person' and states no residency, citizenship, or geographic qualification; the absence of any residency condition is derived from the 'any person' grant in 24-72-203(1)(a).
rules.notes: Emitted as a rule with the shared canonical key per universal-access-symmetry rule (never as a material negative). Paraphrase: statute states the absence implicitly via 'any person', not by an express no-residency clause.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required for general public records
rules.atomic_rule: A requester need not state a purpose or reason to inspect general public records; the right runs to any person at reasonable times.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: The general inspection right in 24-72-203(1)(a) is unconditional as to purpose; no statement-of-purpose is required for ordinary public records (derived from the unqualified 'any person ... at reasonable times' grant).
rules.notes: Shared canonical key per universal-access-symmetry. Caveat for later pass: certain special record categories (e.g., records of names/addresses used for solicitation under 24-72-204/205.5) do carry a purpose/use restriction; this rule covers only ordinary records.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'custodian'
rules.atomic_rule: The 'custodian' is the official custodian or any authorized person having personal custody and control of the public records in question; this identifies who must respond and drives routing.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: "Custodian" means and includes the official custodian or any authorized person having personal custody and control of the public records in question.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver #1: definition the software branches on for routing / who-must-respond.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian may adopt rules for protection of records
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may make and enforce rules reasonably necessary for the protection of the records and to prevent unnecessary interference with the discharge of duties.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: The official custodian of any public records may make such rules with reference to the inspection of such records as are reasonably necessary for the protection of such records and the prevention of unnecessary interference with the regular discharge of the duties of the custodian or the custodian's office.
rules.notes: Source of local intake/procedure rules (e.g., request form, hours). Explains why intake format is a municipal parameter rather than a statewide fixed rule.

rules.legal_concept: Notice when records not in custodian's custody
rules.atomic_rule: If the requested records are not in the custody or control of the person to whom application is made, that person shall so notify the applicant in writing and, if known, state which custodian has custody or control.
rules.trigger: Applied-to person lacks custody/control of the requested record
rules.source_language: If the public records requested are not in the custody or control of the person to whom application is made, such person shall forthwith notify the applicant of this fact, in writing if requested by the applicant. In such notification, such person shall state, in detail to the best of such person's knowledge and belief, the reason for the absence of the records from such person's custody or control, their location, and what person then has custody or control of the records.
rules.notes: Routing/wrong-department rule (keeper-sliver #1 family). 'forthwith' notice is a soft-timed communication; primary effect is routing to the correct custodian.

rules.legal_concept: Extension for extenuating circumstances (max seven working days)
rules.atomic_rule: The three-working-day period may be extended when extenuating circumstances exist, but the extension shall not exceed seven working days.
rules.trigger: Extenuating circumstances exist (as defined in 24-72-203(3)(b))
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: up to 7 additional working days beyond the presumptive 3-working-day period
rules.source_language: Such period may be extended if extenuating circumstances exist. However, such period of extension shall not exceed seven working days.
rules.notes: Extension caps total at 3 + 7 working days. constraint_basis=ceiling (shall not exceed).

rules.legal_concept: Written finding of extenuating circumstances within three-day period
rules.atomic_rule: A finding that extenuating circumstances exist must be made in writing by the custodian and provided to the requester within the three-working-day period.
rules.trigger: Custodian invokes an extenuating-circumstances extension
rules.clock_spec: written finding due within 3 working days of the request (before extension takes effect)
rules.source_language: A finding that extenuating circumstances exist shall be made in writing by the custodian and shall be provided to the person making the request within the three-day period.
rules.notes: Required notice/document gating the extension; a structural step the engine must execute within the base window.

rules.legal_concept: Extenuating circumstances barred for a single identified document
rules.atomic_rule: Extenuating circumstances can never apply to a request that relates to a single, specifically identified document.
rules.trigger: Request relates to a single, specifically identified document
rules.source_language: In no event can extenuating circumstances apply to a request that relates to a single, specifically identified document.
rules.notes: Blocks the extension branch for single-document requests; keeps the base 3-working-day ceiling.

rules.legal_concept: Production in sortable/searchable digital format
rules.atomic_rule: If a public record is stored in a digital format that is sortable, the custodian shall provide a copy in a sortable format; if stored in a searchable format, in a searchable format.
rules.trigger: Requested record is maintained in a digital sortable or searchable format
rules.source_language: If a public record is stored in a digital format that is sortable, the custodian shall provide a copy of the public record in a sortable format. [Companion provision: if stored in a searchable format, the custodian shall provide it in a searchable format.]
rules.notes: Tiered native-format production duty. The sortable-format sentence is verbatim; the searchable-tier companion is captured from the opened source and should be re-verified verbatim in a later pass.

rules.legal_concept: Exception to native-format production (feasibility / licensing)
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian need not produce in the sortable/searchable format if doing so would violate a copyright or licensing agreement, or if it is not technologically or practically feasible to remove withholdable information or to provide the format without purchasing new software.
rules.trigger: Copyright/licensing conflict, or technological/practical infeasibility to produce the native format or redact
rules.source_language: [The custodian is not required to produce a record in a sortable or searchable format if doing so would violate a copyright or licensing agreement, or if it is not technologically or practically feasible to remove information that may be withheld or to provide the record in the requested format without the purchase of software.]
rules.notes: Paraphrase of the (3.5) exceptions as captured from the opened source; exact statutory wording of the feasibility/licensing exceptions should be verified verbatim in a later pass.

rules.legal_concept: Written statement of grounds for denial
rules.atomic_rule: On denial of access, if the applicant requests it, the custodian must furnish forthwith a written statement of the grounds for denial citing the law or regulation under which access is denied.
rules.trigger: Custodian denies access and the applicant requests a written statement
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "forthwith" from the applicant's request for a written statement
rules.source_language: If the custodian denies access to any public record, the applicant may request a written statement of the grounds for the denial, which statement shall cite the law or regulation under which access is denied and shall be furnished forthwith to the applicant.
rules.notes: Soft deadline ('forthwith') -> config_home structural per soft-standard rule. This written statement is a prerequisite document for the judicial show-cause path.

rules.legal_concept: Segregability / inspection of non-withheld portions
rules.atomic_rule: Where only portions of a record are withholdable (e.g., specialized details of security arrangements or investigations), the custodian may deny inspection of only those portions and shall allow inspection of the remaining portions.
rules.trigger: A record contains both withholdable and disclosable portions
rules.source_language: A custodian may deny the right of inspection of only those portions of a record ... that contain specialized details of security arrangements or investigations and shall allow inspection of the remaining portions.
rules.notes: Segregability duty captured verbatim from the security-arrangements exemption; it expresses the redact-and-release principle. Whether a broader general segregability clause exists elsewhere in 204 should be confirmed in a later pass.

rules.legal_concept: Copy fee per standard page
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may charge a fee not to exceed twenty-five cents per standard page for a copy of a public record.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks a copy on a standard page
rules.source_language: A custodian may charge a fee not to exceed twenty-five cents per standard page for a copy of a public record or a fee not to exceed the actual cost of providing a copy, printout, or photograph of a public record in a format other than a standard page.
rules.notes: State sets a ceiling ($0.25/standard page); the municipality supplies the operative value at or below it. constraint_basis=ceiling.

rules.legal_concept: Actual-cost fee for non-standard-page copies
rules.atomic_rule: For a copy, printout, or photograph in a format other than a standard page, the custodian may charge a fee not to exceed the actual cost of providing it.
rules.trigger: Copy provided in a format other than a standard page
rules.source_language: ... a fee not to exceed the actual cost of providing a copy, printout, or photograph of a public record in a format other than a standard page.
rules.notes: Actual-cost ceiling for non-standard formats; municipality supplies the operative charge under the cap.

rules.legal_concept: Research-and-retrieval hourly fee cap
rules.atomic_rule: After the first hour, the custodian may charge a fee for research and retrieval of public records not to exceed thirty dollars per hour.
rules.trigger: Research and retrieval time exceeds the first free hour
rules.source_language: After the first hour of time has been expended, the custodian may charge a fee for the research and retrieval of public records that shall not exceed thirty dollars per hour.
rules.notes: The $30/hour statutory ceiling is periodically adjusted for inflation by the Director of Research of the Legislative Council (the current CPI-adjusted maximum is higher than $30 and should be pulled from the current published figure). constraint_basis=ceiling; municipality sets its own rate at or below the current maximum.

rules.legal_concept: First hour of research and retrieval free
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian shall not impose any charge for the first hour of time expended in research and retrieval of public records.
rules.trigger: Research and retrieval performed on a request
rules.source_language: Under any such policy, the custodian shall not impose a charge for the first hour of time expended in connection with the research and retrieval of public records.
rules.notes: Fixed statutory free allowance (1 hour). Not municipally variable — constraint_basis=fixed.

rules.legal_concept: Published fee policy prerequisite to charging research/retrieval fees
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian may impose a research-and-retrieval fee only if, before receiving the request, it has posted on its website or otherwise published a written policy specifying the applicable conditions and the amount of any current fee.
rules.trigger: Custodian intends to charge a research-and-retrieval fee
rules.source_language: A custodian may impose a fee in response to a request for the research and retrieval of public records only if the custodian has, prior to the date of receiving the request, either posted on the custodian's website or otherwise published a written policy that specifies the applicable conditions concerning the research and retrieval of public records by the custodian, including the amount of any current fee.
rules.notes: Gating precondition: no published policy => no research/retrieval fee may be charged. Structural prerequisite the engine must check before applying the fee parameter.

rules.legal_concept: No transmission fee for records sent by email
rules.atomic_rule: No transmission fee may be charged to the requester for transmitting public records via electronic mail.
rules.trigger: Records are transmitted to the requester via electronic mail
rules.source_language: No transmission fees may be charged to the record requester for transmitting public records via electronic mail.
rules.notes: Fixed $0 for email transmission. Modeled as a parameter fixed at zero (rule_type Prohibition). Subsection number (1)(b) captured from opened source; verify exact placement in later pass.

material_negatives.note: CORA sets a response/inspection window (presumptive 3 working days, 24-72-203(3)(b)) but prescribes no separate mandatory acknowledgment-of-receipt deadline distinct from providing access. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

No express statutory 'deemed denial' or constructive-denial clock (silence for N days = denial). CORA's remedy trigger is an affirmative denial of access (24-72-204(4)-(5)); it does not convert non-response into an automatic denial after a fixed period. Keeper-sliver #3 therefore yields a negative for Colorado.

No statute mandates that a request be in writing or on a specific form. The custodian may adopt reasonable rules (24-72-203(2)(a)); intake format is thus a municipal-level rule, not a statewide fixed requirement.

The statute authorizes copy and research/retrieval fees but states no statutory deposit/prepayment cap or mandatory prepayment procedure. Custodian prepayment practices are local and not fixed by statute in the sections reviewed.

No separate statutory clarification-and-toll mechanism for vague requests. A broadly stated/insufficiently specific request instead qualifies as an 'extenuating circumstance' extending the response period (24-72-203(3)(b)); there is no distinct clarification clock that tolls or resets the deadline.

The sections reviewed do not establish a general commercial-purpose fee surcharge for ordinary records. (Special provisions for records of names/addresses used for solicitation exist under 24-72-204/205.5 and belong to a later special-records pass.)

structural_branches.description: Extenuating-circumstances extension path: on qualifying triggers the engine adds up to 7 working days, but only after issuing a written finding within the base 3-working-day window (CO-0009) and only if the request is not for a single identified document (CO-0010).
Tiered digital-format production branch: sortable-stored records produced sortable, searchable-stored records produced searchable (CO-0012), with a feasibility/licensing off-ramp (CO-0013).
On denial, a requester-triggered branch producing a written, law-citing statement of grounds 'forthwith' (CO-0014), which also serves as the predicate document for the judicial path.
Fee-eligibility gate: research/retrieval fees may be charged only after a pre-published written fee policy exists; without it the fee branch is unavailable (CO-0020).

Judicial-only enforcement path (no internal administrative appeal): mandatory 14-day pre-suit notice to custodian (CO-0023), a 3-business-day expedited variant (CO-0024), then a district-court show-cause hearing at the earliest practical time (CO-0025).

rules.legal_concept: Right of every person to access public records
rules.atomic_rule: Every person has the right to inspect, copy, or receive a copy of any public record maintained or kept on file by any public agency (subject to statutory exemptions).
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right of any person)
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by any federal law or state statute, all records maintained or kept on file by any public agency, whether or not such records are required by any law or by any rule or regulation, shall be public records and every person shall have the right to (1) inspect such records promptly during regular office or business hours, (2) copy such records in accordance with subsection (g) of section 1-212, or (3) receive a copy of such records in accordance with section 1-212.
rules.notes: Universal-access rule per shared eligibility key. 'Person' defined broadly (CT-0004); statute imposes no residency or purpose condition.

rules.legal_concept: No residency requirement to request records
rules.atomic_rule: Access is granted to 'every person' / 'any person' with no in-state residency condition; a requester need not be a Connecticut resident.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: all records maintained or kept on file by any public agency ... shall be public records and every person shall have the right to (1) inspect such records promptly during regular office or business hours
rules.notes: Emitted as a rule with the shared key (not a material negative) per universal-access symmetry. The right runs to 'every person' with no residency qualifier anywhere in Chapter 14.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A requester need not state or justify a purpose to inspect, copy, or receive public records; the right is unconditional as to motive.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: every person shall have the right to (1) inspect such records promptly during regular office or business hours, (2) copy such records in accordance with subsection (g) of section 1-212, or (3) receive a copy of such records in accordance with section 1-212.
rules.notes: Shared-key rule per universal-access symmetry. Chapter 14 attaches no purpose/use condition to the right of access.

rules.legal_concept: Written application required to receive a copy
rules.atomic_rule: To receive a copy of a public record, the requester must apply in writing; an oral request for a copy is not enforceable before the FOI Commission.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks a copy (as opposed to inspection)
rules.source_language: Any person applying in writing shall receive, promptly upon request, a plain, facsimile, electronic or certified copy of any public record.
rules.notes: Case law (130 CA 448) holds the writing requirement makes copy requests enforceable and that promptness was not violated by failing to honor oral copy requests. Note contrast: the right to INSPECT under 1-210(a) carries no writing requirement.

rules.legal_concept: Prompt provision of copies
rules.atomic_rule: Upon a written request, a public agency must provide the requested copy of a public record promptly.
rules.trigger: Written request for a copy
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "promptly upon request" from written request
rules.source_language: Any person applying in writing shall receive, promptly upon request, a plain, facsimile, electronic or certified copy of any public record.
rules.notes: Soft standard - no numeric deadline. Distinct from the 4-business-day denial deadline (CT-0012), which governs only denials.

rules.legal_concept: Denial must issue from the custodian/official with custody or control
rules.atomic_rule: Any denial of access must be made by the public agency official who has custody or control of the public record.
rules.trigger: Agency denies inspection or copying
rules.source_language: Any denial of the right to inspect or copy records provided for under section 1-210 shall be made to the person requesting such right by the public agency official who has custody or control of the public record, in writing, within four business days of such request
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: custodian designation drives routing (who must issue the response).

rules.legal_concept: Written denial within four business days
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency must issue any denial of inspection/copying to the requester in writing within four business days of the request.
rules.trigger: Request that the agency will deny
rules.clock_spec: 4 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: Any denial of the right to inspect or copy records provided for under section 1-210 shall be made to the person requesting such right by the public agency official who has custody or control of the public record, in writing, within four business days of such request
rules.notes: This is the only fixed statutory response window in CT FOIA, and it applies specifically to denials (not to grants, which are governed by 'promptly').

rules.legal_concept: Ten-business-day denial window for personnel/medical-file requests
rules.atomic_rule: When a request is subject to the personnel/medical-file objection process (1-214(b)-(c)), any denial must be made in writing within ten business days of the request.
rules.trigger: Request determined subject to 1-214(b) and (c) (personnel/medical/similar files)
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: except when the request is determined to be subject to subsections (b) and (c) of section 1-214, in which case such denial shall be made, in writing, within ten business days of such request.
rules.notes: Same concept as CT-0012 but a longer window for the personnel-file branch, to accommodate the employee-objection process.

rules.legal_concept: Failure to comply within the applicable window deemed a denial
rules.atomic_rule: An agency's failure to comply with an inspection/copy request within the applicable number of business days is deemed a denial (which then starts the appeal clock).
rules.trigger: Applicable business-day window (4 or 10) elapses without compliance
rules.clock_spec: deemed denial upon expiry of 4 business-days (or 10 for personnel/medical) from request
rules.source_language: Failure to comply with a request to so inspect or copy such public record within the applicable number of business days shall be deemed to be a denial.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: constructive/deemed-denial trigger (silence = denial). Terminal event that opens the 30-day FOIC appeal window (CT-0033). Section 1-214(c) similarly deems failure to comply a denial for personnel-file requests.

rules.legal_concept: Per-page copy fee ceiling - municipal and other agencies
rules.atomic_rule: For all public agencies other than state offices/agencies, the fee for a copy of a public record shall not exceed fifty cents per page.
rules.trigger: Requester receives a copy from a non-state public agency
rules.source_language: (B) By all other public agencies, as defined in section 1-200, shall not exceed fifty cents per page.
rules.notes: Municipal/local rate. Ceiling: the city may set any per-page fee at or below $0.50. 'Page' means one side of a piece of printed matter (108 CA 471).

rules.legal_concept: Per-page copy fee ceiling - state offices/agencies
rules.atomic_rule: For state executive/administrative/legislative offices and state agencies (and judicial offices in their administrative functions), the copy fee shall not exceed twenty-five cents per page.
rules.trigger: Requester receives a copy from a state office/agency
rules.source_language: (A) By an executive, administrative or legislative office of the state, a state agency or a department, institution, bureau, board, commission, authority or official of the state, including a committee of, or created by, such an office ..., and also including any judicial office, official or body or committee thereof but only in respect to its or their administrative functions, shall not exceed twenty-five cents per page
rules.notes: Same concept as CT-0015 with a different ceiling for state agencies; do not merge the values - the constraint differs by agency class.

rules.legal_concept: Transcription fee limited to cost
rules.atomic_rule: Where a copy requires a transcription, or a person requests a transcription of a public record, the transcription fee shall not exceed the agency's cost.
rules.trigger: Copy requires, or requester applies for, a transcription
rules.source_language: If any copy provided in accordance with said Freedom of Information Act requires a transcription, or if any person applies for a transcription of a public record, the fee for such transcription shall not exceed the cost thereof to the public agency.
rules.notes: Ceiling = actual cost to the agency; no fixed number stated.

rules.legal_concept: Fee for computer-stored records limited to cost with enumerated components
rules.atomic_rule: The fee for a copy of computer-stored public records shall not exceed the agency's cost, and (for non-preexisting printouts) may include only enumerated components: employee hourly salary for producing/formatting/programming (not search/retrieval except sub-(4)), outside copying-service cost, actual storage-media cost, and certain computer-time charges.
rules.trigger: Request for a copy of computer-stored public records
rules.source_language: The fee for any copy provided in accordance with subsection (a) of section 1-211 shall not exceed the cost thereof to the public agency. In determining such costs for a copy, other than for a printout which exists at the time that the agency responds to the request for such copy, an agency may include only: (1) An amount equal to the hourly salary attributed to all agency employees engaged in providing the requested computer-stored public record ... but not including search or retrieval costs except as provided in subdivision (4) of this subsection; (2) An amount equal to the cost to the agency of engaging an outside professional electronic copying service ...; (3) The actual cost of the storage devices or media provided ...; and (4) The computer time charges incurred by the agency ... where another agency or contractor provides the agency with computer storage and retrieval services.
rules.notes: Ceiling = cost, with a closed list of includable components. Notably excludes search/retrieval labor except sub-(4). DAS issues guidelines for consistency. Kept in one row (closed enumerated list, not a bundle of independent duties).

rules.legal_concept: Certification fee
rules.atomic_rule: For certifying a copy of records/files (or certifying a fact appearing therein), the fee is one dollar for the first page and fifty cents for each additional page.
rules.trigger: Requester asks the custodian to certify a copy or fact
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law, the fee for any person who has the custody of any public records or files for certifying any copy of such records or files, or certifying to any fact appearing therefrom, shall be for the first page of such certificate, or copy and certificate, one dollar; and for each additional page, fifty cents.
rules.notes: Fixed statewide amount ('except as otherwise provided by law'). Separate from and additive to the per-page copy fee.

rules.legal_concept: Prepayment permitted when fee estimated at $10 or more
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency may require prepayment of any fee if the fee is estimated to be ten dollars or more.
rules.trigger: Estimated fee is $10 or more
rules.source_language: A public agency may require the prepayment of any fee required or permitted under the Freedom of Information Act if such fee is estimated to be ten dollars or more.
rules.notes: Discretionary. $10 is the floor at/above which prepayment may be demanded; the city sets whether/how it invokes it.

rules.legal_concept: Mandatory fee waiver
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency shall waive any copy fee when any enumerated ground applies: requester is indigent; records are exempt under 1-210(b); compliance benefits the general welfare in the agency's judgment; requester is an elected official of the political subdivision certifying the record pertains to official duties; or requester is Public Defender Services personnel/appointed counsel certifying the record pertains to their duties.
rules.trigger: Any one of five enumerated waiver conditions is met
rules.source_language: The public agency shall waive any fee provided for in this section when: (1) The person requesting the records is an indigent individual; (2) The records located are determined by the public agency to be exempt from disclosure under subsection (b) of section 1-210; (3) In its judgment, compliance with the applicant's request benefits the general welfare; (4) The person requesting the record is an elected official of a political subdivision of the state and the official (A) obtains the record from an agency of the political subdivision in which the official serves, and (B) certifies that the record pertains to the official's duties; or (5) The person requesting the records is a member of the Division of Public Defender Services or an attorney appointed by the court as a Division of Public Defender Services assigned counsel under section 51-296 and such member or attorney certifies that the record pertains to the member's or attorney's duties.
rules.notes: Kept as one row (single 'shall waive' duty with disjunctive grounds). Mandatory ('shall'); ground (3) 'general welfare' rests on agency judgment.

rules.legal_concept: Agency discretion over type of copy
rules.atomic_rule: The type of copy provided (plain, facsimile, electronic, or certified) is within the public agency's discretion, subject to the two exceptions in CT-0026 and CT-0027.
rules.trigger: Written request for a copy
rules.source_language: The type of copy provided shall be within the discretion of the public agency, except (1) the agency shall provide a certified copy whenever requested, and (2) if the applicant does not have access to a computer or facsimile machine, the public agency shall not send the applicant an electronic or facsimile copy.
rules.notes: General discretion rule; the two carve-outs are split into CT-0026/CT-0027. Cross-references electronic-format duty for computer records (CT-0028).

rules.legal_concept: Certified copy on demand
rules.atomic_rule: The agency shall provide a certified copy whenever a certified copy is requested.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for a certified copy
rules.source_language: except (1) the agency shall provide a certified copy whenever requested
rules.notes: Certification carries the separate fee in CT-0020. 'Certified' requires a written attestation as a true copy by an authorized official (108 CA 471).

rules.legal_concept: Computer-stored records provided in requested medium
rules.atomic_rule: An agency maintaining public records in a computer storage system shall provide a copy of nonexempt data in the medium the requester specifies (paper, disk, tape, other electronic medium, or email), if the agency can reasonably make or have such copy made.
rules.trigger: Request for computer-stored nonexempt data, format specified
rules.source_language: Any public agency which maintains public records in a computer storage system shall provide, to any person making a request pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, a copy of any nonexempt data contained in such records, properly identified, on paper, disk, tape or any other electronic storage device or medium requested by the person, including an electronic copy sent to the electronic mail address of the person making such request, if the agency can reasonably make any such copy or have any such copy made.
rules.notes: Duty conditioned on 'reasonably' being able to make the copy - a soft feasibility standard. Fee governed by CT-0018.

rules.legal_concept: Notice to employees when disclosure believed to invade privacy
rules.atomic_rule: When an agency receives a request for records in an employee's personnel/medical/similar file and reasonably believes disclosure would legally constitute an invasion of privacy, it shall immediately notify in writing each employee concerned and their collective-bargaining representative.
rules.trigger: Request for personnel/medical/similar file where agency reasonably believes disclosure would invade privacy
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "immediately" notify from receipt of request
rules.source_language: Whenever a public agency receives a request to inspect or copy records contained in any of its employees' personnel or medical files and similar files, and the agency reasonably believes that the disclosure of such records would legally constitute an invasion of privacy, the agency shall immediately notify in writing (A) each employee concerned, provided such notice shall not be required to be in writing where impractical due to the large number of employees concerned, and (B) the collective bargaining representative, if any, of each employee concerned.
rules.notes: Starts the objection process (CT-0031). 'Immediately' is a soft standard. Notice may be non-written where impractical due to large employee numbers.

rules.legal_concept: Disclose then notify when no invasion believed
rules.atomic_rule: When an agency receives a personnel/medical-file request and reasonably believes disclosure would NOT invade privacy, it shall first disclose the records, then within a reasonable time make a reasonable attempt to send the employee(s) and their bargaining representative a copy or brief description of the request.
rules.trigger: Request for personnel/medical file where agency reasonably believes disclosure would not invade privacy
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "within a reasonable time after such disclosure" for post-disclosure notice
rules.source_language: Whenever a public agency receives a request to inspect or copy records contained in any of its employees' personnel or medical files and similar files, and the agency reasonably believes that the disclosure of such records would not legally constitute an invasion of privacy, the agency shall first disclose the requested records to the person making the request ... and subsequently, within a reasonable time after such disclosure, make a reasonable attempt to send a written or an electronic copy of the request ... or a brief description of such request, to each employee concerned and the collective bargaining representative, if any, of each employee concerned.
rules.notes: Alternative branch: no pre-disclosure hold; disclosure precedes notice. Added by P.A. 18-93.

rules.legal_concept: Employee objection window before disclosure
rules.atomic_rule: After giving privacy notice, the agency shall disclose the requested records unless the employee or their bargaining representative files a written objection within seven business days from receipt of the notice (or, absent evidence of receipt, within nine business days from when the notice was mailed/sent/posted/given).
rules.trigger: Privacy notice given under 1-214(b)(1)
rules.clock_spec: 7 business-days from employee receipt of notice; or 9 business-days from mailing/sending if no evidence of receipt
rules.source_language: A public agency which has provided notice under subdivision (1) of subsection (b) of this section shall disclose the records requested unless it receives a written objection from the employee concerned or the employee's collective bargaining representative, if any, within seven business days from the receipt by the employee or such collective bargaining representative of the notice or, if there is no evidence of receipt of written notice, not later than nine business days from the date the notice is actually mailed, sent, posted or otherwise given.
rules.notes: Kept as one row (single objection window with a receipt-based primary and a mailing-based fallback). Objection must be on an agency form, signed under penalty of false statement.

rules.legal_concept: Records withheld once objection filed until FOIC order
rules.atomic_rule: Upon the filing of a valid employee/representative objection, the agency shall not disclose the requested records unless ordered to do so by the Freedom of Information Commission; failure to comply with the request is itself a denial for appeal purposes.
rules.trigger: Written objection filed under 1-214(c)
rules.clock_spec: request enters withheld/hold state pending FOIC order under § 1-206
rules.source_language: Upon the filing of an objection as provided in this subsection, the agency shall not disclose the requested records unless ordered to do so by the Freedom of Information Commission pursuant to section 1-206. Failure to comply with a request to inspect or copy records under this section shall constitute a denial for the purposes of section 1-206.
rules.notes: Request enters a hold state pending FOIC resolution; the employee may later approve disclosure in writing even after a representative objects. This is a state-specific processing branch.

rules.legal_concept: Mandatory redaction of protected residential addresses
rules.atomic_rule: When an agency receives a request that specifically names a person who has filed a confidentiality request for their residential address, the agency shall copy the record and redact that person's residential address before disclosing it (reasonable-effort redaction for list-type requests).
rules.trigger: Request naming/covering a person who filed an address-confidentiality request under § 1-217
rules.source_language: Any public agency that receives a request for a record subject to disclosure under this chapter where such request (A) specifically names a person who has requested that his or her address be kept confidential under subdivision (1) of this subsection, shall make a copy of the record requested to be disclosed and shall redact the copy to remove such person's residential address prior to disclosing such record, (B) is for an existing list that is derived from a readily accessible electronic database, shall make a reasonable effort to redact the residential address ... prior to the release of such list, or (C) is for any list that the public agency voluntarily creates in response to a request for disclosure, shall make a reasonable effort to redact the residential address ... prior to the release of such list.
rules.notes: Creates a redaction workflow triggered by the request. Protected classes (police officers, judges, prosecutors, DCF/correction/parole staff, etc.) are enumerated in 1-217(a)(1). Does not apply to documents/lists exempted by 1-217(e).

rules.legal_concept: Segregation of nonexempt from exempt data (judicial rule)
rules.atomic_rule: When a request encompasses both exempt and nonexempt data, disclosure of the nonexempt portion may be ordered where the agency can reasonably separate the data, but only after inquiry into reasonable separability and (for computerized data) a public-safety assessment.
rules.trigger: Request incorporating both exempt and nonexempt data
rules.source_language: Section does not empower commission to order agency to separate exempt from non-exempt data when request incorporates both and no inquiry is made into whether agency can reasonably separate such data or whether non-exempt data alone would satisfy requester.
rules.source_authority: Director of Info. Tech. v. FOIC, 307 Conn. 648 (2012) (construing Conn. Gen. Stat. § 1-211)
rules.notes: Judicially established. Connecticut FOIA has NO general statutory segregability clause; segregability is governed by this holding (and by 323 Conn. 1 for redacting privileged matter). Quoted language is the official statutory annotation summarizing the holding - verify against the full opinion (318/323/307 Conn.) in a case-law pass. Rule_type secondary: Presumption.

material_negatives.note: Connecticut FOIA sets NO general acknowledgment/response deadline for granting access. The only fixed statutory window is the four-business-day (ten for personnel/medical) deadline to issue a DENIAL (§ 1-206(a)); grants are governed only by the soft 'promptly' standard (§§ 1-210(a), 1-212(a)). Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

No statutory provision requires or authorizes a clarification/narrowing round-trip with a tolling clock. CT law is silent; agencies handle vague requests case-by-case (and may pursue vexatious-requester relief under § 1-206(b)(6)).
Connecticut FOIA draws no commercial-vs-noncommercial fee distinction and defines no 'commercial purpose'. Copy fees are the same per-page/cost ceilings regardless of requester purpose (§ 1-212).

No statute authorizes a separate search or staff-time fee for PAPER copies; the charge is per-page only (§ 1-212(a)). For computer-stored records, staff time for producing/formatting may be included but search/retrieval costs are expressly excluded except limited third-party computer-time charges (§ 1-212(b)).

Chapter 14 contains no express 'adequate/reasonable search' standard governing how an agency must search for responsive records; the obligation is implied through the access right and FOIC adjudication rather than a codified processing rule.

No statute prescribes a required submission channel or a mandatory request form for records requests generally; only that a request for a COPY be in writing (§ 1-212(a)). Inspection carries no writing requirement.

Section 1-206(a) requires a denial to be 'in writing' within the deadline but does not, on its face, require the agency to state the statutory basis/reason for the denial; any reason-statement obligation arises in FOIC practice rather than the statute.

No statute imposes an automatic litigation/preservation hold triggered by a records request or a pending FOIC appeal; retention is governed by separate records-management law (Conn. Gen. Stat. §§ 11-8 et seq.), outside Chapter 14's request-processing rules.

structural_branches.description: Personnel/medical-file request enters a hold state once an employee or bargaining representative files an objection; agency cannot disclose until FOIC orders it (§ 1-214(c)).
Privacy-invasion branch: agency must notify affected employees and unions and pause disclosure pending the objection window (§ 1-214(b)(1)).
No-invasion branch: agency discloses first, then notifies employees within a reasonable time (§ 1-214(b)(2)).
FOIC may relieve an agency from processing a requester's future requests for up to one year on a vexatious-requester petition (§ 1-206(b)(6)).
Inmate/confined-person requests are routed to the Commissioner of Correction (or DMHAS) for exemption review before compliance (§ 1-210(c)).
Requests for § 1-210(b)(19) security records are routed to DAS/DESPP for withholding directive, redirecting who the appeal runs against (§ 1-210(d)).
Privileged appeals follow an expedited 30-day-hearing / 60-day-decision track distinct from the general one-year track (§ 1-206(b)(1)).
Court-review path for FOIC decisions via UAPA § 4-183, distinct from the internal FOIC appeal stage (§ 1-206(d)).
Non-response within the applicable business-day window converts the request into a deemed denial, opening the appeal path (§ 1-206(a)).
A request naming a person with a confidential-address filing forces a redaction step before disclosure (§ 1-217(a)(2)).

rules.legal_concept: Constitutional right of every person to inspect or copy any public record
rules.atomic_rule: Every person has the right to inspect or copy any public record made or received in connection with the official business of any public body, officer, or employee of the state (or persons acting on their behalf), except records exempted under this section or made confidential by the Constitution.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right)
rules.source_language: Every person has the right to inspect or copy any public record made or received in connection with the official business of any public body, officer, or employee of the state, or persons acting on their behalf, except with respect to records exempted pursuant to this section or specifically made confidential by this Constitution.
rules.notes: Source Type: Constitution (self-executing). Anchors the universal-access family; access does not turn on requester status.

rules.legal_concept: Access extends to every person with no residency limitation
rules.atomic_rule: The right of access runs to 'every person' / 'any person' with no residency or citizenship qualification; a custodian may not condition access on the requester being a Florida resident.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: Every person has the right to inspect or copy any public record made or received in connection with the official business of any public body, officer, or employee of the state, or persons acting on their behalf ... [and] It is the policy of this state that all state, county, and municipal records are open for personal inspection and copying by any person.
rules.source_authority: Art. I, § 24(a), Fla. Const.; § 119.01(1), Fla. Stat.
rules.notes: Source Type: Constitution + Statute. No-residency is expressed through the unqualified 'every person'/'any person'; emitted as a rule (per universal-access symmetry), not a negative.

rules.legal_concept: Requester's motive/purpose is immaterial to the right of access
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian may not require the requester to state a reason or purpose for the request; the requester's motivation does not affect the right of access.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: The motivation of the person seeking the records does not impact the person's right to see them under the Public Records Act.
rules.source_authority: Curry v. State, 811 So. 2d 736 (Fla. 4th DCA 2002); Lorei v. Smith, 464 So. 2d 1330 (Fla. 2d DCA 1985)
rules.notes: Source Type: Appellate Decision. Quote taken from secondary sources summarizing the holdings; primary opinions not opened this pass — flagged for case-law verification. Emitted as a rule (universal-access symmetry) rather than a negative.

rules.legal_concept: No prescribed form; oral requests suffice and identity need not be disclosed
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian may not require that a public-records request be made in writing, on a particular form, or in person, and may not require the requester to disclose their identity as a condition of access.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: Requesters are not required to provide a reason for their request. They are also not required to disclose their identity or submit the request in writing.
rules.source_authority: Interpreting § 119.07(1)(a), Fla. Stat.; Fla. AG guidance / Government-in-the-Sunshine Manual
rules.notes: Source Type: Official Guidance / interpretive. No statute expressly states this; derived from § 119.07(1)(a)'s 'any person desiring to do so' and AG guidance. Flagged for AG/manual verification pass.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to provide reasonable public access to electronically maintained records
rules.atomic_rule: As an agency increases its use of electronic recordkeeping it must provide reasonable public access to records electronically maintained and must ensure exempt/confidential records are not disclosed except as permitted by law.
rules.trigger: Agency maintains records in an electronic recordkeeping system
rules.source_language: Automation of public records must not erode the right of access to those records. As each agency increases its use of and dependence on electronic recordkeeping, each agency must provide reasonable public access to records electronically maintained and must ensure that exempt or confidential records are not disclosed except as otherwise permitted by law.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to acknowledge requests promptly
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian and any designee must acknowledge a request to inspect or copy records promptly.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a request to inspect or copy records
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "promptly" from request receipt
rules.source_language: A custodian of public records and his or her designee must acknowledge requests to inspect or copy records promptly and respond to such requests in good faith.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. 'Promptly' is an undefined soft standard — no numeric acknowledgment deadline exists in Florida law. Split from the good-faith duty (FL-0008); same sentence.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to respond in good faith
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian and any designee must respond to requests to inspect or copy records in good faith.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a request to inspect or copy records
rules.source_language: A custodian of public records and his or her designee must acknowledge requests to inspect or copy records promptly and respond to such requests in good faith.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Split from FL-0007 per grain rule.

rules.legal_concept: Every custodian must permit inspection and copying
rules.atomic_rule: Every person who has custody of a public record must permit that record to be inspected and copied by any person desiring to do so.
rules.trigger: A person desires to inspect or copy a record in the custodian's custody
rules.source_language: Every person who has custody of a public record shall permit the record to be inspected and copied by any person desiring to do so, at any reasonable time, under reasonable conditions, and under supervision by the custodian of the public records.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. The duty attaches to whoever has custody — drives routing to the correct custodian/department. Conditions/supervision aspect split to FL-0015.

rules.legal_concept: Designation of another officer to handle requests, with identity disclosure
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian may designate another officer or employee to permit inspection and copying, but must disclose the identity of the designee to the requester.
rules.trigger: Custodian designates a designee to handle the request
rules.source_language: A custodian of public records or a person having custody of public records may designate another officer or employee of the agency to permit the inspection and copying of public records, but must disclose the identity of the designee to the person requesting to inspect or copy public records.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Permission (may designate) carrying a mandatory disclosure (must disclose identity).

rules.legal_concept: Contractor duty to keep and maintain public records
rules.atomic_rule: A contractor providing services to a public agency must keep and maintain the public records required by the agency to perform the service.
rules.trigger: Agency contract for services under which the contractor acts on behalf of the agency
rules.source_language: Keep and maintain public records required by the public agency to perform the service.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Routes requests to contractor-held records into the covered set.

rules.legal_concept: Contractor duty to provide records on the agency's request within a reasonable time
rules.atomic_rule: On the agency custodian's request, a contractor must provide the agency a copy of, or allow inspection/copying of, requested records within a reasonable time at a cost not exceeding the chapter's fees.
rules.trigger: Request from the public agency's custodian of public records to the contractor
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "within a reasonable time" from the agency custodian's request
rules.source_language: Upon request from the public agency's custodian of public records, provide the public agency with a copy of the requested records or allow the records to be inspected or copied within a reasonable time at a cost that does not exceed the cost provided in this chapter.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Fee cap cross-refers to the § 119.07(4) rates (FL-0020..FL-0022).

rules.legal_concept: Transfer or retention of records at contract completion
rules.atomic_rule: At contract completion the contractor must transfer, at no cost, all public records in its possession to the agency, or keep and maintain the records; if transferring, it must destroy exempt/confidential duplicates.
rules.trigger: Completion of the contract
rules.source_language: Upon completion of the contract, transfer, at no cost, to the public agency all public records in possession of the contractor or keep and maintain public records required by the public agency.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Determines whether contractor-held records remain retrievable for future requests after contract end.

rules.legal_concept: Only permissible delay is the limited reasonable time to retrieve and redact
rules.atomic_rule: The only delay permitted in producing records is the limited reasonable time the custodian needs to retrieve the record and delete the portions asserted to be exempt; no automatic or policy-based delay is allowed.
rules.trigger: A request has been received and records must be retrieved/reviewed for exemptions
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "limited reasonable time" to retrieve and redact, from request receipt
rules.source_language: The only delay in producing records permitted under Chapter 119, Florida Statutes, is the limited reasonable time allowed the custodian to retrieve the record and delete those portions of the record the custodian asserts are exempt.
rules.notes: Source Type: Appellate Decision (Fla. Supreme Court). Primary opinion returned HTTP 403 this pass; quote taken from AG opinions/secondary sources that reproduce it verbatim — flagged for case verification. This is the operative production 'deadline' — a soft standard, not a numeric window.

rules.legal_concept: Copy provided in the requested medium if maintained in that medium
rules.atomic_rule: An agency must provide a copy of a record in the medium requested if it maintains the record in that medium; providing a copy in a medium not routinely used, or compiling/manipulating data, is charged under s. 119.07(4).
rules.trigger: Requester specifies a medium; agency maintains an electronic recordkeeping system
rules.source_language: An agency must provide a copy of the record in the medium requested if the agency maintains the record in that medium, and the agency may charge a fee in accordance with this chapter. For the purpose of satisfying a public records request, the fee to be charged by an agency if it elects to provide a copy of a public record in a medium not routinely used by the agency, or if it elects to compile information not routinely developed or maintained by the agency or that requires a substantial amount of manipulation or programming, must be in accordance with s. 119.07(4).
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. The manipulation/programming clause is a trigger for the special service charge (FL-0025).

rules.legal_concept: Redact exempt portion and produce the remainder (segregability)
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian asserting that an exemption applies to part of a record must redact that portion to which the exemption is asserted and validly applies, and must produce the remainder for inspection and copying.
rules.trigger: Custodian asserts an exemption applies to part of a record
rules.source_language: A person who has custody of a public record who asserts that an exemption applies to a part of such record shall redact that portion of the record to which an exemption has been asserted and validly applies, and such person shall produce the remainder of such record for inspection and copying.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Mandatory segregability — a partial exemption never justifies withholding the whole record.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to state the basis of the exemption, including statutory citation
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian contending all or part of a record is exempt must state the basis of the exemption, including the statutory citation to the exemption.
rules.trigger: Custodian contends a record (or part) is exempt
rules.source_language: If the person who has custody of a public record contends that all or part of the record is exempt from inspection and copying, he or she shall state the basis of the exemption that he or she contends is applicable to the record, including the statutory citation to an exemption created or afforded by statute.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Requires the software to capture a statutory citation whenever an exemption is asserted.

rules.legal_concept: On request, written particularized reasons for an exemption/confidentiality determination
rules.atomic_rule: If the requester asks, the custodian must state in writing and with particularity the reasons for the conclusion that the record is exempt or confidential.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for the reasons for an exemption/confidentiality determination
rules.source_language: If requested by the person seeking to inspect or copy the record, the custodian of public records shall state in writing and with particularity the reasons for the conclusion that the record is exempt or confidential.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. A conditional written-notice/document the engine must be able to generate.

rules.legal_concept: Statutory per-copy duplication rate
rules.atomic_rule: For duplicated copies of records not larger than 14 by 8.5 inches, the agency may charge up to 15 cents per one-sided copy.
rules.trigger: Agency provides a standard-size one-sided duplicated copy
rules.source_language: Up to 15 cents per one-sided copy for duplicated copies of not more than 14 inches by 8 1/2 inches.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Basis is a ceiling ('up to 15 cents') — city sets the operative rate at or below $0.15/page.

rules.legal_concept: Additional charge for two-sided copies
rules.atomic_rule: For a two-sided copy, the agency may charge no more than an additional 5 cents.
rules.trigger: Agency provides a two-sided duplicated copy
rules.source_language: No more than an additional 5 cents for each two-sided copy.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Ceiling of an additional $0.05 per two-sided copy.

rules.legal_concept: Actual cost of duplication for other copies
rules.atomic_rule: For all copies other than standard-size paper copies, the agency charges the actual cost of duplication of the public record.
rules.trigger: Agency provides a copy that is not a standard-size paper copy
rules.source_language: For all other copies, the actual cost of duplication of the public record.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. 'Actual cost of duplication' is bounded by the statutory definition in FL-0023.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'actual cost of duplication'
rules.atomic_rule: 'Actual cost of duplication' means the cost of the material and supplies used to duplicate the record, and does not include labor cost or overhead cost associated with such duplication.
rules.trigger: Charging 'actual cost of duplication' under s. 119.07(4)(a)3.
rules.source_language: "Actual cost of duplication" means the cost of the material and supplies used to duplicate the public record, but does not include labor cost or overhead cost associated with such duplication.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Definition the fee engine branches on — labor/overhead are excluded from the base copy charge (they belong only to the special service charge, FL-0025).

rules.legal_concept: Charge for certified copies
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may charge up to $1 per copy for a certified copy of a public record.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for a certified copy
rules.source_language: An agency may charge up to $1 per copy for a certified copy of a public record.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Ceiling of $1.00 per certified copy.

rules.legal_concept: Special service charge for extensive IT or clerical/supervisory assistance
rules.atomic_rule: If the nature or volume of records requires extensive use of IT resources or extensive clerical/supervisory assistance, the agency may charge, in addition to actual duplication cost, a reasonable special service charge based on the cost actually incurred.
rules.trigger: Nature or volume of records requires extensive use of IT resources or extensive clerical/supervisory assistance (or both)
rules.source_language: If the nature or volume of public records requested to be inspected or copied pursuant to this subsection is such as to require extensive use of information technology resources or extensive clerical or supervisory assistance by personnel of the agency involved, or both, the agency may charge, in addition to the actual cost of duplication, a special service charge, which shall be reasonable and shall be based on the cost incurred for such extensive use of information technology resources or the labor cost of the personnel providing the service that is actually incurred by the agency or attributable to the agency for the clerical and supervisory assistance required, or both.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. 'Reasonable' with no fixed number = soft-standard; city sets a rate methodology under the reasonableness constraint. Applies to inspection as well as copying. Trigger term 'extensive' is undefined.

rules.legal_concept: Supervision charge when requester photographs records
rules.atomic_rule: When a person photographs public records, the custodian may charge for supervision services at a rate agreed upon by the parties; if they cannot agree, the custodian determines the charge.
rules.trigger: A person elects to photograph public records rather than obtain agency copies
rules.source_language: The custodian of public records may charge the person making the photographs for supervision services at a rate of compensation to be agreed upon by the person desiring to make the photographs and the custodian of public records. If they fail to agree as to the appropriate charge, the charge shall be determined by the custodian of public records.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. No fixed number — negotiated/custodian-set = soft-standard.

rules.legal_concept: Requester pays expense of a separate room/place to photograph records
rules.atomic_rule: Where another room or place is necessary to photograph public records, the expense of providing it is paid by the person desiring to photograph the records.
rules.trigger: Photographing records requires provision of another room or place
rules.source_language: Where provision of another room or place is necessary to photograph public records, the expense of providing the same shall be paid by the person desiring to photograph the public records.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Charge equals the actual expense incurred (fixed to cost).

rules.legal_concept: Unjustified delay or refusal as a constructive/unlawful denial
rules.atomic_rule: Delay beyond the limited reasonable time needed to retrieve and redact, or a policy-based/automatic delay, constitutes an unlawful (constructive) denial of access.
rules.trigger: Custodian delays production beyond the limited reasonable time, or imposes an automatic/policy delay
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: constructive denial arises once delay exceeds the "limited reasonable time" (no fixed day-count)
rules.source_language: The only delay in producing records permitted under Chapter 119, Florida Statutes, is the limited reasonable time allowed the custodian to retrieve the record and delete those portions of the record the custodian asserts are exempt.
rules.notes: Source Type: Appellate Decision. Keeper-sliver #3 (constructive-denial trigger): Florida sets NO numeric silence-equals-denial period; the trigger is the soft 'reasonable time' standard. Remedy amounts (attorney fees under § 119.12) deliberately excluded. Primary opinion not opened (403) — flagged.

material_negatives.note: Florida sets NO fixed numeric acknowledgment or response deadline. The only standards are 'promptly'/'good faith' (§ 119.07(1)(c)) and the 'limited reasonable time' of Tribune Co. v. Cannella. Captured as soft-standard rules FL-0007 and FL-0014, not numeric parameters. Absence of a day-count is itself the finding.

Chapter 119 contains NO explicit statutory deposit/advance-payment provision. AG opinions and practice permit requiring payment of estimated fees before producing copies, but no codified clock or threshold was found. Deferred to an AG-opinion pass; not emitted as a rule to avoid asserting a statute that does not exist.

No statute imposes a mandatory clarification stage or a nonresponse-abandonment clock. Case law recognizes that overbroad requests may be met with a request to narrow, but no explicit statutory clarification clock or deemed-abandonment trigger was located. Deferred to case-law/AG pass.

Florida provides NO internal administrative appeal stage and no statewide AG administrative-review adjudication for records denials. Enforcement is judicial (civil action / mandamus). Emitted affirmatively as the judicial path FL-0029; the absence of an administrative appeal is a structural fact, not a gap to fill with a value.
No statutory requirement that agencies assign or track a request number, log requests, or report request metrics for an individual municipal request. Nothing for the software to enforce here.
No statutory free-copy allowance or de minimis waiver threshold was found; the fee schedule (§ 119.07(4)) applies from the first copy. Absence noted; cities may adopt their own waiver policy.
