structural_branches.description: FL-0029: Florida's exemption dispute path is judicial — a civil action with mandatory in camera inspection for enumerated exemptions. There is NO statutory internal/administrative appeal stage; the engine must express a court-review fork rather than an appeal.administrative.* stage.
FL-0030: a distinct state the request enters — a 30-day no-disposal hold on the record whenever a written request is made and the custodian disputes the record's public status.
FL-0014: production timing is a soft 'limited reasonable time' standard the engine applies, not a city-filled numeric window — a structural deadline path distinct from a parameter value.
FL-0007: acknowledgment is governed by the soft standard 'promptly' — a structural deadline the engine applies, with no numeric value to configure.
FL-0028: the request can transition to a constructive-denial (unlawful refusal) state once delay exceeds the reasonable time — a terminal branch triggered by a soft standard, not a fixed clock.

FL-0011..FL-0013: when a contractor holds agency records, a distinct routing/production sub-path applies (maintain, provide within reasonable time at chapter cost, transfer/keep at contract completion).
FL-0017..FL-0019: mandatory segregability path — assert exemption with statutory citation, redact, produce remainder, and generate written particularized reasons on request.

rules.legal_concept: Universal right of public inspection and copying
rules.atomic_rule: All public records are open for personal inspection and copying by any person, except records specifically exempted by court order or by law; no requester qualification is imposed for general access.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right of access)
rules.source_language: All public records shall be open for personal inspection and copying, except those which by order of a court of this state or by law are specifically exempted from disclosure. Records shall be maintained by agencies to the extent and in the manner required by Article 5 of this chapter.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Universal-access fact emitted as a rule with shared key per prompt discipline #2. Reinforced by 50-18-71(b)(1)(B): 'any person may make photographic copies.' Verbatim from opened official State of Georgia PDF; core provision confirmed unchanged in 2024 Georgia Code.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required for general records access
rules.atomic_rule: A requester need not state a reason or purpose to obtain general public records; a purpose/'need' showing is required only for enumerated special record types (e.g., motor vehicle accident reports).
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: The general right in O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(a)-(b) imposes no purpose requirement; a 'need' showing is imposed only for specific record types (see O.C.G.A. § 50-18-72(a)(5), motor vehicle accident reports, which defines 'need' by enumerated categories).
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Paraphrase: the general no-purpose rule is stated by absence, and the enumerated 'need' requirement for accident reports is the exception that proves it. Emitted as a rule with shared key per discipline #2, never a negative. Manual verification of the general/no-purpose reading recommended.

rules.legal_concept: No residency or citizenship requirement to request records
rules.atomic_rule: There is no Georgia residency or citizenship condition on the right to request public records; the right runs to any person.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: The Open Records Act conditions access on the record's public status, not the requester's residency; no residency or citizenship qualification appears in O.C.G.A. § 50-18-70 or § 50-18-71.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Paraphrase (stated by absence). Emitted as a rule with shared key per discipline #2. Manual verification recommended.

rules.legal_concept: Request may be made orally or in writing
rules.atomic_rule: A request may be made to the custodian orally or in writing; an oral request is a valid intake path (though it does not unlock the statutory enforcement remedies — see GA-0007).
rules.trigger: Request submitted to custodian
rules.source_language: A request made pursuant to this article may be made to the custodian of a public record orally or in writing.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim from opened official PDF.

rules.legal_concept: Agency option to require written requests to a designated officer
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may (but is not obligated to) require that all written requests be directed to a designated official chosen from an enumerated list (director/chair/CEO, senior satellite official, designated records custodian clerk, or designated open records officer).
rules.trigger: Agency elects to require directed written requests
rules.source_language: An agency may, but shall not be obligated to, require that all written requests be made upon the responder's choice of one of the following: the agency's director, chairperson, or chief executive officer, however denominated; the senior official at any satellite office of an agency; a clerk specifically designated by an agency as the custodian of agency records; or a duly designated open records officer of an agency.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Keeper-sliver #1 (custodian designation / routing). Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Agency must accept written requests by e-mail or facsimile
rules.atomic_rule: An agency shall permit receipt of written requests by e-mail or facsimile in addition to other approved methods, provided the agency uses e-mail or facsimile in the normal course of its business.
rules.trigger: Agency uses e-mail or facsimile in normal course of business
rules.source_language: An agency shall permit receipt of written requests by e-mail or facsimile transmission in addition to any other methods of transmission approved by the agency, provided such agency uses e-mail or facsimile in the normal course of its business.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Open records officer designation, notice, and website posting
rules.atomic_rule: An agency that designates one or more open records officers shall make the designation in writing, immediately provide notice of them to any person on request (orally or in writing), notify the county legal organ, and, if it has a website, prominently display the designation.
rules.trigger: Agency elects to designate an open records officer
rules.source_language: Any agency that designates one or more open records officers upon whom requests for inspection or copying of records may be delivered shall make such designation in writing and shall immediately provide notice to any person upon request, orally or in writing, of those open records officers. If the agency has elected to designate an open records officer, the agency shall so notify the legal organ of the county in which the agency's principal offices reside and, if the agency has a website, shall also prominently display such designation on the agency's website.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Keeper-sliver #1. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Three-day clock start when agency requires requests to a designee
rules.atomic_rule: Where an agency requires that requests be directed to designated individuals, the three-day response period does not begin to run until the request is made in writing upon such individuals.
rules.trigger: Agency has elected to require directed requests; request delivered to a required designee
rules.clock_spec: 3 business-day response clock does not start until written request is delivered to the required designated individual
rules.source_language: In the event an agency requires that requests be made upon the individuals identified in subparagraph (B) of paragraph (1) of this subsection, the three-day period for response to a written request shall not begin to run until the request is made in writing upon such individuals.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. Defines the start event for the GA-0011 clock; only applies when the agency has invoked GA-0005.

rules.legal_concept: Three business day production window
rules.atomic_rule: An agency shall produce responsive records within a reasonable amount of time not to exceed three business days of receipt of the request; the agency is not required to produce records that did not exist at the time of the request.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a request for existing records
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 3 business-days from receipt of request
rules.source_language: Agencies shall produce for inspection all records responsive to a request within a reasonable amount of time not to exceed three business days of receipt of a request; provided, however, that nothing in this chapter shall require agencies to produce records in response to a request if such records did not exist at the time of the request.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. The window is a ceiling ('not to exceed'); the standard within it is 'a reasonable amount of time.' City sets its operative target under the 3-business-day ceiling. Confirmed unchanged in 2024 Georgia Code. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Partial production of locatable records within the window
rules.atomic_rule: Where some but not all responsive records are available within three business days, the agency shall make available within that period those records that can be located and produced.
rules.trigger: Only some responsive records available within three business days
rules.clock_spec: 3 business-days from receipt of request (for the subset that can be located)
rules.source_language: In those instances where some, but not all, records are available within three business days, an agency shall make available within that period those records that can be located and produced.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. Requires rolling/partial production rather than waiting for the full set.

rules.legal_concept: Description-and-timeline notice when records unavailable in three days
rules.atomic_rule: Where responsive records exist but are unavailable within three business days, the agency shall within that period provide the requester a description of the records and a timeline for when they will be available.
rules.trigger: Responsive records exist but cannot be produced within three business days
rules.clock_spec: notice due within 3 business-days of receipt of request
rules.source_language: In any instance where records are unavailable within three business days of receipt of the request, and responsive records exist, the agency shall, within such time period, provide the requester with a description of such records and a timeline for when the records will be available for inspection or copying and provide the responsive records or access thereto as soon as practicable.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. This row is the notice (description + timeline) due within 3 days; GA-0014 splits out the 'as soon as practicable' production duty that the same sentence carries.

rules.legal_concept: Soft-standard production deadline for delayed records
rules.atomic_rule: For records that could not be produced within three business days, the agency shall provide the responsive records or access to them as soon as practicable (a soft, undefined standard, not a fixed day count).
rules.trigger: Records described with a timeline under GA-0013
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "as soon as practicable" from receipt of request
rules.source_language: and provide the responsive records or access thereto as soon as practicable.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Soft-standard deadline per pilot #1: config_home structural, no invented day-count. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Denial notice citing specific exempting authority within three days
rules.atomic_rule: When an agency withholds all or part of a record, it shall notify the requester of the specific legal authority for the exemption by Code section, subsection, and paragraph within three business days (or, if search/retrieval is delayed, no later than three business days after retrieval).
rules.trigger: Agency withholds all or part of a requested record
rules.clock_spec: within 3 business-days of request, or within 3 business-days after retrieval where search/retrieval is delayed
rules.source_language: In any instance in which an agency is required to or has decided to withhold all or part of a requested record, the agency shall notify the requester of the specific legal authority exempting the requested record or records from disclosure by Code section, subsection, and paragraph within a reasonable amount of time not to exceed three business days or in the event the search and retrieval of records is delayed pursuant to this subsection or pursuant to subparagraph (b)(1)(A) of this Code section, then no later than three business days after the records have been retrieved.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. Required denial-notice content (section/subsection/paragraph cite) with an attached 3-business-day ceiling.

rules.legal_concept: Hourly labor charge capped at lowest-paid qualified employee's salary
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may impose a reasonable charge for search, retrieval, and redaction, but that charge shall not exceed the prorated hourly salary of the lowest paid full-time employee who, in the custodian's reasonable discretion, has the necessary skill and training to perform the request.
rules.trigger: Agency performs search, retrieval, or redaction
rules.source_language: In all other instances, the charge for the search, retrieval, or redaction of records shall not exceed the prorated hourly salary of the lowest paid full-time employee who, in the reasonable discretion of the custodian of the records, has the necessary skill and training to perform the request; provided, however, that no charge shall be made for the first quarter hour.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Ceiling basis: state caps the rate at the lowest-paid qualified employee's prorated salary; city supplies the actual dollar figure. Confirmed unchanged in 2024 Georgia Code. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: First quarter hour of labor is free
rules.atomic_rule: No labor charge may be made for the first quarter hour of search, retrieval, or redaction.
rules.trigger: Labor charge assessed
rules.source_language: provided, however, that no charge shall be made for the first quarter hour.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Fixed statutory free increment of 15 minutes. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Copy charge capped at 10 cents per page
rules.atomic_rule: In addition to labor charges, an agency may charge for copying, not to exceed 10 cents per page for letter or legal size documents, or the actual cost of producing the copy for other document types.
rules.trigger: Agency produces paper copies
rules.source_language: In addition to a charge for the search, retrieval, or redaction of records, an agency may charge a fee for the copying of records or data, not to exceed 10¢ per page for letter or legal size documents or, in the case of other documents, the actual cost of producing the copy.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Ceiling of $0.25... note: ceiling is $0.10/page for letter/legal; other sizes at actual cost. City supplies the operative per-page value under the cap. Confirmed unchanged in 2024 Georgia Code. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Electronic records charged at actual cost of media
rules.atomic_rule: For electronic records, the agency may charge the actual cost of the media on which the records or data are produced.
rules.trigger: Agency produces records on electronic media
rules.source_language: In the case of electronic records, the agency may charge the actual cost of the media on which the records or data are produced.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Basis is actual cost of media (a fixed measured cost, not a discretionary rate). Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to use the most economical means of search and production
rules.atomic_rule: An agency shall utilize the most economical means reasonably calculated to identify and produce responsive, nonexcluded documents.
rules.trigger: Agency conducts search and production
rules.source_language: An agency shall utilize the most economical means reasonably calculated to identify and produce responsive, nonexcluded documents.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Soft standard ('most economical means reasonably calculated') that constrains how labor charges accrue; structural, no numeric value. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Specific statutory fees supersede the general fee scheme
rules.atomic_rule: Where a specific fee for certified copies or other records is authorized or prescribed by law, that specific fee applies instead of the general search/retrieval/copy charges when such records are sought.
rules.trigger: Requested record is one for which a specific statutory fee is prescribed (e.g., certified copies)
rules.source_language: Where fees for certified copies or other copies or records are specifically authorized or otherwise prescribed by law, such specific fee shall apply when certified copies or other records to which a specific fee may apply are sought.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Routes certain record types to a different fee basis; branch, not a value. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Cost estimate notice when costs will exceed $25
rules.atomic_rule: Where an agency will seek costs in excess of $25.00 to respond, it shall notify the requester within three business days and inform the requester of the cost estimate.
rules.trigger: Estimated response costs will exceed $25.00
rules.clock_spec: estimate notice due within 3 business-days of receipt of request
rules.source_language: In any instance in which an agency will seek costs in excess of $25.00 for responding to a request, the agency shall notify the requester within a reasonable amount of time not to exceed three business days and inform the requester of the estimate of the costs, and the agency may defer search and retrieval of the records until the requester agrees to pay the estimated costs unless the requester has stated in his or her request a willingness to pay an amount that exceeds the search and retrieval costs.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. The $25.00 threshold is fixed by statute (city cannot change it), so it is a structural trigger, not a city-filled parameter. This row is the estimate-notice duty; GA-0023 splits out the deferral permission the same sentence carries. Confirmed unchanged in 2024 Georgia Code. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Deferral of search/retrieval until requester agrees to pay estimate
rules.atomic_rule: The agency may defer search and retrieval until the requester agrees to pay the estimated costs, unless the request already stated a willingness to pay an amount exceeding the search and retrieval costs.
rules.trigger: Cost estimate issued under GA-0022 and requester has not pre-committed to pay
rules.clock_spec: processing paused until requester agrees to pay the estimated costs
rules.source_language: and the agency may defer search and retrieval of the records until the requester agrees to pay the estimated costs unless the requester has stated in his or her request a willingness to pay an amount that exceeds the search and retrieval costs.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. A pause state pending cost agreement; the pre-commitment carve-out prevents the pause.

rules.legal_concept: Prepayment may be required when estimate exceeds $500
rules.atomic_rule: Where the estimated production cost exceeds $500.00, the agency may insist on prepayment of the costs before beginning search, retrieval, review, or production.
rules.trigger: Estimated production cost exceeds $500.00
rules.clock_spec: processing paused pending prepayment when estimate exceeds $500.00
rules.source_language: In any instance in which the estimated costs for production of the records exceeds $500.00, an agency may insist on prepayment of the costs prior to beginning search, retrieval, review, or production of the records.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. The $500.00 threshold is fixed by statute; structural trigger. Confirmed unchanged in 2024 Georgia Code. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Prepayment for future requests where prior costs unpaid
rules.atomic_rule: Where a requester has not paid costs lawfully incurred for a prior request, the agency may require prepayment for all future requests from that person until the prior costs are paid or the payment dispute is resolved.
rules.trigger: Requester has unpaid lawfully-incurred costs from a prior request
rules.clock_spec: future requests paused pending prepayment until prior costs paid or dispute resolved
rules.source_language: Whenever any person who has requested to inspect or copy a public record has not paid the cost for search, retrieval, redaction, or copying of such records when such charges have been lawfully incurred, an agency may require prepayment for compliance with all future requests for production of records from that person until the costs for the prior production of records have been paid or the dispute regarding payment resolved.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. Requester-level state (delinquent) that gates future requests.

rules.legal_concept: Collection of agreed costs regardless of whether records are accepted
rules.atomic_rule: Where charges were lawfully estimated and agreed and the agency has incurred the agreed-upon costs to make records available, the agency may collect those charges (via tax/fee collection methods) regardless of whether the requester inspects or accepts the records.
rules.trigger: Requester agreed to estimated costs, agency incurred them, and requester does not pay
rules.source_language: Whenever any person has requested to inspect or copy a public record and does not pay the cost for search, retrieval, redaction, or copying of such records when such charges have been lawfully estimated and agreed to pursuant to this article, and the agency has incurred the agreed-upon costs to make the records available, regardless of whether the requester inspects or accepts copies of the records, the agency shall be authorized to collect such charges in any manner authorized by law for the collection of taxes, fees, or assessments by such agency.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. Affects billing/collection state of a request; included as a processing permission rather than a pure damages remedy.

rules.legal_concept: Requester may self-copy with portable devices at inspection
rules.atomic_rule: At the time of inspection, any person may make photographic copies or other electronic reproductions of the records using suitable portable devices brought to the place of inspection.
rules.trigger: Records made available for in-person inspection
rules.source_language: At the time of inspection, any person may make photographic copies or other electronic reproductions of the records using suitable portable devices brought to the place of inspection.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. A no-fee self-copy path at inspection.

rules.legal_concept: Agency may provide copies in lieu of access when redaction needed
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may, in its discretion, provide copies of a record in lieu of providing access to the record when portions contain confidential information that must be redacted.
rules.trigger: Record contains confidential portions requiring redaction
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, an agency may, in its discretion, provide copies of a record in lieu of providing access to the record when portions of the record contain confidential information that must be redacted.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. A production-mode branch used to protect redacted originals.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to create new reports, summaries, or compilations
rules.atomic_rule: No public officer or agency is required to prepare new reports, summaries, or compilations not in existence at the time of the request.
rules.trigger: Request would require creating a record not in existence at time of request
rules.source_language: No public officer or agency shall be required to prepare new reports, summaries, or compilations not in existence at the time of the request.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. Reinforced by the 'did not exist at the time of the request' clause in 50-18-71(b)(1)(A).

rules.legal_concept: Requester's choice of electronic/native/ASCII format
rules.atomic_rule: A requester may request that electronic records, data, or data fields be produced in the format in which the agency keeps them, or in a standard export format such as a flat-file ASCII format, if the agency's existing computer programs support such export; and the agency shall produce electronic copies or, if the requester prefers, printouts.
rules.trigger: Requester requests electronic records in a specified supported format
rules.source_language: A requester may request that electronic records, data, or data fields be produced in the format in which such data or electronic records are kept by the agency, or in a standard export format such as a flat file electronic American Standard Code for Information Interchange (ASCII) format, if the agency's existing computer programs support such an export format. In such instance, the data or electronic records shall be downloaded in such format onto suitable electronic media by the agency.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: No refusal because export/redaction requires query commands
rules.atomic_rule: An agency shall not refuse to produce electronic records, data, or data fields on the ground that exporting or redacting requires inputting range, search, filter, or report commands, so long as those commands can be executed using existing programs the agency uses in the ordinary course of business.
rules.trigger: Production would require running query/filter/report commands in existing agency software
rules.source_language: An agency shall not refuse to produce such electronic records, data, or data fields on the grounds that exporting data or redaction of exempted information will require inputting range, search, filter, report parameters, or similar commands or instructions into an agency's computer system so long as such commands or instructions can be executed using existing computer programs that the agency uses in the ordinary course of business to access, support, or otherwise manage the records or data.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Website access in lieu of copies; no refusal of data fields
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may provide access to records through a public website in lieu of separate printouts or copies, but if it receives a request for data fields it shall not refuse the responsive data on the ground that it is available through a website when the requester seeks the data in the electronic format in which it is kept.
rules.trigger: Records available through a public website; requester seeks data fields in native electronic format
rules.source_language: In lieu of providing separate printouts or copies of records or data, an agency may provide access to records through a website accessible by the public. However, if an agency receives a request for data fields, an agency shall not refuse to provide the responsive data on the grounds that the data is available in whole or in its constituent parts through a website if the requester seeks the data in the electronic format in which it is kept.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. Bundles a permission (website in lieu) and a prohibition (no refusal of native data fields) from one provision.

rules.legal_concept: Private vendor arrangements must not limit public access
rules.atomic_rule: If an agency contracts with a private vendor to collect or maintain public records, the agency shall ensure the arrangement does not limit public access and that the vendor does not impede record access or the method of delivery established by the agency or by law.
rules.trigger: Agency uses a private vendor to collect or maintain public records
rules.source_language: if an agency contracts with a private vendor to collect or maintain public records, the agency shall ensure that the arrangement does not limit public access to those records and that the vendor does not impede public record access and method of delivery as established by the agency or as otherwise provided for in this Code section.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. Relevant where a city routes records through a hosted/third-party system.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to redact narrowly and produce all nonexempt portions
rules.atomic_rule: Exemptions are interpreted narrowly to exclude only the portion of a record to which an exclusion is directly applicable, and the agency having custody has a duty to provide all other portions of the record for inspection or copying.
rules.trigger: A record contains both exempt and nonexempt portions
rules.source_language: This Code section shall be interpreted narrowly so as to exclude from disclosure only that portion of a public record to which an exclusion is directly applicable. It shall be the duty of the agency having custody of a record to provide all other portions of a record for public inspection or copying.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. Reinforced by the narrow-construction mandate in 50-18-70(a).

rules.legal_concept: Mandatory redaction of enumerated personal identifying information
rules.atomic_rule: Enumerated personal identifiers (e.g., social security number, financial/bank/credit-card/account data, personal e-mail or cell number, day and month of birth, medical/insurance information, and similar items) shall be redacted prior to disclosure of any requested record, subject to statutory exceptions.
rules.trigger: Requested record contains enumerated personal identifying information
rules.source_language: Records that reveal an individual's social security number, mother's birth name, credit card information, debit card information, bank account information, account number, utility account number, password used to access his or her account, financial data or information, insurance or medical information in all records, unlisted telephone number if so designated in a public record, personal e-mail address or cellular telephone number, day and month of birth ... Items exempted by this subparagraph shall be redacted prior to disclosure of any record requested pursuant to this article.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim (operative clause; full identifier list abridged with ellipsis, exceptions in (20)(B) not reproduced). A parallel public-employee PII redaction rule appears at 50-18-72(a)(21). Drives a default redaction pass on production.

rules.legal_concept: 90 business day window for University System intercollegiate athletics records
rules.atomic_rule: For records (other than nonclerical staff salary information) of intercollegiate sports programs of any University System of Georgia unit, the period for any production, access, response, or notice is 90 business days from the date the agency received the request.
rules.trigger: Request is for intercollegiate sports program records of a University System of Georgia unit
rules.clock_spec: fixed: 90 business-days from date agency received the request
rules.source_language: Any other provision of this Code section to the contrary notwithstanding, the period within which any production, access, response, or notice is required from an agency with respect to a request for records, other than salary information for nonclerical staff, of intercollegiate sports programs of any unit of the University System of Georgia, including athletic departments and related private athletic associations, shall be 90 business days from the date the agency received the request.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Applicability limit: University System of Georgia athletics only, NOT municipal agencies. Included for cross-state overlap value (record-type-specific extended deadline); a city platform would rarely hit it. Record-Specific authority scope.

rules.legal_concept: Civil litigant requests must be in writing and copied to agency counsel
rules.atomic_rule: Requests by civil litigants for records sought for use in ongoing civil or administrative litigation against the agency shall be made in writing and copied to the agency's counsel of record contemporaneously; the agency shall provide duplicate sets of produced records to that counsel at no cost unless counsel declines.
rules.trigger: Requester is a civil litigant seeking records for use in ongoing litigation against the agency
rules.source_language: Requests by civil litigants for records that are sought as part of or for use in any ongoing civil or administrative litigation against an agency shall be made in writing and copied to counsel of record for that agency contemporaneously with their submission to that agency. The agency shall provide, at no cost, duplicate sets of all records produced in response to the request to counsel of record for that agency unless the counsel of record for that agency elects not to receive the records.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. A requester-type routing/notice branch (copy-to-counsel + duplicate-set delivery).

material_negatives.note: No separate statutory acknowledgment/receipt deadline distinct from substantive response. Georgia's three-business-day period (50-18-71(b)(1)(A)) is a production/response ceiling, not a mere acknowledgment obligation; there is no standalone 'acknowledge within N days' rule.

No statutory deemed/constructive-denial trigger (no 'silence for N days = denial'). Georgia enforcement is judicial and turns on noncompliance/no substantial justification (50-18-73), not an automatic terminal clock. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

No statutory administrative appeal to a state ombudsman or records authority. Review is judicial (superior court, 50-18-73) plus discretionary Attorney General enforcement; the AG's mediation program is informal and non-statutory.
No statutory clarification/narrowing clock and no requester-clarification-then-abandonment (nonresponse-abandonment) mechanism in the Open Records Act.
No statewide statutory requirement to maintain a public request log or assign tracking numbers for open records requests.

No statewide-mandated flat municipal copy or labor rate. The state supplies only ceilings (10 cents/page for letter/legal; lowest-paid qualified employee's prorated hourly salary for labor) and a fixed 15-minute free increment; the city fills in the operative values under those ceilings.

The Act counts in 'business days' for the core response window but does not codify a general holiday/weekend computation method or a rule for when receipt occurs (e.g., after-hours or weekend submissions); computation details are left unspecified. Manual verification / later AG-opinion pass recommended.

structural_branches.description: Optional open-records-officer regime: agency may designate officer(s) in writing, must publicize (county legal organ + website), and may require directed written requests (GA-0005/GA-0008).
Conditional clock-start fork: when the agency requires directed requests, the 3-business-day clock does not start until the written request reaches the required designee (GA-0010).
Delayed-records path: description + timeline notice within 3 business days, then production 'as soon as practicable' (soft standard) (GA-0013/GA-0014).

Cost-estimate/deferral branch at the fixed $25 threshold (estimate + optional deferral) and prepayment branch at the fixed $500 threshold, plus a delinquent-requester prepayment state (GA-0022/GA-0023/GA-0024/GA-0025).
Reverse-FOIA hold: third-party submitter notice, 10-day intent-to-disclose window, and potential submitter court action before release (GA-0041).
Civil-litigant routing: written request copied to agency counsel and duplicate record sets delivered to counsel at no cost (GA-0040).
Judicial enforcement path in superior court, available only for written requests, brought by any person or by the Attorney General (GA-0036/GA-0037).
Record-type fork: 90-business-day response window for University System of Georgia intercollegiate athletics records, overriding the general 3-day rule (GA-0039) (non-municipal).

rules.legal_concept: Right of every person to examine and copy public records
rules.atomic_rule: Any person has the right to examine and take a copy of any public record of the state (no enumerated requester class), subject to statutory exemptions.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right)
rules.source_language: Every person has a right to examine and take a copy of any public record of this state
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule per contract. Note: Idaho differentiates residents vs. nonresidents on fees (74-102) and response deadlines (74-103), but the underlying right to examine extends to every person.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian shall make no inquiry of requester (limited exceptions)
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian shall make no inquiry of any person who requests a public record, except to verify identity, to ensure records are not used for prohibited mailing/telephone number lists, or to protect personal information as allowed by law.
rules.trigger: Person requests a public record
rules.source_language: The custodian shall make no inquiry of any person who requests a public record, except [for identity verification, to ensure records are not used for prohibited mailing/telephone lists, or to protect personal information as provided by law]
rules.notes: Verbatim lead clause captured; the bracketed exceptions are the statutory 'except' list (identity, mailing/telephone list prohibition, personal-information protection). No statement-of-purpose may be required, but a residency attestation IS required (ID-0007), which is a permitted inquiry.

rules.legal_concept: Requests made to the designated custodian
rules.atomic_rule: All requests to examine public records shall be made to the designated custodian of such records as defined in section 74-101(3).
rules.trigger: Requester submits a request
rules.source_language: All requests to examine public records shall be made to the designated custodian of such records as defined in section 74-101(3), Idaho Code
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: drives routing. 'Custodian' = the person(s) having personal custody and control of the records (74-101(3)). The Act references an existing custodian rather than mandating a formally designated FOIA officer.

rules.legal_concept: Request must clearly indicate it is a public records request
rules.atomic_rule: A request must clearly indicate that it is a public records request.
rules.trigger: Requester submits a request
rules.source_language: clearly indicate that it is a public records request
rules.notes: Intake gating condition; the response clock (ID-0008/0009) attaches once a compliant request is received.

rules.legal_concept: Written request describing subject matter, records sought, and date range
rules.atomic_rule: The requester must submit a written request describing the subject matter, the records sought, and the specific date range, together with the requester's name, mailing address, email address, and telephone number.
rules.trigger: Requester submits a request
rules.source_language: Requests must submit written requests describing subject matter, records sought, and specific date ranges [and provide the requester's name, mailing address, email address, telephone number] (paraphrased from 74-102)
rules.notes: Paraphrase flagged: retrieved text summarized the description/contact requirement; needs verbatim re-capture of the exact 74-102 subsection listing required request contents. The contact/name/attestation portion was captured verbatim under ID-0007.

rules.legal_concept: Written declaration of residency status under oath
rules.atomic_rule: The request must include the requester's name, mailing address, email address, telephone number, and a written declaration, attesting or affirming under oath, whether the requester is a resident.
rules.trigger: Requester submits a request
rules.source_language: provide the requester's name, mailing address, email address, telephone number, and a written declaration by the requesting party attesting or affirming under oath whether such requester is a resident
rules.notes: State-specific fork introduced by the 2025 amendment: the sworn residency declaration determines which response-deadline tier (3 working days vs. 21 days) and which fee tier (resident free allotments vs. nonresident actual-cost) apply. 'Resident' = domicile in Idaho continuously >=30 days (74-101(15)).

rules.legal_concept: Grant or deny within 3 working days (resident)
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency or custodian shall either grant or deny a resident's request to examine or copy public records within three (3) working days of receipt of the request.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a resident's request
rules.clock_spec: fixed: 3 working-days from receipt of request (resident)
rules.source_language: A public agency or custodian shall either grant or deny a resident's request to examine or copy public records within three (3) working days of the date of the receipt of the request
rules.notes: Resident tier. Same concept as nonresident window (ID-0009); split by requester tier, not concept. Extendable under ID-0010.

rules.legal_concept: Grant or deny within 21 days (nonresident)
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency or custodian shall either grant or deny a request from a person who is not a resident and not employed by a resident to examine or copy public records within twenty-one (21) days of receipt of the request.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a nonresident's request
rules.clock_spec: fixed: 21 calendar-days from receipt of request (nonresident)
rules.source_language: A public agency or custodian shall either grant or deny a request from a person who is not a resident and not employed by a resident to examine or copy public records within twenty-one (21) days of the date of the receipt
rules.notes: Nonresident tier (2025 amendment). Extendable under ID-0011. Unit appears to be calendar days (contrast the resident 'working days' window).

rules.legal_concept: Extension to 10 working days to locate/retrieve (resident)
rules.atomic_rule: If a longer period is needed to locate or retrieve the records, the public agency shall provide the public records no later than ten (10) working days following a resident's request.
rules.trigger: Longer time needed to locate or retrieve the records
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: no later than 10 working-days from resident's request
rules.source_language: the public agency shall provide the public records no later than ten (10) working days following the person's request, if such person is a resident
rules.notes: Extension of the resident 3-working-day base window (ID-0008), triggered when records must be located or retrieved.

rules.legal_concept: Extension to 35 days to locate/retrieve (nonresident)
rules.atomic_rule: If a longer period is needed to locate or retrieve the records, the public agency shall provide the public records no later than thirty-five (35) days following a nonresident's request.
rules.trigger: Longer time needed to locate or retrieve the records
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: no later than 35 calendar-days from nonresident's request
rules.source_language: no later than thirty-five (35) days following a request from a nonresident
rules.notes: Extension of the nonresident 21-day base window (ID-0009).

rules.legal_concept: Electronic-format conversion extension with written notice and mutually agreed time
rules.atomic_rule: If an existing electronic record must first be converted to another electronic format and the conversion cannot be completed within the response time allotted, the agency shall so notify the requester in writing and provide the converted record at a time mutually agreed upon between the agency and the requester.
rules.trigger: Requested electronic record must be converted to another format and conversion cannot be completed within the allotted response time
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "mutually agreed upon" time from written conversion notice
rules.source_language: Additionally, if it is determined that the existing electronic record requested will first have to be converted to another electronic format by the agency or by a third party and that such conversion cannot be completed within the time allotted for the response, the agency shall so notify in writing the person requesting to examine or copy the records. The agency shall provide the converted public record at a time mutually agreed upon between the agency and the requester, with due consideration given to any limitations that may exist due to the process of conversion or due to the use of a third party to make the conversion.
rules.notes: Soft deadline: no numeric period; requires written notice plus a mutually agreed delivery time -> config_home structural per contract. Distinct sub-path from the ordinary locate/retrieve extension (ID-0010/0011).

rules.legal_concept: Failure to timely respond deemed a denial
rules.atomic_rule: If the public agency or custodian fails to respond within the time allotted for the response, the request shall be deemed to be denied.
rules.trigger: No response within the allotted response time
rules.clock_spec: terminal: deemed denial at expiry of the applicable response window (ID-0008/0009, or extension ID-0010/0011)
rules.source_language: If the public agency or custodian fails to respond within the time allotted for the response, the request shall be deemed to be denied.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: constructive-denial trigger. The deemed denial starts the appeal path; the 180-day judicial petition clock (ID-0028) runs from the date of mailing of a notice of denial.

rules.legal_concept: Written notice of denial or partial denial
rules.atomic_rule: On a denial or partial denial, the person legally responsible for administering the public agency or that person's designee shall notify the person in writing of the denial or partial denial.
rules.trigger: Agency denies or partially denies a request
rules.source_language: the person legally responsible for administering the public agency or that person's designee shall notify the person in writing of the denial or partial denial
rules.notes: Required document on denial. Routes the denial to a named responsible official/designee.

rules.legal_concept: Contents of denial notice: statutory authority and appeal rights/time periods
rules.atomic_rule: The notice of denial or partial denial shall indicate the statutory authority for the denial and clearly indicate the person's right to appeal the denial or partial denial and the time periods for doing so.
rules.trigger: Agency issues a written denial or partial denial
rules.source_language: The notice of denial or partial denial...shall indicate the statutory authority for the denial and indicate clearly the person's right to appeal the denial or partial denial and the time periods for doing so.
rules.notes: Retrieved text also indicated the notice reflects attorney-review status; capture of that specific clause deferred for verbatim confirmation. Notice must state the appeal time period, which corresponds to the 180-day judicial petition window (ID-0028).

rules.legal_concept: Separation of exempt and nonexempt material
rules.atomic_rule: If a record contains both nonexempt and exempt material, the agency shall, upon receipt of a request, separate the exempt and nonexempt material and make the nonexempt material available for examination; a request to copy nonexempt material may not be denied merely because it is contained in the same record as exempt material.
rules.trigger: Record contains both exempt and nonexempt material and a request is received
rules.source_language: If any public record contains material which is not exempt from disclosure as well as material which is exempt from disclosure, the public agency shall, upon receipt of a request for disclosure, separate the exempt and nonexempt material and make the nonexempt material available for examination, provided that a denial of a request to copy nonexempt material in a public record shall not be based upon the fact that such nonexempt material is contained in the same public record as the exempt material.
rules.notes: Full verbatim text captured.

rules.legal_concept: First 2 hours of labor free (resident)
rules.atomic_rule: No fee shall be charged for the first two (2) hours of labor in responding to a resident's public records request.
rules.trigger: Resident request; labor incurred
rules.source_language: no fee shall be charged for the first two (2) hours of labor in responding to a request submitted by a resident for public records, or for copying the first one hundred (100) pages
rules.notes: Resident-only free allotment. Split from the free-copies allotment (ID-0018) which shares the same source sentence.

rules.legal_concept: First 100 pages of copies free (resident)
rules.atomic_rule: No fee shall be charged for copying the first one hundred (100) pages of paper records in responding to a resident's request.
rules.trigger: Resident request; copies made
rules.source_language: no fee shall be charged for the first two (2) hours of labor in responding to a request submitted by a resident for public records, or for copying the first one hundred (100) pages
rules.notes: Resident-only free allotment; charges above the threshold governed by the actual-cost ceiling (ID-0019).

rules.legal_concept: Copy fee may not exceed actual cost (resident)
rules.atomic_rule: The fee charged to a resident may not exceed the actual cost to the agency of copying the record.
rules.trigger: Copies provided beyond the free allotment
rules.source_language: The fee for residents may not exceed the actual cost to the agency of copying the record
rules.notes: Idaho sets no statutory per-page cents rate; the ceiling is 'actual cost' (city supplies the operative rate under it).

rules.legal_concept: Labor charges limited to reasonable cost at lowest-paid staff rate
rules.atomic_rule: Fees for resident requests shall not exceed reasonable labor costs necessarily incurred, charged at the per-hour pay rate of the lowest-paid administrative staff employee or public official of the agency.
rules.trigger: Labor incurred beyond the free 2-hour allotment
rules.source_language: Fees for requests made by residents shall not exceed reasonable labor costs necessarily incurred in responding to a public records request ... shall be charged at the per hour pay rate of the lowest paid administrative staff employee or public official of the public agency
rules.notes: Two verbatim fragments from 74-102(10)(e) joined; the labor rate is bound to a specific staff pay rate (city supplies the actual dollar rate under the ceiling).

rules.legal_concept: Computer/electronic record fee capped at sum of enumerated costs
rules.atomic_rule: For computer records, the agency may charge a fee that does not exceed the sum of the direct cost of copying, the standard cost of publication, and the cost of conversion.
rules.trigger: Request for records maintained in a computer/electronic system
rules.source_language: a public agency or public official may charge a fee...that does not exceed the sum of [direct cost of copying, standard cost of publication, and cost of conversion]
rules.notes: Verbatim lead clause captured with ellipsis; the three enumerated cost components should be re-captured verbatim from 74-102(10)(d) for the exact list.

rules.legal_concept: Nonresident fees may be higher but not exceed actual cost
rules.atomic_rule: The agency may charge nonresidents higher fees than residents (including for labor and copies without the resident free allotments), but such fees may not exceed the actual cost to the agency.
rules.trigger: Nonresident request
rules.source_language: Agencies may charge higher fees for non-residents, though fees cannot exceed actual costs (paraphrased from 74-102)
rules.notes: Paraphrase flagged: retrieved text summarized the nonresident fee treatment; needs verbatim re-capture of the exact 74-102(10) nonresident subsection. Core fork: nonresidents do not receive the resident free-labor/free-copy allotments.

rules.legal_concept: Fee waiver in the public interest for indigent resident requester
rules.atomic_rule: The agency shall not charge a resident any cost or fee for copies or labor when the examination is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding, is not primarily in the individual interest of the requester, and the requester lacks sufficient financial resources such that fees would prevent access.
rules.trigger: Resident requester meets the public-interest and inability-to-pay conditions
rules.source_language: The public agency shall not charge any cost or fee for copies or labor when the requester is a resident [and the examination is likely to contribute to public understanding, is not primarily in the individual interest, and fees would prevent access due to insufficient resources]
rules.notes: Verbatim lead clause captured; the three-part waiver test in brackets was summarized and should be re-captured verbatim. Waiver limited to residents. Multi-factor conjunctive standard kept in one row per grain rule.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian may require advance payment of fees
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may require advance payment of the fees authorized by this section before providing the records.
rules.trigger: Fees are authorized for the request
rules.source_language: The custodian may require advance payment of fees authorized by this section
rules.notes: Discretionary ('may'); permits an advance-payment/deposit gate on production.

rules.legal_concept: Electronic-format copy if available and specifically requested
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may provide a copy of a public record in electronic form if the record is available in electronic form and the person specifically requests an electronic copy.
rules.trigger: Record available in electronic form and requester specifically requests electronic copy
rules.source_language: Nothing contained herein shall prevent a public agency from providing a copy of a public record in electronic form if the record is available in electronic form and if the person specifically requests an electronic copy
rules.notes: Permissive format-provision rule; interacts with the conversion extension (ID-0012) and electronic-record fee (ID-0021).

material_negatives.note: Idaho sets NO statutory per-page cents copy rate. Copy fees are bound only to 'actual cost' (74-102(10)(c)); the city supplies the operative rate under that ceiling.
No separate acknowledgment-of-receipt requirement found; the statute requires the agency to 'grant or deny' within the response window (74-103), not a distinct acknowledgment.

No explicit clarification clock or nonresponse-abandonment provision located in Title 74 Ch. 1. The 'clearly indicate it is a public records request' requirement (ID-0005) is the closest intake gate; absence of a clarification rule is not proof none exists.

The retrieved 74-115 text did not include an explicit burden-of-proof-on-agency, in-camera-examination, or de-novo-review clause. Requires manual verification of the full 74-115 text before asserting or excluding these.
Idaho does not appear to require formally designating/publishing a public-records officer; it references the existing 'custodian' (74-101(3)). Contrast IL/WA which mandate an officer designation.

Idaho Code 74-113 (Access to Records About a Person by a Person) creates a distinct access-to-own-records workflow, and 74-120 prohibits use of records for mailing/telephone lists (driving the permitted custodian inquiry). Not fully captured this pass; flag for a special-records / distinct-workflow follow-up.

Resident windows are stated in 'working days' (3 / 10) while nonresident windows are stated in plain 'days' (21 / 35). Whether nonresident days are calendar days (assumed here) should be confirmed against the exact 74-103(2) text.

structural_branches.description: The 2025 amendment (ch. 298) creates a resident vs. nonresident fork determined by a sworn residency declaration (ID-0007): residents get a 3-working-day response window and free allotments (2 labor hours / 100 pages); nonresidents get a 21-day window and no free allotments. The engine must branch every request on residency status.

Distinct electronic-format conversion sub-path (ID-0012): when a record must be converted and cannot be delivered in the allotted time, the agency issues a written notice and delivers at a mutually agreed time -- a bespoke soft-deadline stage separate from the ordinary locate/retrieve extension.
Nonresponse within the allotted window is a terminal deemed-denial state (ID-0013) that ends normal processing and opens the judicial appeal path.
Idaho's Act provides only a judicial appeal path -- petition to district court (ID-0027) within 180 days (ID-0028). There is no internal/administrative appeal stage to model.

rules.legal_concept: Public records open to any person
rules.atomic_rule: A public body must make all public records available to any person for inspection or copying, except records exempt under Sections 7 and 8.5.
rules.trigger: None stated (any person may request)
rules.source_language: Each public body shall make available to any person for inspection or copying all public records, except as otherwise provided in Sections 7 and 8.5 of this Act.
rules.notes: Shared universal-access key. Sections 7 (exemptions) and 8.5 (mandatory-disclosure carve-outs) are the exception surfaces; not inventoried here.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may not require a requester to state the purpose of a request, except to determine commercial-purpose status or to rule on a fee-waiver request.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: A public body may not require that a request be submitted on a standard form or require the requester to specify the purpose for a request, except to determine whether the records are requested for a commercial purpose or whether to grant a request for a fee waiver.
rules.notes: Two carve-outs: commercial-purpose determination drives fee basis; fee-waiver determination drives fee reduction. Same sentence also supports IL-0004.

rules.legal_concept: No residency requirement
rules.atomic_rule: Any person may request public records; the Act imposes no residency or citizenship condition on the right of access.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: Each public body shall make available to any person for inspection or copying all public records, except as otherwise provided in Sections 7 and 8.5 of this Act.
rules.notes: Shared universal-access key emitted as a rule per discovery discipline #2. Source language is the verbatim any-person clause; the absence of any residency limitation is inferred from that clause and from the broad Section 2 definition of Person. Not a separate operative sentence.

rules.legal_concept: No mandatory request form
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may not require that a request be submitted on a standard form.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: A public body may not require that a request be submitted on a standard form or require the requester to specify the purpose for a request, except to determine whether the records are requested for a commercial purpose or whether to grant a request for a fee waiver.
rules.notes: Section 3(c) also requires that requests be made in writing for the 5-day clock to run, but permits oral requests to be honored (IL-0005).

rules.legal_concept: Freedom of Information officer designation
rules.atomic_rule: Each public body must designate one or more officials or employees to act as its Freedom of Information officer(s).
rules.trigger: None stated (standing duty)
rules.source_language: Each public body shall designate one or more officials or employees to act as its Freedom of Information officer or officers.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver (who-must-respond / routing). Drives routing of an incoming request to a designated FOIA officer.

rules.legal_concept: FOIA officer notes receipt date and computes due date
rules.atomic_rule: Upon receiving a request, the FOIA officer must note the date the public body received the written request and compute and record the date the response period expires.
rules.trigger: Public body receives a written request
rules.clock_spec: start event = date written request received; due-date computed per Section 3(d)/(e)
rules.source_language: Upon receiving a request for a public record, the Freedom of Information officer shall: (1) note the date the public body receives the written request; (2) compute the day on which the period for response will expire and make a notation of that date on the written request...
rules.notes: Establishes the clock-start mechanic that IL-0010 depends on. Verbatim captured for paragraphs (1)-(2); later paragraphs of 3.5(b) continue the officer's duties.

rules.legal_concept: Five-business-day response
rules.atomic_rule: A public body must comply with or deny a written request within 5 business days after receipt, unless the time is properly extended.
rules.trigger: Public body receives a written request
rules.clock_spec: 5 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: Each public body shall, promptly, either comply with or deny a request for public records within 5 business days after its receipt of the request, unless the time for response is properly extended under subsection (e) of this Section.
rules.notes: Statute also imposes a co-standard: response must be prompt (the word promptly modifies the 5-day cap). Commercial (IL-0017), recurrent (IL-0020), and voluminous (IL-0024) requests run on different windows.

rules.legal_concept: Extension of response time
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may extend the response time by not more than 5 business days beyond the original due date for any of seven enumerated reasons.
rules.trigger: One of seven enumerated conditions (records off-site; substantial collection; categorical/extensive search; records not yet located; exemption review; undue operational burden; need for consultation)
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: up to 5 business-days beyond original due date
rules.source_language: The time for response under this Section may be extended by the public body for not more than 5 business days from the original due date for any of the following reasons: (i) the requested records are stored in whole or in part at other locations than the office having charge of the requested records; (ii) the request requires the collection of a substantial number of specified records; (iii) the request is couched in categorical terms and requires an extensive search for the records responsive to it; (iv) the requested records have not been located in the course of routine search and additional efforts are being made to locate them; (v) the requested records require examination and evaluation by personnel having the necessary competence and discretion to determine if they are exempt from disclosure under Section 7 of this Act or should be revealed only with appropriate deletions; (vi) the request for records cannot be complied with by the public body within the time limits prescribed by subsection (d) of this Section without unduly burdening or interfering with the operations of the public body; (vii) there is a need for consultation, which shall be conducted with all practicable speed, with another public body or among 2 or more components of a public body having a substantial interest in the determination or in the subject matter of the request.
rules.notes: Ceiling of 5 business days is fixed by statute; the enumerated reasons are the gating conditions. Extension is optional (may).

rules.legal_concept: Notice of extension
rules.atomic_rule: When it extends, the public body must, within 5 business days after receipt, notify the requester of the reasons for the extension and the date the response will be forthcoming.
rules.trigger: Public body invokes an extension under Section 3(e)
rules.clock_spec: notice due within 5 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: When additional time is required for any of the above reasons, the public body shall, within 5 business days after receipt of the request, notify the person making the request of the reasons for the extension and the date by which the response will be forthcoming.
rules.notes: Required notice (structural) with a fixed timing; failure to give it defaults back to the 5-day denial trigger (IL-0014).

rules.legal_concept: Extension by written agreement
rules.atomic_rule: The requester and the public body may agree in writing to extend the time for compliance for a period determined by the parties.
rules.trigger: Written agreement between requester and public body
rules.clock_spec: period agreed in writing by the parties (no statutory cap)
rules.source_language: The person making a request and the public body may agree in writing to extend the time for compliance for a period to be determined by the parties.
rules.notes: An agreed extension has no statutory day-count; the parties set it. Distinct from the 5-day unilateral extension (IL-0011).

rules.legal_concept: Failure to respond is a denial
rules.atomic_rule: Failure to comply with, extend the time for, or deny a written request within 5 business days after receipt is treated as a denial of the request.
rules.trigger: 5 business days elapse with no compliance, extension, or denial
rules.clock_spec: denial deemed at expiry of 5 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: Failure to comply with a written request, extend the time for response, or deny a request within 5 business days after its receipt shall be considered a denial of the request.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver #3 (constructive denial). A deemed denial opens the PAC-review and judicial-review paths (final denial for review purposes).

rules.legal_concept: Unduly burdensome categorical request
rules.atomic_rule: A request for all records within a category may be denied only if compliance would be unduly burdensome, there is no way to narrow it, and the burden outweighs the public interest in the information.
rules.trigger: Categorical request whose compliance is unduly burdensome with no way to narrow
rules.source_language: Requests calling for all records falling within a category shall be complied with unless compliance with the request would be unduly burdensome for the complying public body and there is no way to narrow the request and the burden on the public body outweighs the public interest in the information.
rules.notes: Conjunctive three-part test kept in one row (not fragmented). Gated by the mandatory confer step in IL-0016.

rules.legal_concept: Opportunity to confer
rules.atomic_rule: Before denying a categorical request as unduly burdensome, the public body must give the requester an opportunity to confer to reduce the request to manageable proportions.
rules.trigger: Public body intends to invoke the unduly-burdensome exemption
rules.source_language: Before invoking this exemption, the public body shall extend to the person making the request an opportunity to confer with it in an attempt to reduce the request to manageable proportions.
rules.notes: Mandatory precondition to the IL-0015 denial path.

rules.legal_concept: Commercial-purpose request response time
rules.atomic_rule: A public body must respond to a request for records to be used for a commercial purpose within 21 working days after receipt.
rules.trigger: Request is for a commercial purpose
rules.clock_spec: 21 working-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: A public body shall respond to a request for records to be used for a commercial purpose within 21 working days after receipt.
rules.notes: Source term is working days (distinct from business days used elsewhere). Commercial-purpose is a Section 2 defined classification branch.

rules.legal_concept: Required content of commercial-request response
rules.atomic_rule: The commercial-request response must do one of four things: give a time-and-fee estimate, deny under an exemption, notify the request is unduly burdensome with an opportunity to narrow, or provide the records.
rules.trigger: Public body responds to a commercial-purpose request
rules.source_language: The response shall (i) provide to the requester an estimate of the time required by the public body to provide the records requested and an estimate of the fees to be charged, which the public body may require the person to pay in full before copying the requested documents, (ii) deny the request pursuant to one or more of the exemptions set out in this Act, (iii) notify the requester that the request is unduly burdensome and extend an opportunity to the requester to attempt to reduce the request to manageable proportions, or (iv) provide the records requested.
rules.notes: Four-branch response menu specific to commercial requests. Prepayment permission split out as IL-0019.

rules.legal_concept: Full prepayment before copying
rules.atomic_rule: When it gives a fee estimate on a commercial or recurrent-requester request, the public body may require the requester to pay the fees in full before copying the requested documents.
rules.trigger: Public body issues a fee estimate on a commercial or recurrent-requester request
rules.source_language: provide to the requester an estimate of the time required by the public body to provide the records requested and an estimate of the fees to be charged, which the public body may require the person to pay in full before copying the requested documents
rules.notes: Payment gate. Identical prepayment language appears in Section 3.2(a) for recurrent requesters; one concept cited to both.

rules.legal_concept: Recurrent-requester response time
rules.atomic_rule: A public body must respond to a request from a recurrent requester within 21 business days after receipt.
rules.trigger: Requester meets the recurrent-requester definition
rules.clock_spec: 21 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: a public body shall respond to a request from a recurrent requester...within 21 business days after receipt
rules.notes: Source term is business days (vs working days for commercial, IL-0017). Elided text in the quote is the intervening statutory clause naming the recurrent requester; captured operative window verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Five-day recurrent-requester notice
rules.atomic_rule: Within 5 business days after receiving a request from a recurrent requester, the public body must notify the requester that it is being treated under the recurrent-requester provisions.
rules.trigger: Public body receives a request from a recurrent requester
rules.clock_spec: notice due within 5 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: Within 5 business days after receiving a request from a recurrent requester...the public body shall notify the requester
rules.notes: Required notice with a fixed 5-business-day timing. Elided text names the recurrent-requester status the notice addresses.

rules.legal_concept: Recurrent requester
rules.atomic_rule: A requester is a recurrent requester if, in the prior 12 months, it submitted to the same public body at least 50 requests, or at least 15 within a 30-day period, or at least 7 within a 7-day period.
rules.trigger: Request-volume thresholds met against the same public body
rules.source_language: "Recurrent requester", as used in Section 3.2 of this Act, means a person that, in the 12 months immediately preceding the request, has submitted to the same public body (i) a minimum of 50 requests for records, (ii) a minimum of 15 requests for records within a 30-day period, or (iii) a minimum of 7 requests for records within a 7-day period.
rules.notes: Definition the software branches on (drives the recurrent-requester workflow). Thresholds are state-fixed; the city cannot change them, so treated as a structural classification fork rather than a city parameter.

rules.legal_concept: Voluminous request
rules.atomic_rule: A request is voluminous if it includes more than 5 individual requests for more than 5 different categories of records within 20 business days, or requires compiling more than 500 letter/legal-sized pages (unless a single record exceeds 500 pages).
rules.trigger: Category-count or page-volume thresholds met
rules.source_language: "Voluminous request" means a request that: (i) includes more than 5 individual requests for more than 5 different categories of records or a combination of individual requests that total requests for more than 5 different categories of records in a period of 20 business days; or (ii) requires the compilation of more than 500 letter or legal-sized pages of public records unless a single requested record exceeds 500 pages.
rules.notes: Definition the software branches on (drives the voluminous-request workflow and its fee tiers). Full statutory definition (including the exclusions for requests from news media, non-profits, etc.) may carry further carve-outs; captured core thresholds verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Voluminous request initial response
rules.atomic_rule: A public body must respond to a voluminous request within 5 business days after receipt (notifying the requester it is being treated as voluminous).
rules.trigger: Request meets the voluminous-request definition
rules.clock_spec: 5 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: a public body shall respond to a voluminous request within 5 business days after receipt.
rules.notes: This initial response notifies the requester the request is voluminous and triggers the requester-response window (IL-0025).

rules.legal_concept: Requester response to voluminous notice
rules.atomic_rule: After the public body's voluminous-request response, the requester must respond within 10 business days; if the requester does not respond (or the request remains voluminous), the public body responds and assesses any fees.
rules.trigger: Public body sends its voluminous-request response
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from the public body's response being sent
rules.source_language: the requester must respond to the public body within 10 business days after the public body's response was sent
rules.notes: Statute does not state that non-response withdraws the request; if the requester does not respond within 10 business days the public body proceeds to respond and assess fees. Requester-facing deadline, so config_home structural.

rules.legal_concept: Voluminous request final response
rules.atomic_rule: The public body must give its final voluminous-request response within the earlier of 5 business days after receiving the requester's response or 5 business days after the final day for the requester to respond.
rules.trigger: Requester responds, or the requester-response window closes
rules.clock_spec: earlier of 5 business-days from requester's response OR 5 business-days from final day for requester to respond
rules.source_language: the public body shall respond within the earlier of 5 business days after it receives the response from the requester or 5 business days after the final day for the requester to respond
rules.notes: Two-branch earlier-of calculation kept in one row.

rules.legal_concept: First 50 pages free
rules.atomic_rule: No fee may be charged for the first 50 pages of black-and-white, letter- or legal-sized copies requested.
rules.trigger: Requester requests black-and-white letter/legal copies
rules.source_language: No fees shall be charged for the first 50 pages of black and white, letter or legal sized copies requested by a requester.
rules.notes: Fixed 50-page free threshold set by state; the city cannot lower it.

rules.legal_concept: Per-page copy fee cap
rules.atomic_rule: The fee for black-and-white, letter- or legal-sized copies (after the free 50) may not exceed 15 cents per page.
rules.trigger: Copies beyond the first 50 black-and-white letter/legal pages
rules.source_language: The fee for black and white, letter or legal sized copies shall not exceed 15 cents per page.
rules.notes: Ceiling of 15 cents; the city sets the operative rate at or below it. Same concept whether a city charges a fixed 10 cents or the full 15 cents.

rules.legal_concept: Color/non-standard copy cost
rules.atomic_rule: For copies in color or in a size other than letter/legal, a public body may not charge more than its actual cost of reproduction.
rules.trigger: Copies in color or a non-letter/legal size
rules.source_language: If a public body provides copies in color or in a size other than letter or legal, the public body may not charge more than its actual cost for reproducing the records.
rules.notes: Ceiling tied to actual cost (no fixed number).

rules.legal_concept: Certification fee cap
rules.atomic_rule: The cost for certifying a record may not exceed $1.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for a certified record
rules.source_language: The cost for certifying a record shall not exceed $1.
rules.notes: Ceiling of $1 per certification.

rules.legal_concept: Electronic recording-medium cost
rules.atomic_rule: For records provided in electronic format, a public body may charge the requester only the actual cost of purchasing the recording medium.
rules.trigger: Records furnished in electronic format on a recording medium
rules.source_language: A public body may charge the requester for the actual cost of purchasing the recording medium, whether disc, diskette, tape, or other medium.
rules.notes: Ceiling tied to actual medium cost. Voluminous electronic requests have their own tiered caps (IL-0038).

rules.legal_concept: No search/review fee (non-commercial)
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may not charge the requester for the cost of any search for and review of the records.
rules.trigger: Any non-commercial request
rules.source_language: a public body may not charge the requester for the costs of any search for and review of the records.
rules.notes: General prohibition on search/review charges; the only exception is the commercial-request hourly fee in Section 6(f) (IL-0035).

rules.legal_concept: Fee waiver in the public interest
rules.atomic_rule: Documents must be furnished without charge or at reduced charge, as determined by the public body, if the requester states a specific purpose and the waiver is in the public interest (principally to disseminate information on public health/safety/welfare or legal rights, not for personal/commercial benefit).
rules.trigger: Requester states a specific purpose and asserts the waiver is in the public interest
rules.source_language: Documents shall be furnished without charge or at a reduced charge, as determined by the public body, if the person requesting the documents states the specific purpose for the request and indicates that a waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest.
