rules.legal_concept: Five-day written determination when public-record status is questioned
rules.atomic_rule: When the custodian raises a question whether an item is a public record, the custodian shall, within five days (excluding weekends and legal holidays) of receipt of the request, notify the requester in writing of the determination and the reasons.
rules.trigger: Custodian raises a question whether the requested item is a public record
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: within 5 business-days from receipt of the written request (excl. Sat/Sun/legal holidays)
rules.source_language: In any case in which a record is requested and a question is raised by the custodian of the record as to whether it is a public record, such custodian shall within five days, exclusive of Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays, of the receipt of the request, in writing for such record, notify in writing the person making such request of his determination and the reasons therefor.
rules.notes: CURRENCY: this window is FIVE business days in current law (older sources say 'three days' — outdated for 44:32(D)). Conditional on the custodian questioning status; not a universal acknowledgment deadline.

rules.legal_concept: Denial notice must cite the legal basis for exemption
rules.atomic_rule: A written determination withholding a record (or part) must reference the basis under law the custodian determined exempts the record, or any part thereof, from inspection, copying, or reproduction.
rules.trigger: Custodian determines a record or part is exempt
rules.source_language: Such written notification shall contain a reference to the basis under law which the custodian has determined exempts a record, or any part thereof, from inspection, copying, or reproduction.
rules.notes: Notice-content requirement; the 'or any part thereof' phrasing is the statute's nearest hook for partial exemption/redaction, but no explicit segregate-and-release-the-remainder mandate exists.

rules.legal_concept: Constructive (deemed) denial after five days of nonresponse
rules.atomic_rule: Passage of five days (excluding weekends and legal holidays) from an in-person, written, or electronic request without receiving a written determination or a time estimate constitutes a denial, entitling the requester to enforcement proceedings.
rules.trigger: Five business days elapse from request with no written determination and no time estimate
rules.clock_spec: terminal: 5 business-days from request (in-person/written/electronic), excl. Sat/Sun/legal holidays, with no determination or estimate
rules.source_language: Any person who has been denied the right to inspect, copy, reproduce, or obtain a copy or reproduction of a record under the provisions of this Chapter, either by a determination of the custodian or by the passage of five days, exclusive of Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays, from the date of his in-person, written, or electronic request without receiving a determination in writing by the custodian or an estimate of the time reasonably necessary for collection, segregation, redaction, examination, or review of a records request, may institute proceedings for the issuance of a writ of mandamus, injunctive or declaratory relief
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver deemed-denial trigger (remedy amounts dropped). This is the closest thing to a universal response deadline: respond (or give a time estimate) within 5 business days or the request is constructively denied.

rules.legal_concept: Time estimate forestalls constructive denial
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may respond within the five-day window with an estimate of the time reasonably necessary for collection, segregation, redaction, examination, or review, which forestalls the constructive denial.
rules.trigger: Custodian cannot produce/determine within five days but responds with a time estimate
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "time reasonably necessary for collection, segregation, redaction, examination, or review" from the estimate
rules.source_language: without receiving a determination in writing by the custodian or an estimate of the time reasonably necessary for collection, segregation, redaction, examination, or review of a records request
rules.notes: Structural alternative response path: providing a reasonable-time estimate prevents the deemed denial in LA-0030. The estimate itself is an undefined-soft standard.

rules.legal_concept: Denial when request would substantially disrupt government operations (after attempt to narrow)
rules.atomic_rule: If the custodian reasonably determines a request would substantially disrupt required government operations, the custodian may deny access, but only after reasonable attempts to narrow or specify the request with the requester.
rules.trigger: Custodian reasonably determines the request would substantially disrupt required government operations
rules.source_language: If the custodian reasonably determines that the request would substantially disrupt required government operations, the custodian may deny access only after reasonable attempts to narrow or specify the request with the requestor.
rules.notes: Discretionary denial gated by a mandatory clarification/narrowing step; embeds the clarification.narrow_request concept. No clock on the narrowing dialogue.

material_negatives.note: No fixed universal acknowledgment deadline for ordinary requests. The 5-business-day 44:32(D) window applies only when the custodian QUESTIONS whether an item is a public record; the general obligation is functionally enforced by the 5-business-day constructive-denial trigger (44:35(A), LA-0030). Absence of a found universal-acknowledgment statute is not proof none exists.

No administrative-appeal stage exists in the Public Records Law. There is no AG/ombudsman/records-authority binding review; the Attorney General issues only advisory opinions. Enforcement is by direct suit in district court (44:35). Emitted as a negative so the cross-state join does not manufacture a phantom administrative stage.

No request- or litigation-triggered preservation/hold provision in the PRL. La. R.S. 44:36 imposes only a routine default 3-year retention (excluded as routine retention). No statute directs a custodian to freeze destruction because a request, appeal, or suit is pending.

No statewide statutory per-page or per-item copy-fee CAP for municipal/local custodians; the only constraint is 'reasonable' (44:32(C)(1)(a), LA-0021). A uniform dollar schedule exists only for STATE agencies (44:32(C)(2)(a), LA-0026).
No deadline governs the clarification/narrowing dialogue. The narrowing step under 44:32(A)(2) (LA-0034) is mandatory before a disruption-based denial but carries no statutory clock.

No statutory right to receive records in a requester-specified format. The custodian must provide copies and MAY transmit electronic copies (44:32(C)(1)(a), LA-0020), but no format-preference or native-format mandate is stated.
No statutory requirement to assign or communicate a tracking/reference number, or to maintain a public request log.

No absolute outer deadline for completing production of a voluminous request; the statute relies on the 'time reasonably necessary for collection, segregation, redaction, examination, or review' estimate (44:35(A), LA-0031) rather than a fixed maximum.

structural_branches.description: 44:33(B) forks on record availability: immediately-available records are presented immediately (LA-0015); records in active use route to a written certificate fixing a day/hour within 3 business days (LA-0016).
44:34 branch: when the record is not in the applied-to person's custody/control, the request routes to a written certification identifying reason, location, and the correct custodian (LA-0018).
44:32(D) branch: when the custodian questions public-record status, the request enters a 5-business-day written-determination-with-legal-basis state (LA-0028/LA-0029).
44:35(A) terminal branch: 5 business days without a written determination or a time estimate moves the request into a constructive-denial state that unlocks judicial enforcement (LA-0030).
44:35(A) alternative branch: issuing a reasonable-time estimate diverts the request off the constructive-denial track into an extended-processing state (LA-0031).
44:32(A)(2) branch: a request deemed to substantially disrupt operations must pass through a mandatory narrow/specify dialogue before a discretionary denial (LA-0034).
44:35 judicial path (no administrative predicate): district-court mandamus/injunctive/declaratory action, venued in the custodian's parish and tried by preference/summarily (LA-0032/LA-0033).

44:32(C)(1)(a) branch: nonpayment after advance notice, or an outstanding prior balance, holds production pending payment (LA-0023/LA-0024); after-hours examination routes to an overtime-compensation-prepaid path (LA-0027).

research_note:
Research date: 2026-07-22. Most recent legislative session reviewed: 2024 Regular Session (statutes verified current via legis.la.gov as of July 2026; codified statutes were available and opened/quoted directly).

CURRENT-LAW STATEMENT: Louisiana's Public Records Law is codified at La. R.S. 44:1 et seq. (Title 44, Chapter 1), grounded in La. Const. art. XII, § 3. The operative request-processing sections (44:1, 44:31, 44:31.1, 44:32, 44:33, 44:34, 44:35) were opened and quoted verbatim from the official Louisiana State Legislature site (legis.la.gov). IMPORTANT CURRENCY NOTE: the custodian "questioned-record" written-determination window under 44:32(D) is FIVE business days in current law; older compilations/handbooks stating "three days" for 44:32(D) are outdated. The separate 3-business-day window survives only in 44:33(B) (fixing a day/hour when a record is in active use). The 44:1 definitions were read from a 2016 official-content compilation and re-confirmed against the 2024 code (public-body, custodian, and security-feature-exclusion language all present); manual re-verification of any post-2024 amendments recommended.

COVERAGE MATRIX: eligibility=Researched-rules-found; municipal coverage=rules-found; intake/submission=rules-found; scope & clarification=Partial (narrowing under 44:32(A)(2), no clock); classification=rules-found (44:32(D) status determination); deadlines & time calc=rules-found; search/identification=Partial (segregation duty; no numeric search-time standard beyond a "reasonably necessary" estimate); custody/routing=rules-found (44:34); communications/notices=rules-found; production/inspection=rules-found; electronic records/format=Partial (transmission permitted; no format-preference mandate); fees=rules-found; payment/deposits=rules-found; redaction/segregability=Partial (44:32(D) "any part thereof"; no explicit segregate-and-release mandate); denials=rules-found; administrative/AG review=Researched-none-found (AG opinions advisory only); appeals=rules-found (judicial only); enforcement trigger=rules-found (deemed denial); request tracking=none-found; special record types=selective (below).

EXCLUDED (with reason): La. R.S. 44:36 preservation/3-year default retention (routine records-retention schedule, NOT request-triggered — no request/litigation hold exists in the PRL); La. R.S. 44:35(E) actual damages and civil penalty not-to-exceed $100/day (remedy amounts — the response-duty trigger is kept via the deemed-denial rule); La. R.S. 44:35(D) attorney-fee award (attorney-fee provision on Remove list); bulk of La. R.S. 44:2–44:29 and the 44:4/44:4.1 incorporated exemption catalog (confidentiality lists — only those altering processing noted as special records); La. R.S. 44:9 criminal-record expungement procedure (record-specific court process, not general request handling); 44:4.1(A) legislative findings (policy statement).

SPECIAL RECORD TYPES (selective — create a distinct workflow/notice/review; flagged for human legal review): (1) Proprietary/trade-secret records (44:3.2) — custodian must immediately notify the developer/owner of the request before disclosure and make a determination within the 44:32(D)/44:33(B) time period; cover-sheet marking regime. (2) Law-enforcement / pending-criminal-litigation records (44:3) — separate withholding standard; the initial arrest/incident report remains public with enumerated fields. (3) Personnel records (44:11) — home address/phone (if requested confidential), SSN, and financial-institution direct-deposit info are confidential, triggering a redaction workflow. (4) Security features / interior building plans of public schools (44:1(A)(2)(b)) — not "public records." These require human legal review before automation.

rules.legal_concept: Public right of access to public records
rules.atomic_rule: A records access officer must permit inspection or furnish a copy of any public record to any requestor, without limiting access to a class of persons.
rules.trigger: A person submits a request for a public record.
rules.source_language: A records access officer appointed pursuant to section 6A, or a designee, shall at reasonable times and without unreasonable delay permit inspection or furnish a copy of any public record as defined in clause twenty-sixth of section 7 of chapter 4, or any segregable portion of a public record, not later than 10 business days following the receipt of the request
rules.notes: The statute grants access without any requester-class limitation (no residency, citizenship, or standing condition). Emitted as the shared universal-access key per cross-state symmetry.

rules.legal_concept: No residency or citizenship condition on access
rules.atomic_rule: Access to public records is not conditioned on the requestor's residency or citizenship; any person may request regardless of state of residence.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: A records access officer appointed pursuant to section 6A, or a designee, shall at reasonable times and without unreasonable delay permit inspection or furnish a copy of any public record ... not later than 10 business days following the receipt of the request, provided that: (i) the request reasonably describes the public record sought; (ii) the public record is within the possession, custody or control of the agency or municipality ...; and (iii) the records access officer receives payment of a reasonable fee
rules.notes: Derived from the ABSENCE of any residency condition in the statutory preconditions (which are limited to description, custody, and fee). is_paraphrase=true because it is an inference from absence, not a verbatim clause. Emitted as a rule with the shared key per universal-access symmetry rather than as a material negative.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A records access officer may not require the requester to state the purpose of a request, except to determine a commercial purpose or to rule on a fee-waiver request.
rules.trigger: A person submits a request; RAO seeks to condition it on purpose.
rules.source_language: a records access officer may not require the requester to specify the purpose for a request, except to determine whether the records are requested for a commercial purpose or whether to grant a request for a fee waiver
rules.notes: Regulatory parallel at 950 CMR 32.06(1)(h), which adds a third exception for records that may be exempt under M.G.L. c. 4, § 7(26)(n).

rules.legal_concept: Commercial purpose (definition)
rules.atomic_rule: 'Commercial purpose' means the sale/resale of a record or use of its information to advance the requester's strategic business interests for profit, excluding news, citizen oversight, and academic/scientific/journalistic/public research.
rules.trigger: RAO must classify a request to set fee basis or evaluate a fee-waiver/excess-fee petition.
rules.source_language: as used in this section ''commercial purpose'' shall mean the sale or resale of any portion of the public record or the use of information from the public record to advance the requester's strategic business interests in a manner that the requester can reasonably expect to make a profit, and shall not include gathering or reporting news or gathering information to promote citizen oversight or further the understanding of the operation or activities of government or for academic, scientific, journalistic or public research or education
rules.notes: Definition the software branches on: drives fee basis and eligibility for excess-fee/waiver treatment.

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable description of record
rules.atomic_rule: A valid request must reasonably describe the public record sought so the RAO can identify and locate it.
rules.trigger: A person submits a request.
rules.source_language: provided that: (i) the request reasonably describes the public record sought
rules.notes: Regulatory parallel 950 CMR 32.06(1)(b). Gates whether the time clock starts (see MA-0015).

rules.legal_concept: Record within possession, custody or control
rules.atomic_rule: The duty to produce applies only where the record is within the possession, custody, or control of the agency or municipality the RAO serves.
rules.trigger: A request is received.
rules.source_language: (ii) the public record is within the possession, custody or control of the agency or municipality that the records access officer serves
rules.notes: Gates routing: records not in custody trigger the written-response identification duty in § 10(b)(ii)-(iii).

rules.legal_concept: Permitted delivery channels for requests
rules.atomic_rule: A request may be delivered by hand, by first class mail to the RAO's business address, or by electronic mail to the posted address (regulations add facsimile if the custodian has fax access).
rules.trigger: A person elects a delivery method.
rules.source_language: A request for public records may be delivered to the records access officer by hand or via first class mail at the record officer's business address, or via electronic mail to the address posted by the agency or municipality that the records access officer serves.
rules.notes: Regulation 950 CMR 32.06(1)(c) adds delivery by facsimile if the custodian has facsimile access.

rules.legal_concept: Oral and telephone requests
rules.atomic_rule: Requests may be made orally in person to a records access officer or custodian; telephone requests may be accepted at the RAO's discretion.
rules.trigger: A person makes an oral request.
rules.source_language: requests for public records may be made orally in person to a records access officer or custodian or may be written. Telephone requests may be accepted at the discretion of the records access officer.
rules.notes: An oral request is valid but cannot be the basis of an administrative appeal (see MA-0064). Clock for oral request begins the day it was made.

rules.legal_concept: No mandatory request form
rules.atomic_rule: A records access officer shall not require requesters to use a particular form, though optional forms may be made available.
rules.trigger: A person submits a request without using an agency form.
rules.source_language: a records access officer shall not require a particular form be used by requesters, but may make forms available for requesters.

rules.legal_concept: Records access officer designation
rules.atomic_rule: Each agency and municipality must designate one or more employees as records access officers to coordinate and respond to public-records requests.
rules.trigger: None stated (ongoing structural obligation).
rules.source_language: Each agency and municipality shall designate 1 or more employees as records access officers.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: lives under officer-designation but drives who-must-respond / routing.

rules.legal_concept: Municipal clerk as records access officer
rules.atomic_rule: In a municipality, the municipal clerk (or the clerk's designees, or any designee the chief executive officer appoints) serves as records access officer.
rules.trigger: Municipal context.
rules.source_language: In a municipality, the municipal clerk, or the clerk's designees, or any designee of a municipality that the chief executive officer of the municipality may appoint, shall serve as records access officers.
rules.notes: Municipal-specific routing default.

rules.legal_concept: Identification of other custodian
rules.atomic_rule: If sought records are not within its possession, custody, or control, the written response must identify those records and identify the agency or municipality that may possess them, if known.
rules.trigger: Requested records are not within the responding entity's custody.
rules.source_language: (ii) identify any public records or categories of public records sought that are not within the possession, custody, or control of the agency or municipality that the records access officer serves; (iii) identify the agency or municipality that may be in possession, custody or control of the public record sought, if known;
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver routing rule; component of the § 10(b) written response.

rules.legal_concept: Computation of time / deemed receipt
rules.atomic_rule: For a written request, time computation begins on the first business day following the date of receipt; an oral request is deemed received the day it was made.
rules.trigger: A valid request is received.
rules.clock_spec: start event: first business day following receipt (written) / day made (oral)
rules.source_language: Unless otherwise provided, the computation of time referred to in 950 CMR 32.00 shall begin with the first business day following the date of receipt of any request, regardless of physical form. The computation of time for an oral request shall begin with the day the oral request was made to the custodian.
rules.notes: Defines the start event for the 10-business-day clock. Parallel deemed-receipt rule at 950 CMR 32.06(2)(e). clock_effect kept 'none' as this is a calculation defining the start, not itself a deadline.

rules.legal_concept: Clock runs only for compliant requests
rules.atomic_rule: Calculation of time commences only for requests made in accordance with the request requirements (e.g., reasonable description, proper delivery).
rules.trigger: A request is received that does or does not meet the request requirements.
rules.source_language: calculation of time will commence only for requests that are made in accordance with 950 CMR 32.06(1).

rules.legal_concept: 10-business-day production/response deadline
rules.atomic_rule: The RAO must permit inspection or furnish a copy (or any segregable portion) not later than 10 business days following receipt of the request.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a valid request.
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from receipt of request
rules.source_language: shall at reasonable times and without unreasonable delay permit inspection or furnish a copy of any public record ... or any segregable portion of a public record, not later than 10 business days following the receipt of the request
rules.notes: Core response window. Fixed by statute (10 business days); the city does not vary it.

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable times / without unreasonable delay
rules.atomic_rule: Independent of the 10-day cap, production or inspection must occur at reasonable times and without unreasonable delay.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a valid request.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "at reasonable times and without unreasonable delay" from request receipt
rules.source_language: shall at reasonable times and without unreasonable delay permit inspection or furnish a copy of any public record
rules.notes: Soft/undefined standard; do not convert to a day count. Config Home structural (a standard the engine applies).

rules.legal_concept: 10-business-day written response
rules.atomic_rule: If the entity will not fully produce within the initial timeframe (or will withhold), it must inform the requestor in writing not later than 10 business days after initial receipt.
rules.trigger: Entity does not intend to permit inspection/copy within subsection (a), or the request unduly burdens it.
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from initial receipt of request
rules.source_language: the agency or municipality shall inform the requestor in writing not later than 10 business days after the initial receipt of the request for public records. The written response shall be made via first class or electronic mail

rules.legal_concept: Required contents of the written response
rules.atomic_rule: The § 10(b) written response must contain nine enumerated elements: receipt confirmation; records not in custody; other custodian; records withheld with specific exemptions; records to be produced with a burden statement; a reasonable production timeframe; a suggested scope modification; an itemized good-faith fee estimate; and a statement of appeal and judicial-review rights.
rules.trigger: A § 10(b) written response is triggered.
rules.source_language: The written response shall ... (i) confirm receipt of the request; ... (iv) identify any records, categories of records or portions of records that the agency or municipality intends to withhold, and provide the specific reasons for such withholding, including the specific exemption or exemptions upon which the withholding is based ... (vi) identify a reasonable timeframe in which the agency or municipality shall produce the public records sought ... (vii) suggest a reasonable modification of the scope of the request ... (viii) include an itemized, good faith estimate of any fees that may be charged to produce the records; and (ix) include a statement informing the requestor of the right of appeal to the supervisor of records under subsection (a) of section 10A and the right to seek judicial review
rules.notes: Kept as one structural notice with its mandatory content set; distinct parametric/clock components (extended timeframe, fee estimate) are split into their own rows.

rules.legal_concept: Extended production timeframe (municipality)
rules.atomic_rule: For a municipality, the reasonable production timeframe stated in the written response shall not exceed 25 business days following initial receipt of the request.
rules.trigger: Municipality invokes the § 10(b) extended-timeframe path.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 25 business-days from initial receipt (municipality)
rules.source_language: provided, that for an agency, the timeframe shall not exceed 15 business days following the initial receipt of the request for public records and for a municipality the timeframe shall not exceed 25 business days following the initial receipt of the request for public records
rules.notes: Municipal ceiling. Same concept as MA-0021 (agency, 15 bd) with different actor/value.

rules.legal_concept: Extended production timeframe (agency)
rules.atomic_rule: For a (state) agency, the reasonable production timeframe stated in the written response shall not exceed 15 business days following initial receipt of the request.
rules.trigger: Agency invokes the § 10(b) extended-timeframe path.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 15 business-days from initial receipt (agency)
rules.source_language: provided, that for an agency, the timeframe shall not exceed 15 business days following the initial receipt of the request for public records
rules.notes: Agency variant of the same ceiling concept. Included for completeness; municipal build uses MA-0020.

rules.legal_concept: Requestor-agreed response date
rules.atomic_rule: The requestor may voluntarily agree to a response date beyond the statutory extended timeframes.
rules.trigger: Requestor agrees to a later response date.
rules.source_language: provided further, that the requestor may voluntarily agree to a response date beyond the timeframes set forth herein
rules.notes: A branch that extends the applicable deadline by mutual agreement; not a numeric value.

rules.legal_concept: RAO petition to Supervisor for extension
rules.atomic_rule: A records access officer may petition the Supervisor of Records for an extension of time as soon as practical and within 20 business days after initial receipt (or within 10 business days after a Supervisor determination that the record is public).
rules.trigger: Magnitude/difficulty of the request or multiple requests unduly burdens the entity so it cannot complete within the § 10(b)(vi) time.
rules.clock_spec: within 20 business-days from initial receipt (or 10 business-days from Supervisor determination)
rules.source_language: a records access officer may, as soon as practical and within 20 business days after initial receipt of the request, or within 10 business days after receipt of a determination by the supervisor of public records that the requested record constitutes a public record, petition the supervisor of records for an extension of the time
rules.notes: Structural extension path with a filing deadline.

rules.legal_concept: Copy of extension petition to requestor
rules.atomic_rule: Upon submitting the extension petition to the Supervisor, the RAO must furnish a copy of the petition to the requestor.
rules.trigger: RAO submits an extension petition.
rules.source_language: The records access officer shall, upon submitting the petition to the supervisor of records, furnish a copy of the petition to the requestor.

rules.legal_concept: Supervisor single extension (municipality)
rules.atomic_rule: Upon a showing of good cause, the Supervisor may grant a single extension to a municipality not to exceed 30 business days.
rules.trigger: Supervisor finds good cause on an RAO extension petition.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: single extension up to 30 business-days (municipality)
rules.source_language: Upon a showing of good cause, the supervisor of records may grant a single extension to an agency not to exceed 20 business days and a single extension to a municipality not to exceed 30 business days.
rules.notes: Municipal variant; single extension only.

rules.legal_concept: Supervisor single extension (agency)
rules.atomic_rule: Upon a showing of good cause, the Supervisor may grant a single extension to a (state) agency not to exceed 20 business days.
rules.trigger: Supervisor finds good cause on an RAO extension petition.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: single extension up to 20 business-days (agency)
rules.source_language: the supervisor of records may grant a single extension to an agency not to exceed 20 business days
rules.notes: Agency variant of the same ceiling concept.

rules.legal_concept: Supervisor decision on extension petition
rules.atomic_rule: The Supervisor must issue a written decision on an RAO extension petition within 5 business days following receipt of the petition.
rules.trigger: Supervisor receives an RAO extension petition.
rules.clock_spec: 5 business-days from Supervisor's receipt of the petition
rules.source_language: The supervisor of records shall issue a written decision regarding a petition submitted by a records access officer under this subsection within 5 business days following receipt of the petition.

rules.legal_concept: Relief for frivolous/harassing request series
rules.atomic_rule: If the Supervisor finds a request is part of a series of contemporaneous requests that are frivolous or designed to intimidate/harass and not for broad public dissemination, the Supervisor may grant a longer extension or relieve the entity of its obligation to provide copies.
rules.trigger: Supervisor's finding of a frivolous/harassing contemporaneous request series.
rules.clock_spec: terminal: obligation to provide copies may be relieved (or a longer extension granted)
rules.source_language: If the supervisor of records determines that the request is part of a series of contemporaneous requests that are frivolous or designed to intimidate or harass, and the requests are not intended for the broad dissemination of information to the public about actual or alleged government activity, the supervisor of records may grant a longer extension or relieve the agency or municipality of its obligation to provide copies of the records sought.
rules.notes: A terminal branch (request obligation may end) available only via Supervisor determination.

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable fee not to exceed actual cost
rules.atomic_rule: A records access officer may assess a reasonable fee for production (except freely-inspectable records), and the fee shall not exceed the actual cost of reproducing the record.
rules.trigger: RAO produces records that are not freely available for inspection.
rules.source_language: A records access officer may assess a reasonable fee for the production of a public record except those records that are freely available for public inspection. The reasonable fee shall not exceed the actual cost of reproducing the record.
rules.notes: Overall ceiling under which the itemized fee components sit.

rules.legal_concept: Per-page copy fee cap
rules.atomic_rule: The fee for standard black-and-white paper copies or printouts shall not exceed 5 cents per page, for both single- and double-sided copies.
rules.trigger: RAO provides paper copies/printouts.
rules.source_language: the fee assessed for standard black and white paper copies or printouts of records shall not exceed 5 cents per page, for both single and double-sided black and white copies or printouts
rules.notes: Ceiling $0.05/page. City may charge at or below.

rules.legal_concept: Storage device/material cost
rules.atomic_rule: The actual cost of any storage device or material provided in response to a request may be included as part of the fee.
rules.trigger: RAO provides records on a storage device/material.
rules.source_language: the actual cost of any storage device or material provided to a person in response to a request for public records under subsection (a) may be included as part of the fee

rules.legal_concept: Hourly labor rate cap (municipality)
rules.atomic_rule: For a municipality, the hourly labor rate must equal or be less than the lowest-paid capable employee's rate and shall not exceed $25 per hour, unless a higher rate is approved by the Supervisor.
rules.trigger: Municipality devotes more than 2 hours of employee time to a request.
rules.source_language: if a municipality is required to devote more than 2 hours of employee time to search for, compile, segregate, redact or reproduce a record requested, the records access officer may include as part of the fee an hourly rate equal to or less than the hourly rate attributed to the lowest paid employee who has the necessary skill required to search for, compile, segregate, redact or reproduce the record requested but the fee (A) shall not be more than $25 per hour unless such rate is approved by the supervisor of records under clause (iv)
rules.notes: Municipal ceiling $25/hr; may be exceeded only with Supervisor approval (MA-0037).

rules.legal_concept: Hourly labor rate cap (agency)
rules.atomic_rule: For a (state) agency, the hourly labor rate must equal or be less than the lowest-paid capable employee's rate and shall not be more than $25 per hour.
rules.trigger: Agency devotes more than 4 hours of employee time to a request.
rules.source_language: if an agency is required to devote more than 4 hours of employee time ... the records access officer may also include as part of the fee an hourly rate equal to or less than the hourly rate attributed to the lowest paid employee who has the necessary skill ... but the fee (A) shall not be more than $25 per hour
rules.notes: Agency variant of the same ceiling concept (agency cannot exceed $25/hr even with approval).

rules.legal_concept: Free labor hours (municipality)
rules.atomic_rule: For a municipality with a population over 20,000, no labor fee may be assessed for the first 2 hours of work performed.
rules.trigger: Municipality (population over 20,000) performs request labor.
rules.source_language: (B) shall not be assessed for the first 2 hours of work performed where the responding municipality has a population of over 20,000 people
rules.notes: Free-hour threshold (2 hrs) applies only to municipalities over 20,000 population; municipalities of 20,000 or fewer are not entitled to charge labor at all under the structure and the 2-hour free tier is population-gated.

rules.legal_concept: Free labor hours (agency)
rules.atomic_rule: For a (state) agency, no labor fee may be assessed for the first 4 hours of work performed.
rules.trigger: Agency performs request labor.
rules.source_language: (B) shall not be assessed for the first 4 hours of work performed
rules.notes: Agency variant of the same free-hours concept (4 hrs).

rules.legal_concept: No fee for segregation/redaction time
rules.atomic_rule: A fee shall not be assessed for time spent segregating or redacting records unless such segregation/redaction is required by law or approved by the Supervisor.
rules.trigger: Entity spends time segregating or redacting records.
rules.source_language: (C) shall not be assessed for time spent segregating or redacting records unless such segregation or redaction is required by law or approved by the supervisor of records under clause (iv)
rules.notes: Regulatory parallel 950 CMR 32.07(2)(d).

rules.legal_concept: Supervisor approval for redaction charge / excess rate
rules.atomic_rule: The Supervisor may approve a petition to charge for segregation/redaction time, or a municipal petition to charge over $25/hour, if the request is for a commercial purpose or the fee is a necessary, reasonable good-faith cost not designed to deter access; the entity must furnish the petition to the requestor and the Supervisor decides within 5 business days.
rules.trigger: Agency/municipality petitions the Supervisor to charge redaction time or exceed $25/hr.
rules.clock_spec: Supervisor written determination within 5 business-days of receipt of the petition
rules.source_language: the supervisor of records may approve a petition from an agency or municipality to charge for time spent segregating or redacting, or a petition from a municipality to charge in excess of $25 per hour, if the supervisor of records determines that (A) the request is for a commercial purpose; or (B) the fee represents an actual and good faith representation by the agency or municipality to comply with the request, the fee is necessary such that the request could not have been prudently completed without the redaction, segregation or fee in excess of $25 per hour and the amount of the fee is reasonable and the fee is not designed to limit, deter or prevent access
rules.notes: Structural fee-petition path; the 5-business-day decision clock is stated in § 10(d)(iv)(3). Contains a multi-factor test kept intact per grain rule.

rules.legal_concept: Fee waiver or reduction
rules.atomic_rule: The RAO may waive or reduce a fee upon a showing that disclosure is in the public interest (likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of government and not primarily in the requestor's commercial interest), or that the requestor lacks the financial ability to pay the full reasonable fee.
rules.trigger: Requestor shows public interest or inability to pay.
rules.source_language: the records access officer may waive or reduce the amount of any fee charged under this subsection upon a showing that disclosure of a requested record is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations or activities of the government and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requestor, or upon a showing that the requestor lacks the financial ability to pay the full amount of the reasonable fee

rules.legal_concept: Itemized good-faith fee estimate
rules.atomic_rule: If fees are to be assessed, the RAO must provide a written, itemized, good-faith estimate of fees before complying, within the 10-business-day response.
rules.trigger: Fees will be charged for a request.
rules.source_language: if fees are being assessed, a records access officer shall provide a written, itemized, good faith estimate of any fees that may be charged to produce the records prior to complying with a public records request within ten business days.
rules.notes: Statutory basis at M.G.L. c. 66, § 10(b)(viii).

rules.legal_concept: No fee unless timely written response
rules.atomic_rule: A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the RAO responded to the requestor within 10 business days under subsection (b).
rules.trigger: RAO failed to provide the § 10(b) response within 10 business days.
rules.clock_spec: terminal: fee right is forfeited if no § 10(b) response within 10 business-days
rules.source_language: A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the records access officer responded to the requestor within 10 business days under subsection (b).
rules.notes: Strong operational consequence tied to the response clock; regulatory parallel 950 CMR 32.06(2)(c). clock_effect terminal reflects the loss of the fee entitlement.

rules.legal_concept: Denial for unpaid prior balances
rules.atomic_rule: The RAO may deny public-records requests from a requester who has failed to compensate the entity for previously produced public records.
rules.trigger: Requester has an unpaid balance for previously produced records.
rules.source_language: the records access officer may deny public records requests from a requester who has failed to compensate the agency or municipality for previously produced public records

rules.legal_concept: Written notice of unpaid-balance denial
rules.atomic_rule: When denying for an unpaid balance, the RAO shall provide written notification detailing the reasons, including an itemized list of balances attributed to previously produced records.
rules.trigger: RAO denies a request under the unpaid-balance provision.
rules.source_language: the records access officer shall provide a written notification to the requester detailing the reasons behind the denial, including an itemized list of any balances attributed to previously produced records

rules.legal_concept: Payment of reasonable fee as precondition
rules.atomic_rule: The production duty is conditioned on the RAO receiving payment of a reasonable fee as set forth in subsection (d).
rules.trigger: A fee is properly assessed for a request.
rules.source_language: (iii) the records access officer receives payment of a reasonable fee as set forth in subsection (d).

rules.legal_concept: Delay of production pending full payment
rules.atomic_rule: A records access officer may delay provision of records until all fees related to the request are paid in full by the person seeking access.
rules.trigger: Assessed fees remain unpaid.
rules.source_language: a records access officer may delay provision of records until all fees related to such requests are paid in full by the person seeking access to the requested records in accordance with 950 CMR 32.07.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to produce segregable portions
rules.atomic_rule: The RAO must furnish any segregable portion of a public record (i.e., disclose non-exempt portions even where other portions are withheld).
rules.trigger: A record contains both disclosable and withheld/exempt portions.
rules.source_language: shall at reasonable times and without unreasonable delay permit inspection or furnish a copy of any public record ... or any segregable portion of a public record

rules.legal_concept: No duty to create a new record
rules.atomic_rule: The RAO is not required to create a new public record to comply with a request; furnishing a segregable portion of an existing record is not creation of a new record.
rules.trigger: A request would require creating a record that does not exist.
rules.source_language: The records access officer shall not be required to create a new public record in order to comply with a request, provided that furnishing a segregable portion of a public record shall not be deemed to be creation of a new record.
rules.notes: Regulatory parallel 950 CMR 32.07(1)(f).

rules.legal_concept: Electronic production by default
rules.atomic_rule: The RAO must provide public records by electronic means unless the record is not available in electronic form or the requestor cannot receive/access a usable electronic form.
rules.trigger: Records are available in electronic form and the requestor can receive them electronically.
rules.source_language: The records access officer shall provide the public records to a requestor by electronic means unless the record is not available in electronic form or the requestor does not have the ability to receive or access the records in a usable electronic form.

rules.legal_concept: Requestor's preferred format
rules.atomic_rule: The RAO must, to the extent feasible, provide the record in the requestor's preferred format or, absent a preference, in a searchable, machine-readable format.
rules.trigger: Requestor states (or does not state) a format preference.
rules.source_language: The records access officer shall, to the extent feasible, provide the public record in the requestor's preferred format or, in the absence of a preferred format, in a searchable, machine readable format.

rules.legal_concept: Electronic records in native form
rules.atomic_rule: The RAO must provide electronic records in native form when possible, presuming machine-readable electronic copies unless the requester specifies otherwise.
rules.trigger: Electronic records are requested.
rules.source_language: the records access officer shall presume that a requester prefers copies provided in machine-readable electronic form, when electronic form is available, unless the requester specifies an alternative preference. the records access officer must provide electronic records in native form when possible.

rules.legal_concept: Written notice of denial
rules.atomic_rule: The RAO must provide written notice by first class or electronic mail of any denial of access, within 10 business days of receipt of the request.
rules.trigger: RAO denies access to any requested record.
rules.clock_spec: within 10 business-days of receipt of the request
rules.source_language: a records access officer shall provide written notice by first class mail or electronic mail to a requester of any denial of access to records. a records access officer shall provide such written notice of denial of access within ten business days of its receipt of a request for public records
rules.notes: Denial-notice deadline coincides with the § 10(b) 10-business-day response clock.

rules.legal_concept: Specific exemption citation on withholding
rules.atomic_rule: A denial/withholding must identify the records withheld and provide the specific reasons, including the specific statutory exemption(s) or common-law privilege and its applicability to each withheld portion.
rules.trigger: Records or portions are withheld.
rules.source_language: identify any records, categories of records or portions of records that the agency or municipality intends to withhold, and provide the specific reasons for such withholding, including the specific exemption or exemptions upon which the withholding is based
rules.notes: Regulatory parallel 950 CMR 32.06(3)(c)5-6 requires identifying each cited exemption/privilege and its applicability to each withheld portion.

rules.legal_concept: Privilege log for attorney-client withholding
rules.atomic_rule: Where a record is withheld on a claim of attorney-client privilege, the written denial must provide a detailed description of the record, including the names of the author and recipients and, in general terms, the subject matter of the withheld information.
rules.trigger: Withholding based on attorney-client privilege.
rules.source_language: where a record has been withheld based on a claim of the attorney-client privilege the records access officer shall provide in its written denial a detailed description of the record, including the names of the author and recipients, and in general terms, the subject matter of the withheld information.
rules.notes: Aligns with M.G.L. c. 66, § 10A(a) requiring a detailed description in lieu of in camera inspection for privileged records on appeal. Flag for human legal review.

rules.legal_concept: Notice of appeal and judicial-review rights
rules.atomic_rule: The response/denial must include a statement informing the requester of the right of administrative appeal to the Supervisor under § 10A(a) and the right to seek judicial review by civil action in the superior court.
rules.trigger: A written response or denial is issued.
rules.source_language: include a statement informing the requestor of the right of appeal to the supervisor of records under subsection (a) of section 10A and the right to seek judicial review of an unfavorable decision by commencing a civil action in the superior court under subsection (c) of section 10A.
rules.notes: Regulatory parallel 950 CMR 32.06(3)(c)8.

material_negatives.note: MA has no automatic 'silence = denial' or 'silence = grant' deeming provision for a municipality's non-response. Instead, failure to respond within the required timeframe opens the administrative-appeal path (petition to the Supervisor within 90 calendar days of the request, 950 CMR 32.08(1)(e)) and enables judicial review upon the Supervisor's failure to issue a timely determination (M.G.L. c. 66, s.10A(a)). Absence of a found deeming rule is not proof none exists.

No explicit statutory preservation/litigation-hold triggered by the request or by an appeal on that request was found in c. 66 s.10/s.10A or 950 CMR 32.00. Records retention is governed separately (records-retention schedules, out of scope under the inclusion test).

MA provides no separate 'acknowledgment' step distinct from substantive action; the s.10(b) written response (which confirms receipt) and the s.10(a) production duty both run on the same 10-business-day clock. Acknowledgment is folded into MA-0016/MA-0018 rather than being an independent deadline.

No fixed statewide per-unit fee for electronic records; electronic production is governed by the general 'actual cost of reproducing' ceiling (MA-0029) plus the labor-rate structure. No separate electronic-record rate parameter exists to configure.

No statute or regulation found requiring municipalities to assign or maintain a tracking/reference number for individual requests. (The Supervisor's own appeal intake is time-stamped under 950 CMR 32.08(1)(j), but that governs the Division, not the municipal RAO.)

MA sets no numeric deposit threshold triggering mandatory prepayment; the RAO 'may delay provision of records until all fees ... are paid in full' (MA-0044) but no dollar threshold or advance-deposit percentage is specified to configure.

structural_branches.description: The M.G.L. c. 66 s.10(b) written response is a mandatory branch triggered when the entity cannot fully produce within the initial timeframe or intends to withhold; it carries nine required content elements (MA-0019).

RAO petition to the Supervisor of Records for a single time extension - a bespoke MA stage inserted between the initial response and production, gated by a 20-business-day filing window and a 5-business-day Supervisor decision (MA-0023, MA-0025/26, MA-0027).
Supervisor may relieve the entity of its obligation to provide copies where a contemporaneous request series is frivolous/harassing - a terminal path ending the request (MA-0028).
Entity petition to the Supervisor to charge for redaction time or (municipality) to exceed $25/hr - a MA-specific fee-approval branch with its own 5-business-day decision clock (MA-0037).

Administrative appeal to the Supervisor of Records (Division of Public Records) - MA's internal review stage before court, with 90-day filing windows and a 10-business-day determination (MA-0057 through MA-0065).
Certiorari review in superior court under c. 249 s.4 of a Supervisor order or untimely determination - MA's designated judicial-review route (MA-0066).
Direct de novo civil enforcement action in superior court, available without exhausting the Supervisor appeal (MA-0067, MA-0068).
Supervisor referral to the Attorney General on non-compliance with a Supervisor order (MA-0069).
Designated records access officer (municipal clerk by default) as the routing/response locus for all municipal requests (MA-0010, MA-0011, MA-0012).

rules.legal_concept: All persons entitled to public records
rules.atomic_rule: Any person (as defined) has a right, upon a sufficient written request to a public body's FOIA coordinator, to inspect, copy, or receive copies of a nonexempt public record.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right, subject to exemptions and the incarcerated-person exclusion).
rules.source_language: It is the public policy of this state that all persons, except those persons incarcerated in state or local correctional facilities, are entitled to full and complete information regarding the affairs of government and the official acts of those who represent them as public officials and public employees, consistent with this act.
rules.notes: Universal-access symmetry: emitted as a rule with the shared eligibility key. 'All persons' carries no requester-class limitation except the incarcerated carve-out captured separately (MI-0002).

rules.legal_concept: Incarcerated persons excluded from 'person'
rules.atomic_rule: An individual serving a sentence of imprisonment in a state, county, or federal correctional facility is not a 'person' entitled to make a request under the act.
rules.trigger: Requester is serving a sentence of imprisonment in a correctional facility.
rules.source_language: "Person" means an individual, corporation, limited liability company, partnership, firm, organization, association, governmental entity, or other legal entity. Person does not include an individual serving a sentence of imprisonment in a state or county correctional facility in this state or any other state, or in a federal correctional facility.
rules.notes: A requester-class gate that the software must branch on to reject ineligible requesters. Structural fork.

rules.legal_concept: No residency or citizenship qualification
rules.atomic_rule: Eligibility to request records extends to all persons with no residency or citizenship qualification.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: It is the public policy of this state that all persons, except those persons incarcerated in state or local correctional facilities, are entitled to full and complete information regarding the affairs of government
rules.notes: Universal-access symmetry: emitted as a rule with the shared key, not a negative. Neither § 15.231(2) nor the 'person' definition in § 15.232(g) contains any residency or citizenship qualifier.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A requester need not state a purpose to obtain records; the required request contents are limited to a sufficient description plus name, address, and contact information.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: upon providing a public body's FOIA coordinator with a written request that describes a public record sufficiently to enable the public body to find the public record, a person has a right to inspect, copy, or receive copies of the requested public record of the public body.
rules.notes: Universal-access symmetry: emitted as a rule with the shared key. The right attaches to a sufficient description; the act nowhere conditions access on a stated purpose. Verbatim clause enumerates the trigger; purpose is absent.

rules.legal_concept: Request must be in writing
rules.atomic_rule: A person desiring to inspect or receive a copy of a public record must make a written request to the public body's FOIA coordinator.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks to invoke enforceable FOIA rights.
rules.source_language: Except as provided in section 3, a person desiring to inspect or receive a copy of a public record shall make a written request for the public record to the FOIA coordinator of a public body.
rules.notes: Michigan does not confer FOIA rights on oral requests; the enforceable-response machinery attaches only to a written request. Compare states permitting oral requests.

rules.legal_concept: Request must sufficiently describe the record
rules.atomic_rule: The written request must describe a public record sufficiently to enable the public body to find the public record.
rules.trigger: Written request submitted.
rules.source_language: upon providing a public body's FOIA coordinator with a written request that describes a public record sufficiently to enable the public body to find the public record, a person has a right to inspect, copy, or receive copies of the requested public record
rules.notes: 'Sufficiently to enable...to find' is a soft standard the public body applies; no statutory clarification-and-toll clock exists for insufficient descriptions (see material negatives).

rules.legal_concept: Request must include requester identity and contact information
rules.atomic_rule: A request (from a non-indigent requester) must include the requesting person's complete name, address, and valid contact information (telephone number or email); a non-individual must give its individual agent's information.
rules.trigger: Written request submitted by a person other than a qualifying indigent individual.
rules.source_language: A request from a person, other than an individual who qualifies as indigent under section 4(2)(a), must include the requesting person's complete name, address, and contact information, and, if the request is made by a person other than an individual, the complete name, address, and contact information of the person's agent who is an individual. An address must be written in compliance with United States Postal Service addressing standards. Contact information must include a valid telephone number or electronic mail address.
rules.notes: Indigent individuals under § 15.234(2)(a) are excepted from the identification requirement.

rules.legal_concept: Written request includes electronic transmission
rules.atomic_rule: A written request may be transmitted by facsimile, electronic mail, or other electronic means.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: "Written request" means a writing that asks for information, and includes a writing transmitted by facsimile, electronic mail, or other electronic means.
rules.notes: Format-of-intake permission; the timing consequence of electronic transmission is captured in MI-0009.

rules.legal_concept: Deemed receipt of electronic requests
rules.atomic_rule: An electronically transmitted written request is not 'received' (starting the response clock) until 1 business day after transmission; if delivered to spam/junk-mail, not received until 1 day after the body first becomes aware, and the body must log both times.
rules.trigger: Written request made by fax, email, or other electronic transmission.
rules.clock_spec: receipt deemed 1 business day after electronic transmission (or 1 day after body first becomes aware, if in spam/junk)
rules.source_language: A written request made by facsimile, electronic mail, or other electronic transmission is not received by a public body's FOIA coordinator until 1 business day after the electronic transmission is made. However, if a written request is sent by electronic mail and delivered to the public body's spam or junk-mail folder, the request is not received until 1 day after the public body first becomes aware of the written request. The public body shall note in its records both the time a written request is delivered to its spam or junk-mail folder and the time the public body first becomes aware of that request.
rules.notes: Defines the start event for the 5-business-day response clock (MI-0016); not a clock effect itself but a receipt-timing calculation the calendar pass must apply.

rules.legal_concept: FOIA coordinator designation (municipal)
rules.atomic_rule: A city, village, township, county, or state department (or a body under its control) must designate an individual as its FOIA coordinator, responsible for accepting and processing requests and approving denials.
rules.trigger: Public body is or is controlled by a city, village, township, county, or state department.
rules.source_language: A public body that is a city, village, township, county, or state department, or under the control of a city, village, township, county, or state department, shall designate an individual as the public body's FOIA coordinator. The FOIA coordinator shall be responsible for accepting and processing requests for the public body's public records under this act and shall be responsible for approving a denial under section 5(4) and (5).
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: custodian designation drives routing. Municipal-facing.

rules.legal_concept: Default FOIA coordinator
rules.atomic_rule: In a county without an executive form of government the county board chairperson is the FOIA coordinator; for all other public bodies the chief administrative officer is the designated FOIA coordinator.
rules.trigger: No individual separately designated / body type not covered by § 15.236(1).
rules.source_language: In a county not having an executive form of government, the chairperson of the county board of commissioners is designated the FOIA coordinator for that county. ... For all other public bodies, the chief administrative officer of the respective public body is designated the public body's FOIA coordinator.
rules.notes: Routing default; determines who must respond when no separate designation is made.

rules.legal_concept: FOIA coordinator may delegate
rules.atomic_rule: A FOIA coordinator may designate another individual to accept and process requests and to approve denials on the coordinator's behalf.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: An FOIA coordinator may designate another individual to act on his or her behalf in accepting and processing requests for the public body's public records, and in approving a denial under section 5(4) and (5).

rules.legal_concept: Employee must forward request to coordinator
rules.atomic_rule: An employee of a public body who receives a request for a public record must promptly forward that request to the FOIA coordinator.
rules.trigger: An employee (not the coordinator) receives a request.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "promptly" from employee receipt
rules.source_language: An employee of a public body who receives a request for a public record shall promptly forward that request to the freedom of information act coordinator.
rules.notes: 'Promptly' is an undefined soft standard; internal routing step, not a numeric deadline.

rules.legal_concept: Law enforcement records management system non-custody referral
rules.atomic_rule: A public body maintaining a law enforcement records management system is not the custodian of records stored for a subscribing body; upon a request for such a record it must, within 10 business days, give written notice identifying the subscribing body and directing the requester to submit the request there.
rules.trigger: Request received by the LE records-management-system host for a record stored on behalf of a subscribing public body.
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from receipt of request (written referral notice)
rules.source_language: If the public body that maintains a law enforcement records management system receives a written request for a public record that is stored on behalf of a subscribing public body, the public body that maintains the law enforcement records management system shall, within 10 business days after receipt of the request, give written notice to the requesting person identifying the subscribing public body and stating that the requesting person shall submit the request to the subscribing public body.
rules.notes: Michigan-specific routing fork with its own clock. Structural branch.

rules.legal_concept: Five-business-day response
rules.atomic_rule: Unless the requester agrees otherwise in writing, a public body must respond to a request within 5 business days after receiving it by granting, denying, partially granting/denying, or extending.
rules.trigger: Public body receives a written request.
rules.clock_spec: 5 business-days from receipt of request (receipt per MI-0009 for electronic)
rules.source_language: Unless otherwise agreed to in writing by the person making the request, a public body shall, subject to subsection (10), respond to a request for a public record within 5 business days after the public body receives the request by doing 1 of the following: (a) Granting the request. (b) Issuing a written notice to the requesting person denying the request. (c) Granting the request in part and issuing a written notice to the requesting person denying the request in part. (d) Issuing a notice extending for not more than 10 business days the period during which the public body shall respond to the request.
rules.notes: The 5-day window is a substantive response deadline (not a bare acknowledgment). Requester may waive/extend by written agreement.

rules.legal_concept: Permitted response dispositions
rules.atomic_rule: A timely response must take one of four forms: grant; written denial; partial grant with written partial denial; or a single extension notice.
rules.trigger: Response due under MI-0016.
rules.source_language: a public body shall...respond to a request for a public record...by doing 1 of the following: (a) Granting the request. (b) Issuing a written notice to the requesting person denying the request. (c) Granting the request in part and issuing a written notice to the requesting person denying the request in part. (d) Issuing a notice extending for not more than 10 business days the period during which the public body shall respond to the request.
rules.notes: The branch set the engine must execute at the response state.

rules.legal_concept: Extension of response period
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may extend the response period by issuing a notice extending it for not more than 10 business days.
rules.trigger: Public body issues an extension notice within the initial 5-business-day window.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: +10 business-days beyond the initial 5-business-day window
rules.source_language: Issuing a notice extending for not more than 10 business days the period during which the public body shall respond to the request.

rules.legal_concept: Only one extension per request
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may not issue more than one notice of extension for a particular request.
rules.trigger: An extension notice has already been issued for the request.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 1 extension per request
rules.source_language: A public body shall not issue more than 1 notice of extension for a particular request.

rules.legal_concept: Contents of extension notice
rules.atomic_rule: An extension notice must specify the reasons for the extension and the date by which the public body will grant, deny, or partially grant/deny the request.
rules.trigger: Public body issues an extension notice.
rules.source_language: If a public body issues a notice extending the period for a response to the request, the notice must specify the reasons for the extension and the date by which the public body will do 1 of the following: (a) Grant the request. (b) Issue a written notice to the requesting person denying the request. (c) Grant the request in part and issue a written notice to the requesting person denying the request in part.

rules.legal_concept: Requester may stipulate response delivery method
rules.atomic_rule: A requester may stipulate that the public body's response be delivered by email, facsimile, or first-class mail, unless the body lacks the technological capability for an emailed response.
rules.trigger: Requester stipulates a delivery method for the response.
rules.source_language: A person making a request under subsection (1) may stipulate that the public body's response under subsection (2) be electronically mailed, delivered by facsimile, or delivered by first-class mail. This subsection does not apply if the public body lacks the technological capability to provide an electronically mailed response.

rules.legal_concept: Failure to respond = final determination to deny
rules.atomic_rule: Failure to respond within the response period constitutes a public body's final determination to deny the request if the failure was willful and intentional, or if the request was flagged (FOIA language within first 250 words, or FOIA keywords/code reference on the envelope or subject line).
rules.trigger: No timely response, AND (willful/intentional) OR (request carried the flagging language/keywords).
rules.clock_spec: terminal on expiry of the 5-business-day (or extended 10-business-day) response period
rules.source_language: Failure to respond to a request under subsection (2) constitutes a public body's final determination to deny the request if either of the following applies: (a) The failure was willful and intentional. (b) The written request included language that conveyed a request for information within the first 250 words of the body of a letter, facsimile, electronic mail, or electronic mail attachment, or specifically included the words, characters, or abbreviations for "freedom of information", "information", "FOIA", "copy", or a recognizable misspelling of such, or appropriate legal code reference to this act, on the front of an envelope or in the subject line of an electronic mail, letter, or facsimile cover page.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: the constructive-denial trigger (silence = deemed denial). Damages remedy attached to it is captured/limited separately; only the terminal trigger is configured here.

rules.legal_concept: Written denial is final determination
rules.atomic_rule: A written notice denying a request in whole or in part is the public body's final determination to deny; it must contain the statutorily required contents.
rules.trigger: Public body denies a request in whole or in part.
rules.source_language: A written notice denying a request for a public record in whole or in part is a public body's final determination to deny the request or portion of that request. The written notice must contain:
rules.notes: Parent row for the denial-notice content requirements MI-0024 through MI-0028.

rules.legal_concept: Denial must explain exemption basis
rules.atomic_rule: If a record or portion is denied as exempt, the written denial must explain the basis under the act or other statute for that exemption determination.
rules.trigger: Denial based on an exemption.
rules.source_language: An explanation of the basis under this act or other statute for the determination that the public record, or portion of that public record, is exempt from disclosure, if that is the reason for denying all or a portion of the request.

rules.legal_concept: Certificate that record does not exist
rules.atomic_rule: If the denial is because the record does not exist, the written notice must contain a certificate that the record does not exist under the name given or another name reasonably known to the public body.
rules.trigger: Denial because the requested record does not exist.
rules.source_language: A certificate that the public record does not exist under the name given by the requester or by another name reasonably known to the public body, if that is the reason for denying the request or a portion of the request.

rules.legal_concept: Denial must describe separated/deleted material
rules.atomic_rule: If a separation or deletion is made, the written notice must describe the public record or information that was separated or deleted under section 14.
rules.trigger: Exempt material separated or deleted from a produced record.
rules.source_language: A description of a public record or information on a public record that is separated or deleted under section 14, if a separation or deletion is made.

rules.legal_concept: Denial must give notice of fees/damages right
rules.atomic_rule: The written denial must include notice of the right to receive attorneys' fees and damages if, after judicial review, the court finds noncompliance and orders disclosure.
rules.trigger: Public body issues a written denial.
rules.source_language: Notice of the right to receive attorneys' fees and damages as provided in section 10 if, after judicial review, the court determines that the public body has not complied with this section and orders disclosure of all or a portion of a public record.

rules.legal_concept: Denial must be signed by responsible individual
rules.atomic_rule: The individual designated as responsible for the denial must sign the written notice of denial.
rules.trigger: A written denial is issued.
rules.source_language: The individual designated in section 6 as responsible for the denial of the request shall sign the written notice of denial.

rules.legal_concept: Separation of exempt and nonexempt material
rules.atomic_rule: If a record contains both exempt and nonexempt material, the public body must separate them and make the nonexempt material available for examination and copying.
rules.trigger: Requested record contains both exempt and nonexempt material.
rules.source_language: If a public record contains material which is not exempt under section 13, as well as material which is exempt from disclosure under section 13, the public body shall separate the exempt and nonexempt material and make the nonexempt material available for examination and copying.
rules.notes: Shared segregability key.

rules.legal_concept: Design records to facilitate separation
rules.atomic_rule: When designing a record the public body must, to the extent practicable, facilitate separation of exempt from nonexempt information, and must generally describe exempted material unless the description would defeat the exemption.
rules.trigger: Public body designs a public record; separation is readily apparent to a requester.
rules.source_language: When designing a public record, a public body shall, to the extent practicable, facilitate a separation of exempt from nonexempt information. If the separation is readily apparent to a person requesting to inspect or receive copies of the form, the public body shall generally describe the material exempted unless that description would reveal the contents of the exempt information and thus defeat the purpose of the exemption.

rules.legal_concept: No charge for re-redacting previously redacted record
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may not charge for redaction labor if it knows or has reason to know it previously redacted the record and the redacted version is still in its possession.
rules.trigger: Public body previously redacted the same record and retains the redacted version.
rules.source_language: A public body shall not charge for labor directly associated with redaction under section 14 if it knows or has reason to know that it previously redacted the public record in question and the redacted version is still in the public body's possession.

rules.legal_concept: Fee limited to actual incremental cost
rules.atomic_rule: A permitted fee is limited to actual mailing costs and the actual incremental cost of duplication or publication, including labor and the cost of search, examination, review, and separation/deletion of exempt material, and the total must not exceed the sum of the six enumerated components.
rules.trigger: Public body charges or estimates a fee.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: sum of the 6 enumerated components (actual incremental cost)
rules.source_language: the fee must be limited to actual mailing costs, and to the actual incremental cost of duplication or publication including labor, the cost of search, examination, review, and the deletion and separation of exempt from nonexempt information as provided in section 14. Except as otherwise provided in this act, if the public body estimates or charges a fee in accordance with this act, the total fee must not exceed the sum of the following components:
rules.notes: Umbrella fee-cap; the six components are MI-0034/0036/0037/0038/0039/0040.

rules.legal_concept: Search labor rate — lowest-paid capable employee
rules.atomic_rule: Labor for searching, locating, and examining records may not be charged at more than the hourly wage of the public body's lowest-paid employee capable of doing so, regardless of who performs the labor.
rules.trigger: Public body charges search/location/examination labor.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: hourly wage of lowest-paid capable employee
rules.source_language: The public body shall not charge more than the hourly wage of its lowest-paid employee capable of searching for, locating, and examining the public records in the particular instance regardless of whether that person is available or who actually performs the labor.
rules.notes: Shared labor-rate ceiling key.

rules.legal_concept: Labor charged in 15-minute increments, rounded down
rules.atomic_rule: Search/examination labor costs must be estimated and charged in increments of 15 minutes or more, with all partial time increments rounded down.
rules.trigger: Public body charges search/examination labor.
rules.clock_spec: fixed: 15-minute increments, partial increments rounded down
rules.source_language: Labor costs under this subdivision shall be estimated and charged in increments of 15 minutes or more, with all partial time increments rounded down.
rules.notes: Same increment rule also applies to redaction labor under (1)(b); duplication labor (1)(e) allows increments of the body's choosing rounded down.

rules.legal_concept: Redaction/separation labor rate ceiling
rules.atomic_rule: Labor to separate/delete exempt from nonexempt information may not exceed the hourly wage of the lowest-paid capable employee; if none is employed, contracted labor may be charged like employee labor but not exceeding 6 times the state minimum hourly wage.
rules.trigger: Public body charges separation/deletion (redaction) labor.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: lowest-paid capable employee wage; contracted labor <= 6x state minimum hourly wage
rules.source_language: For services performed by an employee of the public body, the public body shall not charge more than the hourly wage of its lowest-paid employee capable of separating and deleting exempt information from nonexempt information in the particular instance... Total labor costs calculated under this subdivision for contracted labor costs must not exceed an amount equal to 6 times the state minimum hourly wage rate determined under section 4 of the improved workforce opportunity wage act, 2018 PA 337, MCL 408.934.
rules.notes: Contracted-labor ceiling references a moving external figure (state minimum wage).

rules.legal_concept: Nonpaper physical media at actual economical cost
rules.atomic_rule: For records provided on nonpaper physical media, the charge is limited to the actual and most reasonably economical cost of that media.
rules.trigger: Records provided on nonpaper physical media.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual most-economical cost of the nonpaper media
rules.source_language: For public records provided to the requestor on any form of nonpaper physical media, the actual and most reasonably economical cost of the nonpaper physical media.
rules.notes: Does not apply if the body lacks the technological capability for the stipulated media.

rules.legal_concept: Paper copy charge ceiling — 10 cents per sheet
rules.atomic_rule: The charge for paper copies must not exceed 10 cents per sheet for copies made on 8.5x11 or 8.5x14 paper, calculated as a total cost per sheet.
rules.trigger: Public body provides paper copies.
