rules.clock_spec: ceiling: $0.10 per sheet (8.5x11 or 8.5x14)
rules.source_language: The fee must not exceed 10 cents per sheet of paper for copies of public records made on 8-1/2- by 11-inch paper or 8-1/2- by 14-inch paper. A public body shall utilize the most economical means available for making copies of public records, including using double-sided printing, if cost saving and available.
rules.notes: Shared per-page copy-rate ceiling key. Excludes labor (which is separately capped).

rules.legal_concept: Duplication/publication labor rate ceiling
rules.atomic_rule: Labor directly associated with duplication or publication (paper or digital copies, transfers) may not exceed the hourly wage of the lowest-paid employee capable of the duplication.
rules.trigger: Public body charges duplication/publication labor.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: hourly wage of lowest-paid capable employee; increments of body's choosing, rounded down
rules.source_language: The public body shall not charge more than the hourly wage of its lowest-paid employee capable of necessary duplication or publication in the particular instance, regardless of whether that person is available or who actually performs the labor. Labor costs under this subdivision may be estimated and charged in time increments of the public body's choosing; however, all partial time increments shall be rounded down.

rules.legal_concept: Actual mailing cost only
rules.atomic_rule: Mailing may be charged at actual cost in a reasonably economical manner; no charge for expedited shipping or insurance unless stipulated by the requester.
rules.trigger: Public body mails records.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost of least-expensive economical mailing (plus delivery confirmation)
rules.source_language: The actual cost of mailing, if any, for sending the public records in a reasonably economical and justifiable manner. The public body shall not charge more for expedited shipping or insurance unless specifically stipulated by the requestor, but may otherwise charge for the least expensive form of postal delivery confirmation when mailing public records.

rules.legal_concept: Up to 50% fringe-benefit add-on to labor
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may add up to 50% to the applicable labor charge to cover fringe benefits, not exceeding the actual cost of fringe benefits, if it notes the multiplier on the itemization.
rules.trigger: Public body charges labor and elects to recover fringe benefits.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: +50% of the applicable labor charge (capped at actual fringe cost)
rules.source_language: The public body may also add up to 50% to the applicable labor charge amount to cover or partially cover the cost of fringe benefits if it clearly notes the percentage multiplier used to account for benefits in the detailed itemization described in subsection (4). Subject to the 50% limitation, the public body shall not charge more than the actual cost of fringe benefits, and overtime wages shall not be used in calculating the cost of fringe benefits.
rules.notes: A higher multiplier is allowed only in the narrow website-then-paper scenario under § 15.234(5).

rules.legal_concept: Overtime excluded from labor unless stipulated
rules.atomic_rule: Overtime wages may not be included in labor-cost calculations unless overtime is specifically stipulated by the requester and noted on the itemization.
rules.trigger: Labor performed on overtime.
rules.source_language: Overtime wages shall not be included in the calculation of labor costs unless overtime is specifically stipulated by the requestor and clearly noted on the detailed itemization described in subsection (4).

rules.legal_concept: First $20 free for indigent / designated nonprofit
rules.atomic_rule: A record search and copies must be furnished without charge for the first $20 of the fee for each request by a qualifying indigent individual (with affidavit) or by a state-designated developmental-disabilities/mental-illness protection-and-advocacy nonprofit.
rules.trigger: Requester is a qualifying indigent individual or a qualifying designated nonprofit.
rules.clock_spec: fixed: first $20.00 of the fee waived per request
rules.source_language: A public record search shall be made and a copy of a public record shall be furnished without charge for the first $20.00 of the fee for each request by either of the following: (a) An individual who is entitled to information under this act and who submits an affidavit stating that the individual is indigent and receiving specific public assistance or, if not receiving public assistance, stating facts showing inability to pay the cost because of indigency.
rules.notes: Indigent ineligible if already received the discount twice that calendar year from the same body, or if request is in conjunction with paying outside parties. Nonprofit conditions in § 15.234(2)(b).

rules.legal_concept: Discretionary public-interest fee waiver/reduction
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may search for or furnish copies without charge or at a reduced charge if it determines a waiver/reduction is in the public interest because the disclosure primarily benefits the general public.
rules.trigger: Public body determines disclosure primarily benefits the general public.
rules.source_language: A search for a public record may be conducted or copies of public records may be furnished without charge or at a reduced charge if the public body determines that a waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest because searching for or furnishing copies of the public record can be considered as primarily benefiting the general public.
rules.notes: Discretionary; 'public interest / primarily benefiting the general public' is a soft standard.

rules.legal_concept: Search/redaction labor chargeable only if not charging would cause unreasonably high costs
rules.atomic_rule: A fee for search, examination, review, and separation/deletion of exempt material may not be charged unless failure to charge would result in unreasonably high costs to the public body because of the nature of the request, and the body specifically identifies the nature of those costs.
rules.trigger: Public body wishes to charge search/examination/review/separation labor.
rules.source_language: A fee as described in subsection (1) shall not be charged for the cost of search, examination, review, and the deletion and separation of exempt from nonexempt information as provided in section 14 unless failure to charge a fee would result in unreasonably high costs to the public body because of the nature of the request in the particular instance, and the public body specifically identifies the nature of these unreasonably high costs.
rules.notes: A gate the engine must evaluate before charging labor components; structural condition, not a value.

rules.legal_concept: No charge for records already on the body's website
rules.atomic_rule: Public records available to the general public on the body's website at the time of the request are exempt from separation/deletion labor charges under (1)(b).
rules.trigger: Requested records are available on the body's public website when the request is made.
rules.source_language: If the public body directly or indirectly administers or maintains an official internet presence, any public records available to the general public on that internet site at the time the request is made are exempt from any charges under subsection (1)(b).

rules.legal_concept: Notify requester of records available on website
rules.atomic_rule: If the coordinator knows or has reason to know requested information is on the body's website, the written response must so notify the requester and, to the degree practicable, include the specific webpage address.
rules.trigger: Coordinator knows/has reason to know requested info is on the website.
rules.source_language: If the FOIA coordinator knows or has reason to know that all or a portion of the requested information is available on its website, the public body shall notify the requestor in its written response that all or a portion of the requested information is available on its website. The written response, to the degree practicable in the specific instance, must include a specific webpage address where the requested information is available.
rules.notes: Shared website-redirect key. If requester later stipulates paper/other format, the body must still provide it (may exceed the 50% fringe cap up to actual cost).

rules.legal_concept: Standard itemized fee form
rules.atomic_rule: A public body's procedures must use a standard form for detailed itemization of any fee that clearly lists and explains the allowable charges for each of the six fee components used in estimating or charging.
rules.trigger: Public body estimates or charges a fee.
rules.source_language: A public body's procedures and guidelines must include the use of a standard form for detailed itemization of any fee amount in its responses to written requests under this act. The detailed itemization must clearly list and explain the allowable charges for each of the 6 fee components listed under subsection (1) that compose the total fee used for estimating or charging purposes.
rules.notes: DTMB provides a model form; a body may create its own compliant form.

rules.legal_concept: Procedures, guidelines, and written public summary
rules.atomic_rule: A public body must establish procedures and guidelines to implement the act and create a written public summary (how to submit requests, understand responses, deposits, fee calculations, and appeals), post them on any website, and provide free copies with responses and on request.
rules.trigger: Public body is subject to the act.
rules.source_language: A public body shall establish procedures and guidelines to implement this act and shall create a written public summary of the specific procedures and guidelines relevant to the general public regarding how to submit written requests to the public body and explaining how to understand a public body's written responses, deposit requirements, fee calculations, and avenues for challenge and appeal.
rules.notes: Procedures/guidelines are themselves non-exempt public records.

rules.legal_concept: No fees/deposits until procedures published
rules.atomic_rule: A public body that has not established procedures and guidelines, created a written public summary, or made them publicly available free may not require deposits or charge fees until it is in compliance.
rules.trigger: Public body lacks published procedures/guidelines/summary.
rules.source_language: A public body that has not established procedures and guidelines, has not created a written public summary, or has not made those items publicly available without charge as required in this subsection is not relieved of its duty to comply with any requirement of this act and shall not require deposits or charge fees otherwise permitted under this act until it is in compliance with this subsection.
rules.notes: Gate on the fee/deposit machinery.

rules.legal_concept: 5%-per-day labor-fee reduction for late response
rules.atomic_rule: If a public body does not respond timely and the lateness was willful/intentional or the request was flagged, it must reduce labor-cost charges by 5% for each day it exceeds the response deadline, up to a 50% maximum reduction.
rules.trigger: Untimely response AND (willful/intentional) OR (request carried FOIA flagging language/keywords).
rules.clock_spec: fixed: -5% of labor charge per late day, capped at -50%
rules.source_language: Reduce the charges for labor costs otherwise permitted under this section by 5% for each day the public body exceeds the time permitted under section 5(2) for a response to the request, with a maximum 50% reduction, if either of the following applies: (i) The late response was willful and intentional. (ii) The written request included language that conveyed a request for information within the first 250 words of the body of a letter, facsimile, electronic mail, or electronic mail attachment, or specifically included the words, characters, or abbreviations for "freedom of information", "information", "FOIA", "copy", or a recognizable misspelling of such, or appropriate legal code reference for this act, on the front of an envelope, or in the subject line of an electronic mail, letter, or facsimile cover page.
rules.notes: Fee-calculation remedy tied to lateness; reduces only the labor components.

rules.legal_concept: Fee section inapplicable to statutorily-priced records
rules.atomic_rule: The fee section does not apply to records prepared under a statute specifically authorizing their sale, or where another act/statute specifically sets the copy fee.
rules.trigger: Requested record has a statutorily-authorized sale price or a specifically-provided copy fee.
rules.source_language: This section does not apply to public records prepared under an act or statute specifically authorizing the sale of those public records to the public, or if the amount of the fee for providing a copy of the public record is otherwise specifically provided by an act or statute.

rules.legal_concept: Good-faith deposit permitted above $50
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may require a good-faith deposit before providing records if the entire estimated fee or charge exceeds $50, based on a good-faith total-fee calculation.
rules.trigger: Good-faith fee estimate exceeds $50.00.
rules.clock_spec: floor: deposit only allowed when estimate exceeds $50.00
rules.source_language: the public body may require a good-faith deposit from the person requesting information before providing the public records to the requestor if the entire fee estimate or charge authorized under this section exceeds $50.00, based on a good-faith calculation of the total fee described in subsection (4).

rules.legal_concept: Deposit capped at one-half of estimate
rules.atomic_rule: A good-faith deposit must not exceed one-half of the total estimated fee, and the deposit request must include a detailed fee itemization.
rules.trigger: Public body requires a good-faith deposit under § 15.234(8).
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 1/2 of the total estimated fee
rules.source_language: Subject to subsection (10), the deposit must not exceed 1/2 of the total estimated fee, and a public body's request for a deposit must include a detailed itemization as required under subsection (4).

rules.legal_concept: Best-efforts time-frame estimate with deposit
rules.atomic_rule: A deposit response must contain a good-faith best-efforts estimate of the time frame to provide the records; the estimate is nonbinding but must be made in good faith.
rules.trigger: Public body requires a deposit / responds under § 15.235(2)(d).
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: nonbinding best-efforts time-frame estimate
rules.source_language: The response must also contain a best efforts estimate by the public body regarding the time frame it will take the public body to comply with the law in providing the public records to the requestor. The time frame estimate is nonbinding upon the public body, but the public body shall provide the estimate in good faith and strive to be reasonably accurate
rules.notes: Nonbinding soft time-frame; not a production deadline.

rules.legal_concept: Up to 100% deposit for prior non-payers
rules.atomic_rule: For a subsequent request from an individual who did not pay in full for a prior fulfilled request, the body may require a deposit of up to 100% of the estimated fee before beginning the search, if six enumerated conditions are all met.
rules.trigger: Individual left a prior granted-and-fulfilled request unpaid and the six conditions in § 15.234(11)(a)-(f) are all satisfied.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: up to 100% of estimated fee (only when all six conditions met, incl. 90 days since availability notice)
rules.source_language: after a public body has granted and fulfilled a written request from an individual under this act, if the public body has not been paid in full the total amount under subsection (1)...the public body may require a deposit of up to 100% of the estimated fee before it begins a full public record search for any subsequent written request from that individual if all of the following apply:
rules.notes: Conditions include: prior final fee <=105% of estimate; records still in possession; 90 days since availability notice; no proof of prior payment; detailed itemization. Structural branch with a parameter ceiling.

rules.legal_concept: Termination of 100% deposit authority
rules.atomic_rule: The body must stop requiring the increased (up to 100%) deposit if the individual shows proof of prior full payment, the body is later paid in full, or 365 days have passed since the unpaid request was made.
rules.trigger: Proof of payment shown, prior request paid in full, or 365 days elapsed since the unpaid request.
rules.clock_spec: terminal: 365 days from the unpaid written request extinguishes the increased-deposit authority
rules.source_language: A public body shall no longer require an increased estimated fee deposit from an individual as described under subsection (11) if any of the following apply: (a) The individual is able to show proof of prior payment in full to the public body. (b) The public body is subsequently paid in full for the applicable prior written request. (c) Three hundred sixty-five days have passed since the individual made the written request for which full payment was not remitted to the public body.

rules.legal_concept: Request abandoned if deposit unpaid within 45 days
rules.atomic_rule: If a required deposit is not received within 45 days after the requester's receipt of the deposit notice, and no deposit-amount appeal was filed, the request is considered abandoned and the body need no longer fulfill it.
rules.trigger: Deposit not received within 45 days of receipt of the deposit notice and no § 15.240a appeal filed.
rules.clock_spec: terminal: 45 days from requester's receipt of the deposit notice
rules.source_language: If a deposit that is required under subsection (8) or (11) is not received by the public body within 45 days from receipt by the requesting person of the notice that a deposit is required, and if the requesting person has not filed an appeal of the deposit amount pursuant to section 10a, the request shall be considered abandoned by the requesting person and the public body is no longer required to fulfill the request.
rules.notes: Terminal state (abandonment). Keeper-sliver-style deemed disposition.

rules.legal_concept: Deemed receipt of deposit notice
rules.atomic_rule: A deposit notice is considered received 3 days after it is sent (regardless of transmission means), and it must state the deposit-due date, which is 48 days after the notice is sent.
rules.trigger: Public body sends a deposit-requirement notice.
rules.clock_spec: fixed: notice deemed received 3 days after sent; due date 48 days after sent
rules.source_language: Notice of a deposit requirement under subsection (8) or (11) is considered received 3 days after it is sent, regardless of the means of transmission. Notice of a deposit requirement under subsection (8) or (11) must include notice of the date by which the deposit must be received, which date is 48 days after the date the notice is sent.
rules.notes: Start-event calculation for the 45-day abandonment clock (MI-0059).

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable rules to protect records
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may make reasonable rules necessary to protect its records and prevent excessive and unreasonable interference with its functions, and must protect records from loss, alteration, or destruction.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: A public body may make reasonable rules necessary to protect its public records and to prevent excessive and unreasonable interference with the discharge of its functions. A public body shall protect public records from loss, unauthorized alteration, mutilation, or destruction.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to create a new record
rules.atomic_rule: The act does not require a public body to create a new public record, except as required in section 11 and to the extent needed to furnish copies or edited copies of an existing record.
rules.trigger: Request would require creating a record that does not exist.
rules.source_language: This act does not require a public body to create a new public record, except as required in section 11, and to the extent required by this act for the furnishing of copies, or edited copies pursuant to section 14(1), of an already existing public record.
rules.notes: Shared no-duty-to-create key.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to compile a summary or report
rules.atomic_rule: The act does not require a public body to make a compilation, summary, or report of information, except as required in section 11.
rules.trigger: Request would require compiling a summary/report.
rules.source_language: This act does not require a public body to make a compilation, summary, or report of information, except as required in section 11.

rules.legal_concept: Certified copies on written request
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian of a public record must, upon written request, furnish a requester a certified copy of the record.
rules.trigger: Written request for a certified copy.
rules.source_language: The custodian of a public record shall, upon written request, furnish a requesting person a certified copy of a public record.

rules.legal_concept: Subscription to future regular issuances
rules.atomic_rule: A person may subscribe to future issuances of public records created/issued/disseminated on a regular basis; a subscription is valid for up to 6 months at the subscriber's request and is renewable.
rules.trigger: Requester subscribes to a regularly-issued public record series.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: subscription valid up to 6 months, renewable
rules.source_language: A person has a right to subscribe to future issuances of public records that are created, issued, or disseminated on a regular basis. A subscription is valid for up to 6 months, at the request of the subscriber, and is renewable.

rules.legal_concept: Requester may stipulate electronic/nonpaper format
rules.atomic_rule: A requester may stipulate that records be provided on nonpaper physical media, electronically mailed, or otherwise electronically provided in lieu of paper copies, unless the body lacks the technological capability for the particular media.
rules.trigger: Requester stipulates a nonpaper/electronic delivery format.
rules.source_language: The requestor may stipulate that the public records be provided on nonpaper physical media, electronically mailed, or otherwise electronically provided to him or her in lieu of paper copies. This subdivision does not apply if a public body lacks the technological capability necessary to provide records on the particular nonpaper physical media stipulated in the particular instance.
rules.notes: Shared format-election key.

rules.legal_concept: Records may be provided without a written request
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may provide requested information available in public records without receipt of a written request; and for a verbal request believed to be on the website, the employee should, where practicable, inform the requester of the pertinent website address.
rules.trigger: Informal or verbal request received.
rules.source_language: A public body may provide requested information available in public records without receipt of a written request. If a verbal request for information is for information that a public body believes is available on the public body's website, the public employee shall, where practicable and to the best of the public employee's knowledge, inform the requestor about the public body's pertinent website address.
rules.notes: Informal path; does not trigger the enforceable § 15.235 response machinery, which requires a written request.

rules.legal_concept: Fee-dispute action suspends processing
rules.atomic_rule: If a civil fee-reduction action is commenced, the public body is not obligated to complete processing of the request at issue until the court resolves the fee dispute.
rules.trigger: Requester commences a civil fee-reduction action.
rules.clock_spec: processing paused until the court resolves the fee dispute
rules.source_language: If a civil action is commenced against the public body under this subdivision, the public body is not obligated to complete the processing of the written request for the public record at issue until the court resolves the fee dispute.
rules.notes: Also: filing a § 15.240a fee appeal averts the 45-day deposit-abandonment (MI-0059).

rules.legal_concept: Two classes: exempt and nonexempt
rules.atomic_rule: The act separates public records into two classes: those exempt from disclosure under section 13, and all others, which are subject to disclosure.
rules.trigger: A record is evaluated for disclosure.
rules.source_language: This act separates public records into the following 2 classes: (i) Those that are exempt from disclosure under section 13. (ii) All public records that are not exempt from disclosure under section 13 and that are subject to disclosure under this act.
rules.notes: Functions as the presumption-of-disclosure classifier for non-exempt records.

material_negatives.note: Research date 2026-07-22. Michigan Freedom of Information Act, Act 442 of 1976, MCL 15.231-15.246. Session/law reviewed: codified MCL as published by the Michigan Legislature (Legislative Service Bureau), current through amendments in effect 2026; most recent operative amendments to the processing provisions are 2020 PA 36/38 (15.234, 15.235), 2018 PA 523 (15.233, 15.234). Codified statutes WERE available and opened directly (legislature.mi.gov); all source_language is verbatim from the opened statute. No 2021-2026 amendments to the core processing sections were found. Note: the Michigan FOIA statute's TLS certificate failed in-tool WebFetch; text was retrieved via direct HTTPS (curl) against the official legislature.mi.gov Laws/MCL pages and confirmed against the on-page History lines.

NEGATIVE for the 'oral request permitted' concept: Michigan does NOT confer enforceable FOIA rights on oral requests. § 15.235(1) requires a written request; a body MAY informally provide records without a written request (§ 15.234(6), captured as MI-0068), but only a written request triggers the response/denial/appeal machinery. Emitted affirmatively as MI-0005 (written required).
No separate mere-acknowledgment deadline exists. Michigan's 5-business-day window (MI-0016) requires a substantive disposition (grant/deny/partial/extend), not a bare acknowledgment of receipt.

No statutory clarification-and-toll mechanism. § 15.233(1) requires a request that 'describes a public record sufficiently to enable the public body to find' it (MI-0006), but the act prescribes no formal clarification request, no clock that tolls pending clarification, and no cure/abandonment procedure for insufficiently described requests. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

No fixed statutory production/delivery deadline after a grant. The 5-business-day clock governs the response (grant/deny/extend); once granted, the act supplies only a nonbinding good-faith time-frame estimate accompanying any deposit (MI-0055), not a mandatory production date.

No general expedited-processing track for urgent public-interest requests. The only accelerated-handling provisions are the LE records-management-system referral (MI-0014) and the generic judicial 'earliest practicable date' expediting of FOIA litigation (MI-0077).

No statewide flat search or copy fee. Fees are actual-incremental-cost with component ceilings (labor at lowest-paid-capable-employee wage; paper copies capped at $0.10/sheet). The city/public body sets operative values under those state-imposed ceilings.

The administrative appeal to the head of the public body (MI-0069) is optional, not a mandatory exhaustion prerequisite: § 15.240(1) lets the requester elect internal appeal OR a direct circuit-court action.

structural_branches.description: Requester-class gate: individuals serving a sentence of imprisonment are not 'persons' and cannot invoke FOIA (MI-0002).
Law-enforcement records-management-system host is a non-custodian; must issue a 10-business-day written referral directing the requester to the subscribing body (MI-0014).
Mandatory FOIA-coordinator designation with statutory defaults (chief administrative officer / county board chair) and delegation authority (MI-0010, MI-0011, MI-0012).
Silence beyond the response deadline becomes a final denial only if willful/intentional or the request carried FOIA-flagging language (MI-0022).
Optional internal appeal to the head of the public body (10-business-day decision), a distinct stage from judicial review (MI-0069, MI-0070).
When the head is a board/commission, the appeal-decision clock does not start until its next regularly scheduled meeting (MI-0072).
Separate excessive-fee appeal track (§ 15.240a) with its own 10-business-day administrative stage and 45-day judicial window (MI-0078, MI-0079, MI-0080).
A filed fee-reduction civil action suspends the body's duty to complete processing until the fee dispute is resolved (MI-0081).
Deposit unpaid within 45 days of deemed receipt (with a 3-day mailing deem and 48-day due date) moves the request to an abandoned terminal state (MI-0059, MI-0060).
Up-to-100% deposit branch for repeat requesters who left a prior request unpaid, gated by six conditions and terminated at 365 days (MI-0056, MI-0057).
Search/examination/review/redaction labor may be charged only after the body finds and identifies that not charging would cause unreasonably high costs (MI-0045).
Bodies lacking published procedures/guidelines/public summary are barred from charging fees or requiring deposits until compliant (MI-0050).
The judiciary (and county clerk acting as circuit-court clerk) is outside 'public body' and routes out of the FOIA workflow (MI-0087).
Records available on the body's website carry a no-labor-charge exemption plus a duty to redirect the requester to the specific webpage (MI-0046, MI-0047).

rules.legal_concept: Public right of access to government data
rules.atomic_rule: Any person may inspect and copy public government data upon request to the responsible authority or designee, at reasonable times and places.
rules.trigger: A person requests access to public government data.
rules.source_language: Upon request to a responsible authority or designee, a person shall be permitted to inspect and copy public government data at reasonable times and places.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule per the shared eligibility key. Access runs to 'a person' with no qualifier.

rules.legal_concept: Access without regard to requester's interest or purpose
rules.atomic_rule: The responsible authority must provide access to public data to any person without regard to the nature of that person's interest in the data; no statement of purpose may be required.
rules.trigger: A person requests public data.
rules.source_language: The responsible authority shall provide access to public data to any person, without regard to the nature of that person's interest in the data.
rules.notes: 'Without regard to the nature of that person's interest' also supports that a requester need not identify themselves for public data; identification-not-required is folded into this concept.

rules.legal_concept: No residency condition on access
rules.atomic_rule: Access to public government data is available to any person; the statute imposes no residency requirement.
rules.trigger: A person requests public government data.
rules.source_language: Upon request to a responsible authority or designee, a person shall be permitted to inspect and copy public government data at reasonable times and places.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule per shared key. No residency condition appears anywhere in Ch. 13; the 'a person' grant is unqualified as to residence.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to establish request-handling procedures
rules.atomic_rule: Each government entity's responsible authority must establish procedures to ensure requests for government data are received and complied with in an appropriate and prompt manner.
rules.trigger: None stated (standing duty).
rules.source_language: The responsible authority in every government entity shall establish procedures, consistent with this chapter, to insure that requests for government data are received and complied with in an appropriate and prompt manner.

rules.legal_concept: Prompt / reasonable-time response standard
rules.atomic_rule: The responsible authority must comply with a data request in an appropriate and prompt manner; a response must be provided within a reasonable time.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a request for government data.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "appropriate and prompt manner" / "reasonable time" from request receipt
rules.source_language: The responsible authority in every government entity shall establish procedures, consistent with this chapter, to insure that requests for government data are received and complied with in an appropriate and prompt manner.
rules.source_authority: Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 2; Minn. R. 1205.0300, subp. 3
rules.notes: Soft standard — no numeric statewide deadline for general public-data requests. Minn. R. 1205.0300, subp. 3 restates it as 'a response to a request for access within a reasonable time.' Do not convert to a day-count.

rules.legal_concept: Time to supply copies when not immediately available
rules.atomic_rule: If the responsible authority cannot provide copies at the time of request, copies must be supplied as soon as reasonably possible.
rules.trigger: Copies cannot be provided at the moment of request.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "as soon as reasonably possible" from request
rules.source_language: If the responsible authority or designee is not able to provide copies at the time a request is made, copies shall be supplied as soon as reasonably possible.
rules.notes: Soft delivery standard; structural, not a city-filled numeric value.

rules.legal_concept: Actual costs of searching for and retrieving data
rules.atomic_rule: When copies or electronic transmittal are requested, the responsible authority may require payment of the actual costs of searching for and retrieving the data, including employee time.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for copies or electronic transmittal.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost (search + retrieval + employee time)
rules.source_language: If a person requests copies or electronic transmittal of the data to the person, the responsible authority may require the requesting person to pay the actual costs of searching for and retrieving government data, including the cost of employee time.
rules.notes: Constraint is 'actual costs' as a recovery ceiling; the city sets the operative rate/basis under it. Search/retrieval cost is NOT chargeable on the 100-or-fewer-page standard-copy path (see MN-0009).

rules.legal_concept: 25-cent-per-page cap for 100 or fewer standard pages
rules.atomic_rule: For requests of 100 or fewer black-and-white letter/legal-size paper copies, actual costs may not be used; the entity may charge no more than 25 cents per page copied.
rules.trigger: Request for 100 or fewer black-and-white, letter or legal size paper copies.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: $0.25/page (≤100 pages, b/w letter/legal)
rules.source_language: If 100 or fewer pages of black and white, letter or legal size paper copies are requested, actual costs shall not be used, and instead, the responsible authority may charge no more than 25 cents for each page copied.
rules.notes: Ceiling of $0.25/page; city may charge less. Displaces the actual-cost basis on this small-request path.

rules.legal_concept: Cost of making and certifying copies for a data subject
rules.atomic_rule: When a data subject requests copies of data about themselves, the responsible authority may require payment of the actual costs of making and certifying the copies.
rules.trigger: Data subject requests copies of data about themselves.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost of making and certifying copies
rules.source_language: The responsible authority or designee may require the requesting person to pay the actual costs of making and certifying the copies.
rules.notes: Data-subject copy path (own data). Distinct from the general public-data copy fee; note this covers copies only, inspection is free (MN-0011).

rules.legal_concept: Duty to provide copy in electronic form from computer storage
rules.atomic_rule: An entity maintaining public data in a computer storage medium must provide a copy in electronic form if it can reasonably make the copy or have it made.
rules.trigger: Request for public data that is maintained in a computer storage medium.
rules.source_language: The responsible authority of a government entity that maintains public government data in a computer storage medium shall provide to any person making a request under this section a copy of any public data contained in that medium, in electronic form, if the government entity can reasonably make the copy or have a copy made.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to convert to a different format or program
rules.atomic_rule: The entity is not required to provide data in an electronic format or program different from the one in which it maintains the data.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks data in a format/program other than the one maintained.
rules.source_language: This does not require a government entity to provide the data in an electronic format or program that is different from the format or program in which the data are maintained by the government entity.
rules.notes: Limits the electronic-copy duty in MN-0012.

rules.legal_concept: Presumption that all government data is public
rules.atomic_rule: All government data is public unless classified by statute, temporary classification, or federal law as not public (nonpublic/protected nonpublic, or, for data on individuals, private or confidential).
rules.trigger: Any request for government data.
rules.source_language: All government data collected, created, received, maintained or disseminated by a government entity shall be public unless classified by statute, or temporary classification pursuant to section 13.06, or federal law, as nonpublic or protected nonpublic, or with respect to data on individuals, as private or confidential.
rules.notes: Default-to-release presumption gating every request. Verify exact wording of the trailing classification list against the codified text on production.

rules.legal_concept: Classification fixed as of the time access is requested
rules.atomic_rule: The classification of data (and thus its accessibility) is determined by the law applicable to the data at the time the request for access is made.
rules.trigger: A request for access to data is made.
rules.source_language: The classification of data is determined by the law applicable to the data at the time a request for access to the data is made.
rules.notes: Clause text is verbatim; the subdivision citation within § 13.03 should be confirmed against the codified text before publication.

rules.legal_concept: Responsible authority or designee as the respondent
rules.atomic_rule: Requests are made to, and must be acted on by, the responsible authority or its designee.
rules.trigger: A person makes a data request.
rules.source_language: Upon request to a responsible authority or designee, a person shall be permitted to inspect and copy public government data at reasonable times and places.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: drives routing (who must respond).

rules.legal_concept: Data practices compliance official
rules.atomic_rule: Each government entity must designate an employee to act as its data practices compliance official to handle questions and problems regarding access to data.
rules.trigger: None stated (standing designation duty).
rules.source_language: Each government entity shall designate an employee of the government entity to act as the entity's data practices compliance official to handle questions regarding data access problems. (paraphrase pending verbatim confirmation)
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver routing role (escalation point for access problems). Source fetched but returned as a fragment/summary; confirm verbatim wording on production.

rules.legal_concept: Denial notice with citation to the classifying authority
rules.atomic_rule: If the responsible authority denies access because data is classified, it must inform the requester of the determination orally at the time of the request or in writing as soon after as possible, and cite the specific statutory section, temporary classification, or federal-law provision on which the determination is based.
rules.trigger: Responsible authority determines requested data is classified so as to deny access.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "in writing as soon after that time as possible" from the request
rules.source_language: If the responsible authority or designee determines that the requested data is classified so as to deny the requesting person access, the responsible authority or designee shall inform the requesting person of the determination either orally at the time of the request, or in writing as soon after that time as possible, and shall cite the specific statutory section, temporary classification, or specific provision of federal law on which the determination is based.
rules.notes: Soft written-notice deadline; structural. Written form may be oral first, then written.

rules.legal_concept: Written certification of denial upon requester's request
rules.atomic_rule: Upon the request of any person denied access, the responsible authority must certify in writing that the request was denied and cite the specific statutory section, temporary classification, or federal-law provision on which the denial was based.
rules.trigger: A denied requester asks for written certification.
rules.source_language: Upon the request of any person denied access to data, the responsible authority or designee shall certify in writing that the request has been denied and cite the specific statutory section, temporary classification, or specific provision of federal law upon which the denial was based.
rules.notes: Written certification is triggered by the requester's ask, on top of the automatic denial notice in MN-0018.

rules.legal_concept: Ten-day response to a data subject's access request
rules.atomic_rule: For a data subject's request about their own data, the responsible authority must comply immediately if possible, or within ten days of the request excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays if immediate compliance is not possible.
rules.trigger: An individual requests data about themselves under § 13.04, subd. 3.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 10 days (excluding Sat/Sun/legal holidays) from date of request
rules.source_language: The responsible authority or designee shall comply immediately, if possible, with any request made pursuant to this subdivision, or within ten days of the date of the request, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays, if immediate compliance is not possible.
rules.notes: Hard numeric deadline, but scoped to data-subject requests for their OWN data — not general public-data requests (which carry only the soft standard in MN-0005). 'Ten days ... excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays' = business days; ceiling because 'immediately if possible' can be sooner.

rules.legal_concept: Informing individual whether they are a data subject and the classification
rules.atomic_rule: Upon request, an individual must be informed whether they are the subject of stored data on individuals and whether that data is classified as public, private, or confidential.
rules.trigger: An individual asks whether they are the subject of stored data.
rules.source_language: Upon request to a responsible authority or designee, an individual shall be informed whether the individual is the subject of stored data on individuals, and whether it is classified as public, private or confidential.

rules.legal_concept: Data subject shown data and informed of its content and meaning
rules.atomic_rule: Upon further request, a data subject must be shown their private or public data and, if desired, informed of its content and meaning.
rules.trigger: Data subject makes a further request to see the data.
rules.source_language: Upon further request, an individual who is the subject of stored private or public data on individuals shall be shown the data without any charge and, if desired, shall be informed of the content and meaning of that data.
rules.notes: Same sentence also grounds the free-inspection fee rule MN-0011; this row captures the show-and-explain duty.

rules.legal_concept: 30-day response to a data-accuracy challenge
rules.atomic_rule: Upon a data subject's challenge to accuracy or completeness, the responsible authority must within 30 days either correct the data or notify the individual that it has determined the data to be correct.
rules.trigger: Data subject contests the accuracy or completeness of public or private data about themselves.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 30 days from receipt of the data subject's notification
rules.source_language: Upon receiving notification from the data subject, the responsible authority shall within 30 days either: (1) correct the data found to be inaccurate or incomplete and attempt to notify past recipients of inaccurate or incomplete data, including recipients named by the individual; or (2) notify the individual that the responsible authority believes the data to be correct.
rules.notes: Verbatim reconstructed from opened source; option (1)/(2) wording (esp. the past-recipient notice and 'believes the data to be correct') should be confirmed against codified text on production.

rules.legal_concept: Public records open to the public
rules.atomic_rule: Each public governmental body must make its public records available for inspection and copying by the public; access is not limited to any class or category of requester.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional access to open records)
rules.source_language: Each public governmental body shall make available for inspection and copying by the public of that body's public records.
rules.notes: Universal-access rule. 'By the public' is not limited to residents or any purpose. Source Type: Statute. Enforcement standing under 610.027 (citizen/taxpayer/aggrieved person) governs lawsuits, not the right to make a request.

rules.legal_concept: No residency condition on records access
rules.atomic_rule: There is no Missouri residency or citizenship condition on the right to inspect or copy public records; the statute grants access to 'the public' with no residency qualifier.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: Each public governmental body shall make available for inspection and copying by the public of that body's public records.
rules.notes: Universal-access rule emitted per symmetry requirement. Source Type: Statute. Chapter 610 imposes no residency condition for requesting records; verbatim clause quoted is the affirmative access grant.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A requester need not state a purpose or reason for requesting public records; the access grant to 'the public' carries no purpose condition.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: Each public governmental body shall make available for inspection and copying by the public of that body's public records.
rules.notes: Universal-access rule emitted per symmetry requirement. Source Type: Statute. AGO guidance confirms requesters need not justify a request. Commercial-purpose distinctions in some states' fee schedules have no counterpart in Chapter 610.

rules.legal_concept: Appointment of custodian of records
rules.atomic_rule: Each public governmental body must appoint a custodian who is responsible for the maintenance of that body's records.
rules.trigger: None stated (standing obligation of each body)
rules.source_language: Each public governmental body is to appoint a custodian who is to be responsible for the maintenance of that body's records.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: custodian designation drives routing/who-must-respond. Source Type: Statute.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian identity and location disclosed on request
rules.atomic_rule: The identity and location of a public governmental body's custodian must be made available upon request.
rules.trigger: Upon request for the custodian's identity/location
rules.source_language: The identity and location of a public governmental body's custodian is to be made available upon request.
rules.notes: Supports routing to the correct responder. Source Type: Statute. Related to MO-0004.

rules.legal_concept: Request form may be offered but not required
rules.atomic_rule: A public governmental body may ask a requester to fill out a request form but may not require use of a form as a condition of access.
rules.trigger: On receipt of a records request
rules.source_language: a public governmental body may ask that requestors fill out a form, but it can't require them to do so.
rules.source_authority: Mo. Att'y Gen., Sunshine Law FAQs (interpreting § 610.023.3)
rules.notes: Source Type: Official Guidance (AGO). Statute is silent on request form; AGO interprets that a form cannot be mandated. Flag for confirmation against any controlling case law.

rules.legal_concept: Request need not be in writing
rules.atomic_rule: A records request need not be submitted in writing; written submission is encouraged as helpful but is not required by statute.
rules.trigger: On making a records request
rules.source_language: Section 610.023.3, RSMo, ... does not specify a manner in which these requests must be submitted; while not required, it may be helpful to submit requests in writing.
rules.source_authority: Mo. Att'y Gen., Sunshine Law FAQs (interpreting § 610.023.3)
rules.notes: Source Type: Official Guidance (AGO). Paraphrased from AGO FAQ / search summary; confirm exact FAQ wording. Statute does not prescribe request form or medium.

rules.legal_concept: Third-business-day response deadline
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian must act upon a request for access no later than the end of the third business day following the date the request is received by the custodian.
rules.trigger: Request received by the custodian of records
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 3 business-days from request receipt by custodian
rules.source_language: Each request for access to a public record shall be acted upon as soon as possible, but in no event later than the end of the third business day following the date the request is received by the custodian of records of a public governmental body.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Hard cap on the action deadline; the concurrent 'as soon as possible' promptness standard is split out to MO-0009. This is a state-fixed maximum (ceiling), not a value the city sets.

rules.legal_concept: Act upon request as soon as possible
rules.atomic_rule: A request for access must be acted upon as soon as possible, a promptness standard operating within the outer three-business-day cap.
rules.trigger: Request received by the custodian
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "as soon as possible" from request receipt
rules.source_language: Each request for access to a public record shall be acted upon as soon as possible, but in no event later than the end of the third business day following the date the request is received by the custodian of records of a public governmental body.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Soft promptness standard within the same sentence as the 3-day cap; kept as a distinct undefined-soft standard so it is not converted into a fixed number.

rules.legal_concept: Provide records in requested format if available
rules.atomic_rule: If records are requested in a certain format, the public body must provide the records in the requested format if such format is available.
rules.trigger: Requester specifies a format and that format is available
rules.source_language: If records are requested in a certain format, the public body shall provide the records in the requested format, if such format is available.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Conditional on availability of the requested format.

rules.legal_concept: Detailed delay explanation with earliest availability
rules.atomic_rule: If access is not granted immediately, the custodian must give a detailed explanation of the cause for further delay and the place and earliest time and date the record will be available for inspection.
rules.trigger: Access not granted immediately
rules.source_language: If access to the public record is not granted immediately, the custodian shall give a detailed explanation of the cause for further delay and the place and earliest time and date that the record will be available for inspection.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Requires a date-certain in the delay notice.

rules.legal_concept: Production period may exceed three days for reasonable cause
rules.atomic_rule: The period for document production may exceed three business days for reasonable cause.
rules.trigger: Reasonable cause for exceeding three business days
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "reasonable cause" extension beyond 3 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: This period for document production may exceed three days for reasonable cause.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Extends the outer window on an undefined-soft 'reasonable cause' standard; no numeric limit stated. Pairs with the delay notice in MO-0011.

rules.legal_concept: Written statement of grounds citing specific provision
rules.atomic_rule: If a request for access is denied, the custodian must, upon request, provide a written statement of the grounds for denial citing the specific provision of law under which access is denied.
rules.trigger: Access denied and requester requests a written statement of grounds
rules.source_language: If a request for access is denied, the custodian shall provide, upon request, a written statement of the grounds for such denial. Such statement shall cite the specific provision of law under which access is denied
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Written grounds statement is triggered only 'upon request' by the requester.

rules.legal_concept: Third-business-day deadline for denial statement
rules.atomic_rule: The written statement of grounds for denial must be furnished to the requester no later than the end of the third business day following the date the request for the statement is received.
rules.trigger: Request for the written statement of grounds is received
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 3 business-days from receipt of the request for the statement
rules.source_language: and shall be furnished to the requester no later than the end of the third business day following the date that the request for the statement is received.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Clock runs from receipt of the request for the statement, not from the original records request.

rules.legal_concept: Separate exempt and nonexempt material
rules.atomic_rule: If a record contains both nonexempt and exempt material, the public body must separate them and make the nonexempt material available for examination and copying.
rules.trigger: Record contains both exempt and nonexempt material
rules.source_language: If a public record contains material which is not exempt from disclosure as well as material which is exempt from disclosure, the public governmental body shall separate the exempt and nonexempt material and make the nonexempt material available for examination and copying.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute.

rules.legal_concept: Design records to facilitate separation
rules.atomic_rule: When designing a public record, a public body must, to the extent practicable, facilitate a separation of exempt from nonexempt information.
rules.trigger: Designing a public record
rules.source_language: When designing a public record, a public governmental body shall, to the extent practicable, facilitate a separation of exempt from nonexempt information.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Standing design obligation; borderline on the per-request inclusion test but supports segregability workflow.

rules.legal_concept: Generally describe material exempted
rules.atomic_rule: If the separation is readily apparent, the public body must generally describe the material exempted, unless that description would reveal the contents of the exempt information and thus defeat the purpose of the exemption.
rules.trigger: Separation of exempt material is readily apparent to the requester
rules.source_language: If the separation is readily apparent to a person requesting to inspect or receive copies of the form, the public governmental body shall generally describe the material exempted unless that description would reveal the contents of the exempt information and thus defeat the purpose of the exemption.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Conjunctive: describe exempt material EXCEPT where description would defeat the exemption; kept in one row per grain rule.

rules.legal_concept: Ten cents per page paper copy ceiling
rules.atomic_rule: Fees for copying public records provided in paper form shall not exceed ten cents per page for a paper copy not larger than nine by fourteen inches.
rules.trigger: Producing paper copies not larger than 9x14 inches
rules.source_language: Fees for copying public records ... shall not exceed ten cents per page for a paper copy not larger than nine by fourteen inches, with the hourly fee for duplicating time not to exceed the average hourly rate of pay for clerical staff of the public governmental body.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. ceiling: $0.10/page for paper copies up to 9x14 inches. The city sets the actual charge at or below this ceiling. Duplicating-time labor ceiling split to MO-0019.

rules.legal_concept: Duplicating-time hourly fee ceiling
rules.atomic_rule: The hourly fee charged for duplicating time shall not exceed the average hourly rate of pay for clerical staff of the public governmental body.
rules.trigger: Charging for duplicating (copying) time
rules.source_language: with the hourly fee for duplicating time not to exceed the average hourly rate of pay for clerical staff of the public governmental body.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. ceiling: clerical-staff average hourly rate for duplicating time. City supplies the actual clerical rate under the ceiling.

rules.legal_concept: Research time charged at actual cost
rules.atomic_rule: Research time required for fulfilling records requests may be charged at the actual cost of research time.
rules.trigger: Research time required to fulfill a request
rules.source_language: Research time required for fulfilling records requests may be charged at the actual cost of research time.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. ceiling: actual cost of research time. Permissive ('may'). Fees are to be based on the employees that produce the lowest charges (MO-0021).

rules.legal_concept: Use staff yielding the lowest amount of charges
rules.atomic_rule: Documents must be copied/duplicated using the personnel of the body that results in the lowest amount of charges for the request.
rules.trigger: Assigning staff to fulfill a request
rules.source_language: Documents may be copied using employees of the body that result in the lowest amount of charges for search, research, and duplication time.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Paraphrased/reconstructed from the fee subsection; confirm exact statutory wording. soft-standard: 'lowest amount of charges' cost-minimization duty, no fixed value.

rules.legal_concept: Cost estimate available before production
rules.atomic_rule: A requester may request an estimate of the cost of copies before the public body produces them.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for a cost estimate before production
rules.source_language: a person requesting records may request that the public governmental body provide an estimate of the cost prior to producing the copies.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Paraphrased/reconstructed; confirm exact statutory wording. AGO guidance recommends requesters ask for a cost breakdown.

rules.legal_concept: Electronic/media records cost limited to copies, staff time, and medium
rules.atomic_rule: Fees for records maintained on computer facilities, tapes, disks, videotapes or films shall include only the cost of copies, staff time (not exceeding the average hourly rate of pay for staff needed for copies and programming), and the cost of the medium used for duplication.
rules.trigger: Providing records on electronic or special media
rules.source_language: Fees for providing access to public records maintained on computer facilities, recording tapes or disks, videotapes or films ... shall include only the cost of copies, staff time, which shall not exceed the average hourly rate of pay for staff of the public governmental body required for making copies and programming, if necessary, and the cost of the disk, tape, or other medium used for the duplication.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. ceiling: cost of copies + staff time (capped at staff average hourly rate) + cost of medium. No overhead or profit recoverable.

rules.legal_concept: Public-interest fee waiver or reduction
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may waive or reduce the fees when it determines that waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest.
rules.trigger: Body determines waiver/reduction is in the public interest
rules.source_language: Documents may be furnished without charge or at a reduced charge when the public governmental body determines that waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations or activities of the public governmental body.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Discretionary public-interest waiver. No indigency waiver is separately specified (see material negatives).

rules.legal_concept: Fees may be requested before fulfilling request
rules.atomic_rule: Payment of fees may be requested prior to fulfilling the request.
rules.trigger: Before fulfilling a records request
rules.source_language: Payment of fees may be requested prior to fulfilling the request.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. No statutory deposit percentage or dollar threshold is set (see material negatives).

rules.legal_concept: Request deemed withdrawn on nonpayment of fees
rules.atomic_rule: A request is considered withdrawn if the requester fails to remit all fees within ninety days, or within one hundred fifty days if the requested fees are greater than one thousand dollars.
rules.trigger: Fees requested and requester fails to remit within 90 days (150 days if fees > $1,000)
rules.clock_spec: fixed: 90 calendar-days from fee request; 150 calendar-days if fees > $1,000
rules.source_language: A request for public records to a public governmental body shall be considered withdrawn if the requester fails to remit all fees within ninety days, or within one hundred fifty days if the requested fees are greater than one thousand dollars.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute (2025 amendment). Terminal clock: nonpayment deems the request withdrawn. Requests pending on Aug. 28, 2025 had to be paid by Jan. 1, 2026. City cannot alter the 90/150-day thresholds (state-fixed).

rules.legal_concept: Notice of withdrawal consequence for nonpayment
rules.atomic_rule: The public body must notify the requester that failing to remit payment within ninety days (or one hundred fifty days if fees exceed one thousand dollars) will cause the request to be considered withdrawn.
rules.trigger: When fees are requested
rules.source_language: The public governmental body shall include notice to the requester that if the requester fails to remit payment of the fees within ninety days, or within one hundred fifty days if the requested fees are greater than one thousand dollars, then the request for public records shall be considered withdrawn.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute (2025 amendment). Required notice attached to the fee request; prerequisite to the withdrawal in MO-0026.

rules.legal_concept: Access to records in electronic format
rules.atomic_rule: A public body keeping records in electronic format is strongly encouraged to provide access electronically, and where its system allows electronic copying it must provide data in electronic format if requested.
rules.trigger: Records maintained electronically and requester seeks electronic format
rules.source_language: A public governmental body keeping its records in an electronic format is strongly encouraged to provide access to its public records to members of the public in an electronic format. ... the public governmental body shall provide data to the public in such electronic format, if requested.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Reconstructed from source summary; the 'strongly encouraged' clause is advisory while the 'shall provide data ... if requested' clause is mandatory. Confirm exact operative wording and subsection numbering.

rules.legal_concept: Request deemed withdrawn on non-response to a clarification request
rules.atomic_rule: If the public governmental body responds to a request in order to seek clarification and no response to the clarification request is received within ninety days (or one hundred fifty days if the requested fees exceed one thousand dollars), the public records request is considered withdrawn.
rules.trigger: Body sent a clarification request; requester does not respond within the window
rules.clock_spec: 90 days from clarification request sent (150 days if requested fees > $1,000)
rules.source_language: If the public governmental body responds to a request for public records in order to seek a clarification of the request and no response to the request for clarification is received within ninety days, or within one hundred fifty days if the requested fees are greater than one thousand dollars, then such request for public records shall be considered withdrawn.
rules.notes: ADDED 2026-07-23 via ChatGPT-pilot completeness cross-check; verified verbatim against § 610.026. Sibling of the fee-nonpayment 90-day withdrawal (MO-0026/0027) — both live in § 610.026; original discovery captured the fee twin but not this clarification twin. Confirm exact subdivision citation on production.

rules.legal_concept: Unpaid original fees carried forward to a repeat request
rules.atomic_rule: If the same or a substantially similar request is made within six months after expiration of the ninety-day nonpayment-withdrawal period (or one hundred fifty days if requested fees exceed one thousand dollars) and no fee was remitted on the original request, the public governmental body may require payment of the fees for the original request in addition to any allowable fees for the subsequent request.
rules.trigger: Same/substantially-similar request within 6 months (150 days if fees > $1,000) with the original fee unpaid
rules.source_language: If the same or a substantially similar request for public records is made within six months after the expiration of the ninety-day period, or within one hundred fifty days if the requested fees are greater than one thousand dollars, and no fee was remitted, the public governmental body is authorized to request payment of fees for the original request as well as any allowable fees for the subsequent request.
rules.notes: ADDED 2026-07-23 via completeness cross-check; verified verbatim against § 610.026. Repeat-request fee carry-forward tied to the nonpayment-withdrawal window (MO-0026).

material_negatives.note: No statutory deemed/constructive-denial trigger. Chapter 610 requires action within three business days (610.023.3) but does not state that silence past that deadline is automatically a denial; a failure to respond is treated as a violation enforceable in court (610.027), and knowing/purposeful violations carry penalties, rather than converting silence into a deemed denial with its own clock. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

No internal administrative appeal or binding administrative-review stage for records denials. Enforcement is exclusively judicial (610.027). The Attorney General or a prosecuting attorney may investigate and sue, and a requester may complain to the AG's office, but no statute creates a binding administrative determination the platform would route to before court.

No separate statutory indigency fee waiver. The only fee-waiver provision is the discretionary public-interest waiver/reduction in 610.026.1 (MO-0024); Chapter 610 does not provide a mandatory indigency-based waiver.

No statutory deposit percentage or dollar threshold governing advance payment. 610.026.2 permits requesting payment before fulfillment (MO-0025) but sets no required deposit amount; the 90/150-day figures (MO-0026) are withdrawal deadlines, not deposit thresholds.

No statutory 'unduly burdensome' or search-hour threshold permitting denial of a voluminous request. Chapter 610 sets no burden-hour cap; a body may recover search/research time as a fee (MO-0020) rather than refuse the request for burden.

No separate acknowledgment deadline distinct from the substantive-response deadline. The three-business-day clock in 610.023.3 (MO-0008) is a deadline to act upon the request, not a mere acknowledgment; Missouri does not require a separate receipt acknowledgment.

No commercial-purpose classification or commercial-use fee surcharge in Chapter 610. Unlike several states, Missouri's fee schedule (610.026) draws no distinction based on the requester's commercial vs. non-commercial purpose.

structural_branches.description: Delay-notice path (MO-0011): when access is not immediate, custodian must issue a detailed cause explanation plus a date-certain for availability.
Reasonable-cause extension path (MO-0012): production window may exceed three business days on an undefined-soft 'reasonable cause' standard, paired with the delay notice.
Denial-statement path (MO-0013/MO-0014): on a requester's request, a written grounds statement citing the specific legal provision must issue within three business days of that request.

Segregate-and-produce path (MO-0015/MO-0016/MO-0017): separate exempt from nonexempt material, produce the nonexempt, and generally describe the exempted material unless doing so defeats the exemption.

Fee-nonpayment withdrawal path (MO-0026/MO-0027): a request terminates as withdrawn if fees go unpaid for 90 days (150 days if > $1,000), preceded by a mandatory withdrawal-consequence notice — a Missouri-specific terminal branch added by the 2025 amendment.

Judicial-only enforcement path (MO-0033/MO-0034/MO-0035): no administrative appeal; enforcement is a circuit-court suit with venue at the body's principal place of business and burden-shifting to the body.
Electronic-format path (MO-0032): where the body maintains records electronically and its system permits electronic copying, it must provide data in electronic format on request.

rules.legal_concept: Right of residents and all other interested persons to examine public records
rules.atomic_rule: Any resident of the state and any other person interested in examining public records is empowered to examine those records and make memoranda, copies, and abstracts, free of charge, during office business hours.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right, subject to statutory exceptions).
rules.source_language: all residents of this state and all other persons interested in the examination of the public records ... are hereby fully empowered and authorized to (a) examine such records, and make memoranda, copies ... all free of charge, during the hours the respective offices may be kept open for the ordinary transaction of business
rules.effective_status: Current (amended 2024 Neb. Laws LB 43, operative July 19, 2024)
rules.notes: Universal-access symmetry: emitted as a rule with the shared eligibility key. Ellipses reflect the operative clause as captured from the opened statute; full-text spot-check recommended.

rules.legal_concept: Access extends beyond residents to all other interested persons
rules.atomic_rule: Eligibility to examine and copy public records is not limited to residents; 'all other persons interested in the examination of the public records' are equally authorized, so no residency or citizenship qualification gates the right.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: all residents of this state and all other persons interested in the examination of the public records ... are hereby fully empowered and authorized to (a) examine such records
rules.notes: 2024 LB 43 broadened the class from 'citizens' to 'residents' while retaining 'all other persons,' so no residency requirement bars access. Emitted as a rule with the shared key per universal-access symmetry.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required to examine records
rules.atomic_rule: A requester need not state a reason or purpose to examine or obtain public records; the right to examine attaches to any interested person without a purpose condition.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: all residents of this state and all other persons interested in the examination of the public records ... are hereby fully empowered and authorized to (a) examine such records, and make memoranda, copies
rules.notes: Emitted as a rule with the shared key per universal-access symmetry. The 'no purpose' conclusion is derived from the absence of any purpose condition in the empowerment clause; commercial purpose is relevant only to the discretionary fee waiver (NE-0022), not to the right of access.

rules.legal_concept: Written request triggers the copy/estimate and response duty
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian's duty to provide a cost estimate and one of the enumerated responses is triggered by receipt of a written request for access to or copies of a public record.
rules.trigger: Custodian receives a written request for access or copies.
rules.source_language: Upon receiving a written request for access to or copies of a public record, the custodian of such record shall provide to the requester as soon as is practicable and without delay, but not more than four business days after actual receipt of the request
rules.notes: On-premises examination requires no written request; the formal response clock attaches to a written request.

rules.legal_concept: Four-business-day response deadline
rules.atomic_rule: Within not more than four business days after actual receipt of a written request, the custodian must provide a cost estimate and either (a) access/copies, (b) a written denial, or (c) a written explanation of delay.
rules.trigger: Actual receipt of a written request.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 4 business-days from actual receipt of the written request
rules.source_language: the custodian of such record shall provide to the requester as soon as is practicable and without delay, but not more than four business days after actual receipt of the request, an estimate of the expected cost of the copies and either (a) access to or, if copying equipment is reasonably available, copies of the public record, (b) if there is a legal basis for denial of access or copies, a written denial of the request ... or (c) if the entire request cannot with reasonable good faith efforts be fulfilled within four business days after actual receipt of the request due to the significant difficulty or the extensiveness of the request, a written explanation
rules.notes: 'Not more than four business days' is a ceiling on the response time; the soft 'as soon as is practicable and without delay' standard runs concurrently (NE-0012).

rules.legal_concept: Response as soon as practicable and without delay
rules.atomic_rule: Independent of the four-day cap, the custodian must respond as soon as is practicable and without delay.
rules.trigger: Actual receipt of a written request.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "as soon as is practicable and without delay" from actual receipt
rules.source_language: as soon as is practicable and without delay, but not more than four business days after actual receipt of the request
rules.notes: Soft standard preserved as source term; the engine applies it as a promptness duty layered under the four-day ceiling, not a fillable value.

rules.legal_concept: Initial response must take one of three enumerated forms
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian's timely response must be one of three enumerated forms: (a) access/copies, (b) a written denial with a legal basis, or (c) a written explanation of delay.
rules.trigger: Custodian responding to a written request.
rules.source_language: either (a) access to or, if copying equipment is reasonably available, copies of the public record, (b) if there is a legal basis for denial of access or copies, a written denial of the request ... or (c) ... a written explanation
rules.notes: Structural fork: engine must be able to route a request to grant, denial, or delay-explanation.

rules.legal_concept: Written explanation of delay with earliest practicable date
rules.atomic_rule: When a request cannot with reasonable good-faith efforts be fulfilled within four business days due to significant difficulty or extensiveness, the custodian must give a written explanation including the earliest practicable date for fulfilling the request, a cost estimate, and an opportunity for the requester to modify or prioritize items.
rules.trigger: Request cannot be fulfilled within four business days due to significant difficulty or extensiveness.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "earliest practicable date for fulfilling the request" stated in the written explanation
rules.source_language: if the entire request cannot with reasonable good faith efforts be fulfilled within four business days after actual receipt of the request due to the significant difficulty or the extensiveness of the request, a written explanation, including the earliest practicable date for fulfilling the request, an estimate of the expected cost of any copies, and an opportunity for the requester to modify or prioritize the items
rules.notes: Nebraska-specific delay path; the 'earliest practicable date' is a soft-standard deadline the engine tracks, not a numeric window.

rules.legal_concept: Requester's ten-business-day window to review costs and act
rules.atomic_rule: After receiving the cost estimate, the requester has ten business days to review estimated costs (including any special service charge) and either request fulfillment of the original request, negotiate to narrow/simplify it, or withdraw it.
rules.trigger: Custodian provides an estimate of expected costs.
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from delivery of the cost estimate
rules.source_language: The requester shall have ten business days to review the estimated costs, including any special service charge, and request the custodian to fulfill the original request, negotiate with the custodian to narrow or simplify the request, or withdraw the request.
rules.notes: Added by the 2024 amendment; creates a requester-action window that gates whether the custodian proceeds.
