rules.legal_concept: Custodian may not proceed if requester does not respond in ten business days
rules.atomic_rule: If the requester does not respond to the custodian within ten business days of the cost estimate, the custodian shall not proceed to fulfill the request.
rules.trigger: Requester fails to respond within ten business days of the estimate.
rules.clock_spec: terminal at 10 business-days from cost estimate; nonresponse halts fulfillment
rules.source_language: If the requester does not respond to the custodian within ten business days, the custodian shall not proceed to fulfill the request.
rules.notes: Constructive abandonment: silence after the estimate ends the custodian's obligation to fulfill.

rules.legal_concept: Computation of business days and definition of business day
rules.atomic_rule: The four business days are computed by excluding the day the request is received; a business day excludes Saturdays, Sundays, and any day the custodian's offices are closed.
rules.trigger: Computing a statutory deadline.
rules.source_language: The four business days shall be computed by excluding the day the request is received, after which the designated period of time begins to run. Business day does not include a Saturday, a Sunday, or a day during which the offices of the custodian of the public records are closed.
rules.notes: Calculation rule the engine executes to compute the four-business-day deadline (and, by definition of business day, the ten-business-day window).

rules.legal_concept: Custodian must provide a cost estimate
rules.atomic_rule: With its timely response, the custodian must provide the requester an estimate of the expected cost of the copies.
rules.trigger: Written request for copies received.
rules.source_language: the custodian of such record shall provide to the requester ... an estimate of the expected cost of the copies
rules.notes: The estimate starts the requester's ten-business-day review window (NE-0015).

rules.legal_concept: Copy fee capped at actual added cost
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian may charge a fee for providing copies, but the fee shall not exceed the actual added cost of making the copies available.
rules.trigger: Custodian produces copies for the requester.
rules.source_language: the public body, public entity, or public official which is the custodian of a public record may charge a fee for providing copies of such public record ... which fee shall not exceed the actual added cost
rules.effective_status: Current (fee limits tightened by 2024 Neb. Laws LB 43)
rules.notes: Ceiling of 'actual added cost'; no statewide per-page cents rate — the municipality supplies the operative rate under the ceiling.

rules.legal_concept: First eight cumulative hours of labor not chargeable to residents
rules.atomic_rule: For a Nebraska resident's request, the actual added cost used to calculate a fee shall not include any charge for existing salary/pay obligations for the first eight cumulative hours of searching, identifying, physically redacting, or copying.
rules.trigger: Requester is a resident; labor total is within the first eight cumulative hours.
rules.source_language: the actual added cost used as the basis for the calculation of a fee for records shall not include any charge for the existing salary or pay obligation to the public officers or employees with respect to the first eight cumulative hours of searching, identifying, physically redacting, or copying
rules.notes: Fixed free-labor allowance of eight cumulative hours for residents; labor beyond eight hours may be recovered as a special service charge (referenced in the cost-review clause, NE-0015).

rules.legal_concept: Deposit may be required when estimated cost exceeds fifty dollars
rules.atomic_rule: If the estimated cost of requested copies exceeds fifty dollars, the custodian may require the requester to furnish a deposit before fulfilling the request.
rules.trigger: Estimated cost of copies exceeds $50.
rules.source_language: If copies requested ... are estimated by the custodian of such public records to cost more than fifty dollars, the custodian may require the requester to furnish a deposit prior to fulfilling such request.
rules.notes: The $50 trigger threshold is fixed by statute; the deposit amount itself is discretionary within the actual-cost ceiling.

rules.legal_concept: Discretionary fee waiver or reduction in the public interest
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may waive or reduce any fee if the waiver or reduction would be in the public interest.
rules.trigger: Custodian determines waiver/reduction is in the public interest.
rules.source_language: The custodian may waive or reduce any fee described in this section if the waiver or reduction of the fee would be in the public interest.
rules.notes: Discretionary; no numeric standard, so config_home is structural.

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable fee for modem/electronic transmission of county records
rules.atomic_rule: When a county custodian provides a copy by transmitting it modem-to-modem, a reasonable fee may be charged for the specialized service, which may include a reasonable amortization of added computer equipment/software cost.
rules.trigger: Record delivered by modem-to-modem transmission by a county custodian.
rules.source_language: When a custodian of a public record of a county provides to a member of the public, upon request, a copy of the public record by transmitting it from a modem to an outside modem, a reasonable fee may be charged for such specialized service. Such fee may include a reasonable amount representing a portion of the amortization of the cost of computer equipment, including software, necessarily added in order to provide such specialized service.
rules.notes: 'Reasonable fee' is a soft-standard value; text is county-specific.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to acquire new computer capability to generate records in a new form
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity is not required to acquire computer capability to generate public records in a new or different form when that new form would require additional computer equipment or software the entity does not already possess.
rules.trigger: Request would require generating records in a new/different form needing equipment/software not already held.
rules.source_language: This subsection shall not be construed to require a governmental entity to acquire computer capability to generate public records in a new or different form when that new form would require additional computer equipment or software not already possessed by the governmental entity.
rules.notes: Limits format/creation obligations; engine can gate requests that would require new-form generation.

rules.legal_concept: Data in computer files remains a public record
rules.atomic_rule: Data that is a public record in its original form remains a public record when maintained in computer files.
rules.trigger: Requested data is maintained in computer files.
rules.source_language: Data which is a public record in its original form shall remain a public record when maintained in computer files.
rules.notes: Electronic form does not defeat public-record status.

rules.legal_concept: Denial must be in writing where a legal basis exists
rules.atomic_rule: If there is a legal basis for denial, the custodian must issue a written denial of the request.
rules.trigger: Custodian withholds access/copies on a legal basis.
rules.source_language: if there is a legal basis for denial of access or copies, a written denial of the request together with the information specified in section 84-712.04
rules.notes: Parent denial rule; the required contents are split into NE-0027 through NE-0029 and linked.

rules.legal_concept: Denial must describe withheld records and cite specific statutory exception, correlating portions to reasons
rules.atomic_rule: A denial must include a description of the contents of the records withheld and a statement of specific reasons, correlating specific portions of the records to specific reasons, including citations to the particular statute and subsection expressly providing the exception.
rules.trigger: Custodian issues a written denial.
rules.source_language: A description of the contents of the records withheld and a statement of the specific reasons for the denial, correlating specific portions of the records to specific reasons for the denial, including citations to the particular statute and subsection thereof expressly providing the exception
rules.notes: Portion-by-portion correlation implies a segregability/partial-redaction analysis at the denial stage.

rules.legal_concept: Denial must name the responsible official or employee
rules.atomic_rule: A denial must state the name of the public official or employee responsible for the decision to deny the request.
rules.trigger: Custodian issues a written denial.
rules.source_language: The name of the public official or employee responsible for the decision to deny the request.

rules.legal_concept: Public body must keep a publicly accessible file of denial letters
rules.atomic_rule: Each public body must maintain a file of all letters denying requests, and that file must be made accessible to the public upon request.
rules.trigger: A denial letter is issued.
rules.source_language: Each public body shall maintain a file of all letters of denial of requests for records; such file shall be made accessible to any member of the public upon request.
rules.effective_status: Current — Requires manual verification of exact text
rules.notes: is_paraphrase=true: captured from an opened-source summary, not confirmed verbatim; verify the exact clause. Kept as a rule because it is a document/log step tied to denial processing.

material_negatives.note: No express statute deeming custodian silence a denial. Nebraska instead imposes an affirmative four-business-day duty (§ 84-712(4)) plus remedies for 'denial' (§ 84-712.03); a failure to respond is treated as reviewable noncompliance rather than a statutorily 'deemed denial.' Absence of a found deemed-denial trigger is not proof none exists.

No standalone 'reasonably segregable — release the rest' production mandate located as a discrete clause. Partial coverage exists: § 84-712.04(1) requires denials to correlate specific withheld portions to specific reasons, and § 84-712(1) references 'physically redacting,' both implying portion-level redaction. Verify whether a freestanding segregability duty exists.

No statutory requirement that a public body designate/publicly identify a records or FOIA officer. Duties run to the 'lawful custodian' (whoever holds custody); no designation-and-publication step was found.
No express provision requiring retention/preservation of a requested record while the request or an appeal is pending. Routine retention schedules are governed separately and excluded.
No statewide fixed per-page copy rate. Copy fees are capped only at 'actual added cost' (§ 84-712(1), NE-0019); the municipality supplies the operative rate under that ceiling.

No separate custodian-initiated clarification clock. The nearest mechanism is the post-estimate 10-business-day requester window to negotiate/narrow (§ 84-712(4), NE-0015), which is requester-driven rather than a custodian clarification demand.
No acknowledgment step distinct from the substantive four-business-day response; the single four-day duty (NE-0011) subsumes acknowledgment.

EXCLUDED (inclusion test / Remove list — criminal penalties): § 84-712.09 makes a violating official subject to removal or impeachment and guilty of a Class III misdemeanor. Nothing in per-request software processing changes; recorded as audit trail, not a rule.

EXCLUDED (Remove list — attorney-fee provisions): § 84-712.07 authorizes equitable relief and reasonable attorney fees/litigation costs to a substantially prevailing complainant. Remedy amount, not a request-processing step.

EXCLUDED (exemptions not inventoried): § 84-712.05 lists ~30 discretionary categories a lawful custodian 'may withhold.' Only the general discretionary-withholding posture is captured via classification.presumption_of_openness (NE-0004) and the denial-specificity rules; the individual confidentiality categories do not each create a distinct processing workflow and are not enumerated as rows.

structural_branches.description: The initial response forks into three engine-executable paths: grant access/copies, written denial, or written explanation of delay (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 84-712(4)) — NE-0013.

Option (c) delay path: written explanation with earliest-practicable-date, cost estimate, and requester modify/prioritize opportunity when the request is significantly difficult or extensive — NE-0014.
Post-estimate requester-action stage (10 business days) to fulfill, negotiate, or withdraw, added by 2024 LB 43 — NE-0015; nonresponse halts fulfillment (NE-0016).
Attorney General review path as an alternative to court: petition → AG determination in 15 calendar days → possible AG-brought enforcement suit — NE-0033/0034/0035.
Mandamus enforcement path in district court with docket precedence and burden on the public body — NE-0032/0031/0036.
Denial-letter file each public body must maintain and expose to the public on request — NE-0030.

rules.legal_concept: Public records open to inspection by any person
rules.atomic_rule: All public books and records of a governmental entity must be open during office hours to inspection by any person, and may be fully copied.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right of access)
rules.source_language: all public books and public records of a governmental entity must be open at all times during office hours to inspection by any person, and may be fully copied or an abstract or memorandum may be prepared from those public books and public records.
rules.notes: Universal-access right. Subject to the long list of statutory confidentiality cross-references opened by the 'Except as otherwise provided' clause, which are not inventoried here.

rules.legal_concept: No residency requirement to request records
rules.atomic_rule: Access runs to 'any person'; the statute imposes no residency or citizenship condition on who may request public records.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: all public books and public records of a governmental entity must be open at all times during office hours to inspection by any person
rules.notes: Emitted as a universal-access rule with the shared eligibility key per prompt discipline. The verbatim clause is the 'any person' access grant; 'no residency requirement' is the absence of any residency qualifier anywhere in Chapter 239.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: Access runs to 'any person'; the statute requires no statement of purpose or justification for a request.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: all public books and public records of a governmental entity must be open at all times during office hours to inspection by any person
rules.notes: Emitted as a universal-access rule with the shared eligibility key. Chapter 239 contains no purpose or use limitation on requests generally (a narrow exception exists at NRS 239.0105 for certain recreational-registration records disclosed only to specified requesters).

rules.legal_concept: Request may be written or oral
rules.atomic_rule: A request to inspect, copy or receive a copy may be made either in writing or orally; the response duty is triggered by either form.
rules.trigger: Custodian receives a request from a person
rules.source_language: Not later than the end of the fifth business day after the date on which the person who has legal custody or control of a public book or record of a governmental entity receives a written or oral request from a person to inspect, copy or receive a copy of the public book or record, a governmental entity shall do one of the following, as applicable:
rules.notes: Intake must accept oral as well as written requests. For state Executive Department agencies (not municipalities) a prescribed request form exists under NRS 239.008; no equivalent mandatory form binds municipal entities.

rules.legal_concept: Five-business-day response deadline
rules.atomic_rule: Not later than the end of the fifth business day after receipt of a request, the entity must allow inspection/copying or provide the copy (or give one of the alternative statutory responses).
rules.trigger: Custodian receives a written or oral request
rules.clock_spec: 5 business-days from custodian's receipt of request
rules.source_language: Not later than the end of the fifth business day after the date on which the person who has legal custody or control of a public book or record of a governmental entity receives a written or oral request from a person to inspect, copy or receive a copy of the public book or record, a governmental entity shall do one of the following, as applicable: (a) Except as otherwise provided in subsection 2, allow the person to inspect or copy the public book or record or, if the request is for the person to receive a copy of the public book or record, provide such a copy to the person.
rules.notes: 'Not later than the end of the fifth business day' is an outer limit (may respond sooner). One of four responses (a: produce; b: no-custody referral NV-0011; c: extension NV-0008; d: confidential denial NV-0012) must be given within this window. Chapter 239 does not define 'business day' or provide tolling rules. Added 2007; amended 2013, 2019.

rules.legal_concept: Readily available records provided as expeditiously as practicable
rules.atomic_rule: If a record is readily available for inspection or copying, the custodian must allow the requester to inspect, copy or receive a copy as expeditiously as practicable.
rules.trigger: Requested record is readily available for inspection or copying
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "as expeditiously as practicable" from receipt of request
rules.source_language: If a public book or record of a governmental entity is readily available for inspection or copying, the person who has legal custody or control of the public book or record shall allow a person who has submitted a request to inspect, copy or receive a copy of a public book or record as expeditiously as practicable.
rules.notes: Soft standard ('as expeditiously as practicable') accelerates production of readily-available records ahead of the 5-business-day outer limit; no numeric value — do not convert to a day count.

rules.legal_concept: Written notice of earliest availability date when unable to produce by day five
rules.atomic_rule: If unable to make the record available by the end of the fifth business day, the entity must give the requester written notice of that fact and the earliest date and time the entity reasonably believes the record will be available.
rules.trigger: Entity unable to make record available by end of fifth business day
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "earliest date and time after which the governmental entity reasonably believes" the record will be available, from the end of the 5th business day
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided in paragraph (d), if the governmental entity is unable to make the public book or record available by the end of the fifth business day after the date on which the person who has legal custody or control of the public book or record received the request: (1) Provide to the person, in writing, notice of the fact that it is unable to make the public book or record available by that date and the earliest date and time after which the governmental entity reasonably believes the public book or record will be available for the person to inspect or copy or after which a copy of the public book or record will be available to the person.
rules.notes: A required written notice that also sets a self-declared soft future availability date. Config Home structural because the 'reasonably believes' date is a standard the entity applies, not a value the city fills.

rules.legal_concept: Follow-up written explanation and new date if record still unavailable
rules.atomic_rule: If the record is still not available by the date and time the entity previously represented, the entity must provide a written explanation of the reason and a new reasonably-believed availability date and time.
rules.trigger: Record not available by the date/time previously represented under NV-0008
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: new "date and time after which the governmental entity reasonably believes" availability, from lapse of the previously represented date
rules.source_language: If the public book or record or the copy of the public book or record is not available to the person by that date and time, the governmental entity shall provide to the person, in writing, an explanation of the reason the public book or record is not available and a date and time after which the governmental entity reasonably believes the public book or record will be available for the person to inspect or copy or after which a copy of the public book or record will be available to the person.
rules.notes: Second sentence of the same paragraph as NV-0008; split out as a distinct recurring notice obligation triggered by a missed self-declared date.

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable effort to help requester focus the request
rules.atomic_rule: When unable to produce by day five, the entity must make a reasonable effort to assist the requester to focus the request to maximize the likelihood of obtaining the record as expeditiously as possible.
rules.trigger: Entity unable to make record available by end of fifth business day
rules.source_language: (2) Make a reasonable effort to assist the requester to focus the request in such a manner as to maximize the likelihood the requester will be able to inspect, copy or receive a copy of the public book or record as expeditiously as possible.
rules.notes: A duty to assist in narrowing; not a clarification clock. Chapter 239 contains no provision deeming a request abandoned if the requester does not respond.

rules.legal_concept: Written referral when entity lacks custody or control
rules.atomic_rule: If the entity does not have legal custody or control of the record, it must provide written notice of that fact and the name and address of the entity that does have custody or control, if known.
rules.trigger: Entity lacks legal custody or control of the requested record
rules.source_language: If the governmental entity does not have legal custody or control of the public book or record, provide to the person, in writing: (1) Notice of the fact that it does not have legal custody or control of the public book or record; and (2) The name and address of the governmental entity that has legal custody or control of the public book or record, if known.
rules.notes: Routing/referral response; one of the four permitted responses due within the 5-business-day window (NV-0006).

rules.legal_concept: Written denial with citation to confidentiality authority
rules.atomic_rule: If the entity must deny the request because the record (or part) is confidential, it must provide written notice of that fact and a citation to the specific statute or other legal authority making it confidential.
rules.trigger: Entity must deny because the record or part is confidential
rules.source_language: If the governmental entity must deny the person’s request because the public book or record, or a part thereof, is confidential, provide to the person, in writing: (1) Notice of that fact; and (2) A citation to the specific statute or other legal authority that makes the public book or record, or a part thereof, confidential.
rules.notes: Denial response; due within the 5-business-day window. Requires a specific legal citation, not a bare denial.

rules.legal_concept: No denial where confidential information can be redacted or separated
rules.atomic_rule: The entity must not deny a request on the basis that the record contains confidential information if it can redact, delete, conceal or separate (including electronically) the confidential information from the non-confidential information.
rules.trigger: Requested record contains both confidential and non-confidential information
rules.source_language: A governmental entity that has legal custody or control of a public book or record shall not deny a request made pursuant to subsection 1 to inspect or copy or receive a copy of a public book or record on the basis that the requested public book or record contains information that is confidential if the governmental entity can redact, delete, conceal or separate, including, without limitation, electronically, the confidential information from the information included in the public book or record that is not otherwise confidential.
rules.notes: Segregability/partial-disclosure duty; constrains the denial pathway in NV-0012.

rules.legal_concept: Provision of copy in electronic format on request; exceptions
rules.atomic_rule: If requested, the entity must provide a copy in an electronic format by electronic medium, unless the record was neither created nor available electronically, or doing so would give access to proprietary software or require producing non-separable confidential information.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for an electronic-format copy
rules.source_language: If requested, a governmental entity shall provide a copy of a public record in an electronic format by means of an electronic medium. Nothing in this subsection requires a governmental entity to provide a copy of a public record in an electronic format or by means of an electronic medium if: (a) The public record: (1) Was not created or prepared in an electronic format; and (2) Is not available in an electronic format; or (b) Providing the public record in an electronic format or by means of an electronic medium would: (1) Give access to proprietary software; or (2) Require the production of information that is confidential and that cannot be redacted, deleted, concealed or separated from information that is not otherwise confidential.
rules.notes: Requirement plus its conjunctive exceptions kept in one row per grain rule.

rules.legal_concept: Copy must be provided in the requested medium
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian must not refuse to provide a copy in the requested medium because it has already prepared, or would prefer to provide, the copy in a different medium.
rules.trigger: Requester specifies a medium the custodian would prefer not to use
rules.source_language: An officer, employee or agent of a governmental entity who has legal custody or control of a public record: (a) Shall not refuse to provide a copy of that public record in the medium that is requested because the officer, employee or agent has already prepared or would prefer to provide the copy in a different medium.

rules.legal_concept: Entity must prepare the copy, not the requester
rules.atomic_rule: On request, the custodian must prepare the copy of the record and must not require the requester to prepare the copy himself or herself.
rules.trigger: Requester asks the entity to prepare a copy
rules.source_language: (b) Except as otherwise provided in NRS 239.030, shall, upon request, prepare the copy of the public record and shall not require the person who has requested the copy to prepare the copy himself or herself.
rules.notes: Cross-references NRS 239.030 (certified copies) as an exception.

rules.legal_concept: Furnishing of certified copies on request
rules.atomic_rule: An officer having custody of non-confidential public records must furnish certified copies to any person who requests them and pays or tenders the prescribed copying/certifying fees.
rules.trigger: Person requests certified copies of non-confidential records and tenders fees
rules.source_language: Every officer having custody of public records, the contents of which are not declared by law to be confidential, shall furnish copies certified to be correct to any person who requests them and pays or tenders such fees as may be prescribed for the service of copying and certifying.
rules.notes: Certified-copy production path; distinct from ordinary copies in that fee tender is an express precondition (see NV-0018).

rules.legal_concept: Payment or tender of fees as precondition to certified copies
rules.atomic_rule: For certified copies, the requester must pay or tender the prescribed copying and certifying fees as a condition of the officer's duty to furnish them.
rules.trigger: Request for certified copies
rules.source_language: shall furnish copies certified to be correct to any person who requests them and pays or tenders such fees as may be prescribed for the service of copying and certifying.
rules.notes: Payment gate is expressed only for certified copies under NRS 239.030; Chapter 239 authorizes no general advance deposit or prepayment before search for ordinary copies.

rules.legal_concept: County recorder production of stored item within three working days
rules.atomic_rule: When a county recorder receives a request for a particular item that has been removed to storage, the recorder must produce a microfilmed copy or the original within three working days.
rules.trigger: County recorder receives a request for an item stored under NRS 239.015(1)
rules.clock_spec: 3 working-days from county recorder's receipt of request
rules.source_language: If a county recorder receives a request for a particular item which has been stored pursuant to subsection 1, the county recorder shall produce a microfilmed copy of such item or the original within 3 working days.
rules.notes: Record/entity-specific deadline applicable to county recorders for stored items; distinct from the general 5-business-day window. Uses 'working days' (vs. 'business days' elsewhere).

rules.legal_concept: Copy fee limited to actual cost
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity may charge a fee for a copy, but the fee must not exceed the actual cost to provide the copy unless a specific statute or regulation sets the fee.
rules.trigger: Entity provides a copy of a public record
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost of providing the copy
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, a governmental entity may charge a fee for providing a copy of a public record. Such a fee must not exceed the actual cost to the governmental entity to provide the copy of the public record unless a specific statute or regulation sets a fee that the governmental entity must charge for the copy.
rules.notes: Permission to charge plus its actual-cost ceiling kept in one row. City sets the operative per-copy rate under the actual-cost ceiling; a more specific statute/regulation can override the ceiling. Added 1997; amended 2013.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'actual cost' (excludes overhead/labor)
rules.atomic_rule: 'Actual cost' means direct cost of providing the copy (ink, toner, paper, media, postage) and excludes any cost the entity incurs regardless of whether a copy is requested.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: ‘Actual cost’ means the direct cost incurred by a governmental entity in the provision of a public record, including, without limitation, the cost of ink, toner, paper, media and postage. The term does not include a cost that a governmental entity incurs regardless of whether or not a person requests a copy of a particular public record.
rules.notes: Definition the fee engine branches on: the 'regardless of request' exclusion bars charging for staff/labor time and overhead. Reinforced by 2019 SB287, which also repealed the former extraordinary-use personnel fee (NRS 239.055).

rules.legal_concept: No fee where statute/regulation requires free copy
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity must not charge a fee for a copy if a specific statute or regulation requires it to provide the copy without charge.
rules.trigger: A specific statute or regulation requires the copy to be provided free
rules.source_language: A governmental entity shall not charge a fee for providing a copy of a public record if a specific statute or regulation requires the governmental entity to provide the copy without charge.
rules.notes: Third sentence of NRS 239.052(1); a fee-suppression branch triggered by other free-copy mandates (e.g., NV-0027).

rules.legal_concept: Discretionary fee waiver by written policy
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity may waive all or part of a copy fee if it adopts a written waiver policy and posts a legible sign or notice of the policy's terms at each office providing copies.
rules.trigger: Entity has adopted a written waiver policy and posted notice
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may waive all or a portion of a charge or fee for a copy of a public record if the governmental entity: (a) Adopts a written policy to waive all or a portion of a charge or fee for a copy of a public record; and (b) Posts, in a conspicuous place at each office in which the governmental entity provides copies of public records, a legible sign or notice that states the terms of the policy.
rules.notes: Waiver is discretionary and conditioned on a posted written policy.

rules.legal_concept: Law library copy fee ceiling of 50 cents per page
rules.atomic_rule: The fee for a copy of a record in the custody of a governmental law library must not exceed 50 cents per page.
rules.trigger: Copy provided from a record in a governmental law library's custody
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: $0.50/page
rules.source_language: The fee for providing a copy of a public book or record in the custody of a law library operated by a governmental entity must not exceed 50 cents per page.
rules.notes: Record/entity-specific per-page ceiling; city law library sets the operative rate up to $0.50/page.

rules.legal_concept: Additional fee for administrative-proceeding transcript
rules.atomic_rule: For a copy of a certified-court-reporter transcript of an administrative proceeding, the entity must charge, on top of actual medium cost, a per-page fee equal to the court reporter's contract per-page fee, and remit that amount to the reporter.
rules.trigger: Person requests a copy of a transcribed administrative-proceeding transcript
rules.clock_spec: fixed: court reporter's contract per-page fee + actual medium cost
rules.source_language: If a person requests a copy of a transcript of an administrative proceeding that has been transcribed by a certified court reporter, a governmental entity shall charge, in addition to the actual cost of the medium in which the copy of the transcript is provided, a fee for each page provided which is equal in amount to the fee per page charged by the court reporter for the copy of the transcript, as set forth in the contract between the governmental entity and the court reporter.
rules.notes: Special-record fee; the per-page value is fixed by the entity-reporter contract, not freely set by the city. An exception to the general actual-cost ceiling.

rules.legal_concept: Additional fee for geographic information system data
rules.atomic_rule: A fee for information from a geographic information system may include, in addition to actual medium cost, the reasonable costs of data gathering/entry, database maintenance, hardware, software, quality control, and consultation with personnel.
rules.trigger: Request for information from a geographic information system
rules.source_language: A fee for the provision of information from a geographic information system may include, in addition to the actual cost of the medium in which the information is provided, the reasonable costs related to: (a) The gathering and entry of data into the system; (b) Maintenance and updating of the database of the system; (c) Hardware; (d) Software; (e) Quality control; and (f) Consultation with personnel of the governmental entity.
rules.notes: Special-record fee permitting recovery of 'reasonable costs' beyond actual cost for GIS data — a statutory exception to the actual-cost ceiling; no numeric value (soft-standard).

rules.legal_concept: Certified copies for VA benefit eligibility furnished without charge
rules.atomic_rule: When a public record copy is required by the federal Department of Veterans Affairs to determine benefit eligibility, the custodian must provide a certified copy without charge to the applicant, their representative, or the VA.
rules.trigger: Copy required by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs for benefit-eligibility determination
rules.source_language: Whenever a copy of any public record is required by the Department of Veterans Affairs to be used in determining the eligibility of any person to participate in benefits made available by the Department of Veterans Affairs, the official charged with the custody of such public record shall, without charge, provide the applicant for the benefit or any person acting on behalf of the applicant or the representative of the Department of Veterans Affairs with a certified copy or copies of such records.
rules.notes: Requester/purpose-specific fee exemption (a mandatory free-copy statute that triggers NV-0022).

material_negatives.note: No separate acknowledgment/receipt step distinct from the substantive response. NRS 239.0107(1) sets a single 5-business-day window within which the entity must produce, refer, extend, or deny; there is no earlier statutory duty merely to acknowledge receipt.

No statutory authority in Chapter 239 for an advance deposit or prepayment before search/production of ordinary copies. Fee tender is expressly required only for certified copies (NRS 239.030, NV-0018).

Chapter 239 draws no distinction between commercial and non-commercial requesters and creates no purpose-based fee tier; the actual-cost ceiling (NRS 239.052) applies without regard to requester purpose.

No fee is authorized for staff time, labor, or overhead. The 'actual cost' definition (NRS 239.005(1)) excludes costs incurred regardless of a request, and 2019 SB287 repealed the former extraordinary-use-of-personnel fee (NRS 239.055). Absence of a labor charge is affirmative, not merely unfound.

No fixed constructive/deemed-denial trigger (no 'silence for N days = denial'). The only silence-related trigger is the soft 'unreasonably delayed' standard for a district-court application under NRS 239.011(1) (NV-0028).

No internal or administrative appeal stage exists in Chapter 239; the exclusive review mechanism is a district-court application (NRS 239.011). Emitted as a negative so it does not falsely merge with other states' internal-appeal stages.

Chapter 239 does not define 'business day' or 'working day', nor does it provide tolling, holiday-exclusion, or day-counting rules for the 5-business-day (NRS 239.0107) or 3-working-day (NRS 239.015(2)) periods. Later pass may need general NRS time-computation rules or municipal practice.

No provision deeming a request abandoned or closed if the requester fails to respond to a narrowing/clarification effort. NRS 239.0107(1)(c)(2) imposes a duty to assist but attaches no requester-side deadline or abandonment consequence.

Chapter 239 contains no preservation/litigation hold triggered by the making of a records request or by an appeal on that request. (General records-retention schedules exist under NRS 239.051-239.125 but are routine retention, excluded.)

structural_branches.description: NRS 239.0107(1)(c)(1): a required written notice, given when the entity cannot produce by day five, declaring the earliest reasonably-believed availability date — a distinct processing stage that pauses production against a self-set soft date (NV-0008).
NRS 239.0107(1)(c)(1): a recurring follow-up written explanation plus a new availability date whenever a previously represented date lapses (NV-0009).
NRS 239.0107(1)(c)(2): a mandatory 'reasonable effort' to help the requester focus the request when production cannot occur by day five (NV-0010).
NRS 239.0107(1)(b): a referral branch — written notice of no custody plus name/address of the entity that has the record (NV-0011).
NRS 239.0107(1)(d): the confidential-denial branch requiring written notice with a specific legal citation (NV-0012).
NRS 239.010(3): mandatory partial-disclosure/redaction path barring denial of a record that mixes confidential and non-confidential content (NV-0013).
NRS 239.010(4): electronic-format production branch with its four statutory exceptions (NV-0014).
NRS 239.011(1): the sole external review path — district-court application on denial, unreasonable delay, or fee dispute; Nevada has no internal administrative appeal stage (NV-0028).
NRS 239.0115: a separate district-court path to reach records held 30+ years, carrying a rebuttable presumption of access and enumerated exceptions (NV-0029).
NRS 239.020: a mandatory free-certified-copy branch for federal VA benefit-eligibility determinations (NV-0027).

rules.legal_concept: Right of any person to inspect, examine, and copy government records
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian must permit a government record to be inspected, examined, and copied by any person (no requester qualification beyond being a person) during regular business hours, unless the record is exempt.
rules.trigger: Any person submits a request for a government record.
rules.source_language: The custodian of a government record shall permit the record to be inspected, examined, and copied by any person during regular business hours ... unless a government record is exempt from public access.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(a) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Universal-access anchor. 'any person' is the operative eligibility term; there is no citizenship or standing qualifier at intake.

rules.legal_concept: No residency requirement to request records
rules.atomic_rule: Access is available to any person; OPRA imposes no residency or in-state requirement on the requestor.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional).
rules.source_language: The custodian of a government record shall permit the record to be inspected, examined, and copied by any person during regular business hours.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(a) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Universal-access symmetry rule (shared key), emitted as a rule not a negative. Source clause is verbatim; the no-residency conclusion is the settled reading of 'any person' (see Scheeler v. Atlantic County Muni. Joint Ins. Fund, 454 N.J. Super. 621 (App. Div. 2018), holding OPRA is not limited to NJ citizens) - flag for manual case verification.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required to obtain access
rules.atomic_rule: A requestor need not state a reason or purpose to obtain access; the only purpose-related field is a yes/no certification of whether the record will be used for a commercial purpose, which affects fee basis and response window (deferred), not access eligibility.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional).
rules.source_language: The form shall provide space for the name, address, email address and telephone number of the requestor and a brief description of the government record sought.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(f) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Universal-access symmetry rule (shared key). The required request fields are identity/contact and a description of the record only - no reason field. The commercial-purpose certification (NJ-A16) is the sole purpose disclosure and does not gate access, only fee/timeline treatment.

rules.legal_concept: Anonymous requests permitted; anonymity not a ground for denial
rules.atomic_rule: A request may be submitted anonymously; indicating the request is anonymous is not a ground for denial and an anonymous request is not to be considered incomplete - but an anonymous requestor may not institute an OPRA proceeding under N.J.S.A. 47:1A-6.
rules.trigger: Requestor elects to submit anonymously.
rules.source_language: A request may be submitted anonymously provided, however, that anonymous requestors shall not be permitted to institute proceedings pursuant to section 7 of P.L.2001, c.404 (C.47:1A-6). ... A request that is submitted anonymously shall not be considered incomplete.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(f) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: The loss of standing to sue is enforcement/appeal-scope (sibling); captured here only as the eligibility consequence of anonymity that the intake engine must surface.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian's response duty suspended if requestor does not accurately identify/contact
rules.atomic_rule: If the requestor has elected not to accurately identify themselves or to provide an accurate address, email address, or telephone number, the custodian is not required to respond (and the failure-to-respond deemed-denial does not run) until the requestor contacts the custodian seeking a response.
rules.trigger: Requestor provides no accurate name/address/email/telephone contact.
rules.clock_spec: tolls the custodian's response obligation indefinitely until the requestor contacts the custodian seeking a response to the original request
rules.source_language: If the requestor has elected not to accurately identify themselves or to provide an accurate address, email address, or telephone number, the custodian shall not be required to respond until the requestor contacts the custodian seeking a response to the original request.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: The underlying 7/14-business-day response deadline is Deadlines-scope (sibling); this row is the intake-identification condition that tolls it.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of custodian of a government record
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian who must receive and respond to a request is, for a municipality, the municipal clerk; for any other public agency, the officer officially designated by formal action of that agency's director or governing body.
rules.trigger: Determining who must handle a request.
rules.source_language: "Custodian of a government record" or "custodian" means in the case of a municipality, the municipal clerk and in the case of any other public agency, the officer officially designated by formal action of that agency's director or governing body, as the case may be.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-1.1 (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.1)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver (custodian designation drives routing). For municipalities the custodian is fixed by statute (municipal clerk); for other agencies the city/agency supplies the designated officer.

rules.legal_concept: Request must be in writing and conveyed to the appropriate custodian by an enumerated channel
rules.atomic_rule: A request for access to a government record must be in writing and hand-delivered, mailed, transmitted electronically, or otherwise conveyed to the appropriate custodian.
rules.trigger: A person initiates a records request.
rules.source_language: A request for access to a government record shall be in writing and hand-delivered, mailed, transmitted electronically, or otherwise conveyed to the appropriate custodian.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: 'appropriate custodian' ties intake to the routing rules (NJ-A06/NJ-A30).

rules.legal_concept: Custodian must adopt the GRC form; may deny an incomplete request
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian must adopt the form established by the Government Records Council for use by any person requesting a record; a request shall be submitted in the adopted form and the custodian may deny a request that is incomplete, except that indicating the request is anonymous is not a ground for denial.
rules.trigger: Custodian sets up request intake / receives a request on/off the form.
rules.source_language: The custodian of a public agency shall adopt the form established by the Government Records Council pursuant to subsection b. of section 8 of P.L.2001, c.404 (C.47:1A-7), for the use of any person who requests access to a government record held or controlled by the public agency. ... A request shall be submitted by a requestor in the form adopted by the custodian and the custodian may deny a request that is incomplete, except that a requestor indicating the request is being submitted anonymously shall not be grounds for denial.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(f) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Note: 'may deny a request that is incomplete' is discretion, not a mandatory denial.

rules.legal_concept: Required request fields (identity/contact and record description)
rules.atomic_rule: The request form must provide space for the requestor's name, address, email address, and telephone number, and a brief description of the government record sought.
rules.trigger: Composing/validating a request.
rules.source_language: The form shall provide space for the name, address, email address and telephone number of the requestor and a brief description of the government record sought.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(f) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: The 'brief description of the government record sought' is the intake-side specificity anchor for search identification (NJ-A26).

rules.legal_concept: Letter or email with all required information suffices as a valid request
rules.atomic_rule: A completed adopted form, a letter, or an email from a requestor that includes all of the information required on the adopted form suffices, in place of a completed form, as a valid government record request.
rules.trigger: Request submitted by letter or email rather than the form.
rules.source_language: A completed form adopted by the custodian, a letter, or an email from a requestor including all of the information required on the adopted form shall suffice in place of a completed form as a valid government record request.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(f) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Alternative-format equivalence to the adopted form.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian may deny a letter/email request missing required information
rules.atomic_rule: If a letter or email from a requestor does not include all of the information required on the adopted form, the custodian may deny the record request.
rules.trigger: Letter/email request lacks required form information.
rules.source_language: If a letter or an email from a requestor does not include all of the information required on the adopted form, the custodian may deny the record request.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(f) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Discretionary denial ('may'), not mandatory.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian may deny where a letter/email has excessive information requiring more than reasonable effort to clarify
rules.atomic_rule: If a letter or email from a requestor includes substantially more information than required on the adopted form and requires more than reasonable effort to clarify the information, the custodian may deny the request.
rules.trigger: Request contains substantially more information than required and clarifying it would take more than reasonable effort.
rules.source_language: If the letter or email from a requestor includes substantially more information than required on the adopted form and requires more than reasonable effort to clarify the information, the custodian may deny the request.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(f) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: 'more than reasonable effort to clarify' is a soft standard; the statute permits denial rather than requiring a clarification exchange (no mandatory cure/clarification clock exists - see material negative).

rules.legal_concept: Requestor must certify commercial vs non-commercial use for the request to be fulfilled
rules.atomic_rule: The form must include space for the requestor to certify whether the record will be used by the requestor or another person for a commercial purpose, and the requestor is required to provide this information for the request to be fulfilled.
rules.trigger: Any request; certification is a fulfillment precondition.
rules.source_language: The form also shall include space for a requestor to certify whether the government record will be used by that requestor or another person for a commercial purpose, and the requestor shall be required to provide this information for the request to be fulfilled.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(f) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Feeds the commercial-purpose classification (NJ-A09) that drives the 14-business-day window and special fee (sibling).

rules.legal_concept: Each submission must be made to the custodian of not more than one public agency
rules.atomic_rule: Each submission of a government record request form or email record request must be made to the custodian of not more than one public agency.
rules.trigger: Requestor submits a request.
rules.source_language: Each submission of a government record request form or an email record request shall be made to the custodian of not more than one public agency.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: One-agency-per-submission constraint at intake.

rules.legal_concept: Repeated requests to multiple custodians in the same agency while one is pending may be denied
rules.atomic_rule: Submission of repeated requests to multiple custodians in the same public agency for the same record, while an identical or substantially similar request is pending in the agency, permits the custodian to deny the request.
rules.trigger: Same/substantially similar request already pending in the agency and requestor sends it to multiple custodians.
rules.source_language: Submission of repeated requests to multiple custodians in the same public agency for the same record, while an identical or substantially similar request is pending in the agency, shall permit the custodian to deny the request.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Discretionary denial for duplicative pending requests.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian need not complete an identical repeat request when information is unchanged
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian is not required to complete an identical request for a record from the same requestor if the information has not changed; but this does not prevent periodic requests regarding regularly updated records (e.g., certified payrolls, permits, licensing applications).
rules.trigger: Same requestor resubmits an identical request and the record is unchanged.
rules.source_language: The custodian shall not be required to complete an identical request for access to a government record from the same requestor if the information has not changed. Nothing in this section shall prevent a requestor from filing periodic requests regarding regularly updated public records, including, but not limited to, certified payrolls, permits, and licensing applications.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Kept as one row: the exception (periodic requests for regularly-updated records) is a proviso to the same rule.

rules.legal_concept: Electronic/online portal and fax submission permitted
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency may make available on its website an online form, portal, or software for transmitting requests electronically, and the GRC form may be submitted electronically or by fax.
rules.trigger: Agency offers electronic intake; requestor submits electronically or by fax.
rules.source_language: A public agency may make available to the public on its website an online form, portal, or software for transmitting requests electronically. The form established by the Government Records Council, pursuant to subsection b. of section 8 of P.L.2001, c.404 (C.47:1A-7), may be submitted electronically or by fax.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Permissive electronic-intake channel; agency option, not mandatory.

rules.legal_concept: Custodians with electronic forms must post submission directions on the website
rules.atomic_rule: Custodians who have adopted electronic government record request forms must provide directions on how to submit requests, including any required forms, on the public agency's website.
rules.trigger: Agency has adopted an electronic request form.
rules.source_language: Custodians who have adopted electronic government record request forms shall provide directions on how to submit requests for government records, including any required forms, on the public agency's website.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(f) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Conditional on the agency having adopted electronic forms.

rules.legal_concept: Requestor must certify whether the record is sought in connection with a legal proceeding
rules.atomic_rule: The requestor is required to certify whether the government record is being sought in connection with a legal proceeding and identify the proceeding, for the request to be fulfilled.
rules.trigger: Any request; certification is a fulfillment precondition.
rules.source_language: The requestor shall be required to certify whether the government record is being sought in connection with a legal proceeding and identify the proceeding for the request to be fulfilled.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Mandatory certification feeding the legal-proceeding bar (NJ-A23).

rules.legal_concept: Party to a legal proceeding may not use OPRA for a record subject to a court order/pending discovery
rules.atomic_rule: A party to a legal proceeding may not request a government record if the record sought is the subject of a court order including a pending discovery request, and the custodian is not required to complete such a request.
rules.trigger: Requestor is a party (or its attorney/agent) to a legal proceeding and the record is subject of a court order or pending discovery in that proceeding.
rules.source_language: A party to a legal proceeding may not request a government record if the record sought is the subject of a court order including a pending discovery request, and a custodian shall not be required to complete such a request. ... For purposes of this provision, a party to a legal proceeding shall include a party subject to a court order, any attorney representing that party, and any person acting as an agent for or on behalf of that party.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Statute preserves a carve-out: this does not bar a request by a labor organization or CBA-signatory contractor seeking information material to enforcement of wage/hour, workplace-safety, or public-procurement statutes when not sought in furtherance of discovery. Flag for human legal review before automating the bar.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian must attempt a reasonable solution before denying a request that would substantially disrupt operations
rules.atomic_rule: If a request would substantially disrupt agency operations, the custodian may deny access only after informing the requestor of the potential disruption and attempting to reach a reasonable solution with the requestor that accommodates the interests of both the requestor and the agency.
rules.trigger: Fulfilling the request would substantially disrupt agency operations.
rules.source_language: If a request for access to a government record would substantially disrupt agency operations, the custodian may deny access to the record after informing the requestor of the potential disruption to agency operations and attempting to reach a reasonable solution with the requestor that accommodates the interests of the requestor and the agency.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: The closest OPRA analog to a mandatory clarification/negotiation step, but it is conditioned on substantial disruption, not on request ambiguity. 'reasonable solution' / 'substantially disrupt' are soft standards; no numeric threshold.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian need not perform research or create new records
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian is not required to complete a request if the custodian determines that the request would require research and the collection of information from the contents of government records and the creation of new government records setting forth that research and information.
rules.trigger: Request would require research/collection and creation of a new record.
rules.source_language: A custodian shall not be required to complete a request ... if the custodian determines that the request would require research and the collection of information from the contents of government records and the creation of new government records setting forth that research and information.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Codifies the long-standing OPRA rule that a request must seek identifiable records, not compel research/analysis.

rules.legal_concept: Correspondence-type requests must specify accounts/subject/time period
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian is not required to complete a request for mail, email, text messages, correspondence, or social media postings/messages unless the request identifies a specific job title or accounts to be searched, a specific subject matter, and is confined to a reasonable time period.
rules.trigger: Request seeks correspondence-type records (mail/email/text/social media).
rules.source_language: A custodian shall not be required to complete a request including for, but not limited to, mail, email, text messages, correspondence, or social media postings and messages, if the request does not identify a specific job title or accounts to be searched, a specific subject matter, and is not confined to a reasonable time period.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: 'reasonable time period' is a soft standard bounding the search's date range (not a processing clock). Three conjunctive requirements: (1) job title or accounts, (2) subject matter, (3) reasonable time period.

rules.legal_concept: Identifying custodians/individuals by job title and position suffices for a search
rules.atomic_rule: It is sufficient for a requestor to identify specific individuals to be searched by the individual's job title and position.
rules.trigger: Requestor identifies the accounts/individuals to search.
rules.source_language: It shall be sufficient for a requestor to identify specific individuals by the individual's job title and position.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Companion/proviso to NJ-A26 - a requestor need not name the individual, only the job title/position.

rules.legal_concept: Any employee receiving a request must forward it to, or direct the requestor to, the custodian
rules.atomic_rule: Any officer or employee of a public agency who receives a request for access to a government record must forward the request to the custodian of the record or direct the requestor to the custodian of the record.
rules.trigger: A request is received by a non-custodian officer/employee.
rules.source_language: Any officer or employee of a public agency who receives a request for access to a government record shall forward the request to the custodian of the record or direct the requestor to the custodian of the record.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(h) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: wrong-department routing to the correct custodian.

rules.legal_concept: Request not considered submitted until received by the custodian
rules.atomic_rule: A request is not considered submitted until it is received by the custodian of records.
rules.trigger: Request delivered to a non-custodian and forwarded/redirected.
rules.source_language: The request shall not be considered submitted until it is received by the custodian of records.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(h) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Defines the clock-start event (receipt by custodian) for the response deadline that the Deadlines sibling computes; clock_effect marked none because this row defines the start reference, it does not itself set/run a deadline.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian must refer requestor to the originating agency within seven business days
rules.atomic_rule: If the custodian does not provide a record held only by another agency, the custodian must direct the requestor, within seven business days, to the public agency that (to the best of their knowledge) created, maintains, or received the record; at which time the request is considered completed.
rules.trigger: Custodian declines to provide an out-of-possession record (per NJ-A32).
rules.clock_spec: 7 business days from receipt of the request to direct the requestor to the originating agency; request then deemed completed (terminal)
rules.source_language: In the event the custodian does not provide the record, the custodian shall direct the requestor within seven business days to the public agency that, to the best of their knowledge, created, maintains, or received the requested record, at which time the request shall be considered completed.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Routing path with an intrinsic 7-business-day referral deadline and a terminal outcome (request considered completed). Captured here because the referral is a Custody/Routing fork; the terminal completion also interests the Deadlines sibling.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian may redirect requestor to a record readily available on the agency website
rules.atomic_rule: If a government record in complete and unabridged form is readily available on the public agency's website, the custodian may require the requestor to obtain it from the website (which must contain a search-bar feature on its home page), and the custodian must provide directions to assist in finding the record, including the website URL and the on-site location (search bar, menu, tab, link, landing page).
rules.trigger: Requested record is readily available, complete and unabridged, on the agency website.
rules.source_language: If the government record in a complete and unabridged form is readily available on a public agency's website, the custodian may require the requestor to obtain the record from the website, which shall contain a search bar feature on its home page. The custodian shall provide the requestor with directions to assist in finding the record on the website, including providing the website URL address and the location on the website of the search bar, menu button, tab, link, landing page or equivalent, which contains the requested record.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(e) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Routing-to-self-service fork. Follow-on rules deferred to siblings: the 7-business-day 'deemed fulfilled' clock if the requestor does not respond, the 7-day custodian-assist duty, and the physical-copy fallback at a fee not exceeding twice production cost (Deadlines/Fees scope). Also in this subsection but deferred: immediate-access categories (budgets/bills/vouchers/contracts/salary) and the 24-month immediate-access limit are Production/Deadlines scope.

rules.legal_concept: Time period for custodian's response (grant or deny)
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian shall grant access to, or deny, a government-record request as soon as possible but not later than seven business days after receiving the request, provided the record is currently available and not in storage or archived.
rules.trigger: Custodian receives a request for a currently-available record
rules.clock_spec: 7 business-days from request receipt (ceiling; 'as soon as possible' soft floor overlay)
rules.source_language: Unless a shorter time period is otherwise provided by statute, regulation, or executive order, a custodian of a government record shall grant access to a government record or deny a request for access to a government record as soon as possible, but not later than seven business days after receiving the request, ... provided that the record is currently available and not in storage or archived.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Core response duty and default clock. 'as soon as possible' is a soft floor; seven business days is the hard ceiling. Clock start defined by NJ-T25 (received by custodian).

rules.legal_concept: Extended 14-business-day window for commercial-purpose requests
rules.atomic_rule: The response window is not later than 14 business days if the request is for a commercial purpose.
rules.trigger: Request certified/identified as being for a commercial purpose
rules.clock_spec: 14 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: a custodian of a government record shall grant access to a government record or deny a request for access to a government record as soon as possible, but not later than seven business days after receiving the request, or 14 business days if the request is for a commercial purpose ... but the custodian shall notify the requestor of the additional response time within seven business days
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: 'Commercial purpose' defined at NJ-T47. Additional-time notice within 7 business days is NJ-T04.

rules.legal_concept: Extended 14-business-day window for covered-officer privacy review
rules.atomic_rule: The response window is not later than 14 business days if the records must be reviewed by the agency for compliance with P.L.2021, c.371 (covered-officer home-address protection).
rules.trigger: Records must be reviewed for P.L.2021 c.371 compliance
rules.clock_spec: 14 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: or 14 business days if the request is for a commercial purpose or if the records have to be reviewed by the public agency for the purpose of the agency's compliance with P.L.2021, c.371 (C.47:1B-1 et seq.), but the custodian shall notify the requestor of the additional response time within seven business days
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Same 14-day window as commercial requests but triggered by covered-officer redaction review (see NJ-T36).

rules.legal_concept: Notice of additional response time
rules.atomic_rule: When invoking the 14-business-day window (commercial or c.371 review), the custodian shall notify the requestor of the additional response time within seven business days.
rules.trigger: Custodian invokes the 14-business-day extended window
rules.clock_spec: 7 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: but the custodian shall notify the requestor of the additional response time within seven business days
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Required notice step; the 7-business-day timing is the configurable value within the notice fork.

rules.legal_concept: Additional seven business days for small fire districts
rules.atomic_rule: The seven- or fourteen-business-day response periods are an additional seven business days longer if the public agency is a fire district employing one or fewer full-time employees serving as custodians.
rules.trigger: Agency is a fire district with one or fewer full-time custodian-employees
rules.clock_spec: +7 business-days added to the applicable 7- or 14-business-day window
rules.source_language: The response time periods of seven or 14 business days, as established in this subsection, shall be an additional seven business days longer if the public agency is a fire district which employs one or fewer full-time employees who serve as custodians.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Agency-attribute-driven fixed extension.

rules.legal_concept: Commercial requestor expedite to seven business days
rules.atomic_rule: If a commercial requestor wishes to receive the record within seven business days, the custodian shall provide a copy and may charge a special service fee not exceeding two times the cost of production.
rules.trigger: Commercial requestor elects seven-business-day delivery
rules.clock_spec: 7 business-days from request receipt (elected expedite)
rules.source_language: If a commercial requestor would like to receive the record within seven business days, as established in this subsection, the custodian shall provide the requestor with a copy of the record and may charge a special service fee not exceeding two times the cost of the production of the record.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Expedite path is in-scope (Production/Deadlines); the '2x cost' fee ceiling belongs to the Fees sibling agent.

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable extension for unforeseen circumstances
rules.atomic_rule: If unable to fulfill a request due to unforeseen circumstances or circumstances reasonably necessitating more time, the custodian is entitled to a reasonable extension of any response deadline.
rules.trigger: Unforeseen circumstances reasonably necessitating additional time
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: 'reasonable extension' of the response deadline
rules.source_language: In the event a records custodian is unable to fulfill a records request due to unforeseen circumstances or circumstances that otherwise reasonably necessitate additional time to fulfill the records request, the custodian shall be entitled to a reasonable extension of any response deadline and shall notify the requestor of the time extension within seven business days after receiving the request.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Soft-standard 'reasonable' extension; do not convert to a fixed day-count. Paired notice duty split to NJ-T08.

rules.legal_concept: Notice of time extension
rules.atomic_rule: When taking a reasonable extension for unforeseen circumstances, the custodian shall notify the requestor of the time extension within seven business days after receiving the request.
rules.trigger: Custodian invokes an unforeseen-circumstances extension
rules.clock_spec: 7 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: the custodian shall be entitled to a reasonable extension of any response deadline and shall notify the requestor of the time extension within seven business days after receiving the request.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Distinct from NJ-T04 (which is the commercial/c.371 additional-time notice).

rules.legal_concept: Deemed denial upon failure to respond
rules.atomic_rule: Failure of the custodian to respond within the applicable seven or fourteen business days is deemed a denial of the request (unless the requestor elected not to accurately identify themselves or provide accurate contact information).
rules.trigger: No custodian response by the applicable 7- or 14-business-day deadline
rules.clock_spec: terminal event at expiry of 7 or 14 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: In the event a custodian fails to respond within seven business days or 14 business days, as appropriate, after receiving a request, the failure to respond shall be deemed a denial of the request, unless the requestor has elected not to accurately identify themselves or to provide an accurate address, email address, or telephone number.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver deemed/constructive-denial trigger; remedy amounts (attorney fees/penalties) are excluded and belong to Enforcement sibling.

rules.legal_concept: Suspension of response duty for inaccurately-identified requestor
rules.atomic_rule: If the requestor elected not to accurately identify themselves or to provide an accurate address, email, or telephone number, the custodian is not required to respond until the requestor contacts the custodian seeking a response to the original request.
rules.trigger: Requestor declined to accurately identify or provide accurate contact info
rules.clock_spec: response clock does not run until requestor contacts custodian
rules.source_language: If the requestor has elected not to accurately identify themselves or to provide an accurate address, email address, or telephone number, the custodian shall not be required to respond until the requestor contacts the custodian seeking a response to the original request.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Also disables the deemed-denial trigger (NJ-T09) for such requestors.

rules.legal_concept: Advisement that record is in storage or archived
