rules.atomic_rule: If the record is in storage or archived, the custodian shall so advise the requestor within seven or fourteen business days (as appropriate) after receiving the request, and advise when the record can be made available.
rules.trigger: Requested record is in storage or archived
rules.clock_spec: 7 or 14 business-days from request receipt to advise
rules.source_language: If the government record is in storage or archived, the requestor shall be so advised within seven or 14 business days, as appropriate, after the custodian receives the request. The requestor shall be advised by the custodian when the record can be made available, which shall be no more than 21 business days from the date the requestor is so advised.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Entry point of the storage/archived processing path.

rules.legal_concept: Maximum time to make stored/archived record available
rules.atomic_rule: A stored or archived record must be made available no more than 21 business days from the date the requestor is advised it is in storage/archived.
rules.trigger: Custodian has advised requestor the record is in storage/archived
rules.clock_spec: 21 business-days from date requestor is advised
rules.source_language: The requestor shall be advised by the custodian when the record can be made available, which shall be no more than 21 business days from the date the requestor is so advised.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Ceiling on the storage-path production window.

rules.legal_concept: Deemed denial if stored/archived record not timely produced
rules.atomic_rule: If a stored/archived record is not made available by the advised availability time (max 21 business days), access shall be deemed denied.
rules.trigger: Stored/archived record not made available by the advised deadline
rules.clock_spec: terminal event at expiry of the storage-availability window (<=21 business-days)
rules.source_language: If the record is not made available by that time, access shall be deemed denied.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Terminal event for the storage path.

rules.legal_concept: Requestor window to retrieve completed records
rules.atomic_rule: A requestor shall have 14 business days to retrieve the government records following the custodian's notice that the request is completed and the records are available.
rules.trigger: Custodian notifies requestor the request is completed and records available
rules.clock_spec: 14 business-days from completion/availability notice
rules.source_language: A requestor shall have 14 business days to retrieve the government records following notice from the custodian that the request has been completed and the records are available.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Requestor-side pickup window (fixed grant to requestor).

rules.legal_concept: Suspension of response deadlines during declared emergency
rules.atomic_rule: During a declared state of emergency, public health emergency, or state of local disaster emergency, the response deadlines under (i)(1) and subsection e. do not apply, but the custodian shall make a reasonable effort to respond within 7 or 14 business days, or as soon as possible thereafter.
rules.trigger: Declared state of emergency / public health emergency / local disaster emergency
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: statutory deadlines do not apply; 'reasonable effort ... as soon as possible' from request receipt
rules.source_language: During a period declared pursuant to the laws of this State as a state of emergency, public health emergency, or state of local disaster emergency, the deadlines by which to respond to a request for, or grant or deny access to, a government record under paragraph (1) of this subsection or subsection e. of this section shall not apply, provided, however, that the custodian of a government record shall make a reasonable effort, as the circumstances permit, to respond to a request for access to a government record within seven business days or 14 business days, as appropriate, or as soon as possible thereafter.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(2), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Tolls both the (i)(1) response clock and the subsection-e immediate-access requirement.

rules.legal_concept: Redirect to agency that created/maintains the record
rules.atomic_rule: For a record created/maintained/received by another agency and made available only by remote access or courtesy copy (unless that agency is in the judicial branch), the custodian is not obligated to produce it and, if not providing it, shall direct the requestor within seven business days to the originating agency, at which time the request is considered completed.
rules.trigger: Requested record was created/maintained/received by another non-judicial-branch agency and made available only via remote access or courtesy copy
rules.clock_spec: 7 business-days from request receipt to redirect; redirect completes the request (terminal)
rules.source_language: A public agency shall not be considered to be in possession of a public record that is created, maintained, or received by another public agency and made available to the public agency either by remote access to a computer network or by distribution as a courtesy copy, unless the agency that created, maintained, or received the record resides within the judicial branch of the State Government. A records custodian of a public agency that receives a request for a record created, maintained, or received by another public agency, shall not be obligated to provide the record to the requestor. In the event the custodian does not provide the record, the custodian shall direct the requestor within seven business days to the public agency that, to the best of their knowledge, created, maintains, or received the requested record, at which time the request shall be considered completed.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Routing keeper-sliver; also a terminal completion event on redirect.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to complete unchanged identical repeat request
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian is not required to complete an identical request for access from the same requestor if the information has not changed.
rules.trigger: Same requestor submits an identical request and the information has not changed
rules.source_language: The custodian shall not be required to complete an identical request for access to a government record from the same requestor if the information has not changed.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Limited by the periodic-request carve-out (NJ-T18).

rules.legal_concept: Periodic requests for regularly-updated records permitted
rules.atomic_rule: Nothing prevents a requestor from filing periodic requests regarding regularly updated public records, including certified payrolls, permits, and licensing applications.
rules.trigger: Requestor files periodic requests for regularly-updated records
rules.source_language: Nothing in this section shall prevent a requestor from filing periodic requests regarding regularly updated public records, including, but not limited to, certified payrolls, permits, and licensing applications.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Carve-out to the identical-request limitation.

rules.legal_concept: Prompt compliance with request
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian shall promptly comply with a request to inspect, examine, copy, or provide a copy of a government record.
rules.trigger: Custodian receives a valid request
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: 'promptly' from request receipt
rules.source_language: A custodian shall promptly comply with a request to inspect, examine, copy, or provide a copy of a government record.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Soft 'promptly' standard operating alongside the seven-business-day ceiling (NJ-T01).

rules.legal_concept: Notice of specific basis when unable to comply
rules.atomic_rule: If unable to comply with a request, the custodian shall indicate the specific basis on the request form, promptly return it to the requestor, and sign and date the form and provide the requestor a copy.
rules.trigger: Custodian is unable to comply with a request for access
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: 'promptly' return of the form
rules.source_language: If the custodian is unable to comply with a request for access, the custodian shall indicate the specific basis therefor on the request form and promptly return it to the requestor. The custodian shall sign and date the form and provide the requestor with a copy thereof.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Denial reason-statement notice; the denial-remedy/appeal itself is a sibling (Denials/Appeals) area.

rules.legal_concept: Denial for substantial disruption after notice and attempted solution
rules.atomic_rule: If a request would substantially disrupt agency operations, the custodian may deny access after informing the requestor of the potential disruption and attempting to reach a reasonable solution accommodating both parties' interests.
rules.trigger: Request would substantially disrupt agency operations
rules.source_language: If a request for access to a government record would substantially disrupt agency operations, the custodian may deny access to the record after informing the requestor of the potential disruption to agency operations and attempting to reach a reasonable solution with the requestor that accommodates the interests of the requestor and the agency.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: In-scope for the mandatory communication step (inform + attempt solution) preceding any denial.

rules.legal_concept: Explanation and itemized list of special service fees
rules.atomic_rule: When imposing a special service charge, the custodian shall provide the requestor with an explanation for, and an itemized list of, the fees or charges.
rules.trigger: Custodian imposes a special service charge
rules.source_language: The custodian shall provide the requestor with an explanation for and an itemized list of the fees or charges.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(c), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Communication duty is in-scope; the underlying special-service-charge amount/basis belongs to the Fees sibling.

rules.legal_concept: Opportunity to review and object to fees before incurred
rules.atomic_rule: The requestor shall have the opportunity to review and object to any fee or charge prior to it being incurred; there is a rebuttable presumption fees are reasonable, and on objection the burden is on the requestor to show they are unreasonable.
rules.trigger: A fee or charge is to be imposed on a request
rules.source_language: The requestor shall have the opportunity to review and object to any fee or charge prior to it being incurred. There shall be a rebuttable presumption that the fees or charges presented by the custodian are reasonable. If the requestor objects to the fees or charges, the burden of proof shall be on the requestor to demonstrate that the fees or charges are unreasonable.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(c), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Pre-charge review-and-object communication step plus reasonableness presumption/burden.

rules.legal_concept: Publication of appeal rights on website and request form
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian shall include, on the agency's website and public-records request form, information regarding a requestor's right to appeal a denial of or failure to provide access and the appeal procedure, including the GRC's website address and toll-free information line phone number.
rules.trigger: None stated (standing obligation)
rules.source_language: A custodian shall include information on the public agency's website and public records request form regarding a requestor's right to appeal a denial of, or failure to provide, access to a government record and the procedure by which an appeal may be filed, which shall include the website address and toll-free information line phone number of the Government Records Council.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(j), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: 2024 amendment replaced the prior physical-posting requirement with website/form publication.

rules.legal_concept: Forwarding request to custodian; receipt defines submission
rules.atomic_rule: Any officer or employee who receives a records request shall forward it to, or direct the requestor to, the custodian; the request is not considered submitted until received by the custodian of records.
rules.trigger: An officer or employee other than the custodian receives a request
rules.source_language: Any officer or employee of a public agency who receives a request for access to a government record shall forward the request to the custodian of the record or direct the requestor to the custodian of the record. The request shall not be considered submitted until it is received by the custodian of records.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(h), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Wrong-department routing keeper-sliver; second sentence defines the clock-start event for NJ-T01 (receipt by custodian).

rules.legal_concept: Access in requested medium/format if maintained
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian shall permit access and provide a copy in the medium or format requested if the agency maintains the record in that medium or format.
rules.trigger: Requestor specifies a medium/format the agency maintains
rules.source_language: A custodian shall permit access to a government record and provide a copy thereof in the medium or format requested if the public agency maintains the record in that medium or format.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(d), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2

rules.legal_concept: Conversion to requested format when available
rules.atomic_rule: If the agency does not maintain the record in the requested medium/format, the custodian shall convert it to the requested medium/format if that medium/format is available to the agency and does not require a substantial amount of manipulation or programming of information technology or the services of a third-party vendor.
rules.trigger: Requested medium/format not maintained but available without substantial IT manipulation
rules.source_language: If the public agency does not maintain the record in the medium or format requested, the custodian shall convert the record to the medium or format requested, if the medium or format is available to the public agency and does not require a substantial amount of manipulation or programming of information technology, or the services of a third party vendor.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(d), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: The conversion special-service-fee (labor/IT cost) belongs to the Fees sibling.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to convert electronic format requiring substantial manipulation
rules.atomic_rule: If the agency does not maintain the record in the requested electronic medium/format and it is not available without substantial IT manipulation or programming, the custodian need not convert it but shall at minimum provide a copy in the electronic format maintained by the agency.
rules.trigger: Requested electronic format unavailable without substantial IT manipulation
rules.source_language: If the public agency does not maintain the record in the electronic medium or format requested, and the medium or format is not available to the public agency without a substantial amount of manipulation or programming of information technology, the custodian shall be under no obligation to convert the record to the electronic medium or format requested but shall, at a minimum, provide a copy in the electronic format maintained by the public agency.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(d), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Fallback-format production floor.

rules.legal_concept: Immediate access record categories
rules.atomic_rule: Immediate access ordinarily shall be granted to budgets, bills, vouchers, contracts (including collective negotiations agreements and individual employment contracts), and public employee salary and overtime information.
rules.trigger: Request for one of the enumerated immediate-access record categories
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: 'immediate access' from request receipt
rules.source_language: Immediate access ordinarily shall be granted to budgets, bills, vouchers, contracts, including collective negotiations agreements and individual employment contracts, and public employee salary and overtime information.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(e), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Special expedited category; 'immediate' is a soft standard, tolled during declared emergencies (NJ-T15).

rules.legal_concept: Immediate access not required for records over 24 months old
rules.atomic_rule: Immediate access to government records is not required to be granted for documents over 24 months old.
rules.trigger: Requested immediate-access document is more than 24 months old
rules.source_language: Immediate access to government records shall not be required to be granted for documents over 24 months old.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(e), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: 2024 amendment raised the threshold from 12 to 24 months. Age threshold is the configurable value.

rules.legal_concept: Redirect requestor to record available on agency website
rules.atomic_rule: If the government record in complete and unabridged form is readily available on the agency's website (which must have a home-page search bar), the custodian may require the requestor to obtain it from the website and shall provide directions (URL and location of the search bar/menu/tab/link/landing page) to find it.
rules.trigger: Requested record available complete and unabridged on the agency website
rules.source_language: If the government record in a complete and unabridged form is readily available on a public agency's website, the custodian may require the requestor to obtain the record from the website, which shall contain a search bar feature on its home page. The custodian shall provide the requestor with directions to assist in finding the record on the website, including providing the website URL address and the location on the website of the search bar, menu button, tab, link, landing page or equivalent, which contains the requested record.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(e), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Entry point of the website-fulfillment path (NJ-T32 through NJ-T34).

rules.legal_concept: Website request deemed fulfilled after seven business days
rules.atomic_rule: If the requestor does not respond within seven business days of the custodian providing website information, the request is deemed fulfilled, unless the website version omits non-protected information in the original, in which case the custodian shall produce the original subject to required redactions.
rules.trigger: Requestor does not respond within seven business days of website-location notice
rules.clock_spec: terminal (deemed fulfilled) at 7 business-days from custodian providing website info
rules.source_language: If the requestor does not respond to the custodian within seven business days of the custodian providing information about a record on the public agency's website, the request shall be deemed fulfilled unless the version of the government record on the public agency's website fails to contain non-protected information contained in the original record, in which case the custodian shall produce the original version of the record subject to any redactions required by law.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(e), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Terminal fulfillment event with a completeness carve-back to original-record production.

rules.legal_concept: Website location assistance on good-faith failure
rules.atomic_rule: If the requestor cannot find the record after a good-faith effort, the requestor shall notify the custodian within seven business days, and the custodian shall make a reasonable attempt to assist within seven business days of that notification.
rules.trigger: Requestor unable to locate record on website after good-faith effort
rules.clock_spec: 7 business-days for requestor to notify; 7 business-days for custodian to assist
rules.source_language: If, after the custodian has provided instructions on how to find a record on a public agency's website, the requestor is unable to find the record upon making a good faith effort to locate the record on the website, the requestor shall notify the custodian within seven business days of the custodian providing the information. Upon receiving such a request for assistance from a requestor, the custodian shall make a reasonable attempt to assist the requestor in finding the record on the website within seven business days of the requestor notifying the custodian.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(e), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Two paired seven-business-day windows in the website path.

rules.legal_concept: Physical copy when website record cannot be located
rules.atomic_rule: If the requestor is still unable to locate the record and requests a physical copy, the custodian shall provide a physical copy within seven business days of the request for a physical copy, for a fee not exceeding two times the cost of production.
rules.trigger: Requestor still cannot locate the website record and requests a physical copy
rules.clock_spec: 7 business-days from the request for a physical copy
rules.source_language: If the requestor is still unable to locate the record and requests a physical copy, the custodian shall provide the requestor with a physical copy of the record, for a fee not exceeding two times the cost of the production of the document. The custodian shall provide the requestor with the physical copy of the record within seven business days of the request for a physical copy.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(e), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Production step; the '2x cost' fee ceiling belongs to the Fees sibling.

rules.legal_concept: Mandatory redaction of personal identifiers
rules.atomic_rule: Prior to allowing access to any record, the custodian shall redact any information disclosing the social security number, credit card number, personal telephone number, or driver license number of any person (subject to enumerated government-use and child-support exceptions).
rules.trigger: Record to be disclosed contains SSN, credit card, personal telephone, or driver license number
rules.source_language: Prior to allowing access to any government record, the custodian thereof shall redact from that record any information which discloses the social security number, credit card number, personal telephone number, or driver license number of any person ... except for use by any government agency, including any court or law enforcement agency, in carrying out its functions, or any private person or entity acting on behalf thereof, or any private person or entity seeking to enforce payment of court-ordered child support
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(a), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: 2024 amendment changed 'unlisted telephone number' to 'personal telephone number.' A broader draft redaction (email/medical/financial/personal info) was NOT enacted (deleted in the second reprint).

rules.legal_concept: Mandatory redaction of covered-officer home address (Daniel's Law)
rules.atomic_rule: Prior to allowing access, the custodian shall redact, per P.L.2021, c.371, the home address (primary or secondary) of any active, formerly active, or retired judicial officer, prosecutor, law enforcement officer, or child protective investigator in DCP&P, or any immediate family member.
rules.trigger: Record to be disclosed contains the home address of a covered person or immediate family member
rules.source_language: the custodian thereof shall redact from that record any information which discloses ... in accordance with section 2 of P.L.2021, c.371 (C.47:1B-2), the home address, whether a primary or secondary residence, of any active, formerly active, or retired judicial officer, prosecutor, law enforcement officer, or child protective investigator in the Division of Child Protection and Permanency, or, as defined in section 1 of P.L.2021, c.371 (C.47:1B-1), any immediate family member thereof
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(a), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Redaction operationalized through the Office of Information Privacy approval process (NJ-T38); triggers the 14-day review window (NJ-T03).

rules.legal_concept: Segregate exempt portion and produce remainder
rules.atomic_rule: If the custodian asserts part of a record is exempt, the custodian shall delete or excise from a copy the portion asserted exempt and shall promptly permit access to the remainder of the record.
rules.trigger: Custodian asserts part of a particular record is exempt from access
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: 'promptly' permit access to remainder
rules.source_language: If the custodian of a government record asserts that part of a particular record is exempt from public access pursuant to P.L.1963, c.73 (C.47:1A-1 et seq.) as amended and supplemented, the custodian shall delete or excise from a copy of the record that portion which the custodian asserts is exempt from access and shall promptly permit access to the remainder of the record.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Core segregability duty; 'promptly' is a soft production standard for the non-exempt remainder.

rules.legal_concept: 30-day compliance to redact OIP-approved covered-person address
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency shall redact or cease disclosing the home address of a covered person approved by the Office of Information Privacy no later than 30 days following the approval, and shall discontinue redaction for an approved revocation within 30 days of that approval.
rules.trigger: Office of Information Privacy approves a covered-person redaction (or revocation) request
rules.clock_spec: 30 calendar-days from OIP approval
rules.source_language: A public agency shall redact or cease to disclose, in accordance with section 6 of P.L.2001, c.404 (C.47:1A-5) and section 1 of P.L.1995, c.23 (C.47:1A-1.1), respectively, the home address of a covered person approved by the Office of Information Privacy not later than 30 days following the approval. A public agency shall also discontinue the redaction or nondisclosure of the home address of any covered person for whom a revocation request has been approved not later than 30 days following the approval.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1B-2(b)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.6
rules.notes: Redaction compliance window keyed to an external OIP approval event, not to a records request.

rules.legal_concept: Criminal-investigation information within 24 hours
rules.atomic_rule: Enumerated information concerning a criminal investigation shall be available to the public within 24 hours or as soon as practicable of a request for such information.
rules.trigger: Request for enumerated criminal-investigation information
rules.clock_spec: 24 hours (or 'as soon as practicable') from request
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding the provisions of P.L.1963, c. 73 (C. 47:1A-1 et seq.), as amended and supplemented, the following information concerning a criminal investigation shall be available to the public within 24 hours or as soon as practicable, of a request for such information:
rules.effective_status: Current (P.L. 2001, c.404, s.4; not amended by P.L. 2024, c.16)
rules.notes: Distinct expedited special-records workflow. Source: GRC official 'Readable Version' PDF (this section unchanged by the 2024 amendments). Hybrid 24-hour ceiling with an 'as soon as practicable' soft alternative.

rules.legal_concept: Limited redaction of election records by election agencies
rules.atomic_rule: For enumerated election records, an election agency shall not redact the provided information except for voter signatures, Social Security numbers, driver license numbers, and non-driver identification numbers.
rules.trigger: Request to an election agency for enumerated election records
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding any other law, rule, or regulation to the contrary, except as otherwise provided in sections 2 and 3 of P.L.2021, c.371 (C.47:1B-1 et seq.), subsection b. of section 1 of P.L.1994, c.148 (C.19:31-3.2), or in any rules or regulations promulgated by the Secretary of State pursuant to subsection f. of this section, the following shall be records for which the provided information shall not be redacted by an election agency except for voter signatures, Social Security numbers, driver license numbers, and non-driver identification numbers:
rules.effective_status: Effective September 3, 2024 (P.L. 2024, c.16, new section); current
rules.notes: Special election-agency redaction rule narrowing redactable fields for voter-registration, party-affiliation, VBM applications, nominating/recall/public-question petitions, and related submissions.

rules.legal_concept: Two-business-day immediate access to election records
rules.atomic_rule: An election agency shall make enumerated election records available for immediate access and email transmission as soon as possible but not later than two business days after receipt of the request, provided the request is not for a commercial purpose, with no fee charged.
rules.trigger: Non-commercial request to an election agency for enumerated election records (filed within preceding 90 days)
rules.clock_spec: 2 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding any other law, rule, or regulation to the contrary, the following shall be records and information that an election agency shall make available to requestors for immediate access and transmission via email as soon as possible, but not later than two business days after receipt of the request, provided the request is not for a commercial purpose, for which a fee shall not be charged nor collected:
rules.effective_status: Effective September 3, 2024 (P.L. 2024, c.16, new section); current
rules.notes: Special expedited election workflow; commercial requests fall outside this expedited/no-fee track.

rules.legal_concept: Election-eve expedited access to voter lists
rules.atomic_rule: For non-commercial requests pertaining only to an election within 16 days, election agencies shall provide enumerated voter lists for immediate access; transmission is not later than two business days after receipt when the request is made 1-15 days before the election, and a request submitted by noon the day before an election must be completed by noon on election day, with no fee.
rules.trigger: Non-commercial request pertaining only to an election within 16 days
rules.clock_spec: 2 business-days from receipt (1-15 days pre-election); if submitted by noon day-before-election, complete by noon election day
rules.source_language: the following in paragraphs (1) through (4) of this subsection shall be records and information that an election agency shall make available to requestors for immediate access and transmission via email as soon as possible, provided the request pertains only to an election to be held within 16 days after the date of the request and is not for a commercial purpose. The transmission shall be not later than two business days after receipt of the request when said request is made between one and 15 days before the date of the election pertaining to the request. For any request submitted the day before an election by noon, the request shall be completed by noon the day of the election. A fee shall not be charged nor collected.
rules.effective_status: Effective September 3, 2024 (P.L. 2024, c.16, new section); current
rules.notes: Bespoke election-eve deadline fork (noon-before/noon-of); privacy-preserving production required where disclosure would violate a voter's privacy.

rules.legal_concept: Website posting satisfies election-record deadlines
rules.atomic_rule: The inspection and transmission deadline requirements are deemed satisfied if the election agency posts the records and information on its website.
rules.trigger: Election agency posts the applicable election records on its website
rules.clock_spec: deadline requirement deemed satisfied upon website posting
rules.source_language: The inspection and transmission deadline requirements of this subsection shall be deemed satisfied if an election agency posts on its website the records and information referred to in this subsection.
rules.effective_status: Effective September 3, 2024 (P.L. 2024, c.16, new section); current
rules.notes: Satisfies both the two-business-day (c) and election-eve (d) deadlines.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'commercial purpose'
rules.atomic_rule: 'Commercial purpose' means direct or indirect use of any part of a government record for sale, resale, solicitation, rent, or lease of a service, or any use by which the user expects a profit; it excludes use by the news media, news/journalistic/educational/scientific/scholarly/governmental organizations, authorized campaign/committee agents, labor organizations, and CBA-signatory contractors seeking enforcement information.
rules.trigger: Requestor certifies (or request is identified as) commercial-purpose use
rules.source_language: "Commercial purpose" means the direct or indirect use of any part of a government record for sale, resale, solicitation, rent, or lease of a service, or any use by which the user expects a profit either through commission, salary, or fee. "Commercial purpose" shall not include the use of a government record for any purpose by: (1) the news media, or any parent company, subsidiary, or affiliate of any news media, as defined by section 2 of P.L.1977, c.253 (C.2A:84A-21a); (2) any news, journalistic, educational, scientific, scholarly, or governmental organization; (3) any person authorized to act on behalf of a candidate committee, joint candidate committee, political committee, continuing political committee, political party committee, or legislative leadership committee ...; (4) any labor organization; (5) any contractor signatory to a collective bargaining agreement seeking information material to the enforcement of State or federal statutes or regulations regarding, but not limited to, wage and hour protections ...
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-1.1, as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.1
rules.notes: Definition the engine branches on: commercial purpose drives the 14-business-day window (NJ-T02), the expedite-fee option (NJ-T06), and fee treatment (Fees sibling).

rules.legal_concept: Statutory per-page duplication fee for printed matter
rules.atomic_rule: For a government record embodied in printed matter, the custodian shall assess a duplication fee of $0.05 per letter-size page or smaller and $0.07 per legal-size page or larger.
rules.trigger: Requestor purchases a copy of a printed government record
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law or regulation and except as provided in paragraph (2) of this subsection, the fee assessed for the duplication of a government record embodied in the form of printed matter shall be $0.05 per letter size page or smaller, and $0.07 per legal size page or larger.
rules.notes: Set as a fixed statutory amount, not a ceiling; 'except as otherwise provided by law or regulation' allows a different rate where another statute/regulation prescribes one.

rules.atomic_rule: Access to electronic records and non-printed materials shall be provided free of charge (fee = $0).
rules.trigger: Record requested in electronic or non-printed form
rules.source_language: Access to electronic records and non-printed materials shall be provided free of charge, but the public agency may charge for the actual costs of any needed supplies such as computer discs.
rules.notes: Split from the supply-cost permission (NJ-M03), which is bundled in the same sentence.

rules.atomic_rule: When providing electronic/non-printed records free of charge, the public agency may charge for the actual costs of any needed supplies such as computer discs.
rules.trigger: Supplies (e.g., discs) needed to deliver electronic records
rules.source_language: Access to electronic records and non-printed materials shall be provided free of charge, but the public agency may charge for the actual costs of any needed supplies such as computer discs.
rules.notes: 'Actual costs' is an undefined-cost standard, not a fixed rate.

rules.atomic_rule: No fee shall be charged if the request is completed by directing the requestor to the record available on the public agency's website or another public agency's website.
rules.trigger: Requested record is available on a public agency website and request is completed by direction to it
rules.source_language: No fee shall be charged if the request is completed by directing the requestor to the requested government record that is available on the public agency's website or the website of another public agency.
rules.notes: If requestor still cannot find the record and requests a physical copy, a capped fee applies (NJ-M11).

rules.atomic_rule: No fee shall be charged to a victim of a crime for a copy of a record to which the crime victim is entitled to access.
rules.trigger: Requestor is a crime victim entitled to the record under C.47:1A-1.1
rules.source_language: No fee shall be charged to a victim of a crime for a copy or copies of a record to which the crime victim is entitled to access, as provided in section 1 of P.L.1995, c.23 (C.47:1A-1.1).

rules.legal_concept: Special service charge for extraordinary printed-record requests
rules.atomic_rule: Where a printed record cannot be reproduced by ordinary copying equipment or involves an extraordinary expenditure of time and effort, the agency may charge, in addition to actual duplication cost, a reasonable special service charge based on the actual direct cost of providing the copies.
rules.trigger: Nature, format, collation or volume of a printed record makes it unreproducible by ordinary equipment or requires extraordinary time/effort
rules.source_language: Whenever the nature, format, manner of collation, or volume of a government record embodied in the form of printed matter to be inspected, examined, or copied pursuant to this section is such that the record cannot be reproduced by ordinary document copying equipment in ordinary business size or involves an extraordinary expenditure of time and effort to accommodate the request, the public agency may charge, in addition to the actual cost of duplicating the record, a special service charge that shall be based upon the actual direct cost of providing the copy or copies, and such special service charge shall be reasonable.
rules.notes: Amount is bounded by a 'reasonable / actual direct cost' standard, not a number.

rules.atomic_rule: The custodian shall provide the requestor with an explanation for, and an itemized list of, the fees or charges.
rules.trigger: Fees or charges (including special service charges) are to be assessed
rules.source_language: The custodian shall provide the requestor with an explanation for and an itemized list of the fees or charges.
rules.notes: Required document/notice generated during request handling.

rules.atomic_rule: The requestor shall have the opportunity to review and object to any fee or charge before it is incurred.
rules.trigger: A fee or charge is proposed
rules.source_language: The requestor shall have the opportunity to review and object to any fee or charge prior to it being incurred.
rules.notes: A required state/step: pre-charge review-and-object gate before charges are incurred.

rules.atomic_rule: If the agency converts a record to a requested medium/format, it may charge, in addition to actual duplication cost, a reasonable special service fee based on the cost of extensive IT use or the labor cost of personnel providing the service.
rules.trigger: Agency converts a record to a medium/format it does not maintain
rules.source_language: If the public agency converts the record to the medium or format requested, the agency may charge, in addition to the actual cost of duplication, a special service fee that shall be reasonable and shall be based on the cost for any extensive use of information technology, or for the labor cost of personnel providing the service, that is actually incurred by the agency or attributable to the agency for the programming, clerical, and supervisory assistance required, or both.

rules.atomic_rule: Where a requestor directed to a website record still cannot find it and requests a physical copy, the custodian shall provide a physical copy for a fee not exceeding two times the cost of production of the document.
rules.trigger: Requestor directed to website record cannot locate it after custodian assistance and requests a physical copy
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 2x cost of production
rules.source_language: If the requestor is still unable to locate the record and requests a physical copy, the custodian shall provide the requestor with a physical copy of the record for a fee not exceeding two times the cost of the production of the document.
rules.notes: Clock Spec cell used here to carry the fee ceiling (2x), not a time value.

rules.atomic_rule: If a commercial requestor wants the record within seven business days (rather than the 14-day commercial window), the custodian may charge a special service fee not exceeding two times the cost of production of the record.
rules.trigger: Commercial-purpose requestor elects expedited (7 business-day) delivery
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 2x cost of production
rules.source_language: If a commercial requestor would like to receive the record within seven business days, as established in this subsection, the custodian shall provide the requestor with a copy of the record and may charge a special service fee not exceeding two times the cost of the production of the record.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'commercial purpose' governing fee basis and response time
rules.atomic_rule: A request has a 'commercial purpose' where any part of the record is used, directly or indirectly, for sale, resale, solicitation, rent, or lease of a service, or any use by which the user expects a profit through commission, salary, or fee; this classification triggers the 14-business-day response window and special expedite fees.
rules.trigger: Requestor's certified use of the record
rules.source_language: "Commercial purpose" means the direct or indirect use of any part of a government record for sale, resale, solicitation, rent, or lease of a service or any use by which the user expects a profit either through commission, salary, or fee.
rules.notes: Definition the software branches on (fee basis + response-time fork). Excludes use by news media (and other listed exclusions not reproduced here). Requestor must certify commercial purpose for the request to be fulfilled; intentional failure to certify carries a penalty (NJ-M55).

rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may require prepayment of fees or a deposit, and the request form must state whether prepayment of fees or a deposit is required.
rules.trigger: Fees or a deposit are required to process the request
rules.source_language: The form shall also include the following: ... (2) a statement as to whether prepayment of fees or a deposit is required; ... The custodian may require a deposit against costs for reproducing documents sought through a request whenever the custodian anticipates that the information thus requested will cost in excess of $5 to reproduce.
rules.notes: Split from the $5 deposit threshold (NJ-M15).

rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may require a deposit against costs whenever the custodian anticipates the requested reproduction will cost in excess of $5.
rules.trigger: Custodian anticipates reproduction cost exceeding $5
rules.source_language: The custodian may require a deposit against costs for reproducing documents sought through a request whenever the custodian anticipates that the information thus requested will cost in excess of $5 to reproduce.
rules.notes: $5 is a fixed statutory trigger threshold for the deposit permission.

rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may deny a request that is incomplete (missing information required on the adopted form), including a letter/email request that omits all required information.
rules.trigger: Request omits information required on the adopted request form
rules.source_language: A request shall be submitted by a requestor in the form adopted by the custodian and the custodian may deny a request that is incomplete, except that a requestor indicating the request is being submitted anonymously shall not be grounds for denial. ... If a letter or an email from a requestor does not include all of the information required on the adopted form, the custodian may deny the record request.

rules.atomic_rule: A request submitted anonymously shall not be considered incomplete and anonymity is not grounds for denial.
rules.trigger: Requestor indicates the request is submitted anonymously
rules.source_language: A request may be submitted anonymously provided, however, that anonymous requestors shall not be permitted to institute proceedings pursuant to section 7 of P.L.2001, c.404 (C.47:1A-6). A request that is submitted anonymously shall not be considered incomplete.
rules.notes: Anonymity permitted for the request but bars later appeal/proceedings (see NJ-M31).

rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may deny repeated requests submitted to multiple custodians in the same public agency for the same record while an identical or substantially similar request is pending in that agency.
rules.trigger: Repeated submissions to multiple custodians in one agency for the same record while a like request is pending
rules.source_language: Submission of repeated requests to multiple custodians in the same public agency for the same record, while an identical or substantially similar request is pending in the agency, shall permit the custodian to deny the request.

rules.atomic_rule: If unable to comply with a request, the custodian shall indicate the specific basis on the request form, promptly return it to the requestor, and sign, date, and provide the requestor a copy.
rules.trigger: Custodian is unable to comply with (denies) a request for access
rules.source_language: If the custodian is unable to comply with a request for access, the custodian shall indicate the specific basis therefor on the request form and promptly return it to the requestor. The custodian shall sign and date the form and provide the requestor with a copy thereof.
rules.notes: Required written-denial notice with specific basis; 'promptly' is an undefined-soft timing standard on the return.

rules.atomic_rule: If a request would substantially disrupt agency operations, the custodian may deny access after informing the requestor of the potential disruption and attempting to reach a reasonable solution accommodating both parties' interests.
rules.trigger: Request would substantially disrupt agency operations
rules.source_language: If a request for access to a government record would substantially disrupt agency operations, the custodian may deny access to the record after informing the requestor of the potential disruption to agency operations and attempting to reach a reasonable solution with the requestor that accommodates the interests of the requestor and the agency.
rules.notes: Denial conditioned on a mandatory notice-and-negotiation step.

rules.atomic_rule: A party to a legal proceeding may not request a record that is the subject of a court order (including a pending discovery request); the custodian shall not be required to complete such a request, and the requestor must certify whether the record is sought in connection with a legal proceeding.
rules.trigger: Requestor is a party to a legal proceeding and the record is subject to a court order or pending discovery request
rules.source_language: A party to a legal proceeding may not request a government record if the record sought is the subject of a court order, including a pending discovery request, and a custodian shall not be required to complete such a request. The requestor shall be required to certify whether the government record is being sought in connection with a legal proceeding and identify the proceeding for the request to be fulfilled.
rules.notes: Carve-out: does not bar requests by a labor organization or CBA-signatory contractor for enforcement-related information not sought in furtherance of litigation discovery (see NJ-M61).

rules.atomic_rule: The custodian is not required to complete a request (e.g., for mail, email, texts, correspondence, social media) that does not identify a specific job title/accounts, a specific subject matter, and a reasonable time period, or that would require research and creation of new records.
rules.trigger: Request lacks specific job title/accounts, subject matter, or reasonable time period, or would require research/creation of new records
rules.source_language: A custodian shall not be required to complete a request, including for, but not limited to, mail, email, text messages, correspondence, or social media postings and messages, if the request does not identify a specific job title or accounts to be searched, a specific subject matter, and is not confined to a reasonable time period, or if the custodian determines that the request would require research and the collection of information from the contents of government records and the creation of new government records setting forth that research and information.

rules.atomic_rule: The custodian is not required to complete an identical request from the same requestor if the information has not changed (periodic requests for regularly-updated records remain permitted).
rules.trigger: Same requestor submits an identical request and the information has not changed
rules.source_language: The custodian shall not be required to complete an identical request for access to a government record from the same requestor if the information has not changed. Nothing in this section shall prevent a requestor from filing periodic requests regarding regularly updated public records, including, but not limited to, certified payrolls, permits, and licensing applications.

rules.legal_concept: Constructive (deemed) denial on custodian's failure to respond
rules.atomic_rule: If the custodian fails to respond within seven business days (or 14 business days for commercial-purpose/redaction-review requests) after receiving a request, the failure to respond is deemed a denial of the request.
rules.trigger: Custodian does not respond within the applicable 7- or 14-business-day period
rules.clock_spec: 7 business-days from request receipt (14 business-days if commercial purpose or C.47:1B compliance review); +7 business-days for a fire district with one or fewer full-time custodial employees
rules.source_language: In the event a custodian fails to respond within seven business days or 14 business days, as appropriate, after receiving a request, the failure to respond shall be deemed a denial of the request, unless the requestor has elected not to accurately identify themselves or to provide an accurate address, email address, or telephone number.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: constructive-denial trigger (clock with terminal event). The underlying 7/14-day response deadline itself is a Deadlines-category rule (sibling scope). During a declared state of emergency the deadlines do not apply.

rules.atomic_rule: Where the requestor elected not to accurately identify themselves or provide an accurate address/email/phone, the deemed-denial does not run and the custodian need not respond until the requestor contacts the custodian seeking a response.
rules.trigger: Requestor did not accurately identify themselves or provide accurate contact information
rules.clock_spec: response obligation suspended until requestor contacts custodian seeking a response
rules.source_language: If the requestor has elected not to accurately identify themselves or to provide an accurate address, email address, or telephone number, the custodian shall not be required to respond until the requestor contacts the custodian seeking a response to the original request.

rules.atomic_rule: If the record is in storage or archived, the requestor must be so advised within 7/14 business days and told when the record can be made available, which shall be no more than 21 business days from that advisory; if not made available by then, access is deemed denied.
rules.trigger: Requested record is in storage or archived
rules.clock_spec: advise within 7/14 business-days of receipt; availability no more than 21 business-days from the advisory; non-availability = deemed denied
rules.source_language: If the government record is in storage or archived, the requestor shall be so advised within seven or 14 business days, as appropriate, after the custodian receives the request. The requestor shall be advised by the custodian when the record can be made available, which shall be no more than 21 business days from the date the requestor is so advised. If the record is not made available by that time, access shall be deemed denied.
rules.notes: Storage/archived processing branch with its own terminal deemed-denial.

material_negatives.note: OPRA contains no mandatory clarification/deficiency-cure step or nonresponse-abandonment clock. When a request is incomplete, over-broad, or requires more than reasonable effort to clarify, the statute PERMITS denial (N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(f), NJ-A14/NJ-A15) rather than requiring the custodian to seek clarification and toll a clock. The only affirmative negotiation duty is the 'reasonable solution' attempt for requests that would substantially disrupt operations (NJ-A24). No abandonment deadline for an unclarified request was found.

OPRA has no separate acknowledgment-of-receipt step distinct from the substantive grant/deny response deadline. There is no statutory duty to send an interim acknowledgment; the first required communication is the grant/deny (or storage/archive advisory) within the response window (Deadlines sibling).

No requestor identity-verification or proof-of-identity requirement at intake. Requests may be anonymous (NJ-A04); the only consequence of not accurately identifying is loss of standing to sue and suspension of the response duty until the requestor makes contact (NJ-A05). No government-ID or notarization requirement found.

No fixed numeric search-burden threshold (e.g., a maximum number of search hours or a defined 'unduly burdensome' cap) exists. Burden limits are expressed as soft standards - 'substantially disrupt agency operations' (NJ-A24) and 'reasonable time period' for correspondence (NJ-A26) - with no day/hour count.

The confidentiality/exemption catalogue within N.J.S.A. 47:1A-1.1 (deliberative/ACD material, criminal investigatory records, victims' records, legislative constituent records, etc.), the enacted 'personal identifying information' redaction definition, and the judicial-officer home-address protection (N.J.S.A. 47:1B-1/-2) are Denials/Redaction scope and are deferred to the sibling agent; only the core government-record and public-agency coverage definitions are captured here.

OPRA has no separate receipt-acknowledgment step or deadline distinct from the substantive grant/deny response. The seven-business-day (or 14) response under 47:1A-5(i)(1) is the sole required response; there is no statutory 'we received your request' acknowledgment clock.

Within my scope areas, no statutory clock or mandatory back-and-forth to cure a deficient request appears. The custodian may deny incomplete/overbroad requests (47:1A-5(f),(g)) but no fixed cure window is prescribed. Intake/clarification is primarily a sibling area; noted here only to record the absence of a cure deadline.

A broad mandatory redaction of email, medical, financial, birthdate, or general 'personal information' was proposed in earlier reprints of S2930 but was DELETED before enactment. Enacted 47:1A-5(a) mandates redaction only of SSN, credit card number, personal telephone number, driver license number, and covered-officer home addresses. Do not treat the broad PII list as an operative redaction rule.

A provision requiring denial of all requests by or for data brokers (and a data-broker registration/fee scheme) was in earlier reprints but was DELETED and NOT enacted. No data-broker processing rule exists in current OPRA.

P.L.2024, c.16, s.10 bars a non-subject who obtained a photo/video via OPRA from disclosing indecent/graphic images of intimate parts without consent (disorderly persons offense). Excluded from rules: it is a downstream use-restriction with a criminal penalty, not something the platform does differently while processing a request.

Beyond 'provide in the medium/format maintained' and 'convert if available without substantial IT manipulation' (47:1A-5(d)), OPRA states no ranked hierarchy of production formats the platform must apply.

OPRA creates no general fee waiver for indigent, non-profit, or public-interest requestors. The only statutory zero-fee cases are crime victims (NJ-M05) and records available on a public agency website (NJ-M04). Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

OPRA attaches fees only to copies/duplication; no fee is prescribed for mere inspection or examination during business hours (47:1A-5(a),(b)). No affirmative 'inspection is free' clause exists, so this is stated cautiously as an absence rather than an express rule.

No statutory provision imposes interest, late fees, or penalties on a requestor for unpaid or delayed OPRA fee payments; the only leverage is prepayment/deposit (NJ-M14, NJ-M15) and the 14-business-day record-retrieval window.

No numeric cap on cumulative special service charges (47:1A-5(c),(d)); charges are bounded only by 'reasonable / actual direct cost' with a rebuttable presumption of reasonableness (NJ-M06, NJ-M09, NJ-M10).
No statutory deadline governs completion of GRC mediation; mediation time is expressly excluded from the 90-day adjudication clock (NJ-M47), leaving mediation duration open-ended.
No bond or filing fee is required to appeal to the GRC (the statute affirmatively bars GRC fees, NJ-M45). No provision addresses a bond for Superior Court OPRA actions within OPRA itself.

structural_branches.description: NJ-A06: custodian identity forks by entity type - municipal clerk for a municipality vs. a formally designated officer for any other public agency - determining who must receive and answer the request.

NJ-A30/NJ-A31: a request landing on a non-custodian must be forwarded or redirected to the custodian, and is not deemed submitted (clock does not start) until the custodian receives it - a routing stage the engine must model before intake completes.

NJ-A32/NJ-A33: for records held only via remote access or courtesy copy from another (non-judicial-branch) agency, the request branches to a referral path - custodian directs the requestor to the originating agency within seven business days and the request is deemed completed.

NJ-A34: for records readily available in complete form on the agency website, the request branches to a self-service path - custodian may require retrieval from the website while providing locating directions - with downstream fulfillment/assist/physical-copy sub-branches (deferred to Deadlines/Fees).

NJ-A22/NJ-A23: requests branch on a mandatory legal-proceeding certification; a party to a proceeding is barred from OPRA for records subject to a court order/pending discovery, with a labor-organization/CBA-contractor carve-out - a gate the engine must evaluate before processing.
NJ-A24: requests that would substantially disrupt operations branch into a mandatory notify-and-negotiate-a-reasonable-solution stage before any denial is permitted.
Storage/archived records follow a distinct path: advise within 7/14 business days (NJ-T11), make available within 21 business days of advisement (NJ-T12), else deemed denied (NJ-T13).

Website-redirect fulfillment fork: redirect with directions (NJ-T31) -> deemed fulfilled after 7 business days or completeness carve-back (NJ-T32) -> good-faith assistance within 7 business days (NJ-T33) -> physical copy within 7 business days (NJ-T34).
Not-in-possession/courtesy-copy fork: custodian may decline and must redirect the requestor within 7 business days to the originating (non-judicial-branch) agency, completing the request (NJ-T16).
Declared-emergency fork suspending the (i)(1) and subsection-e deadlines, replaced by a reasonable-effort soft standard (NJ-T15).
Election-agency-specific processing: limited redaction (NJ-T41), 2-business-day immediate access (NJ-T42), election-eve noon deadlines (NJ-T43), website posting satisfies deadlines (NJ-T44).
Court protective-order path that can toll, limit, or eliminate the agency's duty to respond to a vexatious requestor (NJ-T46).
Daniel's Law path: OIP-approved covered-person home-address redaction (NJ-T36) with a 30-day agency compliance deadline (NJ-T38) and a triggered 14-business-day review window (NJ-T03).
Commercial requestor may elect 7-business-day delivery instead of the default 14, for up to 2x production cost (NJ-T06).

A denied requestor must elect one of two mutually exclusive review paths within 45 days: an action in Superior Court before a designated judge, OR a complaint to the Government Records Council ('in lieu of' filing in Superior Court). NJ-M28 / NJ-M29.

Certification of 'commercial purpose' forks the request into a distinct track: a 14-business-day response window (vs 7), an optional 2x expedite fee, and miscertification-penalty exposure. NJ-M13 / NJ-M12 / NJ-M55.

Custodian silence past the 7/14-business-day window converts the request to a constructive denial (terminal state opening the 45-day appeal clock), unless the requestor withheld accurate identity/contact info, which pauses the obligation. NJ-M25 / NJ-M26.
A record in storage/archive routes to a separate timeline: advise within 7/14 days, produce within no more than 21 business days, else deemed denied. NJ-M27.

GRC processing is a staged pipeline: mediation offer -> (on decline/failure) investigation and frivolous/jurisdiction screen -> agency response -> APA contested-case hearing if accessibility cannot be decided on the papers -> majority-vote decision. NJ-M39 through NJ-M44.

An agency may open a separate Superior Court track (verified complaint, clear-and-convincing standard) to obtain a protective order that limits or eliminates its future duty to respond to a requestor found to intend substantial interruption of government function, subject to a labor-organization carve-out. NJ-M58 / NJ-M59 / NJ-M60 / NJ-M61.
A request that would substantially disrupt agency operations routes to a mandatory notice-and-negotiation step before the custodian may deny access. NJ-M21.

rules.legal_concept: Public right of access (Freedom of Information Law)
rules.atomic_rule: Any member of the public may request access to the records of government; access is a public right exercisable by any person.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional public right)
rules.source_language: The legislature therefore declares that government is the public's business and that the public, individually and collectively and represented by a free press, should have access to the records of government in accordance with the provisions of this article.
rules.notes: Affirmative right; § 89(3)(a) runs the response duty to 'the person requesting it.' Shared universal-access key.

rules.legal_concept: No showing of need, good faith or purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A requester need not state a reason, need, good faith, or legitimate purpose to obtain accessible records.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: New York's Court of Appeals and the Committee on Open Government hold that FOIL does not require the party requesting records to make any showing of need, good faith or legitimate purpose as a condition to access.
rules.source_authority: Matter of M. Farbman & Sons v. N.Y.C. Health & Hosps. Corp., 62 N.Y.2d 75 (1984); Committee on Open Government advisory opinions
rules.notes: Emitted as a rule per universal-access symmetry (never a material negative). Paraphrase: statutory text imposes no purpose condition; principle stated in case law and COOG opinions. Verify exact holding language.

rules.legal_concept: Equal availability irrespective of requester status/residency
rules.atomic_rule: Accessible records are equally available to any person regardless of residency, citizenship, or status; an agency may not condition access on proof of residency or identity.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: When records are accessible under the Freedom of Information Law, they must be made equally available to any person, irrespective of the status, residence, interest or intended use of the person making the request.
rules.source_authority: Committee on Open Government advisory opinions (construing N.Y. Pub. Off. Law art. 6)
rules.notes: Emitted as rule per universal-access symmetry. No statutory residency condition exists; COOG consistently so construes. Verify verbatim opinion text.

rules.legal_concept: Written request triggers statutory duty
rules.atomic_rule: The agency's five-business-day response duty is triggered by receipt of a written request for a record.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a written request
rules.source_language: Each entity subject to the provisions of this article, within five business days of the receipt of a written request for a record reasonably described, shall make such record available to the person requesting it, deny such request in writing or furnish a written acknowledgement of the receipt of such request...
rules.notes: Written form is the trigger; § 89(3)(b) additionally requires accepting email requests where reasonable means exist.

rules.legal_concept: Record must be reasonably described
rules.atomic_rule: The response duty attaches only where the requested record is reasonably described.
rules.trigger: Written request received
rules.source_language: ...within five business days of the receipt of a written request for a record reasonably described, shall make such record available to the person requesting it...
rules.notes: 'Reasonably described' is the statutory adequacy standard; FOIL provides no explicit clarification-cure clock (see material negatives).

rules.legal_concept: Acceptance of and response to email requests
rules.atomic_rule: An entity with reasonable means available shall accept requests submitted by email and respond by email, unless the request seeks a response in another form.
rules.trigger: Email request received; entity has reasonable means
rules.source_language: All entities shall, provided such entity has reasonable means available, accept requests for records submitted in the form of electronic mail and shall respond to such requests by electronic mail, using forms, to the extent practicable, consistent with the form or forms developed by the committee on open government pursuant to subdivision one of this section and provided that the written requests do not seek a response in some other form.
rules.notes: Applies to all entities (municipal included). § 89(3)(c) online-submission duty is limited to STATE agencies.

rules.legal_concept: Standard request form on the internet
rules.atomic_rule: The Committee on Open Government develops a request form, made available on the internet, that the public may use to request a record.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: The committee shall: ... v. develop a form, which shall be made available on the internet, that may be used by the public to request a record;
rules.notes: Form use is permissive for the requester; agencies respond 'using forms, to the extent practicable.'

rules.legal_concept: Five-business-day initial response
rules.atomic_rule: Within five business days of receipt of a written request, the agency shall grant access, deny the request in writing, or furnish a written acknowledgement of receipt with an approximate date.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a written request reasonably describing a record
rules.clock_spec: 5 business-days from receipt of written request
rules.source_language: Each entity subject to the provisions of this article, within five business days of the receipt of a written request for a record reasonably described, shall make such record available to the person requesting it, deny such request in writing or furnish a written acknowledgement of the receipt of such request and a statement of the approximate date, which shall be reasonable under the circumstances of the request, when such request will be granted or denied...
rules.notes: Three-way branch (grant / written denial / acknowledgement). 5 business days is fixed by statute; municipalities cannot lengthen it.

rules.legal_concept: Approximate-date standard in acknowledgement
rules.atomic_rule: A written acknowledgement must state an approximate date, reasonable under the circumstances, when the request will be granted or denied.
rules.trigger: Agency issues an acknowledgement instead of granting/denying within 5 business days
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "reasonable under the circumstances" from date of acknowledgement
rules.source_language: ...furnish a written acknowledgement of the receipt of such request and a statement of the approximate date, which shall be reasonable under the circumstances of the request, when such request will be granted or denied...
rules.notes: Soft standard — do not encode a fixed day count; the engine applies a reasonableness standard.

rules.legal_concept: Twenty-business-day disclosure checkpoint
rules.atomic_rule: If the agency grants a request but circumstances prevent disclosure within twenty business days from the acknowledgement, it must act (state reasons and a date certain).
rules.trigger: Request granted in whole or part; disclosure not achievable within 20 business days of acknowledgement
rules.clock_spec: 20 business-days from date of acknowledgement
rules.source_language: If an agency determines to grant a request in whole or in part, and if circumstances prevent disclosure to the person requesting the record or records within twenty business days from the date of the acknowledgement of the receipt of the request, the agency shall state, in writing, both the reason for the inability to grant the request within twenty business days and a date certain within a reasonable period, depending on the circumstances, when the request will be granted in whole or in part.
rules.notes: 20 business days is a checkpoint, not a hard production deadline; failing it triggers the delay-notice duty (NY-0012), not automatic denial.

rules.legal_concept: Delay notice with reason and date certain
rules.atomic_rule: When disclosure cannot occur within twenty business days, the agency must state in writing both the reason for the inability and a date certain, within a reasonable period, when the request will be granted.
rules.trigger: Disclosure not achievable within 20 business days of acknowledgement
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "date certain within a reasonable period" from the delay notice
rules.source_language: ...the agency shall state, in writing, both the reason for the inability to grant the request within twenty business days and a date certain within a reasonable period, depending on the circumstances, when the request will be granted in whole or in part.
rules.notes: The 'date certain' is agency-set and reasonableness-bounded (soft), so Config Home is structural.

rules.legal_concept: Constructive denial for non-conformance
rules.atomic_rule: An agency's failure to conform to the subdivision-three response provisions constitutes a denial of the request.
rules.trigger: Agency fails to meet the § 89(3) response obligations
rules.clock_spec: on lapse of the § 89(3) response obligations
rules.source_language: Failure by an agency to conform to the provisions of subdivision three of this section shall constitute a denial.
rules.notes: Deemed-denial trigger (keeper sliver): silence/non-conformance = denial, which opens the administrative appeal right.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to create records
rules.atomic_rule: An entity is not required to prepare any record it does not possess or maintain (except the statutorily specified subject-matter/vote records).
rules.trigger: Request seeks a record not possessed or maintained
rules.source_language: Nothing in this article shall be construed to require any entity to prepare any record not possessed or maintained by such entity except the records specified in subdivision three of section eighty-seven and subdivision three of section eighty-eight of this article.
rules.notes: Distinguish from electronic retrieval/extraction, which IS required (NY-0015).

rules.legal_concept: Duty to retrieve/extract from computer storage
rules.atomic_rule: When an agency can retrieve or extract a record or data from a computer storage system with reasonable effort, it shall do so.
rules.trigger: Requested record/data is in a computer storage system and retrievable with reasonable effort
rules.source_language: When an agency has the ability to retrieve or extract a record or data maintained in a computer storage system with reasonable effort, it shall be required to do so.
rules.notes: 'Reasonable effort' is a soft standard on the duty's scope.

rules.legal_concept: Electronic retrieval preferred when it takes less time
rules.atomic_rule: Where electronic retrieval/extraction requires less employee time than manual retrieval or redaction from non-electronic records, the agency shall retrieve or extract the record electronically.
rules.trigger: Electronic retrieval requires less employee time than manual
rules.source_language: When doing so requires less employee time than engaging in manual retrieval or redactions from non-electronic records, the agency shall be required to retrieve or extract such record or data electronically.
rules.notes: Affects fee (labor time) as well as method.

rules.legal_concept: Copy provided on payment/offer to pay; certification
rules.atomic_rule: Upon payment of, or offer to pay, the prescribed fee, the entity shall provide a copy of the record and, if requested, certify its correctness.
rules.trigger: Requester pays or offers to pay the prescribed fee
rules.source_language: Upon payment of, or offer to pay, the fee prescribed therefor, the entity shall provide a copy of such record and certify to the correctness of such copy if so requested, or as the case may be, shall certify that it does not have possession of such record or that such record cannot be found after diligent search.
rules.notes: An OFFER to pay suffices to trigger the duty — production is gated on payment/offer, not on completed prepayment of the full charge.

rules.legal_concept: Certification of non-possession after diligent search
rules.atomic_rule: Where applicable, the entity shall certify that it does not possess the record or that the record cannot be found after a diligent search.
rules.trigger: Record not in possession or not found after diligent search
rules.source_language: ...or as the case may be, shall certify that it does not have possession of such record or that such record cannot be found after diligent search.
rules.notes: Split from NY-0019 (same sentence): a distinct terminal outcome — certified no-record response.

rules.legal_concept: Records in the medium requested
rules.atomic_rule: An agency shall provide records in the medium requested if it can reasonably make the copy or have it made by engaging an outside professional service.
rules.trigger: Requester specifies a medium and the copy can reasonably be made
rules.source_language: An agency shall provide records on the medium requested by a person, if the agency can reasonably make such copy or have such copy made by engaging an outside professional service.
rules.notes: Applies to electronic/computer formats.

rules.legal_concept: Computer-format records not encrypted
rules.atomic_rule: Records provided in a computer format shall not be encrypted.
rules.trigger: Records provided in computer format
rules.source_language: Records provided in a computer format shall not be encrypted.
rules.notes: Constrains the delivery format of electronic production.

rules.legal_concept: Paper copy fee ceiling (25 cents/page)
rules.atomic_rule: Fees for paper copies shall not exceed 25 cents per photocopy not exceeding 9 by 14 inches, unless a different fee is prescribed by statute.
rules.trigger: Paper photocopy up to 9x14 inches provided
rules.source_language: except when a different fee is otherwise prescribed by statute: (1) the fees for paper copies of records shall not exceed twenty-five cents per photocopy not in excess of nine inches by fourteen inches, or the actual cost of reproducing any other record in accordance with the provisions of paragraph (c) of this subdivision.
rules.notes: Ceiling, not a fixed rate: the city sets its actual per-page fee up to $0.25. A statute-specified different fee overrides this ceiling.

rules.legal_concept: Actual cost of reproduction for other records
rules.atomic_rule: For records other than 9x14 paper photocopies, the fee shall not exceed the actual cost of reproduction determined under § 87(1)(c).
rules.trigger: Reproduction of a record that is not a 9x14 paper photocopy
rules.source_language: ...or the actual cost of reproducing any other record in accordance with the provisions of paragraph (c) of this subdivision.
rules.notes: 'Actual cost' is capped and its composition is fixed by § 87(1)(c) (NY-0027 through NY-0030).

rules.legal_concept: No fee for recently prepared identical electronic record
rules.atomic_rule: Where an identical record was prepared for a prior request within the past six months and an electronic copy is available, the agency shall charge no fee except the actual cost of a storage device/media if provided.
rules.trigger: Identical record prepared within past 6 months and electronic copy available
rules.source_language: In the case where an identical record has been prepared for a previous request within the past 6 months and an electronic copy is available, an agency shall not charge a fee for the reproduction of such record, except for the actual cost of a storage device or media if one is provided to the requester in complying with such request.
rules.notes: Fee fixed at $0 (plus media cost); 6-month lookback is the trigger condition.

rules.legal_concept: Preparation labor billed at lowest-paid qualified employee's rate
