rules.atomic_rule: Actual reproduction cost may include only the hourly salary attributed to the lowest-paid agency employee who has the necessary skill to prepare the copy.
rules.trigger: Copy preparation requires employee labor (subject to the 2-hour threshold)
rules.source_language: In determining the actual cost of reproducing a record, an agency may include only: i. an amount equal to the hourly salary attributed to the lowest paid agency employee who has the necessary skill required to prepare a copy of the requested record;
rules.notes: Basis is fixed by statute (lowest-paid qualified employee); the city supplies the actual wage figure as the operative value.

rules.legal_concept: Two-hour preparation threshold for any labor fee
rules.atomic_rule: No preparation fee may be charged unless at least two hours of agency employee time is needed to prepare the copy.
rules.trigger: Copy preparation requires agency employee time
rules.source_language: ...no fee shall be charged unless at least two hours of agency employee time is needed to prepare a copy of the record requested.
rules.notes: Two-hour floor gates the labor fee entirely; fixed by statute.

rules.legal_concept: Search time and administrative costs excluded from fee
rules.atomic_rule: Preparing a copy shall not include search time or administrative costs; these may not be charged to the requester.
rules.trigger: Fee calculation for copy preparation
rules.source_language: ...preparing a copy shall not include search time or administrative costs, and no fee shall be charged unless at least two hours of agency employee time is needed to prepare a copy of the record requested.
rules.notes: Constrains the fee calculation — the recoverable labor is copy-preparation time only, not search/admin.

rules.legal_concept: Outside professional service cost only when IT equipment inadequate
rules.atomic_rule: The actual cost of engaging an outside professional service to prepare a copy may be included only when the agency's information technology equipment is inadequate to prepare the copy and the service is used.
rules.trigger: Agency IT equipment inadequate; outside service used to prepare copy
rules.source_language: iii. the actual cost to the agency of engaging an outside professional service to prepare a copy of a record, but only when an agency's information technology equipment is inadequate to prepare a copy, if such service is used to prepare the copy;
rules.notes: Branch condition on recovering outside-service cost; ties to the no-burden-refusal rule (NY-0018).

rules.legal_concept: Estimated cost notice
rules.atomic_rule: The requester shall be informed of the estimated cost of preparing the copy if more than two hours of employee time is needed or if an outside professional service would be retained.
rules.trigger: Preparation needs more than 2 hours of employee time, or an outside service is to be retained
rules.source_language: A person requesting a record shall be informed of the estimated cost of preparing a copy of the record if more than two hours of an agency employee's time is needed, or if an outside professional service would be retained to prepare a copy of the record.
rules.notes: Cost-estimate notice is a required communication before charging preparation fees.

rules.legal_concept: Deletion of identifying details
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may delete identifying details when it makes records available to prevent an unwarranted invasion of personal privacy.
rules.trigger: Record contains identifying details whose disclosure would invade privacy
rules.source_language: In the absence of such guidelines, an agency may delete identifying details when it makes records available.
rules.notes: Redaction to enable partial release rather than wholesale denial; privacy categories enumerated in § 89(2)(b).

rules.legal_concept: Segregation and retrieval for maximum access
rules.atomic_rule: Where electronic records mix accessible and withholdable items, the agency shall, whenever practicable and reasonable, design retrieval to permit segregation and retrieval of the accessible items to provide maximum public access.
rules.trigger: Electronically maintained records contain both available and withholdable items
rules.source_language: When records maintained electronically include items of information that would be available under this article, as well as items of information that may be withheld, an agency in designing its information retrieval methods, whenever practicable and reasonable, shall do so in a manner that permits the segregation and retrieval of available items in order to provide maximum public access.
rules.notes: Segregability principle — withholdable portions do not justify denying the whole record.

rules.legal_concept: Particularized and specific justification for denial
rules.atomic_rule: A denial of access is valid only when there is a particularized and specific justification for the denial.
rules.trigger: Agency denies access to a record or portion
rules.source_language: A denial of access shall not be based solely on the category or type of such record and shall be valid only when there is a particularized and specific justification for such denial.
rules.notes: Governs the content/validity of a denial notice.

rules.legal_concept: No denial based solely on record category
rules.atomic_rule: A denial of access shall not be based solely on the category or type of the record.
rules.trigger: Agency denies access
rules.source_language: A denial of access shall not be based solely on the category or type of such record and shall be valid only when there is a particularized and specific justification for such denial.
rules.notes: Split from NY-0034 (same sentence): a distinct prohibition on blanket category-based withholding.

rules.legal_concept: Thirty-day window to file administrative appeal
rules.atomic_rule: The requester must file the written administrative appeal within thirty days of the denial.
rules.trigger: Denial of access
rules.clock_spec: 30 days from denial (requester's filing window)
rules.source_language: ...any person denied access to a record may within thirty days appeal in writing such denial to the head, chief executive or governing body of the entity...
rules.notes: Statute says 'within thirty days' (day-type not specified as business days). Fixed statutory window.

material_negatives.note: No explicit statutory clarification/cure clock. FOIL's only intake-adequacy standard is that a record be 'reasonably described' (§ 89(3)(a)); there is no statutory deadline for a requester to narrow or clarify a request. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists (COOG guidance encourages agencies to assist).

No statutory abandonment/closure trigger for requester non-response (e.g., failure to pay or clarify). Statute conditions production on 'payment of, or offer to pay' (§ 89(3)(a)) but sets no time limit after which a request is deemed abandoned.

No statutory advance-deposit percentage or dollar threshold in Article 6. Production is gated on 'payment of, or offer to pay' the prescribed fee (§ 89(3)(a)); no formula (e.g., '50% deposit if over $X') is provided by statute.

No fixed numeric outer deadline for actual production. After the 5-business-day response and the 20-business-day checkpoint, the operative standard is a 'date certain within a reasonable period' (§ 89(3)(a)) — a soft standard, not a hard statewide cap.

There is no fixed statewide per-page fee. The 25 cents/page figure is a CEILING (§ 87(1)(b)(iii)); municipalities set their own per-page fee up to that cap, and no statutory floor exists. (Captured affirmatively as NY-0024.)

No statutory requirement or prohibition governing rolling/installment production of voluminous requests; the statute addresses timing via the acknowledgement/date-certain mechanism rather than mandated installments.

Article 6 uses 'business days' for the 5-, 20-, and 10-day windows but 'days' (unqualified) for the 30-day appeal-filing window (§ 89(4)(a)); the article does not itself define how business days are counted (e.g., holidays).

EXCLUDED — § 89(4)(c) attorney's fees and litigation costs ('may assess' / 'shall assess' where petitioner 'substantially prevailed' and agency 'had no reasonable basis'): a Remedy on the Remove list. The linked constructive-denial trigger it references is captured at NY-0013/NY-0040.
EXCLUDED — § 89(4)(d) and § 89(5)(d) appellate procedure (preference, 60-day abandonment, CPLR 5513 appeals): litigation procedure, not request-handling behavior.

EXCLUDED — § 89(4)(b) / § 89(5)(f) burden of proof in an Article 78 proceeding (agency must prove exemption): litigation burden; the operational duty to give particularized justification is captured at NY-0034.

EXCLUDED — § 87(3)(a)-(b) duty to maintain a final-vote record and an employee name/title/salary roster, and § 87(3)(c) annually-updated subject-matter list: general recordkeeping obligations (Remove list), not per-request processing.
EXCLUDED — § 89(8) criminal violation for willful concealment/destruction of a record: a penalty provision (Remove list).

EXCLUDED — § 89(7) non-disclosure of home addresses of officers/employees/retirees/applicants: an exemption (special record content), not a processing step; belongs to the exemption catalog rather than the workflow.

SCOPE FLAG (not excluded, but municipally inapplicable) — § 89(3)(c) online-submission duty and § 87(3)(c)/§ 87(4)(c) website-posting duties apply to 'state agency' only, so they do not bind ordinary municipalities. Municipal platforms should treat these as state-agency configuration.

structural_branches.description: Within 5 business days the agency takes ONE of three paths: (a) grant/make available, (b) written denial, or (c) written acknowledgement stating a reasonable approximate date. The acknowledgement path opens the 20-business-day checkpoint and the delay-notice/date-certain obligations (§ 89(3)(a)).

Mandatory internal FOIL appeal stage: initial determination -> written appeal to head/CEO/governing body within 30 days -> 10-business-day written appeal determination -> immediate forwarding of appeal+determination to the Committee on Open Government. Exhaustion is a prerequisite to Article 78 (§ 89(4)(a)-(b)).

Composed actual-cost fee engine for non-standard reproduction: labor at the lowest-paid qualified employee's hourly rate, only above a 2-hour preparation threshold; plus actual storage-device/media cost; plus outside-professional-service cost only when agency IT equipment is inadequate; excluding search time and administrative costs (§ 87(1)(c)).

STATE-AGENCY-ONLY pre-submission exception path (§ 89(5); 'agency' there = state department/board/office and gubernatorially-appointed public corporations — NOT ordinary municipalities): submitter requests exception at submission; info maintained apart until 15 days after entitlement finally determined; on a later request, agency notifies submitter, who has 10 business days to submit a written statement; agency issues a written determination within 7 business days; a denial may be appealed within 7 business days and is determined within 10 business days; Article 78 review must be commenced within 15 days. Flag: largely inapplicable to municipal requests.

Law-enforcement disciplinary records path (§ 86(6), § 89(2-b) mandatory and § 89(2-c) permissive redactions): before disclosure, a law-enforcement agency must redact enumerated items (officer medical history, home/personal contact info, SSNs, EAP/mental-health/substance-abuse use) and may redact technical-infraction records. Creates a record-type-specific redaction workflow and an employee-notification policy duty (§ 89 subd. relating to notification / § 87(6)).

rules.legal_concept: Right of any person to inspect and copy public records
rules.atomic_rule: Any person may inspect, examine, and obtain copies of public records held by a custodian; access is not limited to a class of requesters.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional)
rules.source_language: Every custodian of public records shall permit any record in the custodian's custody to be inspected and examined at reasonable times and under reasonable supervision by any person, and shall, as promptly as possible, furnish copies thereof upon payment of any fees as may be prescribed by law.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule with the shared eligibility key per symmetry rule. 'By any person' is the operative eligibility grant.

rules.legal_concept: No disclosure of purpose or motive required
rules.atomic_rule: A requester may not be required to disclose the purpose or motive for inspecting, examining, or copying public records.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional)
rules.source_language: No person requesting to inspect and examine public records, or to obtain copies thereof, shall be required to disclose the purpose or motive for the request.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule with the shared key, never a negative.

rules.legal_concept: No residency requirement to request records
rules.atomic_rule: There is no residency requirement to request public records; access runs to any person.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: Every custodian of public records shall permit any record in the custodian's custody to be inspected and examined at reasonable times and under reasonable supervision by any person...
rules.notes: Emitted as a rule with the shared key per universal-access symmetry. NC imposes no residency limit; the no-residency conclusion is inferred from the 'any person' grant (statute does not use the word 'residency'). Source Language is the verbatim any-person clause.

rules.legal_concept: Copies furnished 'as promptly as possible'
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian must furnish copies as promptly as possible upon payment of any lawful fees.
rules.trigger: Request for copies received
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "as promptly as possible" from request receipt
rules.source_language: ...and shall, as promptly as possible, furnish copies thereof upon payment of any fees as may be prescribed by law.
rules.notes: Soft deadline; Config Home structural per contract. NC sets no fixed numeric response/acknowledgment deadline (see material negative).

rules.legal_concept: Online availability satisfies copy duty
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may satisfy the access/copy duty by making records available online in a viewable, printable/savable format; if so maintained, it need not provide copies any other way.
rules.trigger: Agency maintains the record online in a viewable/printable/savable format
rules.source_language: A public agency or custodian may satisfy the requirements in subsection (a) of this section by making public records available online in a format that allows a person to view the public record and print or save the public record to obtain a copy. If the public agency or custodian maintains public records online in a format that allows a person to view and print or save the public records to obtain a copy, the public agency or custodian is not required to provide copies to these public records in any other way.
rules.notes: A processing branch: online-availability path can terminate the copy-production obligation.

rules.legal_concept: Political subdivision may not use NDA to restrict access
rules.atomic_rule: A political subdivision may not withhold or deny access on the basis of a nondisclosure agreement entered to restrict access to records subject to disclosure.
rules.trigger: Agency asserts an NDA as basis to restrict access
rules.source_language: No political subdivision of this State may enter into a nondisclosure agreement in order to restrict access to public records subject to disclosure under this Chapter. The contract by which a political subdivision of this State agrees not to disclose information deemed confidential under State law shall be a public record, unless the existence of the contract is also deemed confidential under State law.
rules.notes: Gates a denial basis: an NDA cannot be the ground for withholding disclosable records. Added by 2023-134/2023-138.

rules.legal_concept: No denial because confidential info is commingled
rules.atomic_rule: A request may not be denied on the ground that confidential information is commingled with the requested nonconfidential information; the agency must segregate.
rules.trigger: Requested nonconfidential info is commingled with confidential info
rules.source_language: No request to inspect, examine, or obtain copies of public records shall be denied on the grounds that confidential information is commingled with the requested nonconfidential information.
rules.notes: Segregability requirement; drives a redact-and-produce path rather than denial.

rules.legal_concept: Agency bears cost of separating confidential from nonconfidential
rules.atomic_rule: When separation of confidential from nonconfidential information is necessary to permit access, the public agency bears the cost of separation.
rules.trigger: Separation is necessary to permit inspection/copying
rules.source_language: If it is necessary to separate confidential from nonconfidential information in order to permit the inspection, examination, or copying of the public records, the public agency shall bear the cost of such separation.
rules.notes: Cost-bearer is fixed by state (agency); a city cannot shift separation cost to the requester.

rules.legal_concept: Withholding of specific business/industrial project records
rules.atomic_rule: Records relating to the proposed expansion or location of a specific business or industrial project may be withheld so long as inspection or copying would frustrate the purpose for which they were created.
rules.trigger: Record relates to proposed expansion/location of a specific business or industrial project and disclosure would frustrate its purpose
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding the provisions of subsections (a) and (b) of this section, public records relating to the proposed expansion or location of specific business or industrial projects may be withheld so long as their inspection, examination or copying would frustrate the purpose for which such public records were created; provided, however, that nothing herein shall be construed to permit the withholding of public records relating to general economic development policies or activities.
rules.notes: Creates a temporary withhold state that ends on announcement/final decision; general economic development records not covered.

rules.legal_concept: 25-business-day disclosure after project announcement
rules.atomic_rule: Once the withholding basis no longer applies, the agency must disclose the requested announced-project records (not otherwise confidential) as soon as practicable and within 25 business days.
rules.trigger: Withholding basis under § 132-6(d) no longer applies (project announced/committed or final decision not to proceed)
rules.clock_spec: 25 business-days from the point the withholding basis ceases (as soon as practicable)
rules.source_language: Once the provisions of this subsection no longer apply, the agency shall disclose as soon as practicable, and within 25 business days, public records requested for the announced project that are not otherwise made confidential by law.
rules.notes: One of the few hard numeric deadlines in NC's public-records law; state-fixed at 25 business days.

rules.legal_concept: 25-business-day disclosure for qualifying-site records
rules.atomic_rule: Once the qualifying-site withholding basis no longer applies, the agency must disclose the requested qualifying-site records (not otherwise confidential) as soon as practicable and within 25 business days.
rules.trigger: Qualifying site (megasite/selectsite) acquired, or evaluated and deemed unsuitable, so § 132-6(d1) withholding ceases
rules.clock_spec: 25 business-days from the point the withholding basis ceases (as soon as practicable)
rules.source_language: Once the provisions of this subsection no longer apply, the agency shall disclose as soon as practicable, and within 25 business days, public records requested for the qualifying site that are not otherwise made confidential by law.
rules.notes: Parallel to § 132-6(d) but for state-funded megasite/selectsite acquisition. Same 25-business-day parameter, different trigger.

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable restrictions to preserve fragile records
rules.atomic_rule: Inspection or copying of a record that could be damaged due to its age or condition may be made subject to reasonable restrictions intended to preserve the record.
rules.trigger: Record could be damaged during inspection/copying because of its age or condition
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding the provisions of subsections (a) and (a1) of this section, the inspection or copying of any public record which, because of its age or condition could be damaged during inspection or copying, may be made subject to reasonable restrictions intended to preserve the particular record.
rules.notes: 'Reasonable restrictions' is a soft standard; the city sets the specific handling restrictions under it.

rules.legal_concept: Requester may elect media/format of copies
rules.atomic_rule: A requester may elect to obtain copies in any and all media in which the agency is capable of providing them.
rules.trigger: Requester requests copies in a particular medium
rules.source_language: Persons requesting copies of public records may elect to obtain them in any and all media in which the public agency is capable of providing them.
rules.notes: Requester-driven format branch, bounded by agency capability.

rules.legal_concept: No denial because agency prefers another medium
rules.atomic_rule: A request for copies in a particular medium may not be denied on the ground that the custodian has made or prefers another medium.
rules.trigger: Requester requests a particular medium the agency is capable of providing
rules.source_language: No request for copies of public records in a particular medium shall be denied on the grounds that the custodian has made or prefers to make the public records available in another medium.
rules.notes: Blocks a denial action; paired with the format-election permission.

rules.legal_concept: Different fees for different media as prescribed by law
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may assess different fees for different media, as prescribed by law.
rules.trigger: Copies provided in a particular medium
rules.source_language: The public agency may assess different fees for different media as prescribed by law.
rules.notes: Per-medium fee value is set 'as prescribed by law'; still bounded by the actual-cost ceiling in § 132-6.2(b).

rules.legal_concept: Fees for certifying copies as provided by law
rules.atomic_rule: A requester may request certified or uncertified copies; fees for certifying copies are as provided by law.
rules.trigger: Requester requests certified copies
rules.source_language: Persons requesting copies of public records may request that the copies be certified or uncertified. The fees for certifying copies of public records shall be as provided by law.
rules.notes: Certification fee value fixed by other law; the actual-cost ceiling applies only to uncertified copies.

rules.legal_concept: Uncertified-copy fee may not exceed actual cost
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may not charge a fee for an uncertified copy of a public record that exceeds the actual cost to the agency of making the copy.
rules.trigger: Charging a fee for an uncertified copy
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost of making the copy
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law, no public agency shall charge a fee for an uncertified copy of a public record that exceeds the actual cost to the public agency of making the copy.
rules.notes: Ceiling constraint; the city fills the operative rate under the actual-cost cap. Same concept as a fixed-rate state, different basis.

rules.legal_concept: Special service charge for extensive IT/clerical use
rules.atomic_rule: Where a request requires extensive use of information technology resources or extensive clerical/supervisory assistance, the agency may charge a reasonable special service charge (based on actual cost) in addition to duplication cost.
rules.trigger: Request requires extensive use of IT resources or extensive clerical/supervisory assistance, or the requested medium causes greater IT-resource use than the agency established for that volume
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding the provisions of this subsection, if the request is such as to require extensive use of information technology resources or extensive clerical or supervisory assistance by personnel of the agency involved, or if producing the record in the medium requested results in a greater use of information technology resources than that established by the agency for reproduction of the volume of information requested, then the agency may charge, in addition to the actual cost of duplication, a special service charge, which shall be reasonable and shall be based on the actual cost incurred for such extensive use of information technology resources or the labor costs of the personnel providing the services, or for a greater use of information technology resources that is actually incurred by the agency or attributable to the agency.
rules.notes: Charge must be 'reasonable' (soft) and based on actual cost; 'extensive' is an undefined trigger threshold. City sets the operative charge under the reasonableness standard.

rules.legal_concept: Computer-database copy requests may be required in writing
rules.atomic_rule: For copies of computer databases, the agency may require the request to be made or submitted in writing.
rules.trigger: Request is for copies of a computer database
rules.source_language: Persons requesting copies of computer databases may be required to make or submit such requests in writing.
rules.notes: Writing may be required only for computer-database copies; no general written-request mandate for ordinary records (see material negative).

rules.legal_concept: Prompt response to computer-database requests
rules.atomic_rule: Custodians must respond to computer-database copy requests as promptly as possible, and if granted provide copies as soon as reasonably possible.
rules.trigger: Computer-database copy request received
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "as promptly as possible" to respond / "as soon as reasonably possible" to provide, from request receipt
rules.source_language: Custodians of public records shall respond to all such requests as promptly as possible. If the request is granted, the copies shall be provided as soon as reasonably possible.
rules.notes: Soft deadlines; Config Home structural. Applies specifically to computer-database requests.

rules.legal_concept: Database denial must include basis explanation
rules.atomic_rule: If a computer-database copy request is denied, the denial must be accompanied by an explanation of the basis for the denial.
rules.trigger: Computer-database copy request is denied
rules.source_language: If the request is denied, the denial shall be accompanied by an explanation of the basis for the denial.
rules.notes: Statutory duty to give a reason applies to computer-database denials; no general statutory written-denial mandate for all record types.

rules.legal_concept: Reduce database-denial explanation to writing on request
rules.atomic_rule: On request, the person denying a computer-database copy request must, as promptly as possible, reduce the explanation for the denial to writing.
rules.trigger: Requester asks that the denial explanation be put in writing
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "as promptly as possible" from the requester's ask
rules.source_language: If asked to do so, the person denying the request shall, as promptly as possible, reduce the explanation for the denial to writing.
rules.notes: Written explanation is triggered by the requester's ask; soft timing standard.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to respond outside usual business hours
rules.atomic_rule: An agency is not required to respond to copy requests outside of its usual business hours.
rules.trigger: Request would require response outside usual business hours
rules.source_language: Nothing in this section shall be construed to require a public agency to respond to requests for copies of public records outside of its usual business hours.
rules.notes: Bounds when the promptness clock runs (business hours only).

rules.legal_concept: No duty to create or compile a nonexistent record
rules.atomic_rule: An agency is not required to respond by creating or compiling a record that does not exist.
rules.trigger: Request would require creating/compiling a nonexistent record
rules.source_language: Nothing in this section shall be construed to require a public agency to respond to a request for a copy of a public record by creating or compiling a record that does not exist.
rules.notes: Classification gate: no-such-record path.

rules.legal_concept: Negotiated charge for voluntarily created records
rules.atomic_rule: If an agency voluntarily elects, as a service, to create or compile a record, it may negotiate a reasonable charge for the service with the requester.
rules.trigger: Agency voluntarily elects to create/compile a record as a service
rules.source_language: If a public agency, as a service to the requester, voluntarily elects to create or compile a record, it may negotiate a reasonable charge for the service with the requester.
rules.notes: 'Reasonable' negotiated charge; a soft-standard fee value the parties set.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to put a non-electronic record into electronic medium
rules.atomic_rule: An agency is not required to put into electronic medium a record that is not kept in electronic medium.
rules.trigger: Requested electronic format for a record not kept in electronic medium
rules.source_language: Nothing in this section shall be construed to require a public agency to put into electronic medium a record that is not kept in electronic medium.
rules.notes: Bounds the format-election right: election limited to media the agency is capable of and already keeps.

rules.legal_concept: Online database access satisfies § 132-6 duty
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may satisfy the § 132-6 database-access duty by making database records individually available online (viewable/printable/savable), but must still allow inspection of any such records it also maintains in a nondigital medium.
rules.trigger: Agency provides individual online access to computer-database records
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding G.S. 132-6.2(a), a public agency may satisfy the requirement under G.S. 132-6 to provide access to public records in computer databases by making public records in computer databases individually available online in a format that allows a person to view the public record and print or save the public record to obtain a copy. A public agency that provides access to public records under this subsection is not required to provide access to the public records in the computer database in any other way; provided, however, that a public agency that provides access to public records in computer databases shall also allow inspection of any of such public records that the public agency also maintains in a nondigital medium.
rules.notes: Database-specific online-satisfaction branch with a nondigital-inspection carve-out.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to create a computer database not otherwise created
rules.atomic_rule: An agency is not required to create a computer database it has not otherwise created or is not otherwise required to create.
rules.trigger: Request would require creating a new computer database
rules.source_language: Nothing in this section shall require a public agency to create a computer database that the public agency has not otherwise created or is not otherwise required to be created.
rules.notes: Database analogue of the no-duty-to-create rule.

material_negatives.note: NC sets no fixed numeric acknowledgment or response deadline for ordinary public-records requests. The only timing standard is the soft 'as promptly as possible' in § 132-6(a) (captured as rule NC-0005). Absence of a found numeric rule is not proof none exists.
No statutory clarification-and-narrowing clock or deemed-abandonment-for-nonresponse provision found in Chapter 132. NC statute does not create a clarification round-trip with a deadline.

No statutory deemed/constructive-denial trigger (e.g., 'silence for N days = denial') found in Chapter 132. Enforcement under § 132-9 is available upon a denial of access/copies but the statute does not define a silence-based constructive denial.

No administrative or Attorney-General appeal stage exists for public-records denials; the remedy is a Superior Court action under § 132-9 (after G.S. 7A-38.3E mediation). A fee-specific mediation path via the State CIO exists separately (NC-0022).

No statutory requirement that ordinary (non-computer-database) public-records requests be submitted in writing; writing may be required only for computer-database copies (§ 132-6.2(c), captured as NC-0023).

No general statutory deposit/prepayment or cost-estimate-before-work rule found in Chapter 132. § 132-6(a) conditions furnishing copies on 'payment of any fees as may be prescribed by law' but sets no deposit mechanism.
No explicit search or record-identification time standard beyond the general 'as promptly as possible' promptness requirement.

Chapter 132 defines 'custodian' and excludes agencies that merely store/safekeep or provide data processing for others (§ 132-6(a)), but states no explicit wrong-department routing/forwarding duty for a misdirected request.

structural_branches.description: Online-availability path (§ 132-6(a1)): if the agency maintains a record online in viewable/printable/savable form, the copy-production obligation can be satisfied without providing copies any other way.
Database-specific online-satisfaction path (§ 132-6.1(a1)) with a mandatory carve-out that nondigital-medium copies of the same records must still be open to inspection.

Economic-development withhold-then-disclose fork (§ 132-6(d)): specific business/industrial project records enter a temporary withhold state that terminates on announcement/final decision, triggering a 25-business-day disclosure clock (NC-0012).
Qualifying-site (megasite/selectsite) parallel fork (§ 132-6(d1)) with its own withhold state and 25-business-day disclosure clock (NC-0013).
Fee-dispute mediation path through the State Chief Information Officer (§ 132-6.2(b)) — a non-judicial review stage unique to fee unfairness/unreasonableness claims.
Mandatory pre-suit mediation under G.S. 7A-38.3E as a jurisdictional gate before a § 132-9 court action to compel disclosure can proceed.
Judicial enforcement stage (§ 132-9): Superior Court action to compel disclosure/copying, set for immediate hearing and given priority — NC has no administrative appeal alternative.

rules.atomic_rule: Any person may request public records; upon such a request all responsive public records shall be promptly prepared and made available for inspection at all reasonable times during regular business hours.
rules.trigger: A request for public records is made by any person.
rules.legal_concept: Public right of access — any person may inspect public records
rules.source_language: Upon request by any person and subject to division (B)(8) of this section, all public records responsive to the request shall be promptly prepared and made available for inspection to the requester at all reasonable times during regular business hours.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule per symmetry rule. 'Any person' establishes standing without qualification.

rules.atomic_rule: A public office may not condition availability of records on the requester disclosing the intended use of the record; requiring intended-use disclosure constitutes a denial.
rules.trigger: Office would condition access on disclosure of intended use.
rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.source_language: Unless specifically required or authorized by state or federal law or in accordance with division (B) of this section, no public office or person responsible for public records may limit or condition the availability of public records by requiring disclosure of the requester's identity or the intended use of the requested public record. Any requirement that the requester disclose the requester's identity or the intended use of the requested public record constitutes a denial of the request.
rules.notes: Same operative clause also supports OH-0003; split into two atomic rows for identity vs. purpose.

rules.atomic_rule: A public office may not condition availability of records on the requester disclosing the requester's identity; requiring identity disclosure constitutes a denial.
rules.trigger: Office would condition access on disclosure of requester identity.
rules.legal_concept: No identification required to request
rules.source_language: Unless specifically required or authorized by state or federal law or in accordance with division (B) of this section, no public office or person responsible for public records may limit or condition the availability of public records by requiring disclosure of the requester's identity or the intended use of the requested public record. Any requirement that the requester disclose the requester's identity or the intended use of the requested public record constitutes a denial of the request.

rules.atomic_rule: Access is available to any person with no residency limitation; the statute extends the right to 'any person' without an Ohio-residency qualifier.
rules.trigger: A non-resident requests public records.
rules.legal_concept: No residency requirement
rules.source_language: Upon request by any person and subject to division (B)(8) of this section, all public records responsive to the request shall be promptly prepared and made available for inspection to the requester at all reasonable times during regular business hours.
rules.notes: No-residency concept is derived from the unqualified 'any person' language (the verbatim clause quoted); the statute states no residency element. Emitted as a rule per universal-access symmetry rule rather than as a material negative.

rules.atomic_rule: A written request is not mandatory; a requester may make an oral request and the office must honor it.
rules.trigger: A requester submits an oral (non-written) request.
rules.legal_concept: Written request not required
rules.source_language: A public office or person responsible for public records may ask a requester to make the request in writing, may ask for the requester's identity, and may inquire about the intended use of the information requested, but may do so only after disclosing to the requester that a written request is not mandatory, that the requester may decline to reveal the requester's identity or the intended use, and when a written request or disclosure of the identity or intended use would benefit the requester by enhancing the ability of the public office or person responsible for public records to identify, locate, or deliver the public records sought by the requester.

rules.atomic_rule: A public office may ask for a written request, identity, or intended use only after first disclosing to the requester that these are not mandatory and may be declined.
rules.trigger: Office wishes to ask the requester for writing, identity, or intended use.
rules.legal_concept: Precondition disclosure before inquiring into identity/use
rules.source_language: A public office or person responsible for public records may ask a requester to make the request in writing, may ask for the requester's identity, and may inquire about the intended use of the information requested, but may do so only after disclosing to the requester that a written request is not mandatory, that the requester may decline to reveal the requester's identity or the intended use, and when a written request or disclosure of the identity or intended use would benefit the requester by enhancing the ability of the public office or person responsible for public records to identify, locate, or deliver the public records sought by the requester.
rules.notes: A required-notice step (structural), not a value. Engine must present the disclosure before any identity/purpose/writing inquiry.

rules.atomic_rule: Copies of requested public records shall be made available at cost and within a reasonable period of time.
rules.trigger: A requester asks for copies of public records.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "within a reasonable period of time" from request receipt
rules.legal_concept: Copies within a reasonable period of time
rules.source_language: Subject to division (B)(8) of this section, upon request by any person, a public office or person responsible for public records shall make copies of the requested public record available to the requester at cost and within a reasonable period of time.
rules.notes: Two distinct soft standards in (B)(1): 'promptly' for inspection (OH-0007) and 'reasonable period of time' for copies (this rule). Kept as separate atomic deadlines.

rules.atomic_rule: A public office must organize and maintain its public records so that they can be made available for inspection or copying.
rules.trigger: None stated (ongoing obligation that conditions retrievability of records for any request).
rules.legal_concept: Duty to organize and maintain records for access
rules.source_language: To facilitate broader access to public records, a public office or the person responsible for public records shall organize and maintain public records in a manner that they can be made available for inspection or copying in accordance with division (B) of this section.
rules.notes: Kept (not routine retention governance) because it directly conditions per-request retrievability and is the basis the office uses when informing a requester how records are maintained (OH-0012).

rules.atomic_rule: A public office may deny a request that is ambiguous or overly broad, or that does not reasonably identify what public records are being requested.
rules.trigger: A request is ambiguous, overly broad, or does not reasonably identify the records sought.
rules.legal_concept: Denial of ambiguous or overly broad requests
rules.source_language: If a requester makes an ambiguous or overly broad request or has difficulty in making a request for copies or inspection of public records under this section such that the public office or the person responsible for the requested public record cannot reasonably identify what public records are being requested, the public office or the person responsible for the requested public record may deny the request.
rules.notes: The permission to deny is conditioned on the mandatory revise-opportunity in OH-0012; split into two atomic rows.

rules.atomic_rule: If a request is denied as ambiguous or overly broad, the office shall provide the requester an opportunity to revise the request by informing the requester of the manner in which records are maintained and accessed in the ordinary course of duties.
rules.trigger: The office denies a request as ambiguous or overly broad.
rules.legal_concept: Opportunity to revise an ambiguous/overly broad request
rules.source_language: If the request is denied because it is ambiguous or overly broad, the public office or the person responsible for the requested public record shall provide the requester with an opportunity to revise the request by informing the requester of the manner in which records are maintained by the public office and accessed in the ordinary course of the public office's or person's duties.
rules.notes: No statutory clock attached to the revise opportunity — clock effect none.

rules.atomic_rule: If a request is ultimately denied in part or whole, the office shall provide the requester an explanation, including legal authority, setting forth why the request was denied.
rules.trigger: A request is ultimately denied in part or in whole.
rules.legal_concept: Denial explanation with legal authority
rules.source_language: If a request is ultimately denied, in part or in whole, the public office or the person responsible for the requested public record shall provide the requester with an explanation, including legal authority, setting forth why the request was denied.

rules.atomic_rule: If the initial request was provided in writing, the denial explanation shall also be provided to the requester in writing.
rules.trigger: A written request is denied in part or in whole.
rules.legal_concept: Written denial explanation for written requests
rules.source_language: If the initial request was provided in writing, the explanation also shall be provided to the requester in writing.
rules.notes: (B)(3) attaches no numeric deadline to the written explanation — clock effect none. The lack of a stated day count is a material negative.

rules.atomic_rule: If a public record contains information exempt from disclosure, the office shall make available all of the information within the record that is not exempt.
rules.trigger: A responsive record contains a mix of exempt and non-exempt information.
rules.legal_concept: Segregation of exempt from non-exempt information
rules.source_language: If a public record contains information that is exempt from the duty to permit public inspection or to copy the public record, the public office or the person responsible for the public record shall make available all of the information within the public record that is not exempt.
rules.notes: Some codifications place this text at (B)(9); verify exact subsection label. Content confirmed verbatim from opened source.

rules.atomic_rule: When making a record available, the office shall notify the requester of any redaction or make the redaction plainly visible.
rules.trigger: The office redacts exempt information before producing a record.
rules.legal_concept: Notice of redaction
rules.source_language: When making that public record available for public inspection or copying that public record, the public office or the person responsible for the public record shall notify the requester of any redaction or make the redaction plainly visible.

rules.atomic_rule: Copies of public records shall be made available 'at cost' — the office may not charge more than its actual cost of making the copy.
rules.trigger: A requester asks for copies of a public record.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost of the copy (no statutory per-page rate)
rules.legal_concept: Copies at cost
rules.source_language: Subject to division (B)(8) of this section, upon request by any person, a public office or person responsible for public records shall make copies of the requested public record available to the requester at cost and within a reasonable period of time.
rules.notes: Ohio sets no statutory per-page rate; 'at cost' is a ceiling of actual cost the city fills in. City must set the operative value under this ceiling.

rules.atomic_rule: A law enforcement agency or prosecuting attorney's office may charge the actual cost of preparing a video record, not to exceed $75 per hour of video produced and not to exceed $750 total.
rules.trigger: A request is for a video record held by a law enforcement agency or prosecuting attorney's office.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: $75.00 per hour of video produced; ceiling: $750.00 total
rules.legal_concept: Video record preparation charge
rules.source_language: a state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office may charge a requester the actual cost associated with preparing a video record for inspection or production, not to exceed seventy-five dollars per hour of video produced, nor seven hundred fifty dollars total.
rules.notes: Two bounds in one conjunctive rule (per-hour ceiling AND total cap). Kept in one row per grain rule. Record-specific to video from law-enforcement/prosecutor offices.

rules.atomic_rule: A public office may require the requester to pay in advance the cost of providing a copy, in accordance with the format the requester chose.
rules.trigger: A requester asks for a copy of a public record.
rules.legal_concept: Advance payment for copies
rules.source_language: If any person requests a copy of a public record in accordance with division (B) of this section, the public office or person responsible for the public record may require the requester to pay in advance the cost involved in providing the copy of the public record in accordance with the choice made by the requester under this division.
rules.notes: A payment gate/branch (require prepayment before producing), so structural. No statutory deposit percentage is set — that is a material negative.

rules.atomic_rule: The office shall permit the requester to choose to have the record duplicated on paper, on the same medium the office keeps it, or on any other medium the office determines it can reasonably be duplicated on, and shall provide the copy in accordance with that choice.
rules.trigger: A requester requests a copy and selects a delivery/duplication medium.
rules.legal_concept: Requester's choice of copy format/medium
rules.source_language: The public office or the person responsible for the public record shall permit the requester to choose to have the public record duplicated upon paper, upon the same medium upon which the public office or person responsible for the public record keeps it, or upon any other medium upon which the public office or person responsible for the public record determines that it reasonably can be duplicated as an integral part of the normal operations of the public office or person responsible for the public record. When the requester makes a choice under this division, the public office or person responsible for the public record shall provide a copy of it in accordance with the choice made by the requester.

rules.atomic_rule: Nothing requires a public office to allow a requester to make the copies of a public record themselves.
rules.trigger: A requester proposes to make copies of the record personally.
rules.legal_concept: No duty to allow requester self-copying
rules.source_language: Nothing in this section requires a public office or person responsible for the public record to allow the requester of a copy of the public record to make the copies of the public record.

rules.atomic_rule: A public office may transmit copies of public records to a requester by United States mail or by any other means of delivery or transmission the requester chooses, if the requester pays the postage/delivery cost in advance.
rules.trigger: A requester asks to have copies delivered rather than picked up.
rules.legal_concept: Transmission of copies by mail or other means
rules.source_language: A public office or person responsible for public records may transmit by United States mail or by any other means of delivery or transmission a copy of a public record requested under this division, upon the requester's payment in advance of the cost of postage or other delivery, and of the copying cost.
rules.notes: is_paraphrase=true: the opening permission of (B)(7) was rendered from the source rather than captured as a clean verbatim string this pass; the mail-volume-limit clause (OH-0024) was captured verbatim. Recommend verbatim verification of the (B)(7) opening sentence.

rules.atomic_rule: A public office may limit the number of records it will physically deliver by U.S. mail or another delivery service to ten per month, unless the requester certifies in writing non-commercial use.
rules.trigger: A requester seeks physical mail/delivery of more than ten records in a month without a non-commercial certification.
rules.clock_spec: floor: office may not cap physical-mail delivery below 10 records per month
rules.legal_concept: Ten-per-month mail delivery limit
rules.source_language: A public office may limit the number of records requested by a person that the office will physically deliver by United States mail or by another delivery service to ten per month, unless the person certifies to the office in writing that the person does not intend to use or forward the requested records, or the information contained in them, for commercial purposes.
rules.notes: constraint_basis floor: the statute permits a limit of ten/month, meaning the city may restrict but must allow at least ten. The commercial-use exception is split into OH-0025.

rules.atomic_rule: The ten-per-month delivery limit does not apply if the requester certifies in writing that they do not intend to use or forward the records, or the information in them, for commercial purposes.
rules.trigger: The requester provides a written non-commercial-use certification.
rules.legal_concept: Non-commercial-use certification (commercial purpose branch)
rules.source_language: unless the person certifies to the office in writing that the person does not intend to use or forward the requested records, or the information contained in them, for commercial purposes.
rules.notes: Keeper: a definition/branch the software acts on (commercial purpose) — it lifts the delivery cap. Kept per keeper-sliver guidance on branchable definitions.

rules.atomic_rule: A public office that makes records available online may limit the number of records it will transmit electronically (or otherwise) to a person to ten per month, unless the records are not available online or the requester certifies non-commercial use.
rules.trigger: A requester seeks electronic transmission of more than ten records in a month for records available online, without a non-commercial certification.
rules.clock_spec: floor: office may not cap electronic delivery below 10 records per month
rules.legal_concept: Ten-per-month electronic delivery limit
rules.source_language: A public office that makes available online at least ninety-five per cent of its public records may limit the number of records that the office will transmit to ten per month, unless the requested records are not available online or the person certifies to the office in writing that the person does not intend to use or forward the requested records, or the information contained in them, for commercial purposes.
rules.notes: is_paraphrase=true: the online-availability threshold (reported by the fetch as web-accessible records) and exact subsection wording were rendered rather than confirmed verbatim; the 'ninety-five per cent' figure requires verbatim verification. Structure (ten/month with online-availability and non-commercial exceptions) is confirmed.

rules.atomic_rule: A public office need not permit a person incarcerated pursuant to a criminal conviction to inspect or copy a record concerning a criminal investigation or prosecution unless the sentencing judge (or successor) finds the information is necessary to support what appears to be a justiciable claim of the person.
rules.trigger: An incarcerated person requests a record concerning a criminal investigation or prosecution.
rules.legal_concept: Incarcerated-requester screening for criminal records
rules.source_language: unless the request to inspect or to obtain a copy of the record is for the purpose of acquiring information that is subject to release as a public record under this section and the judge who imposed the sentence or made the adjudication with respect to the person, or the judge's successor in office, finds that the information sought in the public record is necessary to support what appears to be a justiciable claim of the person.
rules.notes: A distinct processing branch (requester status + record type gate requiring a judicial finding). Requires human legal review before automating the justiciable-claim determination.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to respond to a vexatious litigator's request without court leave and a particularized order
rules.atomic_rule: A person subject to a vexatious-litigator order may not request public records without first obtaining leave from the court of common pleas and an accompanying order specifying with particularity what records the person may request; until evidence of both is presented to the public office, the office is under no duty to respond to that person's request.
rules.trigger: Request received from a person subject to a vexatious-litigator order under R.C. 2323.52(D)(1), without evidence of court leave and a particularized order
rules.source_language: A person who is subject to an order entered pursuant to division (D)(1) of this section shall not be permitted to request public records from a public office or person responsible for public records without first receiving both leave to proceed from the court of common pleas as described in this section and an accompanying order from the court that specifies with particularity what public records the person may request from the public office or person responsible for public records. Until the requirements set forth in this division are satisfied and evidence of satisfaction is presented to the public office or person responsible for public records, the public office or person responsible for public records is under no duty to respond to a public records request submitted by a person who is subject to an order entered pursuant to division (D)(1) of this section.
rules.notes: ADDED 2026-07-26 via desktop-research recency cross-check; verified verbatim against codes.ohio.gov (April 9, 2025 version). Eligibility-gate family (cf. incarcerated-requester gates and UT vexatious-requester UT-0051..53); the Supreme Court of Ohio maintains the vexatious-litigator list online.

rules.legal_concept: ID may be required when a requester is known or reasonably believed to be a vexatious litigator
rules.atomic_rule: If a public office receives an anonymous records request (or one whose listed name matches) and knows or has reasonable cause to believe the requester is a vexatious litigator, it may require the person to present an acceptable form of identification before responding - an exception to the R.C. 149.43(B)(4) no-identity-condition rule.
rules.trigger: Anonymous or named request where the office knows or reasonably believes the requester is a vexatious litigator
rules.source_language: Pursuant to division (B)(4) of section 149.43 of the Revised Code, if a public office or person responsible for public records receives an anonymous public records request and knows or has reasonable cause to believe that a person who is a vexatious litigator has submitted a public records request, or if, based upon the requestor's listed name, the public office or person responsible for public records knows or has reasonable cause to believe that a person who is a vexatious litigator has submitted a public records request, the public office or person responsible for public records may require that the person present an acceptable form of identification prior to responding to the public records request.
rules.notes: ADDED 2026-07-26; verified verbatim against codes.ohio.gov. Identity/ID config dimension (see requester-class eligibility cluster): Ohio stays no-ID-required EXCEPT this narrow suspected-vexatious carve-out.

material_negatives.note: Ohio sets NO fixed numeric acknowledgment or response deadline. The only processing timing standards are the soft 'promptly' (inspection) and 'within a reasonable period of time' (copies) in R.C. 149.43(B)(1), captured as soft-standard rules OH-0007 and OH-0008. No day-count for acknowledgment exists.
R.C. 149.43(B)(3) requires a written denial explanation for written requests but attaches NO numeric deadline to providing it. Absence of a found day-count is not proof none exists elsewhere.
The opportunity-to-revise duty (R.C. 149.43(B)(2)) carries no statutory clock — no deadline by which the office must offer revision or the requester must respond.

Ohio has no fixed 'silence for N days = denial' trigger. A failure to respond within a reasonable time may be treated as a denial for mandamus/Court-of-Claims purposes, but the statute states no numeric constructive-denial day count.

No statewide statutory per-page copy rate. R.C. 149.43(B)(1) sets only an 'at cost'/actual-cost ceiling (OH-0018); the city fills in the operative rate. (Older R.C. 149.43(B)(1) practice historically referenced actual cost; no fixed cents-per-page in statute.)
R.C. 149.43(B)(6) permits requiring advance payment of the full cost but sets no partial-deposit percentage or threshold above which prepayment may be demanded.

No explicit statutory duty to forward a misdirected request to the correct office/custodian. The duty is stated as resting on the office or 'person responsible for public records' (OH-0013); routing/forwarding is not statutorily prescribed.

No statutory requirement to log/track requests or assign tracking numbers for an individual request under R.C. 149.43. (A public-records policy is required at the office level but tracking of individual requests is not mandated.)

structural_branches.description: Before asking a requester for a written request, identity, or intended use, the engine must present a disclosure that all three are optional and may be declined (R.C. 149.43(B)(5)).
On an ambiguous/overly-broad denial, the engine must branch into a revise-opportunity state that informs the requester how records are maintained and accessed (R.C. 149.43(B)(2)).
When exempt content is redacted, the engine must attach a redaction notice to the requester or render the redaction plainly visible (R.C. 149.43(B)(9)).
A written non-commercial-use certification is a branch that lifts the ten-per-month delivery cap (R.C. 149.43(B)(7)).
Service of a complaint opens a 3-business-day cure state before the requester may proceed to mandamus or the Court of Claims (R.C. 149.43(C)(1)).
Ohio-specific expedited review path: Court of Claims complaint -> mandatory mediation -> office response -> special master report -> objections, distinct from ordinary court action (R.C. 2743.75).
A mandatory mediation stage the special master must open immediately upon assignment, before any adjudication (R.C. 2743.75(E)).
The alternative court path — a mandamus action to compel compliance — that a requester may elect instead of the Court of Claims route (R.C. 149.43(C)(1)).
A status+record-type gate: incarcerated-person requests for criminal investigation/prosecution records route to a sentencing-judge justiciable-claim finding before release (R.C. 149.43(B)(8)).

rules.legal_concept: Records open to any person
rules.atomic_rule: Any person may inspect, copy, or mechanically reproduce the records of public bodies and public officials during regular business hours.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right, subject to enumerated exemptions).
rules.source_language: All records of public bodies and public officials shall be open to any person for inspection, copying, or mechanical reproduction during regular business hours; provided:
rules.effective_status: Current (last amended Laws 2026, SB 2184, c. 217, § 72, emerg. eff. May 6, 2026; operative access clause unchanged)
rules.notes: Maps to dictionary key eligibility.any_person__1 (TX/CA/NY/FL/IL/WA). 'Any person' carries no requester-class limitation.

rules.legal_concept: No residency or citizenship qualification
rules.atomic_rule: The right to inspect/copy records extends to any person with no residency or citizenship qualification.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: All records of public bodies and public officials shall be open to any person for inspection, copying, or mechanical reproduction during regular business hours
rules.notes: Universal-access symmetry: emitted as a rule with shared key, not a negative. Source clause 'any person' contains no residency qualifier; the Act states none anywhere.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required for access
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may not impose access procedures beyond those specified in the Act; no statement of purpose is required to inspect/copy records (purpose matters only to fees, not access).
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: Except as may be required by other statutes, public bodies do not need to follow any procedures for providing access to public records except those specifically required by the Oklahoma Open Records Act.
rules.notes: Universal-access symmetry: emitted as a rule with shared key. The Act nowhere requires a purpose statement; commercial-purpose classification affects only whether a search fee may be charged (OK-0019), not the right of access.

rules.legal_concept: Segregability of exempt portions
rules.atomic_rule: Any reasonably segregable portion of a record containing exempt material must be provided after deletion of the exempt portions.
rules.trigger: Record contains both exempt and non-exempt material.
rules.source_language: Any reasonably segregable portion of a record containing exempt material shall be provided after deletion of the exempt portions;
rules.notes: Maps to dictionary key redaction.segregability__1 (CA/FL/VA/WA). The same paragraph adds a DPS/OSBI carve-out (need not assemble records where requester fails to supply identifiers) — captured as a material negative/special note, not a general processing rule.

rules.legal_concept: Discretionary redaction of Social Security numbers
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may treat Social Security numbers in a record as confidential and redact or delete them prior to release, regardless of the person's status.
rules.trigger: Record to be released contains a Social Security number.
rules.source_language: All Social Security numbers included in a record may be confidential regardless of the person's status as a public employee or private individual and may be redacted or deleted prior to release of the record by the public body;
rules.notes: New coined key redaction.ssn_permitted. Unlike TX (redaction.ssn_no_ag), Oklahoma has no AG-predicate; redaction is a bare permission.

rules.legal_concept: Prompt, reasonable access
rules.atomic_rule: A public body must provide prompt, reasonable access to its records.
rules.trigger: Record request received.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "prompt, reasonable access" from request receipt
rules.source_language: A public body must provide prompt, reasonable access to its records but may establish reasonable procedures which protect the integrity and organization of its records and to prevent excessive disruptions of its essential functions.
rules.notes: Maps to dictionary key production.promptly__1 (TX/CA/AZ). Soft standard — config_home=structural, no invented day-count. Oklahoma has NO fixed statutory response/acknowledgment deadline (see material negatives).

rules.legal_concept: Internet availability satisfies prompt-access duty
rules.atomic_rule: A public body that makes the requested records available on the Internet is deemed to meet its obligation to provide prompt, reasonable access.
rules.trigger: Requested records are available on the body's Internet site.
rules.source_language: Any public body which makes the requested records available on the Internet shall meet the obligation of providing prompt, reasonable access to its records as required by this paragraph;
rules.notes: Maps loosely to dictionary key production.website_redirect (CA); Oklahoma states it as satisfaction of the prompt-access duty rather than a conditional redirect.

rules.legal_concept: Designation of persons authorized to release records
rules.atomic_rule: A public body must designate certain persons authorized to release its records for inspection, copying, or mechanical reproduction.
rules.trigger: None stated (standing obligation of the body).
rules.source_language: A public body shall designate certain persons who are authorized to release records of the public body for inspection, copying, or mechanical reproduction.
rules.effective_status: Current (paragraph may be renumbered by post-2022 amendments; operative text confirmed present in current OSCN version)
rules.notes: Maps to dictionary key custody.foia_officer_designation (IL/VA/WA). Drives routing (keeper-sliver #1).

rules.legal_concept: At least one release agent available at all times
rules.atomic_rule: At least one authorized person must be available at all times to release records during the public body's regular business hours.
rules.trigger: During regular business hours.
rules.source_language: At least one person shall be available at all times to release records during the regular business hours of the public body.
rules.notes: New coined key custody.release_agent_availability. Atomic-split from OK-0014.

rules.legal_concept: Copy fee limited to reasonable direct cost
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may charge a fee only to recover the reasonable, direct costs of record copying or mechanical reproduction.
rules.trigger: Body charges a copy fee (non-commercial, non-disruptive request).
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: reasonable direct cost of copying/reproduction
rules.source_language: Otherwise, a public body may charge a fee only for recovery of the reasonable, direct costs of record copying, or mechanical reproduction.
rules.notes: Maps to dictionary key fee.copy_actual_cost_ceiling__1 (CA/VA/WA). Search/labor cost is NOT recoverable except in the two circumstances in OK-0019.

rules.legal_concept: 25-cent-per-page copy fee cap
rules.atomic_rule: The record copying fee may not exceed twenty-five cents ($0.25) per page for records 8.5 by 14 inches or smaller.
rules.trigger: Body charges a per-page copy fee for standard-size pages.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: $0.25/page (pages <= 8.5 x 14 in)
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding any state or local provision to the contrary, in no instance shall the record copying fee exceed twenty-five cents ($0.25) per page for records having the dimensions of eight and one-half (8 1/2) by fourteen (14) inches or smaller,
rules.notes: Maps to dictionary key fee.per_page_rate_ceiling__1 (NY/FL/IL/WA). 'Notwithstanding any state or local provision to the contrary' pre-empts higher local rates for standard requests.

rules.legal_concept: Certified-copy fee cap
rules.atomic_rule: The fee for a certified copy may not exceed One Dollar ($1.00) per copied page.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks a certified copy.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: $1.00/page (certified copy)
rules.source_language: or a maximum of One Dollar ($1.00) per copied page for a certified copy.
rules.notes: Maps to dictionary key fee.certified_copy_charge (FL/IL).

rules.legal_concept: Search fee permitted only for commercial or excessively-disruptive requests
rules.atomic_rule: If a request is solely for a commercial purpose, or would clearly cause excessive disruption of the body's essential functions, the body may charge a reasonable fee to recover the direct cost of record search and copying.
rules.trigger: Request is solely for commercial purpose OR would clearly cause excessive disruption of essential functions.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: reasonable direct cost of search and copying
rules.source_language: However, if the request: a. is solely for commercial purpose, or b. would clearly cause excessive disruption of the essential functions of the public body, then the public body may charge a reasonable fee to recover the direct cost of record search and copying;
rules.notes: New coined key fee.search_fee_conditional. Structural because it is a fee-basis fork gated by request classification (commercial purpose is a definition the software branches on — keeper-sliver). Search-fee recovery is otherwise prohibited (contrast OK-0016).

rules.legal_concept: News-media use is not a commercial purpose
rules.atomic_rule: Newspaper publication or news-media broadcast for news purposes is not a resale or commercial/trade use, and charges for electronic data provided to news media for a news purpose may not exceed the direct cost of copying.
rules.trigger: Requester is news media using the record for a news purpose.
rules.source_language: however, publication in a newspaper or broadcast by news media for news purposes shall not constitute a resale or use of a record for trade or commercial purpose and charges for providing copies of electronic data to the news media for a news purpose shall not exceed the direct cost of making the copy.
rules.notes: New coined key classification.commercial_purpose_news_exclusion. Definition the software branches on: prevents news-media requests from triggering the commercial-purpose search fee (OK-0019).

rules.legal_concept: Public posting of fee schedule
rules.atomic_rule: A public body that establishes fees must post a written schedule of the fees at its principal office and with the county clerk.
rules.trigger: Body establishes fees under the Act.
rules.source_language: Any public body establishing fees under this act shall post a written schedule of the fees at its principal office and with the county clerk.
rules.notes: New coined key fee.schedule_posting. A precondition to charging fees.

rules.legal_concept: No search fee when release is in the public interest
rules.atomic_rule: No search fee may be charged when release of the records is in the public interest, including release to news media, scholars, authors, and taxpayers seeking to determine whether officials are performing their duties.
rules.trigger: Release of records is in the public interest.
rules.source_language: In no case shall a search fee be charged when the release of records is in the public interest, including, but not limited to, release to the news media, scholars, authors and taxpayers seeking to determine whether those entrusted with the affairs of the government are honestly, faithfully, and competently performing their duties as public servants.
rules.notes: Maps to dictionary key fee.waiver_public_interest__1 (TX/IL). Overrides the search-fee permission (OK-0019) for public-interest requests.

rules.legal_concept: Fees not to be used to discourage requests
rules.atomic_rule: Fees may not be used to discourage requests for information or as obstacles to disclosure of requested information.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: The fees shall not be used for the purpose of discouraging requests for information or as obstacles to disclosure of requested information;
rules.notes: New coined key fee.no_discouragement. Anti-obstruction constraint on fee-setting.

rules.legal_concept: Per-record fee where prescribed by other state law
rules.atomic_rule: Where the cost of copying/reproducing/certifying each individual record is otherwise prescribed by state law, the body may assess that cost per individual record or portion requested.
rules.trigger: Request contains individual records whose copy/certification cost is set by another state statute.
rules.source_language: Any request for a record which contains individual records of persons, and the cost of copying, reproducing or certifying each individual record is otherwise prescribed by state law, the cost may be assessed for each individual record, or portion thereof requested as prescribed by state law.
rules.notes: New coined key fee.statutory_per_record. A branch to externally-prescribed fee schedules that displaces the $0.25/page cap.

rules.legal_concept: Access-notice duty for bodies open fewer than 30 hours/week
rules.atomic_rule: A public body without at least 30 regular business hours per week must post and maintain a written notice (at its principal office and with the county clerk) designating the days records are available, the name/mailing address/telephone of the individual in charge of records, and detailed procedures for obtaining access at least two days per week excluding Sunday.
rules.trigger: Public body/office lacks regular business hours of at least 30 hours per week.
rules.source_language: If a public body or its office does not have regular business hours of at least thirty (30) hours a week, the public body shall post and maintain a written notice at its principal office and with the county clerk where the public body is located which notice shall: 1. Designate the days of the week when records are available for inspection, copying or mechanical reproduction; 2. Set forth the name, mailing address, and telephone number of the individual in charge of the records; and 3. Describe in detail the procedures for obtaining access to the records at least two days of the week, excluding Sunday.
rules.notes: New coined key intake.limited_hours_notice. Structural branch: a distinct intake/availability path for low-hours bodies (routing + a minimum 2-day access floor).

rules.legal_concept: Access by mutual agreement outside designated days
rules.atomic_rule: The requester and the authorized release person may agree to inspection/copying on a day and time other than that designated in the sub-30-hours notice.
rules.trigger: Body operates under a § 24A.6 limited-hours notice.
rules.source_language: The person requesting the record and the person authorized to release the records of the public body may agree to inspection, copying, or mechanical reproduction on a day and at a time other than that designated in the notice.
rules.notes: New coined key intake.appointment_by_agreement.

rules.legal_concept: Discretionary denial of law-enforcement records
rules.atomic_rule: Except for records made open by § 24A.8(A) or other law, a law enforcement agency may deny access to law enforcement records unless a court finds the public interest or an individual's interest outweighs the reason for denial.
rules.trigger: Request for law-enforcement records not within the mandatory-disclosure list of § 24A.8(A).
rules.source_language: Except for the records listed in subsection A of this section and those made open by other state or local laws, law enforcement agencies may deny access to law enforcement records except where a court finds that the public interest or the interest of an individual outweighs the reason for denial.
rules.notes: New coined key denial.law_enforcement_discretion. Record-Specific discretion path; the court-balancing standard is flagged for human legal review (not auto-configurable). See Special Records for the § 24A.8(A) mandatory list and body-camera redaction workflow.

rules.legal_concept: Request form permitted; clarification for requests lacking reasonable specificity (3-element definition)
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may require a requestor to complete a records request form, and may ask the requestor to clarify a request that does not describe the records with reasonable specificity. Reasonable specificity requires: (a) a general time frame of creation/transmission, (b) identifiable records rather than general information, and (c) search terms sufficiently specific to assist the body in identifying the records.
rules.trigger: Request does not describe the requested records with reasonable specificity
rules.source_language: A public body may require a requestor to complete a records request form. If a records request does not describe the requested records with reasonable specificity, a public body may ask the requestor to clarify the request. To have reasonable specificity, a request shall: a. specify a general time frame within which the requested records would have been created or transmitted, b. seek identifiable records, rather than general information without any qualifiers or other specifications, and c. include search terms that are sufficiently specific to assist the public body in identifying the requested records.
