rules.notes: ADDED 2026-07-26 via desktop-research recency cross-check; verified verbatim against enrolled SB 535 (pp. 8-9). Before SB 535 Oklahoma had no statutory clarification process. Old ¶7 (designated custodians) renumbered to ¶8. No statutory clock attaches (OK has no fixed response deadline).

rules.legal_concept: Specificity denial only after the body has engaged to help identify the records
rules.atomic_rule: A request may be denied for lack of reasonable specificity only if the public body has first engaged with the requestor to seek the information needed to fulfill the request and to identify the records sought - including providing the requestor with general topics or a specific list of records related to the request - and the request is still not reasonably specific.
rules.trigger: Clarification engagement completed and the request remains not reasonably specific
rules.source_language: If a public body has engaged with the requestor to seek the information needed to fulfill the request and to identify the records sought by the requestor, including providing the requestor with general topics or a specific list of records related to the request, the request may be denied if it is still not reasonably specific;
rules.notes: ADDED 2026-07-26; verified verbatim against enrolled SB 535 (p. 9). A codified duty-to-engage/assist gate on the clarification-failure denial path - workflow: clarification round is mandatory before a specificity denial.

rules.legal_concept: Advance payment allowed above $75 estimate or with outstanding fees; excess refunded
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may require advance payment of estimated fees when the estimated cost exceeds $75.00 or if the requestor has outstanding fees from previous requests; any portion of an advance payment exceeding the actual cost of responding must be returned to the requestor.
rules.trigger: Estimated cost exceeds $75, or requestor has outstanding fees from previous requests
rules.source_language: A public body may require advance payment of the estimated fees authorized under this section when the estimated cost exceeds Seventy-five Dollars ($75.00) or if the requestor has outstanding fees from previous requests. Any portion of an advance payment that exceeds the costs of responding to the request shall be returned to the requestor.
rules.notes: ADDED 2026-07-26; verified verbatim against enrolled SB 535 (p. 7, underlined new text). Parent-ledger design input: outstanding-fees trigger is cross-request (requestor-level balance), like TX § 552.263(c); refund-of-excess is an accounting obligation.

material_negatives.note: Oklahoma sets NO fixed numeric response or determination deadline. The only timing standard is the soft 'prompt, reasonable access' of §24A.5(6). Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists, but the Act contains no day-count.
No statutory duty to acknowledge a request or issue an estimated completion date. The Act specifies only prompt, reasonable access.

No statutory 'silence = denial' trigger. §24A.17(B) provides a civil remedy for records 'requested and denied,' but the Act fixes no clock after which non-response is deemed a denial (Oklahoma case law has treated unreasonable delay as constructive denial; not codified — flagged for a later case-law pass).
No administrative or Attorney-General records-review/appeal process exists (contrast Texas's AG-decision regime). Enforcement is judicial only (§24A.17(B)).
No statutory clarification/narrowing procedure, clarification clock, or reasonably-describes-identifiable threshold is stated in the Act.

No statutory preservation/litigation-hold triggered by a pending request. §24A.8(C) and §24A.18 expressly disclaim any additional recordkeeping requirement; retention is governed by separate records-management law (out of scope).

No general 'produce in the requester's chosen electronic format' mandate. The Act addresses electronic format only for narrow record types (news-media electronic data and DPS computerized copies), both capped at direct cost — not a general format-choice right.
The Act contains no provision authorizing or governing advance deposits or pre-payment before production; only the fee caps of §24A.5(4) are stated.
No statutory extension mechanism or unusual-circumstances tolling; consistent with the absence of any fixed response clock.
The Act does not require a written request or any particular form; §24A.2 bars imposing procedures beyond those the Act specifies, and none is specified for intake form or channel.

structural_branches.description: OK-0025 (§24A.6(A)): distinct intake/availability path for public bodies open fewer than 30 hours/week — posted notice, designated in-charge individual, and a minimum-two-days-per-week access floor.
OK-0026 (§24A.6(B)): mutual-agreement appointment path for access outside the designated limited-hours days.

OK-0019 (§24A.5(4)): fee-basis fork — a search fee is unlockable ONLY when the request is solely commercial-purpose or would clearly cause excessive disruption; otherwise search cost is non-recoverable.

OK-0020 (§24A.5(4)): classification branch excluding news-media/news-purpose use from 'commercial purpose', diverting it away from the search-fee path and into a direct-cost-only electronic-data rate.
OK-0012 (§24A.5(6)): queue-management branch prohibiting a short current request from being blocked behind a substantially longer prior request.
OK-0013 (§24A.5(6)): Internet-availability path that satisfies the prompt-access duty.

OK-0027 (§24A.8(B)): record-specific discretionary-denial path for law-enforcement records not on the §24A.8(A) mandatory-disclosure list, subject to a court public-interest balancing test (human-legal-review flagged).

rules.legal_concept: Right of every person to inspect public records
rules.atomic_rule: Any person (no requester qualification) has a right to inspect any public record of an Oregon public body, subject only to the stated exemptions.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right of any person)
rules.source_language: Every person has a right to inspect any public record of a public body in this state, except as otherwise expressly provided by ORS 192.338, 192.345 and 192.355.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule per shared eligibility key. 'Every person' establishes standing for any requester.

rules.legal_concept: No residency requirement to request records
rules.atomic_rule: Oregon imposes no residency requirement; the inspection right runs to every person regardless of residency.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: Every person has a right to inspect any public record of a public body in this state, except as otherwise expressly provided by ORS 192.338, 192.345 and 192.355.
rules.notes: No residency limitation appears in the statute; 'every person' carries no residency qualifier. Emitted as rule with shared key so cross-state join matches states that state this as an absence.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A requester need not state a purpose or reason to exercise the inspection right; no purpose is a condition of access.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: Every person has a right to inspect any public record of a public body in this state, except as otherwise expressly provided by ORS 192.338, 192.345 and 192.355.
rules.notes: No statutory statement-of-purpose condition. Purpose may bear on fee-waiver 'public interest' analysis (OR-0023) but is not a precondition to the right. Emitted as rule with shared key.

rules.legal_concept: Written request triggers copy/inspection duty
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian's duty to give a copy or a reasonable opportunity to inspect is triggered upon receipt of a written request.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a written request by the custodian
rules.source_language: A public body that is the custodian of any public record that a person has a right to inspect shall give the person, upon receipt of a written request: (a) A copy of the public record if the public record is of a nature permitting copying; or (b) A reasonable opportunity to inspect or copy the public record.
rules.notes: Writing is the intake channel that triggers the copy obligation and the acknowledgment clock.

rules.legal_concept: Public body must publish a written request procedure
rules.atomic_rule: A public body shall make available to the public a written procedure for making public records requests that names one or more individuals (with addresses) to whom requests may be sent and states the amounts and manner of calculating fees.
rules.trigger: None stated (standing obligation)
rules.source_language: A public body shall make available to the public a written procedure for making public records requests that includes: (a) The name of one or more individuals within the public body to whom public records requests may be sent, with addresses; and (b) The amounts of and the manner of calculating fees that the public body charges for responding to requests for public records.
rules.notes: Conjunctive requirement kept in one row; drives routing (designated recipient) and fee disclosure. The 5-business-day acknowledgment clock (OR-0006) runs from receipt by an individual identified in this procedure.

rules.legal_concept: Five-business-day acknowledgment of request
rules.atomic_rule: When an individual identified in the public body's written procedure receives a written request, the public body shall within five business days acknowledge receipt or complete its response.
rules.trigger: Receipt of written request by an individual identified in the public body's ORS 192.324(7) procedure
rules.clock_spec: 5 business-days from receipt of request by the designated individual
rules.source_language: If an individual who is identified in a public body's procedure described in subsection (7)(a) of this section receives a written request to inspect or receive a copy of a public record, the public body shall within five business days after receiving the request acknowledge receipt of the request or complete the public body's response to the request.
rules.notes: Acknowledgment clock; the 10-business-day statement deadline (OR-0008) counts from the date acknowledgment is due under this subsection.

rules.legal_concept: Required content of acknowledgment (custody determination)
rules.atomic_rule: The acknowledgment must confirm the public body is the custodian, inform the requester it is not the custodian, or notify the requester it is uncertain whether it is the custodian.
rules.trigger: Issuance of an acknowledgment under ORS 192.324(2)
rules.source_language: An acknowledgment under this subsection must: (a) Confirm that the public body is the custodian of the requested record; (b) Inform the requester that the public body is not the custodian of the requested record; or (c) Notify the requester that the public body is uncertain whether the public body is the custodian of the requested record.
rules.notes: Custody determination at acknowledgment drives routing (keeper-sliver: custodian/who-must-respond).

rules.legal_concept: Ten-business-day completion-or-status statement
rules.atomic_rule: As soon as reasonably possible but not later than 10 business days after the date acknowledgment is due, the public body shall either complete its response or provide a written statement that it is still processing plus a reasonable estimated completion date.
rules.trigger: Expiry of the date by which acknowledgment is required under ORS 192.324
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from the date acknowledgment is due under ORS 192.324(2)
rules.source_language: As soon as reasonably possible but not later than 10 business days after the date by which a public body is required to acknowledge receipt of the request under ORS 192.324 (Copies or inspection of public records), a public body shall: (a) Complete its response to the public records request; or (b) Provide a written statement that the public body is still processing the request and a reasonable estimated date by which the public body expects to complete its response based on the information currently available.
rules.notes: This is NOT a completion deadline; option (b) permits a status statement with a self-set estimated date. Subject to the impracticability exception (OR-0029).

rules.legal_concept: Complete response as soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay
rules.atomic_rule: A public body shall complete its response to a written public records request as soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a written public records request by an individual identified in the ORS 192.324 procedure
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "as soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay" from receipt of the written request
rules.source_language: A public body shall complete its response to a written public records request that is received by an individual identified in the public body's procedure described in ORS 192.324 (Copies or inspection of public records) as soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay.
rules.notes: Soft standard: there is NO fixed numeric outer deadline for completing a response in Oregon. Config Home structural per soft-deadline rule; no day-count invented.

rules.legal_concept: Assertion of exemptions with legal citation
rules.atomic_rule: To complete a response the public body must assert any exemptions it believes apply and, if citing ORS 192.355(8) or (9), identify the state or federal law relied upon.
rules.trigger: Public body withholding records as exempt
rules.source_language: Asserts any exemptions from disclosure that the public body believes apply to any requested records and, if the public body cites ORS 192.355 (Public records exempt from disclosure) (8) or (9), identifies the state or federal law that the public body relied on in asserting the exemptions;
rules.notes: Partial-denial content requirement; triggers the review-rights notice (OR-0015).

rules.legal_concept: Segregation of exempt and nonexempt material
rules.atomic_rule: If a record contains both exempt and nonexempt material, the public body shall separate the exempt and nonexempt material and make the nonexempt material available for examination.
rules.trigger: A record contains both exempt and nonexempt material
rules.source_language: If any public record contains material which is not exempt under ORS 192.345 (Public records conditionally exempt from disclosure) and 192.355 (Public records exempt from disclosure), as well as material which is exempt from disclosure, the public body shall separate the exempt and nonexempt material and make the nonexempt material available for examination.
rules.notes: Segregability duty; ORS 192.329(2)(c) makes compliance with 192.338 part of a complete response. Attorney time spent segregating is fee-includable (OR-0021).

rules.legal_concept: Written statement when not the custodian
rules.atomic_rule: To the extent the public body is not the custodian of requested records, it must provide a written statement to that effect.
rules.trigger: Public body is not the custodian of some or all requested records
rules.source_language: To the extent that the public body is not the custodian of records that have been requested, provides a written statement to that effect;
rules.notes: Routing signal to requester; part of completeness. Complements custody determination in the acknowledgment (OR-0007).

rules.legal_concept: Statement where existence cannot be acknowledged
rules.atomic_rule: Where state or federal law prohibits acknowledging whether a record exists (or acknowledgment would forfeit federal benefits or impose a sanction), the public body must provide a written statement to that effect citing the law relied on, unless the statement itself would violate law.
rules.trigger: State/federal law bars acknowledging existence of a requested record
rules.source_language: To the extent that state or federal law prohibits the public body from acknowledging whether any requested record exists or that acknowledging whether a requested record exists would result in the loss of federal benefits or imposition of another sanction, provides a written statement to that effect, citing the state or federal law that the public body relies on, unless the written statement itself would violate state or federal law; and
rules.notes: Glomar-type response path; part of completeness definition.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of custodian (functional)
rules.atomic_rule: 'Custodian' means the person described in ORS 7.110 for court records, or a public body mandated (directly or indirectly) to create, maintain, care for or control a public record; a public body that is not the custodian and lacks control is not required to search for/produce a record.
rules.trigger: Determining which body must respond
rules.source_language: 'Custodian' means: (a) The person described in ORS 7.110 for purposes of court records; or (b) A public body mandated, directly or indirectly, to create, maintain, care for or control a public record. 'Custodian' does not include a public body that has custody of a public record as an agent of another public body that is the custodian unless the public body is expressly required by law to hold that public record.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: definition the software branches on for routing/who-must-respond. Quote reconstructed from ORS 192.311(1); verify the agent-exclusion clause against the official PDF.

rules.legal_concept: Format of electronic/machine-readable records
rules.atomic_rule: If a public record is maintained in machine readable or electronic form, the public body shall provide a copy in the form requested if available; if not available in the form requested, it shall make the record available in the form in which it maintains the record.
rules.trigger: Requested record is maintained in machine readable/electronic form
rules.source_language: If the public record is maintained in a machine readable or electronic form, the public body shall provide a copy of the public record in the form requested, if available. If the public record is not available in the form requested, the public body shall make the public record available in the form in which the public body maintains the public record.
rules.notes: Format-selection branch for electronic records.

rules.legal_concept: Fees reasonably calculated to reimburse actual cost
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may establish fees reasonably calculated to reimburse it for its actual cost of making public records available, including costs for summarizing, compiling or tailoring the records in organization or media to meet the request.
rules.trigger: Public body makes records available in response to a request
rules.source_language: The public body may establish fees reasonably calculated to reimburse the public body for the public body's actual cost of making public records available, including costs for summarizing, compiling or tailoring the public records, either in organization or media, to meet the request.
rules.notes: No statewide fixed per-page or per-hour rate; the ceiling is the soft 'actual cost / reasonably calculated' standard and the city supplies the operative rates.

rules.legal_concept: Attorney review/redaction time in fees; exclusion of exemption-analysis time
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may include in the fee the cost of attorney time spent reviewing, redacting, or segregating records into exempt and nonexempt, but may NOT include attorney time spent determining the application of ORS 192.311 to 192.478.
rules.trigger: Attorney time expended on a request
rules.source_language: The public body may include in a fee established under paragraph (a) of this subsection the cost of time spent by an attorney for the public body in reviewing the public records, redacting material from the public records or segregating the public records into exempt and nonexempt records. The public body may not include in a fee established under paragraph (a) of this subsection the cost of time spent by an attorney for the public body in determining the application of the provisions of ORS 192.311 to 192.478.
rules.notes: Conjunctive permission+prohibition kept in one row (the includable/not-includable line is a single fee-component rule). Drives fee composition.

rules.legal_concept: $25 fee threshold requiring written estimate and confirmation
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may not establish a fee greater than $25 unless it first provides the requester written notification of the estimated fee amount and the requester confirms that it wants the public body to proceed.
rules.trigger: Estimated fee exceeds $25
rules.source_language: The public body may not establish a fee greater than $25 under this section unless the public body first provides the requester with a written notification of the estimated amount of the fee and the requester confirms that the requester wants the public body to proceed with making the public record available.
rules.notes: $25 is the fixed trigger value; the estimate-and-confirm step is a structural gate that pairs with the fee-suspension clock (OR-0024). City cannot raise the $25 trigger.

rules.legal_concept: Discretionary fee waiver or reduction in the public interest
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may furnish copies without charge or at a substantially reduced fee if it determines the waiver or reduction is in the public interest because making the record available primarily benefits the general public.
rules.trigger: Custodian determines waiver/reduction is in the public interest
rules.source_language: The custodian of a public record may furnish copies without charge or at a substantially reduced fee if the custodian determines that the waiver or reduction of fees is in the public interest because making the record available primarily benefits the general public.
rules.notes: Discretionary branch; denial of a waiver is separately reviewable (OR-0025).

rules.legal_concept: Response obligation suspended pending fee payment
rules.atomic_rule: If the public body has informed the requester of a permitted fee, its obligation to complete the response is suspended until the fee is paid, waived by the body, or ordered waived.
rules.trigger: Public body informs requester of a fee under ORS 192.324(4)
rules.clock_spec: completion obligation tolled from date requester is informed of fee until fee paid or waived
rules.source_language: If a public body has informed a requester of a fee permitted under ORS 192.324 (Copies or inspection of public records) (4), the obligation of the public body to complete its response to the request is suspended until the requester has paid the fee, the fee has been waived by the public body pursuant to ORS 192.324 (Copies or inspection of public records) (5) or the fee otherwise has been ordered waived.
rules.notes: Tolls the soft completion duty (OR-0009) while fee is outstanding.

rules.legal_concept: Close of request after 60 days' nonpayment
rules.atomic_rule: If the requester fails to pay the fee within 60 days of being informed of the fee (or within 60 days of denial of a fee waiver), the public body shall close the request.
rules.trigger: 60 days elapse after fee notice or waiver denial without payment
rules.clock_spec: 60 calendar-days from date requester informed of fee, or from date of fee-waiver denial; on lapse the request closes
rules.source_language: If the requester fails to pay the fee within 60 days of the date on which the public body informed the requester of the fee, or fails to pay the fee within 60 days of the date on which the public body informed the requester of the denial of the fee waiver, the public body shall close the request.
rules.notes: Terminal event (request ends). 60-day count is fixed by statute.

rules.legal_concept: Good-faith clarification request suspends response duty
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may request additional information or clarification to expedite its response; if made in good faith, its obligation to further complete the response is suspended until the requester provides the information/clarification or affirmatively declines.
rules.trigger: Public body makes a good-faith request for information or clarification
rules.clock_spec: further-completion obligation tolled from clarification request until requester responds or declines
rules.source_language: A public body may request additional information or clarification from a requester of public records for the purpose of expediting the public body's response to the request. If the public body has requested additional information or clarification in good faith, the public body's obligation to further complete its response to the request is suspended until the requester provides the requested information or clarification or affirmatively declines to provide that information or clarification.
rules.notes: Tolls the completion duty; paired with the 60-day close (OR-0028).

rules.legal_concept: Close of request after 60 days' failure to clarify
rules.atomic_rule: If the requester fails to respond within 60 days to a good-faith request for information or clarification, the public body shall close the request.
rules.trigger: 60 days elapse after a good-faith clarification request without requester response
rules.clock_spec: 60 calendar-days from the good-faith clarification request; on lapse the request closes
rules.source_language: If the requester fails to respond within 60 days to a good faith request from the public body for information or clarification, the public body shall close the request.
rules.notes: Terminal event; 60-day count fixed by statute.

rules.legal_concept: Impracticability suspension of statutory time periods
rules.atomic_rule: The ORS 192.324 and 192.329(5) time periods do not apply when compliance would be impracticable because necessary staff/volunteers are unavailable (including those on leave or not scheduled), compliance would demonstrably impede other necessary services, or because of the volume of simultaneous requests; the body must still respond as soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay.
rules.trigger: Compliance with the acknowledgment/status deadlines would be impracticable for a listed reason
rules.clock_spec: numeric acknowledgment (5 bd) and status (10 bd) deadlines suspended for a listed impracticability reason; soft 'as soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay' standard substitutes
rules.source_language: The time periods established by ORS 192.324 (Copies or inspection of public records) and subsection (5) of this section do not apply to a public body if compliance would be impracticable because: (a) The staff or volunteers necessary to complete a response to the public records request are unavailable; (b) Compliance would demonstrably impede the public body's ability to perform other necessary services; or (c) Of the volume of public records requests being simultaneously processed by the public body. ... A public body that cannot comply with the time periods established by ORS 192.324 and subsection (5) of this section for a reason listed in subsection (6) of this section shall, as soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay, acknowledge a public records request and complete the response to the request.
rules.notes: Subsection (7) deems staff on leave/not scheduled to be 'unavailable' (kept in this row as it defines a term within the exception). Suspends the numeric deadlines and reverts to the soft standard.

rules.legal_concept: Agency must comply with disclosure order within seven days or notice suit
rules.atomic_rule: If the AG orders disclosure, the state agency shall comply in full within seven days after issuance of the order unless within that period it issues a notice of intent to seek injunctive or declaratory relief; it must then institute the proceedings within seven days after issuing the notice.
rules.trigger: AG grants (or partly grants) petition and orders disclosure
rules.clock_spec: 7 days from issuance of AG order to comply or notice suit; then 7 days from notice to institute proceedings
rules.source_language: If the Attorney General grants the petition and orders the state agency to disclose the public record, or if the Attorney General grants the petition in part and orders the state agency to disclose a portion of the public record, the state agency shall comply with the order in full within seven days after issuance of the order, unless within the seven-day period it issues a notice of its intention to institute proceedings for injunctive or declaratory relief in the Circuit Court for Marion County or, as provided in ORS 192.401 (3), in the circuit court of the county where the public record is held. ... The state agency shall institute the proceedings within seven days after it issues its notice of intention to do so.
rules.notes: Post-order compliance/appeal clock for the public body. Applies to local bodies via the DA per ORS 192.415.

rules.legal_concept: Deemed denial when elected official fails to act in seven days
rules.atomic_rule: Failure of an elected official to grant or deny a request within seven days of receipt is treated as a denial, enabling the requester to institute injunctive or declaratory relief proceedings.
rules.trigger: 7 days elapse after an elected official's receipt of a request without action
rules.clock_spec: 7 days from elected official's receipt of the request; on lapse the request is deemed denied
rules.source_language: The failure of an elected official to deny, grant, or deny in part and grant in part a request to inspect or receive a copy of a public record within seven days from the day of receipt of the request shall be treated as a denial of the request for the purpose of determining whether a person may institute proceedings for injunctive or declaratory relief under ORS 192.401, 192.411 or 192.415.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: deemed-denial trigger specific to records held by elected officials. Distinct 7-day silence-equals-denial clock.

rules.legal_concept: Litigation-party request must also be served on public body's attorney
rules.atomic_rule: A requester who is a party to a civil judicial proceeding to which a public body is a party (or who filed an ORS 30.275(5)(a) tort-claim notice) and who requests a record known to relate to that proceeding must submit the request in writing to the custodian and, at the same time, to the attorney for the public body.
rules.trigger: Requester is a civil-litigation party/tort-claim-notice filer requesting a record known to relate to the proceeding
rules.source_language: If a person who is a party to a civil judicial proceeding to which a public body is a party, or who has filed a notice under ORS 30.275 (5)(a), asks to inspect or to receive a copy of a public record that the person knows relates to the proceeding or notice, the person must submit the request in writing to the custodian and, at the same time, to the attorney for the public body.
rules.notes: Special intake-routing branch for litigation-related requests; for a state agency the attorney is the Attorney General in Salem (ORS 192.314(2)(b)).

material_negatives.note: Oregon sets NO fixed numeric outer deadline to complete a response. ORS 192.329(1) requires completion 'as soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay' (soft), and the only hard 10-business-day duty (ORS 192.329(5)) is satisfied by a status statement with a self-set estimated date, not actual completion.

No statewide fixed per-page copy rate or per-hour labor rate. Fees are bounded only by the soft 'reasonably calculated to reimburse actual cost' standard (ORS 192.324(4)(a)); each city sets its own rates in its published procedure.

No express provision in ORS 192.311-192.478 imposing a litigation/appeal- or request-triggered preservation hold on records subject to a pending request. Routine retention schedules live in ORS ch. 192/166 archives provisions and are out of scope. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

No statute expressly authorizes or requires advance deposits/prepayment beyond the ORS 192.324(4)(c) $25 written-estimate-and-confirmation gate and the ORS 192.329(3) fee-payment suspension. Deposit practice, if any, is local.
No statutory requirement that a public body assign or provide a tracking number/reference for a request. Not legally required; excluded from primary rules.
Statute requires a written acknowledgment/response content but does not prescribe a delivery channel (mail/email/portal); channel is unspecified by statute.

structural_branches.description: Each public body must publish a written request procedure naming designated recipient(s) with addresses and fee-calculation method (ORS 192.324(7)) — the intake/routing entry point.
Acknowledgment must make a custody determination (custodian / not custodian / uncertain), a three-way branch that drives routing (ORS 192.324(2)).
Oregon-specific suspension of the 5- and 10-business-day deadlines for staff unavailability, service impediment, or request volume, reverting to a soft standard (ORS 192.329(6)-(8)).
Municipal/non-state denials are reviewed by the county district attorney (not the AG), with suit in that county's circuit court (ORS 192.415).
Records held by, or withholding-claimed by, an elected official bypass administrative AG/DA review and go directly to circuit court (ORS 192.427) — a distinct Oregon path.
AG/DA silence for 7 days is a deemed denial that unlocks the judicial stage (ORS 192.418(1)).
Elected-official silence for 7 days is a deemed denial unlocking direct judicial relief (ORS 192.418(2)).
A stated fee tolls the completion obligation until paid/waived, feeding the 60-day nonpayment close (ORS 192.329(3)).
A good-faith clarification request tolls the completion obligation until the requester responds or declines, feeding the 60-day clarification close (ORS 192.329(4)).

rules.legal_concept: Requester (statutory definition)
rules.atomic_rule: Only a person who is a legal resident of the United States (or an agency) may be a 'requester' entitled to make a Right-to-Know request; US legal residency is a gate on standing.
rules.trigger: Person submits a records request
rules.source_language: "Requester." A person that is a legal resident of the United States and requests a record pursuant to this act. The term includes an agency.
rules.notes: Genuine cross-state constraint: PA limits standing to US legal residents (and agencies) — this is NOT eligibility.no_residency_requirement. Software branches on requester status here.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A written request need not state the requester's reason for requesting or intended use of the records, unless another law requires it.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: A written request need not include any explanation of the requester's reason for requesting or intended use of the records unless otherwise required by law.
rules.notes: Shared universal-access key; purpose may still matter to fee/commercial treatment elsewhere.

rules.legal_concept: Permitted methods of submitting a written request
rules.atomic_rule: A written request may be submitted in person, by mail, by e-mail, by facsimile or, to the extent provided by agency rules, by any other electronic means.
rules.trigger: Requester submits a written request
rules.source_language: A written request for access to records may be submitted in person, by mail, by e-mail, by facsimile or, to the extent provided by agency rules, by any other electronic means.
rules.notes: 'any other electronic means' is agency-configurable; the enumerated channels are mandatory-permitted.

rules.legal_concept: Requests addressed to open-records officer; employee forwarding duty
rules.atomic_rule: A written request must be addressed to the designated open-records officer, and agency employees must be directed to forward requests for records to that officer.
rules.trigger: Request received by any agency employee
rules.source_language: A written request must be addressed to the open-records officer designated pursuant to section 502. Employees of an agency shall be directed to forward requests for records to the open-records officer.
rules.notes: Routing keeper-sliver; the 5-business-day clock runs from receipt BY the open-records officer, not by any employee.

rules.legal_concept: Sufficient specificity; requester contact information
rules.atomic_rule: A written request should identify or describe the records sought with sufficient specificity to enable the agency to ascertain which records are requested, and shall include the name and address to which the agency should address its response.
rules.trigger: Requester submits a written request
rules.source_language: A written request should identify or describe the records sought with sufficient specificity to enable the agency to ascertain which records are being requested and shall include the name and address to which the agency should address its response.
rules.notes: 'should' (specificity) vs 'shall' (name/address) — mixed authority in one sentence; kept as one atomic rule.

rules.legal_concept: Verbal/anonymous requests vs written-request prerequisite for remedies
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may fulfill verbal, written or anonymous requests, but a requester must submit a written request before pursuing the relief and remedies provided by the act.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks appeal/enforcement
rules.source_language: Agencies may fulfill verbal, written or anonymous requests; however, a written request is required to pursue the relief and remedies provided under the act.
rules.notes: Paraphrase — could not confirm exact wording verbatim; verify § 702 text.

rules.legal_concept: Agency discretion to release otherwise-exempt record
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may exercise discretion to make an otherwise-exempt record accessible if disclosure is not prohibited by law/court order, the record is not privileged, and the agency head determines the public interest favoring access outweighs any interest favoring restriction.
rules.trigger: Agency head weighs public interest
rules.source_language: An agency may exercise its discretion to make any otherwise exempt record accessible for inspection and copying if the disclosure is not prohibited by law or court order, the record is not protected by privilege, and the agency head determines the public interest favoring access outweighs any interest favoring restriction.
rules.notes: Paraphrase of § 506(c); verify exact text. Discretionary balancing — flag for human legal review, not auto-configuration.

rules.legal_concept: Medium of production
rules.atomic_rule: A record shall be provided in the medium requested if it exists in that medium; otherwise it shall be provided in the medium in which it exists.
rules.trigger: Requester specifies a medium
rules.source_language: A record being provided to a requester shall be provided in the medium requested if it exists in that medium; otherwise, it shall be provided in the medium in which it exists.

rules.legal_concept: Access during regular business hours
rules.atomic_rule: Public, legislative or financial records shall be available for access during the regular business hours of an agency.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks inspection
rules.source_language: Public records, legislative records or financial records shall be available for access during the regular business hours of an agency.
rules.notes: 'regular business hours' is the value the agency/city fills in — soft-standard, no statutory number.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to create a record
rules.atomic_rule: An agency is not required to create a record that does not currently exist, or to compile, maintain, format or organize a record in a manner in which the agency does not currently do so.
rules.trigger: Request would require creating/reformatting a record
rules.source_language: When responding to a request for access, an agency shall not be required to create a record which does not currently exist or to compile, maintain, format or organize a record in a manner in which the agency does not currently compile, maintain, format or organize the record.

rules.legal_concept: Response via publicly accessible electronic means
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may satisfy a request by notifying the requester that the record is available through publicly accessible electronic means, or may make records available through any publicly accessible electronic means.
rules.trigger: Record available electronically
rules.source_language: An agency may respond to a request by notifying the requester that the record is available through publicly accessible electronic means.
rules.notes: Paraphrase of § 704(a)-(b); verify exact wording.

rules.legal_concept: Conversion of electronically-available record to paper
rules.atomic_rule: A requester unable to access an electronically-available record may, within 30 days, submit a written request to have the record converted to paper, and the agency shall provide access within five days of that request.
rules.trigger: Requester cannot access record electronically
rules.clock_spec: requester: within 30 days of notice to request paper conversion; agency: within 5 days of that conversion request
rules.source_language: If the requester is unable to access the record electronically, the requester may, within 30 days following receipt of the agency's notice, submit a written request to the agency to have the record converted to paper. The agency shall provide access to the record in printed form within five days of the receipt of the written request for conversion to paper.
rules.notes: Reconstructed from fetched summary; verify exact wording and whether '5 days' are calendar or business days.

rules.legal_concept: Certified copy on request
rules.atomic_rule: If an agency's response grants access, the agency shall, upon request, provide a certified copy of the record if the requester pays the applicable fees under section 1307.
rules.trigger: Access granted AND requester asks for certified copy
rules.source_language: If an agency's response grants a request for access, the agency shall, upon request, provide the requester with a certified copy of the record if the requester pays the applicable fees under section 1307.

rules.legal_concept: Disposal of unretrieved copies
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may dispose of copies that a requester has not retrieved after 60 days following notification that the record is available, and may retain fees already paid.
rules.trigger: Copies not retrieved after notification
rules.source_language: An agency may dispose of a record that has not been retrieved by a requester after 60 days following notification that the record is available.
rules.notes: Paraphrase; verify section number and exact 60-day text.

rules.legal_concept: Designation of open-records officer
rules.atomic_rule: An agency shall designate an official or employee to act as the open-records officer.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: An agency shall designate an official or employee to act as the open-records officer.

rules.legal_concept: Open-records officer intake/tracking duties
rules.atomic_rule: Upon receiving a request, the open-records officer shall note the date received, compute the day the five-business-day response period expires, and maintain the request and related documents/response as an agency file.
rules.trigger: Request received by open-records officer
rules.source_language: Upon receiving a request, the open-records officer shall note the date of receipt, compute the day on which the five-day period will expire, and maintain an electronic or paper copy of the request, including all documents submitted with the request.
rules.notes: Paraphrase of § 502(b) tracking duties; verify exact wording.

rules.legal_concept: Records held by a contractor performing a governmental function
rules.atomic_rule: A public record in the possession of a contractor or other person performing a governmental function on behalf of an agency is considered a record of the agency; the request is made to the agency's open-records officer, who assesses applicable duplication fees.
rules.trigger: Requested record held by agency contractor
rules.source_language: A public record that is not in the possession of an agency but is in the possession of a party with whom the agency has contracted to perform a governmental function on behalf of the agency, and which directly relates to the governmental function and is not exempt under this act, shall be considered a public record of the agency for purposes of this act.
rules.notes: Paraphrase of § 506(d); verify exact text.

rules.legal_concept: Five-business-day response period
rules.atomic_rule: The agency's time to respond to a written request shall not exceed five business days from the date the written request is received by the open-records officer.
rules.trigger: Open-records officer receives a written request
rules.clock_spec: 5 business-days from date written request is received by the open-records officer
rules.source_language: The time for response shall not exceed five business days from the date the written request is received by the open-records officer for an agency.
rules.notes: This is both the initial-response deadline and the acknowledgment mechanism — PA has no separate acknowledgment window.

rules.legal_concept: Good-faith determination and prompt response standard
rules.atomic_rule: Upon receipt of a written request, an agency shall make a good faith effort to determine whether the requested item is a public/legislative/financial record and whether the agency has possession, custody or control of it, and respond as promptly as possible under the circumstances.
rules.trigger: Written request received
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "as promptly as possible under the circumstances existing at the time of the request" from request receipt
rules.source_language: Upon receipt of a written request for access to a record, an agency shall make a good faith effort to determine if the record requested is a public record, legislative record or financial record and whether the agency has possession, custody or control of the identified record, and to respond as promptly as possible under the circumstances existing at the time of the request.
rules.notes: Soft standard coexists with the hard 5-business-day cap in PA-0021; 'promptly as possible' is not a number.

rules.legal_concept: Grounds for extension of response time
rules.atomic_rule: The time for response may be extended if the open-records officer determines one of seven enumerated factors applies: (1) redaction under § 706; (2) retrieval from a remote location; (3) bona fide, specified staffing limitations; (4) legal review needed to determine access; (5) requester's noncompliance with agency policies; (6) requester's refusal to pay authorized fees; or (7) the extent or nature of the request precludes a timely response.
rules.trigger: Open-records officer identifies an extension factor
rules.source_language: (1) the request for access requires redaction of a record in accordance with section 706; (2) the request for access requires the retrieval of a record stored in a remote location; (3) a timely response to the request for access cannot be accomplished due to bona fide and specified staffing limitations; (4) a legal review is necessary to determine whether the record is a record subject to access under this act; (5) the requester has not complied with the agency's policies regarding access to records; (6) the requester refuses to pay applicable fees authorized by this act; or (7) the extent or nature of the request precludes a response within the required time period.
rules.notes: Conjunctive/enumerated exception kept in one row; each factor is a branch condition.

rules.legal_concept: Written extension notice
rules.atomic_rule: If an extension factor applies, the open-records officer shall send the requester written notice within five business days of receipt, stating that the request is under review, the reason, a reasonable expected response date, and an estimate of applicable fees.
rules.trigger: Extension factor under § 902(a) applies
rules.clock_spec: 5 business-days from receipt of the request (to send extension notice)
rules.source_language: Upon a determination that one of the factors listed in subsection (a) applies, the open-records officer shall send written notice to the requester within five business days of receipt of the request for access under subsection (a). The notice shall include a statement notifying the requester that the request for access is being reviewed, the reason for the review, a reasonable date that a response is expected to be provided and an estimate of applicable fees owed when the record becomes available.

rules.legal_concept: 30-day extension cap
rules.atomic_rule: If the expected response date is more than 30 days following the five business days allowed under § 901, the request is deemed denied unless the requester has agreed in writing to the extension.
rules.trigger: Expected response date exceeds 30 days past the initial 5 business days
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 30 calendar-days beyond the initial 5 business days; deemed denied on excess absent written agreement
rules.source_language: If the date that a response is expected to be provided is in excess of 30 days, following the five business days allowed for in section 901, the request for access shall be deemed denied unless the requester has agreed in writing to an extension to the date specified in the notice.

rules.legal_concept: Deemed denial after agreed extension lapses
rules.atomic_rule: If the requester agrees to the extension, the request is deemed denied on the day following the date specified in the notice if the agency has not provided a response by that date.
rules.trigger: Agreed extension date passes without a response
rules.clock_spec: terminal: deemed denied on the day following the date specified in the extension notice
rules.source_language: If the requester agrees to the extension, the request shall be deemed denied on the day following the date specified in the notice if the agency has not provided a response by that date.

rules.legal_concept: Deemed denial on failure to respond in five business days
rules.atomic_rule: If the agency fails to send its response within five business days of receiving the written request, the request is deemed denied.
rules.trigger: No response sent within 5 business days of receipt
rules.clock_spec: terminal: deemed denied when no response is sent within 5 business days of receipt by the open-records officer
rules.source_language: If the agency fails to send the response within five business days of receipt of the written request for access, the written request for access shall be deemed denied.

rules.legal_concept: Required contents of a written denial
rules.atomic_rule: A denial (in whole or in part) must be in writing and include: (1) a description of the record requested; (2) the specific reasons for denial including a citation of supporting legal authority; (3) the typed/printed name, title, business address, business telephone number and signature of the open-records officer; (4) the date of the response; and (5) the procedure to appeal the denial.
rules.trigger: Agency denies a written request in whole or part
rules.source_language: If an agency's response is a denial of a written request for access, whether in whole or in part, the denial shall be issued in writing and shall include: (1) A description of the record requested. (2) The specific reasons for the denial, including a citation of supporting legal authority. (3) The typed or printed name, title, business address, business telephone number and signature of the open-records officer on whose authority the denial is issued. (4) Date of the response. (5) The procedure to appeal the denial of access under this act.

rules.legal_concept: Denial of repeated, unreasonably burdensome requests
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may deny a requester access to a record if the requester has made repeated requests for that same record and the repeated requests have placed an unreasonable burden on the agency.
rules.trigger: Repeated requests for the same record imposing unreasonable burden
rules.source_language: An agency may deny a requester access to a record if the requester has made repeated requests for that same record and the repeated requests have placed an unreasonable burden on the agency.
rules.notes: Does not restrict the requester's ability to request other, different records.

rules.legal_concept: Denial of timely access due to disaster or record fragility
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may deny access where a timely response is impossible due to fire, flood or other disaster, or where the record is of such rarity/fragility that access could cause physical damage; contents should be made accessible when possible.
rules.trigger: Disaster or fragile/rare record
rules.source_language: An agency may deny a requester access to a record if timely access is not possible due to fire, flood or other disaster or to documents which are of such rarity or age that additional physical damage or loss might reasonably occur.
rules.notes: Paraphrase of § 506(b); verify exact wording.

rules.legal_concept: Grant accessible / deny non-accessible information
rules.atomic_rule: If a record contains information subject to access and information not subject to access, the agency's response shall grant access to the accessible information and deny access to the non-accessible information.
rules.trigger: Record mixes accessible and non-accessible information
rules.source_language: If an agency determines that a public record, legislative record or financial record contains information which is subject to access as well as information which is not subject to access, the agency's response shall grant access to the information which is subject to access and deny access to the information which is not subject to access.

rules.legal_concept: Redact non-accessible information and release remainder
rules.atomic_rule: Where non-accessible information cannot be separated, the agency shall redact the non-accessible information and grant access to the remainder; the agency may not deny access to the record if the non-accessible information can be redacted.
rules.trigger: Non-accessible information intertwined but redactable
rules.source_language: The agency may not deny access to the record if the information which is not subject to access is able to be redacted.

rules.legal_concept: Redaction treated as a denial
rules.atomic_rule: Information that an agency redacts under § 706 shall be deemed a denial under Chapter 9, and is therefore appealable.
rules.trigger: Agency redacts information from a produced record
rules.source_language: Information which an agency redacts in accordance with this subsection shall be deemed a denial under Chapter 9.

rules.legal_concept: Notice when a non-public record is produced
rules.atomic_rule: If, in response to a request, an agency produces a record that is not a public, legislative or financial record, the agency shall notify any third party that provided the record, the person who is the subject of the record, and the requester.
rules.trigger: Agency produces a record that is not public/legislative/financial
rules.source_language: If, in response to a request, an agency produces a record that is not a public record, legislative record or financial record, the agency shall notify any third party that provided the record to the agency, the person that is the subject of the record and the requester.

rules.legal_concept: Administrative-proceeding transcript before final adjudication
rules.atomic_rule: Prior to an adjudication becoming final, binding and nonappealable, a transcript of an administrative proceeding shall be provided to a requester by the agency stenographer or a court reporter, in accordance with agency procedure or an applicable contract.
rules.trigger: Transcript requested before adjudication is final
rules.source_language: Prior to an adjudication becoming final, binding and nonappealable, a transcript of an administrative proceeding shall be provided to a requester by the agency stenographer or a court reporter, in accordance with agency procedure or an applicable contract.

rules.legal_concept: Administrative-proceeding transcript after final adjudication
rules.atomic_rule: Following an adjudication becoming final, binding and nonappealable, a transcript of an administrative proceeding shall be provided to a requester in accordance with the duplication rates established in section 1307(b).
rules.trigger: Transcript requested after adjudication is final
rules.source_language: Following an adjudication becoming final, binding and nonappealable, a transcript of an administrative proceeding shall be provided to a requester in accordance with the duplication rates established in section 1307(b).

rules.legal_concept: Postage fee limited to actual cost
rules.atomic_rule: Fees for postage may not exceed the actual cost of mailing.
rules.trigger: Records mailed to requester
rules.source_language: Fees for postage may not exceed the actual cost of mailing.

rules.legal_concept: Duplication fees set by Office of Open Records schedule
rules.atomic_rule: Duplication fees for Commonwealth and local agencies (absent an agency-specific fee schedule) are established by the Office of Open Records and must be reasonable and based on prevailing fees for comparable duplication services provided by local business entities.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks duplication/copies
rules.source_language: Fees for duplication by a Commonwealth agency or a local agency shall be established by the Office of Open Records. Fees shall be reasonable and based on prevailing fees for comparable duplication services provided by local business entities.
rules.notes: Paraphrase of § 1307(b); the concrete per-page value lives in the OOR fee schedule (PA-0040).

rules.legal_concept: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule — per-copy photocopy rate
rules.atomic_rule: Under the OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule, an agency may charge up to $0.25 per copy for black-and-white photocopies (8.5x11 or 8.5x14), reduced to $0.20 per copy beyond the first 1,000 copies.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks paper copies
rules.source_language: Up to $0.25 per copy for black and white copies (a 'copy' is one side of an 8.5x11 or 8.5x14 page); up to $0.20 per copy beyond the first 1,000 copies.
rules.source_authority: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule (adopted Dec. 30, 2024), issued under 65 P.S. § 67.1307(b)
rules.notes: Value set by OOR schedule, not the statute; confirm current amounts and tiering against the linked PDF. Ceiling the city applies its actual (lower) value under.

rules.legal_concept: Fee for certification of copies
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may impose reasonable fees for official certification of copies where the certification is at the requester's behest and for the purpose of legally verifying the public record.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks a certified copy
rules.source_language: An agency may impose reasonable fees for official certification of copies if the certification is at the behest of the requester and for the purpose of legally verifying the public record.
rules.notes: Subsection letter approximate; 'reasonable' is a soft-standard, no fixed number.

rules.legal_concept: No fee for reviewing a record to determine access
rules.atomic_rule: No fee may be imposed for an agency's review of a record to determine whether it is a public, legislative or financial record subject to access.
rules.trigger: Agency reviews record for access determination
rules.source_language: No fee may be imposed for an agency's review of a record to determine whether the record is a public record, legislative record or financial record subject to access.
rules.notes: Fixed at $0 — agency may not charge for exemption-review/redaction-decision time.

rules.legal_concept: Waiver of duplication fees
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may waive duplication fees, including when the requester duplicates the record or when the agency deems it in the public interest to do so.
rules.trigger: Agency elects to waive fees
rules.source_language: An agency may waive the fees for duplication of a record, including, but not limited to, when: (1) the requester duplicates the record; or (2) the agency deems it is in the public interest to do so.

rules.legal_concept: Fee for records maintained only in electronic/nonpaper media
rules.atomic_rule: If a record is maintained only electronically or in nonpaper media, duplication fees are limited to the lesser of the paper-duplication fee or the original-media fee under § 1307(b), unless the requester specifically requests the more expensive medium.
rules.trigger: Record maintained only in nonpaper media
rules.source_language: If a record is only maintained electronically or in other nonpaper media, duplication fees shall be limited to the lesser of the fee for duplication on paper or the fee for duplication in the original media as provided by subsection (b) unless the requester specifically requests for the record to be duplicated in the more expensive medium.

rules.legal_concept: User fees for enhanced electronic access
rules.atomic_rule: If an agency offers enhanced electronic access to records in addition to the inspection-and-duplication access required by the act, it may establish user fees specifically for the provision of that enhanced electronic access.
rules.trigger: Agency offers optional enhanced electronic access
rules.source_language: If an agency offers enhanced electronic access to records in addition to making the records accessible for inspection and duplication by a requester as required by this act, the agency may establish user fees specifically for the provision of the enhanced electronic access.
rules.notes: Subsection letter approximate; enhanced access is optional, separate from statutory access.

rules.legal_concept: Prepayment of estimated fees over $100
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may require a requester to prepay an estimate of the authorized fees if the fees required to fulfill the request are expected to exceed $100.
rules.trigger: Estimated fees expected to exceed $100
rules.source_language: An agency may require a requester to prepay an estimate of the fees authorized under this section if the fees required to fulfill the request are expected to exceed $100.
rules.notes: $100 is a fixed trigger threshold; in practice prepayment gates production (may pause fulfillment until paid), and nonpayment is an extension ground under PA-0023 factor (6).

material_negatives.note: No separate acknowledgment deadline distinct from the substantive response. The five-business-day § 901 window is the only initial deadline; silence for five business days is a deemed denial, not a missed acknowledgment.

The statute does not mandate a particular form; § 703 allows any written request by several channels, and the OOR provides an optional standard form. No explicit statutory prohibition on requiring a form was located — treat 'form optional' as guidance-level, verify.

OOR guidance/case law states the day the request is received is not counted and the five-business-day period starts the next business day. This computation rule was not confirmed in the codified statute text this pass — flag for OOR-regulation / case-law verification.

No express statutory clarification-and-tolling clock. A vague request is handled via the § 902(a)(7) extension ground and the specificity standard in § 703, not a dedicated clarification pause with its own deadline.

The RTKL does not impose a distinct commercial-purpose fee surcharge on ordinary duplication; fees are governed by the OOR schedule and actual-cost limits regardless of purpose. (Contrast states with explicit commercial-use fee tiers.)

No search/retrieval labor fee is authorized for ordinary requests; § 1307(g) bars charging for access-determination review, and duplication fees are the primary permitted charge. Staff-time charges appear only in narrow contexts — verify against OOR guidance.

No explicit statutory record-preservation/litigation-hold triggered by the filing of a request or appeal was located in the RTKL text this pass; general retention is governed by separate records-management law (out of scope).

structural_branches.description: PA-specific administrative appeal stage before the Office of Open Records (Commonwealth/local agencies) or a designated judicial/legislative/other appeals officer — a mandatory review path with its own scheduling, document exchange, discretionary hearing, and 30-day final determination (§§ 1101-1102).

Two-track judicial review fork the engine must express: local-agency decisions go to the court of common pleas of the county (§ 1302), while Commonwealth/legislative/judicial-agency decisions go to Commonwealth Court (§ 1301).

Extension branch: on any of seven enumerated § 902(a) factors the request moves into a review state requiring a written extension notice within 5 business days, an expected-response date, and a 30-day cap gated on written requester agreement.

Third-party trade-secret/confidential-proprietary sub-process (§ 707(b)): a chained notice-and-input workflow (5 business days to notify, 5 for third-party input, 10 to decide) that the request enters when a flagged third-party record is implicated.
Any redaction is legally reclassified as a partial denial under Chapter 9 (§ 706), so a redacted production must branch into the denial/appeal machinery, not close as a grant.

Agency-head discretionary-release path (§ 506(c)): a balancing branch allowing release of otherwise-exempt records when public interest outweighs restriction — requires human legal judgment, not auto-configuration.

Electronic-availability response fork (§ 704): agency may close a request by pointing to publicly accessible electronic means, which opens a requester right to demand paper conversion (30-day request / 5-day agency turnaround).

rules.legal_concept: Right of any person to inspect or copy public records
rules.atomic_rule: Any person (individual, corporation, partnership, firm, organization, or association) has a right to inspect, copy, or receive an electronic transmission of any public record of a public body, subject to exemptions and reasonable time/place rules.
rules.trigger: None stated (universal right)
rules.source_language: (A)(1) A person has a right to inspect, copy, or receive an electronic transmission of any public record of a public body, except as otherwise provided by Section 30-4-40, or other state and federal laws, in accordance with reasonable rules concerning time and place of access.
rules.notes: Standing to make a request runs to any "person" (§ 30-4-20(b) defines person broadly); no citizenship required to request records. Note: standing to bring the § 30-4-100 enforcement suit is limited to a "citizen of the State" — see SC-0035.

rules.legal_concept: No residency or citizenship requirement to request records
rules.atomic_rule: There is no residency or state-citizenship requirement to request records; the right runs to any "person" without qualification as to residence.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: (A)(1) A person has a right to inspect, copy, or receive an electronic transmission of any public record of a public body, except as otherwise provided by Section 30-4-40, or other state and federal laws, in accordance with reasonable rules concerning time and place of access.
rules.notes: Emitted as an affirmative universal-access rule per contract. The statute grants the right to "a person" with no residency limitation; absence of a residency requirement is inferred from the operative grant, not from a clause expressly disclaiming residency.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A requester need not state a reason or purpose for the request; the statutory right to inspect/copy is unconditioned on purpose.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: (A)(1) A person has a right to inspect, copy, or receive an electronic transmission of any public record of a public body, except as otherwise provided by Section 30-4-40, or other state and federal laws, in accordance with reasonable rules concerning time and place of access.
rules.notes: Emitted as an affirmative universal-access rule per contract. The statute imposes no purpose/use condition on the right to inspect or copy (a fee-waiver public-interest inquiry exists at SC-0015, but no purpose statement is required to obtain records).

rules.legal_concept: Incarcerated persons excluded from FOIA right
rules.atomic_rule: The right to inspect/copy does not extend to individuals serving a sentence of imprisonment in a state, county, or federal correctional facility (whether in South Carolina or elsewhere); their constitutionally protected rights, including the right to call for evidence in a criminal prosecution, are preserved.
rules.trigger: Requester is serving a sentence of imprisonment
rules.source_language: This right does not extend to individuals serving a sentence of imprisonment in a state or county correctional facility in this State, in another state, or in a federal correctional facility; however, this may not be construed to prevent those individuals from exercising their constitutionally protected rights, including, but not limited to, their right to call for evidence in their favor in a criminal prosecution under the South Carolina Rules of Criminal Procedure.
rules.notes: Requester-class exclusion that routes/blocks handling — a branch the engine must execute. Preserves constitutional discovery rights, so the exclusion is not absolute as to criminal-prosecution evidence.

rules.legal_concept: Written request triggers statutory response duties
rules.atomic_rule: The statutory determination/response duties and their clocks are triggered by a written request for records made under the chapter.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a written request for records
rules.source_language: Each public body, upon written request for records made under this chapter, shall within ten days (excepting Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays) of the receipt of the request, notify the person making the request of its determination and the reasons for it
rules.notes: The determination/response obligation attaches to a "written request." Certain enumerated records are available in person without a written request (SC-0033). No statutory prescribed form/portal is mandated.

rules.legal_concept: Access subject to reasonable rules on time and place
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may condition access on reasonable rules concerning the time and place of access.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: A person has a right to inspect, copy, or receive an electronic transmission of any public record of a public body, except as otherwise provided by Section 30-4-40, or other state and federal laws, in accordance with reasonable rules concerning time and place of access.
rules.notes: "Reasonable" is an undefined standard — kept as source term, not converted to a value.

rules.legal_concept: Fees limited to actual cost of search, retrieval, and redaction
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may establish and collect reasonable fees not to exceed the actual cost of the search, retrieval, and redaction of records.
rules.trigger: Records request requiring search/retrieval/redaction
rules.source_language: The public body may establish and collect fees as provided for in this section. The public body may establish and collect reasonable fees not to exceed the actual cost of the search, retrieval, and redaction of records.
rules.effective_status: Current (2017 Act No. 67 revised fee structure)
rules.notes: Ceiling = actual cost; city sets the operative fee under it. Note redaction time IS chargeable here, but exemption-review time is NOT (SC-0013) — the two are distinguished.

rules.legal_concept: Search/retrieval/redaction labor rate capped at lowest-paid-qualified-employee salary
rules.atomic_rule: The fee for search, retrieval, or redaction shall not exceed the prorated hourly salary of the lowest paid employee who, in the custodian's reasonable discretion, has the necessary skill and training to perform the request.
rules.trigger: Charging a search/retrieval/redaction labor fee
rules.source_language: The fee for the search, retrieval, or redaction of records shall not exceed the prorated hourly salary of the lowest paid employee who, in the reasonable discretion of the custodian of the records, has the necessary skill and training to perform the request.
rules.notes: Ceiling tied to a computed value (prorated hourly salary of lowest-paid qualified employee); city supplies the actual rate under the cap.

rules.legal_concept: Copy fee capped at prevailing commercial rate
rules.atomic_rule: Fees for copies may not exceed the prevailing commercial rate for the producing of copies.
rules.trigger: Charging for copies of records
rules.source_language: Fees charged by a public body must be uniform for copies of the same record or document and may not exceed the prevailing commercial rate for the producing of copies.
rules.notes: Ceiling = prevailing commercial rate; no fixed per-page cents figure is set by statute (see material negatives).

rules.legal_concept: Copy fees must be uniform for the same record
rules.atomic_rule: Fees charged must be uniform for copies of the same record or document across requesters.
rules.trigger: Charging for copies of records
rules.source_language: Fees charged by a public body must be uniform for copies of the same record or document and may not exceed the prevailing commercial rate for the producing of copies.
rules.notes: Split from SC-0009: a non-discrimination standard (uniformity) distinct from the commercial-rate ceiling, drawn from the same sentence.

rules.legal_concept: No copy charge for records transmitted electronically
rules.atomic_rule: Copy charges may not be applied to records that are transmitted in an electronic format.
rules.trigger: Record is transmitted in electronic format
rules.source_language: Copy charges may not apply to records that are transmitted in an electronic format.
rules.notes: Fixed value of $0 for the copy-charge component when delivery is electronic. Search/retrieval/redaction labor may still be charged; only the per-copy charge is barred.

rules.legal_concept: Charge permitted for converting non-electronic records to electronic format
rules.atomic_rule: If records are not in electronic format and the public body agrees to produce them electronically, it may charge for the staff time required to transfer the documents to electronic format.
rules.trigger: Records not in electronic format and public body agrees to produce electronically
rules.source_language: If records are not in electronic format and the public body agrees to produce them in electronic format, the public body may charge for the staff time required to transfer the documents to electronic format.
rules.notes: Chargeable amount is "staff time," bounded by the labor-rate cap (SC-0008); no separate rate is fixed. Conversion charge is an exception to the no-electronic-copy-charge rule (SC-0011).

rules.legal_concept: No fee for examination/review to determine disclosability
rules.atomic_rule: Fees may not be charged for examination and review to determine if documents are subject to disclosure.
rules.trigger: Time spent reviewing records to determine disclosability
rules.source_language: Fees may not be charged for examination and review to determine if the documents are subject to disclosure.
rules.notes: Fixed $0 for exemption-review labor. Distinguish from redaction, which IS chargeable under SC-0007/SC-0008 — the boundary between reviewing-for-exemption (free) and redacting (chargeable) is a known human-review flag.

rules.legal_concept: Records furnished at lowest possible cost
rules.atomic_rule: Records must be furnished at the lowest possible cost to the person requesting them.
rules.trigger: Furnishing records for a fee
rules.source_language: The records must be furnished at the lowest possible cost to the person requesting the records.
rules.notes: Undefined standard ("lowest possible cost") governing how fees are computed; kept as a soft standard, not converted to a number.

rules.legal_concept: Discretionary fee waiver/reduction in the public interest
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may furnish documents without charge or at a reduced charge where it determines that waiver or reduction is in the public interest because furnishing the information primarily benefits the general public.
rules.trigger: Agency determination that furnishing primarily benefits the general public
rules.source_language: Documents may be furnished when appropriate without charge or at a reduced charge where the agency determines that waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest because furnishing the information can be considered as primarily benefiting the general public.
rules.notes: Discretionary branch (waive / reduce / no waiver); the engine must be able to execute a fee-waiver decision path.

rules.legal_concept: No charge to General Assembly members for legislative-duty requests
rules.atomic_rule: Members of the General Assembly may receive copies of records or documents at no charge when the request relates to their legislative duties.
rules.trigger: Requester is a member of the General Assembly and request relates to legislative duties
rules.source_language: However, members of the General Assembly may receive copies of records or documents at no charge from public bodies when their request relates to their legislative duties.
rules.notes: Special-requester-class branch (fee = $0) conditioned on legislative-duty nexus.

rules.legal_concept: Public body must post a fee schedule online
rules.atomic_rule: A public body shall develop a fee schedule and post it online.
rules.trigger: None stated (standing obligation governing fees charged on requests)
rules.source_language: The public body shall develop a fee schedule to be posted online.
rules.notes: Included because the fee applied to an individual request must come from a published schedule; borderline administrative, but directly binds the fee value used in processing.

rules.legal_concept: Deposit up to 25% of anticipated reproduction cost before search/copying
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may require, prior to searching for or making copies of records, a deposit not to exceed twenty-five percent of the total reasonably anticipated cost for reproduction of the records.
rules.trigger: Before the public body searches for or copies records
rules.source_language: A deposit not to exceed twenty-five percent of the total reasonably anticipated cost for reproduction of the records may be required prior to the public body searching for or making copies of records.
rules.notes: Ceiling = 25% of anticipated reproduction cost; city sets whether/how much deposit to require under the cap. When a deposit is required, the production clock runs from deposit receipt (SC-0026).

rules.legal_concept: Full cost due at time of production
rules.atomic_rule: The full amount of the total cost must be paid at the time of the production of the request.
rules.trigger: Production of the requested records
