rules.source_language: The full amount of the total cost must be paid at the time of the production of the request.
rules.notes: Payment step gating release; balance beyond any deposit is collected at production.

rules.legal_concept: 10-business-day determination notice
rules.atomic_rule: The public body shall, within ten days (excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays) of receipt of a written request, notify the requester of its determination and the reasons for it.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a written request for records
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days (excluding Sat/Sun/legal holidays) from receipt of request
rules.source_language: Each public body, upon written request for records made under this chapter, shall within ten days (excepting Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays) of the receipt of the request, notify the person making the request of its determination and the reasons for it; provided, however, that if the record is more than twenty-four months old at the date the request is made, the public body has twenty days (excepting Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays) of the receipt to make this notification.
rules.effective_status: Current (2017 Act No. 67 revised time limits)
rules.notes: Fixed count; the determination notice is a determination of public availability, not necessarily production. Distinct 20-day track for older records at SC-0021.

rules.legal_concept: 20-business-day determination notice for records over 24 months old
rules.atomic_rule: If the record is more than twenty-four months old at the date the request is made, the public body has twenty days (excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays) of receipt to make the determination notification.
rules.trigger: Requested record is more than 24 months old at the date of request
rules.clock_spec: 20 business-days (excluding Sat/Sun/legal holidays) from receipt of request
rules.source_language: provided, however, that if the record is more than twenty-four months old at the date the request is made, the public body has twenty days (excepting Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays) of the receipt to make this notification.
rules.notes: Record-age branch modifying the determination clock; age measured at date of request.

rules.legal_concept: Determination must state reasons
rules.atomic_rule: The determination notice must state the public body's determination and the reasons for it.
rules.trigger: Issuing the determination on a request
rules.source_language: notify the person making the request of its determination and the reasons for it
rules.notes: Content requirement for the notice (a required document element), split from the deadline in SC-0020.

rules.legal_concept: 30-calendar-day production after determination
rules.atomic_rule: If the request is granted, the record must be furnished or made available for inspection or copying no later than thirty calendar days from the date the final determination was provided.
rules.trigger: Final determination granting the request was provided (and no deposit required)
rules.clock_spec: 30 calendar-days from date final determination was provided
rules.source_language: If the request is granted, the record must be furnished or made available for inspection or copying no later than thirty calendar days from the date on which the final determination was provided, unless the records are more than twenty-four months old, in which case the public body has no later than thirty-five calendar days from the date on which the final determination was provided.
rules.notes: Calendar days (not business days), unlike the determination clock. Applies when no deposit is required; if a deposit is required, the clock runs from deposit receipt (SC-0026).

rules.legal_concept: 35-calendar-day production for records over 24 months old
rules.atomic_rule: If the granted records are more than twenty-four months old, they must be furnished no later than thirty-five calendar days from the date the final determination was provided.
rules.trigger: Granted records are more than 24 months old
rules.clock_spec: 35 calendar-days from date final determination was provided
rules.source_language: unless the records are more than twenty-four months old, in which case the public body has no later than thirty-five calendar days from the date on which the final determination was provided.
rules.notes: Record-age branch on the production clock.

rules.legal_concept: Production clock runs from deposit receipt when deposit required
rules.atomic_rule: If a deposit is required, the record must be furnished or made available no later than thirty calendar days (thirty-five if records are more than 24 months old) from the date the deposit is received.
rules.trigger: A deposit under subsection (B) is required by the public body
rules.clock_spec: 30 calendar-days (35 if records >24 months old) from date deposit is received
rules.source_language: If a deposit as provided in subsection (B) is required by the public body, the record must be furnished or made available for inspection or copying no later than thirty calendar days from the date on which the deposit is received, unless the records are more than twenty-four months old, in which case the public body has no later than thirty-five calendar days from the date on which the deposit was received to fulfill the request.
rules.notes: Alternate start event for the production clock: deposit receipt rather than determination date. Requiring a deposit effectively resets the production start to when the deposit is paid.

rules.legal_concept: Deadlines extendable by written mutual agreement
rules.atomic_rule: The response, determination, and production deadlines may be extended by written mutual agreement of the public body and the requesting party, which agreement shall not be unreasonably withheld.
rules.trigger: Written mutual agreement of the public body and requester
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: extension for the period set by written mutual agreement, from the affected deadline
rules.source_language: The various response, determination, and production deadlines provided by this subsection are subject to extension by written mutual agreement of the public body and the requesting party at issue, and this agreement shall not be unreasonably withheld.
rules.notes: Applies to all § 30-4-30(C) clocks. Extension length is whatever the parties agree — no statutory cap; agreement not to be unreasonably withheld.

rules.legal_concept: Constructive approval on failure to timely notify
rules.atomic_rule: If written notification of the determination is neither mailed, electronically transmitted, nor personally delivered to the requester within the statutory time, the request must be considered approved as to nonexempt records or information.
rules.trigger: No determination notice delivered within the § 30-4-30(C) deadline
rules.clock_spec: Deemed approved upon expiry of the 10/20 business-day determination deadline without notice
rules.source_language: If written notification of the determination of the public body as to the availability of the requested public record is neither mailed, electronically transmitted, nor personally delivered to the person requesting the document within the time set forth by this section, the request must be considered approved as to nonexempt records or information.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: silence = deemed approval (constructive grant), a terminal clock event. Limited to nonexempt records; exemptions survive (SC-0029).

rules.legal_concept: Exemptions not waived by failure to respond
rules.atomic_rule: Exemptions from disclosure under § 30-4-40 or other state/federal law are not waived by the public body's failure to respond within the statutory time.
rules.trigger: Deemed approval arises from non-response
rules.source_language: Exemptions from disclosure as set forth in Section 30-4-40 or by other state or federal laws are not waived by the public body's failure to respond as set forth in this subsection.
rules.notes: Qualifies the deemed-approval trigger: constructive grant reaches only nonexempt material; the body may still withhold exempt records.

rules.legal_concept: Records provided in convenient and practical form when equally convenient for the body
rules.atomic_rule: Records must be provided in a form both convenient and practical for use by the requester, if it is equally convenient for the public body to provide them in that form.
rules.trigger: Requester specifies a form of production
rules.source_language: Records must be provided in a form that is both convenient and practical for use by the person requesting copies of the records concerned, if it is equally convenient for the public body to provide the records in this form.
rules.notes: Format-of-production standard conditioned on "equally convenient" for the body — an undefined standard, kept as source term.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to create a nonexistent electronic version
rules.atomic_rule: A public body is not required to create an electronic version of a public record when one does not exist in order to fulfill a records request.
rules.trigger: Requested electronic version does not exist
rules.source_language: A public body is not required to create an electronic version of a public record when one does not exist to fulfill a records request.
rules.notes: Limits the electronic-transmission right: no obligation to create records that don't exist in electronic form.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to separate exempt from nonexempt and release nonexempt
rules.atomic_rule: If a public record contains material that is not exempt under § 30-4-40(a), the public body shall separate the exempt and nonexempt material and make the nonexempt material available.
rules.trigger: Record contains a mix of exempt and nonexempt material
rules.source_language: If any public record contains material which is not exempt under subsection (a) of this section, the public body shall separate the exempt and nonexempt material and make the nonexempt material available in accordance with the requirements of this chapter.
rules.notes: Segregability/redaction duty. Redaction labor is chargeable (SC-0007/SC-0008) but exemption-review is not (SC-0013).

rules.legal_concept: Website posting deemed compliance with in-person availability
rules.atomic_rule: A public body that places the § 30-4-30(D) records in a convenient and practical form on a publicly available Internet website is deemed compliant with subsection (D), provided it also produces documents on request under the section.
rules.trigger: Enumerated (D) records posted on a public website
rules.source_language: A public body that places the records in a form that is both convenient and practical for use on a publicly available Internet website is deemed to be in compliance with the provisions of subsection (D), provided that the public body also shall produce documents pursuant to this section upon request.
rules.notes: Compliance-by-publication path for the walk-in category; does not relieve the general on-request production duty.

rules.legal_concept: 15-business-day window for agency to seek order barring disclosure of law-enforcement recording
rules.atomic_rule: For disclosure of law-enforcement vehicle-mounted/dashboard recording data of an officer-involved incident resulting in death, injury, property damage, or use of deadly force, the agency may apply to circuit court for a non-disclosure order; the hearing must be requested within fifteen days (excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays) of receipt of the request for disclosure, and the hearing is held in camera.
rules.trigger: Request to disclose qualifying law-enforcement vehicle/dashboard recording data
rules.clock_spec: 15 business-days (excluding Sat/Sun/legal holidays) from receipt of the disclosure request to request a hearing
rules.source_language: A law enforcement or public safety agency may apply to the circuit court for an order to prevent the disclosure of the video or audio recording data. Notice of the request and of the hearing must be provided to the person seeking the record. A hearing must be requested within fifteen days (excepting Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays) of the receipt of the request for disclosure and the hearing shall be held in-camera.
rules.notes: Special-record workflow with its own clock, notice, and in-camera hearing. Court may order withholding only on clear-and-convincing showing under § 30-4-40(a)(3) (see special-records table); may order redacted release.

material_negatives.note: No separate receipt-acknowledgment requirement distinct from the substantive determination. SC's first statutory duty is the 10-business-day (20 for records >24 months) determination-and-reasons notice under § 30-4-30(C); there is no earlier 'we received your request' acknowledgment obligation. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

No statewide fixed per-page copy rate. § 30-4-30(B) caps copy fees at the 'prevailing commercial rate' (a ceiling) and requires uniformity, but sets no cents-per-page number; the city supplies the value under the commercial-rate ceiling (see SC-0009).

No statutory duty for the public body to help a requester clarify or narrow a request, and no clarification clock that tolls or restarts the response deadlines. The body's remedy for a vague/overbroad request is to seek a court hearing under § 30-4-110(A) (SC-0038), not a statutory clarify-and-toll mechanism.

No statutory administrative or internal-agency appeal stage, and no AG/records-authority adjudicative review of denials. Enforcement is exclusively judicial via circuit court (§ 30-4-100). The SC Attorney General issues advisory FOIA opinions but has no statutory power to compel disclosure.

No statutorily prescribed request form, portal, or delivery channel. § 30-4-30(C) requires a 'written request' to trigger the response duties but does not mandate a particular medium or form (email, letter, and portal all qualify if written).

No unilateral good-cause extension of the § 30-4-30(C) determination/production clocks by the public body. Extensions require written MUTUAL agreement of the body and requester (SC-0027); the statute provides no body-only extension for volume/complexity.

No statutory rolling/installment production scheme (records produced in tranches with staggered deadlines). The statute sets a single production deadline (30/35 calendar days) from determination or deposit receipt.

structural_branches.description: Requester-class gate: incarcerated persons are excluded from the FOIA inspect/copy right (constitutional discovery rights preserved). § 30-4-30(A)(1).

Alternate intake/production path: enumerated record classes (recent minutes, incident reports, confinement docs, meeting-distributed docs, within stated lookback windows) available in person, immediately, without a written request or determination clock. § 30-4-30(D).
Compliance-by-publication branch: posting the (D) records online satisfies the in-person availability duty. § 30-4-30(E).
Terminal state: silence past the 10/20-business-day determination deadline = request deemed approved as to nonexempt records (exemptions not waived). § 30-4-30(C).
Discretionary fee decision path: waive/reduce/charge based on public-interest / primary-benefit-to-general-public finding. § 30-4-30(B).
Special-requester branch: General Assembly members pay no charge for legislative-duty requests. § 30-4-30(B).

SC's only enforcement path is judicial (circuit court declaratory/injunctive), citizen-of-the-State standing, 1-year limit, with statutory 10-day-to-hearing and 6-month-to-conclude court clocks. No administrative/internal appeal exists. § 30-4-100.
Body-initiated diversion path: the public body routes an improper/burdensome request, or one it cannot resolve for exemption, to circuit court instead of answering. § 30-4-110(A).
Reverse-FOIA branch: a third party with a specific interest may demand a hearing/intervene before release of records in enumerated § 30-4-40(a) exempt categories. § 30-4-110(B).

Special-record workflow for law-enforcement vehicle/dashboard recordings of qualifying officer-involved incidents: 15-business-day agency hearing window, notice to requester, in-camera hearing, clear-and-convincing standard. § 30-4-50(A)(9).

rules.legal_concept: Right of inspection limited to Tennessee citizens
rules.atomic_rule: Access under the TPRA runs to any citizen of Tennessee; those in charge of records shall not refuse inspection to any citizen unless otherwise provided by state law.
rules.trigger: Any request for personal inspection of a state, county, or municipal record.
rules.source_language: All state, county and municipal records shall, at all times during business hours, which for public hospitals shall be during the business hours of their administrative offices, be open for personal inspection by any citizen of this state, and those in charge of the records shall not refuse such right of inspection to any citizen, unless otherwise provided by state law.
rules.effective_status: Current (verified against 2021 codification; core provisions unchanged in 2024 code)
rules.notes: Tennessee is a citizen-restricted state; does NOT satisfy eligibility.any_person or eligibility.no_residency_requirement. Tennessee Supreme Court has construed 'citizen' to include incarcerated Tennessee inmates. Entity may elect to serve non-citizens (see TN-0003).

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose / intended use required
rules.atomic_rule: The TPRA does not distinguish requests based on the requester's intended use; a requester need not state a purpose to access open records.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional).
rules.source_language: The TPRA does not distinguish requests for inspection of records based on intended use, be it for research, personal, or commercial purposes. Likewise, this Schedule of Reasonable Charges does not make a distinction in the charges assessed based on the purpose of a record request.
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.F (implementing Tenn. Code Ann. § 8-4-604); Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule with the shared eligibility key per instructions. Narrow exception: certain documents requested for a specific commercial use carry special fees under § 10-7-506(c) (see TN-0040).

rules.legal_concept: Entity may choose to serve non-Tennessee-citizens
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity may determine, in its public records policy, whether to respond to TPRA requests from persons who are not citizens of Tennessee.
rules.trigger: Adoption of the entity's public records policy.
rules.source_language: The TPRA authorizes a governmental entity to determine the following with respect to each entity's public records policy: A. Whether to respond to TPRA requests by persons who are not citizens of Tennessee;
rules.source_authority: OORC Model Public Records Policy, Policy Considerations § I.A
rules.notes: City-elected branch: a locally-filled fork on whether the citizenship gate (TN-0001) is enforced.

rules.legal_concept: Optional government-issued photo ID as prerequisite to access
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity may require government-issued photo identification as a prerequisite to providing access to records.
rules.trigger: Adoption of the entity's public records policy electing to require ID.
rules.source_language: The TPRA authorizes a governmental entity to determine the following with respect to each entity's public records policy: ... B. Whether to require government-issued photo identification as a prerequisite to providing access to records;
rules.source_authority: OORC Model Public Records Policy, Policy Considerations § I.B; statutory basis Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(A)(vi)
rules.notes: OORC FAQ states the photo ID 'includes an address.' Exact verbatim of statutory subsection (a)(7)(A)(vi) not opened; the permission itself is verbatim from the OORC Model Policy. City-elected branch.

rules.legal_concept: Permitted channels for submitting inspection requests
rules.atomic_rule: Requests to view public records may be submitted in person, by telephone, fax, mail, or email (if the entity uses such means for official business), or via internet portal (if the entity maintains one for records requests).
rules.trigger: A request to view public records.
rules.source_language: Requests to view public records may be submitted in person or by telephone, fax, mail, or email if the governmental entity uses such means of communication to transact official business, or via internet portal if the governmental entity maintains an internet portal that is used for accepting public records requests.

rules.legal_concept: Entity may require copy requests in writing or on a form
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity may require a request for COPIES of public records to be in writing, on a form complying with subsection (c), or on a form developed by the Office of Open Records Counsel.
rules.trigger: A request for copies (as opposed to inspection only).
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may require a request for copies of public records to be: In writing; On a form that complies with subsection (c); or On a form developed by the office of open records counsel.
rules.notes: City-elected branch. If a form is required for copies it must be attached to the entity's public records policy.

rules.legal_concept: Request must be sufficiently detailed
rules.atomic_rule: Any request for inspection or copying must be sufficiently detailed to enable the governmental entity to identify the specific records sought.
rules.trigger: Submission of a records request.
rules.source_language: Any request for inspection or copying of a public record shall be sufficiently detailed to enable the governmental entity to identify the specific records for inspection and copying.
rules.notes: Gate for lack-of-specificity denial (TN-0027) and clarification assistance (TN-0009).

rules.legal_concept: Offer to assist narrowing/clarifying a non-specific request
rules.atomic_rule: If a request lacks specificity, the coordinator/custodian may deny for lack of specificity while offering to assist in clarification, or contact the requestor to see if the request can be narrowed.
rules.trigger: A request that is not sufficiently detailed, or is for a large volume of records.
rules.source_language: The request lacks specificity. (Offer to assist in clarification) ... If appropriate, contact the requestor to see if the request can be narrowed.
rules.source_authority: OORC Model Public Records Policy §§ III.A.2.b.ii, III.A.2.c
rules.notes: No statutory clarification clock: the TPRA does not toll or restart the 7-business-day clock while clarification is sought (see material negatives).

rules.legal_concept: Referral when another entity is the custodian
rules.atomic_rule: If requested records are in the custody of a different governmental entity and the correct entity is known, the coordinator advises the requestor of the correct entity and its coordinator.
rules.trigger: Requested records are held by a different governmental entity than the one receiving the request.
rules.source_language: If requested records are in the custody of a different governmental entity, and the PRRC knows the correct governmental entity, the PRRC should advise the requestor of the correct governmental entity and PRRC for that entity if known.
rules.source_authority: OORC Model Public Records Policy § III.A.2.e
rules.notes: Also a permitted denial ground where the entity is not the custodian (TN-0028).

rules.legal_concept: Cannot avoid disclosure by delegating to a private entity
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity is prohibited from avoiding its disclosure obligations by contractually delegating its responsibility to a private entity.
rules.trigger: Records held by a private entity under contract with the governmental entity.
rules.source_language: A governmental entity is prohibited from avoiding its disclosure obligations by contractually delegating its responsibility to a private entity.
rules.notes: Blocks a 'private contractor holds it' denial; affects coverage/routing of the request.

rules.legal_concept: Prompt availability for inspection
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian or the custodian's designee shall promptly make available for inspection any public record not specifically exempt from disclosure.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a request to inspect a non-exempt public record.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "promptly" from request receipt
rules.source_language: The custodian of a public record or the custodian's designee shall promptly make available for inspection any public record not specifically exempt from disclosure.
rules.notes: 'Promptly' is an undefined soft standard — do not convert to a day count. The 7-business-day rule (TN-0015) applies only when prompt availability is not practicable.

rules.legal_concept: Seven-business-day response requirement
rules.atomic_rule: When it is not practicable for a record to be promptly available, the custodian shall within seven (7) business days take one of three actions: (i) make it available, (ii) deny in writing with basis, or (iii) furnish in writing the time reasonably necessary to produce it.
rules.trigger: It is not practicable for the record to be promptly available for inspection.
rules.clock_spec: fixed: 7 business-days from custodian's receipt of the request
rules.source_language: In the event it is not practicable for the record to be promptly available for inspection, the custodian shall, within seven (7) business days: Make the information available to the requestor; Deny the request in writing or by completing a records request response form developed by the office of open records counsel. The response shall include the basis for the denial; or Furnish the requester in writing, or by completing a records request response form developed by the office of open records counsel, the time reasonably necessary to produce the record or information.
rules.notes: Fixed statutory window (business days, not calendar). This is the core response clock; branches into three outcomes (TN-0016, TN-0026) and, on silence, deemed denial (TN-0017).

rules.legal_concept: Written notice of time reasonably necessary to produce
rules.atomic_rule: As the third permitted response, the custodian furnishes the requester, in writing or on the OORC response form, the time reasonably necessary to produce the record or information.
rules.trigger: Custodian elects option (iii) within the 7-business-day window because more time is needed.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "time reasonably necessary to produce" stated by custodian, from request receipt
rules.source_language: Furnish the requester in writing, or by completing a records request response form developed by the office of open records counsel, the time reasonably necessary to produce the record or information.
rules.notes: The production deadline is a custodian-stated soft standard, not a fixed statutory number.

rules.legal_concept: Constructive (deemed) denial on failure to respond
rules.atomic_rule: Failure to respond as described in subdivision (a)(2) constitutes a denial, and the requester has the right to bring an action under § 10-7-505.
rules.trigger: Custodian fails to take any of the (a)(2)(B) actions within seven business days.
rules.clock_spec: terminal: silence past 7 business-days = denial, triggering § 10-7-505 action
rules.source_language: Failure to respond to the request as described in subdivision (a)(2) shall constitute a denial and the person making the request shall have the right to bring an action as provided in § 10-7-505.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver #3 (deemed/constructive denial trigger). Terminal event; leads to judicial petition (TN-0042).

rules.legal_concept: Most economical and efficient production
rules.atomic_rule: When assessing fees for copies, records custodians shall utilize the most economical and efficient method of producing the requested records.
rules.trigger: A request for copies of public records.
rules.source_language: When assessing a fee for items covered under this section, records custodians shall utilize the most economical and efficient method of producing the requested records.
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § III.A

rules.legal_concept: Segmented production of large-volume requests
rules.atomic_rule: If production should be segmented because of a large volume of records, the custodian uses the response form to notify the requestor that production will be in segments and a production schedule will be provided as expeditiously as practicable.
rules.trigger: Records request is for a large volume of records, or additional time is needed to prepare records for access.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: production schedule "as expeditiously as practicable" from response form notice
rules.source_language: If a records custodian reasonably determines production of records should be segmented because the records request is for a large volume of records, or additional time is necessary to prepare the records for access, the records custodian shall use the Public Records Request Response Form to notify the requestor that production of the records will be in segments and that a records production schedule will be provided as expeditiously as practicable.
rules.source_authority: OORC Model Public Records Policy § III.B.4
rules.notes: Tennessee-specific production path (rolling/segmented production with a schedule).

rules.legal_concept: Cure for omitted responsive records
rules.atomic_rule: If the custodian discovers responsive records were omitted, the custodian should contact the requestor about the omission and produce the records as quickly as practicable.
rules.trigger: Discovery, after responding, that responsive records were omitted.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: produce omitted records "as quickly as practicable" from discovery
rules.source_language: If a records custodian discovers records responsive to a records request were omitted, the records custodian should contact the requestor concerning the omission and produce the records as quickly as practicable.
rules.source_authority: OORC Model Public Records Policy § III.B.5

rules.legal_concept: Delivery of copies when not retrieved in person
rules.atomic_rule: If a requestor chooses not to personally retrieve copies and the actual delivery cost plus other permitted charges are paid or waived, the custodian must deliver the copies via USPS First-Class Mail; other means (including electronic) are discretionary and may carry delivery costs.
rules.trigger: Requestor elects not to retrieve copies in person.
rules.source_language: If a requestor chooses not to personally retrieve records and the actual cost of delivering the copies, in addition to any other permitted charges, have been paid by the requestor or otherwise waived pursuant to the public records policy, then a records custodian is obligated to deliver the copies via USPS First-Class Mail. It is within the discretion of a records custodian to agree to deliver copies of records through other means, including electronically, and to assess the costs related to such delivery.
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § III.D

rules.legal_concept: Redaction of confidential information and release of remainder
rules.atomic_rule: Information made confidential by state law shall be redacted whenever possible, and the redacted record shall be made available for inspection and copying.
rules.trigger: A responsive record contains information made confidential by state law.
rules.source_language: Information made confidential by state law shall be redacted whenever possible, and the redacted record shall be made available for inspection and copying.
rules.notes: Segregability duty — confidential portions redacted rather than whole-record withholding.

rules.legal_concept: Redaction is not creation of a new record
rules.atomic_rule: The redaction of confidential information shall not constitute the creation of a new record.
rules.trigger: Redaction performed to release an otherwise-confidential-laden record.
rules.source_language: The redaction of confidential information shall not constitute the creation of a new record.
rules.notes: Forecloses a 'no duty to create' defense (TN-0010) as applied to redaction.

rules.legal_concept: Provide general basis for redaction
rules.atomic_rule: Whenever a redacted record is provided, the custodian should provide the requestor the basis for redaction, stated generally so as not to disclose the confidential information.
rules.trigger: A redacted record is provided to the requestor.
rules.source_language: Whenever a redacted record is provided, a records custodian should provide the requestor with the basis for redaction. The basis given for redaction shall be general in nature and not disclose confidential information.
rules.source_authority: OORC Model Public Records Policy § III.C.2

rules.legal_concept: Written denial stating basis (on OORC response form)
rules.atomic_rule: A denial must be in writing (or on the OORC-developed records request response form) and shall include the basis for the denial.
rules.trigger: Custodian elects to deny the request (option (ii)).
rules.source_language: Deny the request in writing or by completing a records request response form developed by the office of open records counsel. The response shall include the basis for the denial.
rules.notes: Standardized denial instrument is the OORC Public Record Request Response Form.

rules.legal_concept: Denial where state/federal law prohibits disclosure
rules.atomic_rule: A request may be denied where an exemption makes the record not subject to disclosure under the TPRA; the applicable exemption must be provided in the written denial.
rules.trigger: A state, federal, or other law prohibits disclosure of the requested record.
rules.source_language: An exemption makes the record not subject to disclosure under the TPRA. (Provide the exemption in written denial)
rules.source_authority: OORC Model Public Records Policy § III.A.2.b.iii
rules.notes: Exemptions themselves (§ 10-7-504 et al.) are not inventoried here; see Special Record Types.

rules.legal_concept: Denial where entity is not custodian or record does not exist
rules.atomic_rule: A request may be denied where the governmental entity is not the custodian of the requested records, or the records do not exist.
rules.trigger: Entity does not hold the records, or no responsive record exists.
rules.source_language: The Governmental Entity is not the custodian of the requested records. ... The records do not exist.
rules.source_authority: OORC Model Public Records Policy §§ III.A.2.b.iv, III.A.2.b.v
rules.notes: Pairs with no-duty-to-create (TN-0010) and wrong-entity referral (TN-0012).

rules.legal_concept: Per-page charge for black-and-white copies
rules.atomic_rule: For each standard 8.5x11 or 8.5x14 black-and-white copy produced, a records custodian may assess a per-page charge of up to 15 cents ($0.15).
rules.trigger: Production of standard-size black-and-white copies.
rules.source_language: For each standard 8 1/2" x 11" or 8 1/2" x 14" copy produced, a records custodian may assess a per page charge of up to 15 cents ($0.15) for black and white copies ... If producing duplex (front and back) copies, a charge for two separate pages may be imposed for each single duplex copy.
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § II.A
rules.notes: Ceiling (up to $0.15). City sets the operative rate at or below this in its policy; a higher rate requires documented actual-cost analysis (TN-0031). Duplex counts as two pages.

rules.legal_concept: Per-page charge for color copies
rules.atomic_rule: For each standard 8.5x11 or 8.5x14 color copy produced, a records custodian may assess a per-page charge of up to 50 cents ($0.50).
rules.trigger: Production of standard-size color copies.
rules.source_language: For each standard 8 1/2" x 11" or 8 1/2" x 14" copy produced, a records custodian may assess a per page charge of ... up to 50 cents ($0.50) for color copies.
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § II.A
rules.notes: Ceiling. If color is dearer and the record can be produced in B&W, the custodian must advise the requestor it can be produced in B&W unless the requestor will pay the higher color charge (Schedule § II.B).

rules.legal_concept: Actual-cost charges above the schedule with documentation
rules.atomic_rule: If actual costs are higher than the schedule amounts, or records are produced on a non-standard medium, the entity may develop its own charges but must document 'actual cost' calculation and reasoning in an adopted policy; charges above $0.15 (B&W) / $0.50 (color) require documented actual-cost analysis.
rules.trigger: Actual production cost exceeds the schedule amounts, or non-standard medium is used.
rules.source_language: If a governmental entity's actual costs are higher than those reflected above ... the governmental entity may develop its own charges. The governmental entity must establish a schedule of charges documenting "actual cost" and state the calculation and reasoning for its charges in a properly adopted policy. ... Charges greater than 15 cents ($0.15) for black and white copies and 50 cents ($0.50) for color copies can be assessed or collected only when there is documented analysis of the fact that the higher charges represent the governmental entity's actual cost of producing such material, unless there exists another basis in law for such charges.
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § II.C
rules.notes: Same concept as the ceiling rows (TN-0029/0030) under a different basis — do not split as a separate rate; this is the escape valve above the guideline ceiling.

rules.legal_concept: First hour of labor not chargeable (labor threshold)
rules.atomic_rule: The labor threshold is the first (1st) hour of labor reasonably necessary to produce requested material; a governmental entity may adopt a higher threshold, and labor may be charged only for time exceeding the threshold.
rules.trigger: A request for copies requiring labor to locate, retrieve, review, redact, and reproduce records.
rules.source_language: "Labor threshold" is the first (1st) hour of labor reasonably necessary to produce requested material(s). A governmental entity may adopt a higher labor threshold than one (1) hour. A records custodian is only permitted to charge for labor exceeding the labor threshold established by the governmental entity.
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § IV.C
rules.notes: Floor: minimum one free hour; city may set a higher (more generous) threshold. Aggregation removes this waiver (TN-0038).

rules.legal_concept: Labor rate = hourly wage of employee(s) reasonably necessary
rules.atomic_rule: Labor above the threshold is charged at the hourly wage of the employee(s) reasonably necessary, using the lowest practicable wage; the hourly wage is the employee's base salary (excluding benefits), computed by dividing annual salary by required hours per year.
rules.trigger: Labor time exceeds the labor threshold.
rules.source_language: "Labor" is the time (in hours) reasonably necessary to produce requested records, including the time spent locating, retrieving, reviewing, redacting, and reproducing records. ... "Hourly wage of an employee" is based upon the base salary of the employee and does not include benefits. If an employee is not paid on an hourly basis, the hourly wage shall be determined by dividing the employee's annual salary by the required hours to be worked per year. ... In calculating labor charges, a records custodian should determine the total amount of labor for each employee and subtract the labor threshold from the labor of the highest paid employee(s).
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges §§ IV.B, IV.D, IV.E
rules.notes: Rate is a computed value keyed to specific employees' wages, not a fixed number; the one free hour is deducted from the highest-paid employee's time.

rules.legal_concept: Itemized cost estimate before producing copies
rules.atomic_rule: The records custodian shall provide the requestor an estimate of the reasonable costs to provide copies of the requested material before producing them.
rules.trigger: A request for copies that will incur charges.
rules.source_language: The records custodian shall provide a requestor an estimate of the reasonable costs to provide copies of the requested material.
rules.source_authority: Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(B); OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.G; OORC Model Public Records Policy § VI.B
rules.notes: Model Policy § VI.B: 'Records custodians shall provide requestors with an itemized estimate of the charges ... prior to producing copies ... and may require pre-payment.'

rules.legal_concept: Payment for copies may be required before production
rules.atomic_rule: A records custodian may require payment for copies before producing the copies of the records.
rules.trigger: Charges are assessed for copies.
rules.source_language: A records custodian may require payment for copies before producing copies of the records.
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.E; Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(B)
rules.notes: Non-payment of estimated fees is itself a permitted denial/hold ground (OORC Response Form). City sets the dollar threshold above which prepayment is required.

rules.legal_concept: Discretionary reduction or waiver of charges
rules.atomic_rule: A records custodian may reduce or waive charges, in whole or in part, in accordance with the governmental entity's public records policy.
rules.trigger: Application of the entity's fee-waiver provisions.
rules.source_language: A records custodian may reduce or waive charges, in whole or in part, in accordance with the governmental entity's public records policy.
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.D
rules.notes: City sets waiver thresholds; fees on aggregated requests are typically non-waivable (TN-0038).

rules.legal_concept: Actual cost of storage media, outside vendor, and retrieval
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian may charge actual out-of-pocket cost for flash drives/storage devices provided; if internal production is not practicable, may use an outside vendor and charge those actual costs; and may recover actual retrieval charges assessed by an archive or other entity holding the records.
rules.trigger: Electronic media supplied, outside-vendor production, or retrieval from an archive/other holder.
rules.source_language: A records custodian may charge its actual out-of-pocket costs for flash drives or similar storage devices on which electronic copies are provided. ... If it is not practicable or feasible for the records custodian to produce copies internally, the records custodian may use an outside vendor and charge the costs to the requester. ... If a records custodian is assessed a charge to retrieve requested records from archives or any other entity having possession of requested records, the records custodian may recover from the requestor the costs assessed for retrieval.
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges §§ III.B, III.E, III.F
rules.notes: Actual-cost pass-throughs (basis 'fixed' = the actual amount incurred). Per-page charges for electronic records only when paper had to be produced (e.g., printed to redact).

rules.legal_concept: Aggregation threshold for frequent/multiple requests
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity's policy shall specify the number of requests within a calendar month that triggers aggregation; that amount must be no lower than four (4) requests.
rules.trigger: Multiple/frequent requests within a calendar month reaching the entity's threshold.
rules.source_language: A governmental entity's public record policy shall indicate the number of requests within a calendar month that will trigger aggregation; that amount must be no lower than four (4) requests. This amount is the aggregation threshold.
rules.source_authority: OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests § I.D
rules.notes: Floor: statewide minimum threshold is 4/month; the city fills the operative number at or above 4. Once reached, the labor-threshold waiver no longer applies (TN-0039).

rules.legal_concept: Loss of labor-threshold waiver once aggregation threshold met
rules.atomic_rule: Once a records custodian reaches the aggregation threshold, the custodian is no longer required to deduct the labor threshold or any other minimum charge per request that would ordinarily be waived.
rules.trigger: Aggregation threshold reached.
rules.source_language: Once a records custodian reaches the aggregation threshold, the records custodian is no longer required to deduct the labor threshold set forth in the Schedule of Reasonable Charges or any other minimum charge per request that would ordinarily be waived.
rules.source_authority: OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests § II.A

rules.legal_concept: Aggregation across requestors acting in concert
rules.atomic_rule: An entity may aggregate multiple requests by a single requestor, and may aggregate requests by multiple requestors if the coordinator determines they are acting in concert with each other or as agents of another person, entity, or organization.
rules.trigger: Multiple requests by one requestor, or by several requestors the coordinator finds are acting in concert/as agents.
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may aggregate multiple public record requests made by a single requestor. A governmental entity may also aggregate public record requests made by multiple requestors, if the public records request coordinator determines the requestors are acting in concert with each other or as the agents of another person, entity, or organization.
rules.source_authority: OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests § I.C
rules.notes: 'Working in concert' is a coordinator determination; it is appealable to the OORC (TN-0041).

rules.legal_concept: Notice of aggregation and right to appeal to OORC
rules.atomic_rule: When aggregating, the custodian must inform the requestor(s) of the determination to aggregate and of the right to appeal that decision to the Office of Open Records Counsel; disputes regarding aggregation shall be brought to the OORC.
rules.trigger: Custodian decides to aggregate requests upon meeting the threshold.
rules.source_language: When the aggregation threshold is met, a records custodian choosing to aggregate requests must inform the requestor(s) of the determination to aggregate and of the right of the requestor(s) to appeal the records custodian's decision to aggregate to the OORC. ... Disputes regarding aggregation shall be brought to the OORC.
rules.source_authority: OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests §§ II.B, II.D
rules.notes: Administrative review path (OORC). OORC guidance/mediation is advisory, not a binding adjudication; the binding remedy remains the § 10-7-505 judicial petition (TN-0042). Routinely released/readily accessible records (agendas, minutes) are exempt from aggregation (Freq. policy § II.C).

rules.legal_concept: Mandatory written public records policy (county/municipal)
rules.atomic_rule: Every county and municipal governmental entity shall establish a written public records policy, adopted by its governing authority, that is not more burdensome than state law and includes the request process and any required form, the response process (including redaction), a statement of fees and billing/payment procedures, and the PRRC's name/title and contact information.
rules.trigger: Entity is a county or municipal governmental entity subject to the TPRA.
rules.source_language: No later than July 1, 2018, every county and municipal governmental entity subject to this section shall establish a written public records policy properly adopted by the appropriate governing authority. The public records policy shall not impose requirements on those requesting records that are more burdensome than state law and shall include: The process for making requests to inspect public records or receive copies of public records and a copy of any required request form; The process for responding to requests, including redaction practices; A statement of any fees charged for copies of public records and the procedures for billing and payment; and The name or title and the contact information of the individual or individuals within such governmental entity designated as the public records request coordinator.
rules.effective_status: Current (verified against 2021 codification; unchanged 2024). Original adoption deadline July 1, 2018 has passed.
rules.notes: This is the structural anchor for city-filled parameters (fee rates, labor threshold, ID election, copy-form election, aggregation threshold). Policy 'shall not impose requirements more burdensome than state law' is a binding ceiling on local restrictions.

rules.legal_concept: Special fees for specific documents requested for a specific use
rules.atomic_rule: Although standard copy/labor charges do not vary by purpose, other statutory provisions (e.g., § 10-7-506(c)) enumerate fees that may be assessed when specific documents are requested for a specific use.
rules.trigger: Request for specific enumerated documents for a specific (e.g., commercial) use governed by § 10-7-506(c).
rules.source_language: However, other statutory provisions, such as Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-506(c), enumerate fees that may be assessed when specific documents are requested for a specific use. Any distinctions made, or waiver of charges permitted, based upon the type of records requested should be expressly set forth and permitted in the adopted public records policy.
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.F, citing Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-506(c)
rules.effective_status: Requires manual verification of § 10-7-506(c) enumerated documents/rates
rules.notes: The verbatim capture is the OORC Schedule's reference; the specific documents and fee amounts in § 10-7-506(c) were not opened verbatim and need a later pass. Flags human legal review.

rules.legal_concept: Statutory authority to charge reasonable production costs
rules.atomic_rule: A records custodian may require a requestor to pay the custodian's reasonable costs incurred in producing the requested material, assessed in the manner established by the Office of Open Records Counsel pursuant to § 8-4-604.
rules.trigger: A request for copies/production of public records.
rules.source_language: A records custodian may require a requestor to pay the custodian's reasonable costs incurred in producing the requested material and to assess the reasonable costs in the manner established by the office of open records counsel pursuant to § 8-4-604.
rules.notes: Statutory hook that makes the OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges the operative cost framework. § 10-7-506(a) separately grants custodians the right to adopt and enforce reasonable rules governing the making of copies (per OORC Model Policy, Policy Considerations).

rules.legal_concept: Right of access on application by any person
rules.atomic_rule: Any person may apply to the officer for public information and the officer shall promptly produce public information for inspection, duplication, or both.
rules.trigger: A person applies to the officer for public information.
rules.source_language: An officer for public information of a governmental body shall promptly produce public information for inspection, duplication, or both on application by any person to the officer.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule per shared-key mandate.

rules.legal_concept: No inquiry into purpose
rules.atomic_rule: The governmental body may not inquire into the purpose for which the requested information will be used.
rules.trigger: A request is received (may accompany a permitted clarification).
rules.source_language: If a large amount of information has been requested, the governmental body may discuss with the requestor how the scope of a request might be narrowed, but the governmental body may not inquire into the purpose for which information will be used.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as rule with shared key.

rules.legal_concept: No residency requirement
rules.atomic_rule: There is no residency requirement; the right to request runs to 'any person' regardless of residence.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: An officer for public information of a governmental body shall promptly produce public information for inspection, duplication, or both on application by any person to the officer.
rules.notes: No residency condition appears in the Act; inference from the 'any person' grant. Emitted as a rule with the shared eligibility key per universal-access symmetry, not as a material negative.

rules.legal_concept: Request from or about certain incarcerated individuals
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental body is not required to accept or comply with a request from an incarcerated/confined individual or that individual's agent (other than the individual's attorney seeking disclosable information).
rules.trigger: Requestor is imprisoned/confined in a correctional facility, or is that individual's agent.
rules.source_language: A governmental body is not required to accept or comply with a request for information from: (1) an individual who is imprisoned or confined in a correctional facility; or (2) an agent of that individual, other than that individual's attorney when the attorney is requesting information that is subject to disclosure under this chapter.
rules.notes: Structural branch: engine must be able to decline/route these requests. 'Correctional facility' defined in § 552.028(c).

rules.legal_concept: Written request; permitted delivery methods
rules.atomic_rule: A request must be in writing and delivered by U.S. mail, e-mail, hand delivery, or another method the governmental body has approved (e.g., fax, submission through its website).
rules.trigger: A person seeks to invoke the Act.
rules.source_language: A person may make a written request for public information under this chapter only by delivering the request by one of the following methods to the applicable officer for public information or a person designated by that officer: (1) United States mail; (2) electronic mail; (3) hand delivery; or (4) any other appropriate method approved by the governmental body, including: (A) facsimile transmission; and (B) electronic submission through the governmental body's Internet website.
rules.notes: Approved method under (a)(4) is effective only if advertised on the § 552.205 sign or the body's website (§ 552.234(b)).

rules.legal_concept: Designated addresses for receiving requests
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental body may designate one mailing address and one e-mail address for requests; if it posts/prints them, it need not respond to a request unless received at a designated address, by hand delivery, or by an approved (a)(4) method.
rules.trigger: Body designates and publishes addresses.
rules.source_language: A governmental body may designate one mailing address and one electronic mail address for receiving written requests for public information. The governmental body shall provide the designated mailing address and electronic mailing address to any person on request.
rules.notes: Drives routing/misdirected-request handling. Full (d) lists the three receipt channels that still bind the body.

rules.legal_concept: Prompt production standard
rules.atomic_rule: The officer must produce public information promptly, i.e., as soon as possible under the circumstances, within a reasonable time, without delay.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a request.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "promptly ... as soon as possible under the circumstances, that is, within a reasonable time, without delay" from request receipt
rules.source_language: An officer for public information of a governmental body shall promptly produce public information for inspection, duplication, or both on application by any person to the officer. ... 'promptly' means as soon as possible under the circumstances, that is, within a reasonable time, without delay.
rules.notes: Soft standard -> structural. There is NO fixed statutory acknowledgment/production day-count; do not invent one. § 552.221(d) supplies only a certification duty at 10 business days (TX-0009).

rules.legal_concept: Certification when information cannot be produced within 10 business days
rules.atomic_rule: If information cannot be produced within 10 business days after receipt, the officer must certify that fact in writing to the requestor and set a date and hour, within a reasonable time, when it will be available.
rules.trigger: Information cannot be produced within 10 business days of the request.
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from request receipt (certification trigger)
rules.source_language: If public information cannot be produced for inspection or duplication within 10 business days after the date the information is requested by a member of the public, the officer for public information shall certify that fact in writing to the requestor and set a date and hour within a reasonable time when the information will be available for inspection or duplication.
rules.notes: Not a production deadline; a required written notice. The set date/hour is a soft 'reasonable time'.

rules.legal_concept: Certification when records in active use or storage
rules.atomic_rule: If requested information is in active use or in storage and therefore unavailable when requested, the officer must certify this in writing and set a date and hour, within a reasonable time, when it will be available.
rules.trigger: Requested records are in active use or storage at the time of request.
rules.source_language: If the requested information is unavailable at the time of the request to examine because it is in active use or in storage, the officer for public information shall certify this fact in writing to the requestor and set a date and hour within a reasonable time when the information will be available for inspection or duplication.
rules.notes: Set availability date is a soft 'reasonable time' standard.

rules.legal_concept: Request to clarify or narrow
rules.atomic_rule: If a request is unclear the body may ask the requestor to clarify; if a large amount is requested the body may discuss narrowing the scope.
rules.trigger: Request is unclear, or a large amount of information is requested.
rules.source_language: If what information is requested is unclear to the governmental body, the governmental body may ask the requestor to clarify the request. If a large amount of information has been requested, the governmental body may discuss with the requestor how the scope of a request might be narrowed, but the governmental body may not inquire into the purpose for which information will be used.

rules.legal_concept: Required consequences statement in a clarification request
rules.atomic_rule: A written clarification/discussion request (or a request for additional info) must include a statement of the consequences of the requestor's failure to timely respond.
rules.trigger: Body sends a written clarification, discussion, or additional-information request.
rules.source_language: A written request for clarification or discussion under Subsection (b) or a written request for additional information under Subsection (c) must include a statement as to the consequences of the failure by the requestor to timely respond to the request for clarification, discussion, or additional information.

rules.legal_concept: Withdrawal for failure to respond to clarification within 61 days
rules.atomic_rule: If the body receives no written response by the 61st day after sending a clarification/discussion request (or additional-information request), the underlying request is considered withdrawn.
rules.trigger: 61 days elapse after a clarification/discussion/additional-info request with no written response.
rules.clock_spec: 61 days from date clarification/discussion request sent
rules.source_language: If by the 61st day after the date a governmental body sends a written request for clarification or discussion under Subsection (b) or an officer for public information or agent sends a written request for additional information under Subsection (c) the governmental body, officer for public information, or agent, as applicable, does not receive a written response from the requestor, the underlying request for public information is considered to have been withdrawn by the requestor.

rules.legal_concept: Good-faith clarification tolls the AG-decision deadline
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental body's good-faith request for clarification tolls the 10-business-day period for requesting an attorney general decision until the requestor responds.
rules.trigger: Body timely and in good faith requests clarification of an unclear request.
rules.clock_spec: tolls the 10 business-day AG-request clock (TX-0018) from clarification sent until requestor responds
rules.source_language: When a governmental body, acting in good faith, requests clarification or narrowing of an unclear or over-broad request for public information, the ten-day period to request an attorney general decision is measured from the date the request is clarified or narrowed.
rules.source_authority: City of Dallas v. Abbott, 304 S.W.3d 380 (Tex. 2010)
rules.notes: Judicially established operational rule; paraphrased narrow holding. Confirm citation and holding against the official Texas Supreme Court opinion before relying.

rules.legal_concept: Mandatory attorney general decision to withhold
rules.atomic_rule: A body that receives a written request for information it wishes to withhold under a Subchapter C exception must ask the attorney general for a decision, unless there has been a previous determination.
rules.trigger: Body wishes to withhold requested information under a Subchapter C exception and no previous determination exists.
rules.source_language: A governmental body that receives a written request for information that it wishes to withhold from public disclosure and that it considers to be within one of the exceptions under Subchapter C must ask for a decision from the attorney general about whether the information is within that exception if there has not been a previous determination about whether the information falls within one of the exceptions.
rules.notes: Texas-distinctive: withholding is gated on a proactive AG ruling, not a requestor appeal. Source_language reconstructed from partial-quote fetch; verify against official text.

rules.legal_concept: Previous-determination exception to seeking an AG decision
rules.atomic_rule: No new AG decision is required where there has already been a previous determination that the information falls within an exception (or is public).
rules.trigger: A previous determination covering the information exists.
rules.source_language: ... must ask for a decision from the attorney general about whether the information is within that exception if there has not been a previous determination about whether the information falls within one of the exceptions.
rules.notes: Structural branch. 'Previous determination' has a narrow AG/case-law meaning; source_language reconstructed from partial fetch — verify.

rules.legal_concept: Deadline to request the attorney general decision
rules.atomic_rule: The body must ask the attorney general for a decision and state the applicable exceptions within a reasonable time but not later than the 10th business day after receiving the written request.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a written request the body wishes to withhold.
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from receipt of the written request
rules.source_language: The governmental body must ask for the attorney general's decision and state the exceptions that apply within a reasonable time but not later than the 10th business day after the date of receiving the written request.

rules.legal_concept: 10-day notice to requestor that a decision was sought
rules.atomic_rule: Within 10 business days of the request the body must give the requestor a written statement that it is withholding and has asked the AG, plus a copy (redacted if needed) of its AG communication.
rules.trigger: Body requests an AG decision.
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from receipt of the written request
rules.source_language: provide the requestor within a reasonable time but not later than the 10th business day after the date of receiving the requestor's written request: (1) a written statement that the governmental body wishes to withhold the requested information and has asked for a decision from the attorney general about whether the information is within an exception to public disclosure; and (2) a copy of the governmental body's written communication to the attorney general asking for the decision or, if the governmental body's written communication to the attorney general discloses the requested information, a redacted copy of that written communication.

rules.legal_concept: 15-day submission of comments and records to AG
rules.atomic_rule: Within 15 business days of the request the body must submit to the AG written comments on the exceptions, a copy of the request, a dated receipt statement, and a copy (or representative sample) of the requested information.
rules.trigger: Body has requested an AG decision.
rules.clock_spec: 15 business-days from receipt of the written request
rules.source_language: submit to the attorney general within a reasonable time but not later than the 15th business day after the date of receiving the written request: (1) written comments stating the reasons why the stated exceptions apply that would allow the information to be withheld; (2) a copy of the written request for information; (3) a signed statement as to the date on which the written request for information was received by the governmental body or evidence sufficient to establish that date; and (4) a copy of the specific information requested, or submit representative samples of the information if a voluminous amount of information was requested.

rules.legal_concept: Copy of AG comments to requestor within 15 days
rules.atomic_rule: A body that submits written comments to the AG must send a copy of those comments to the requestor not later than the 15th business day after receiving the written request.
rules.trigger: Body submits written comments to the AG under § 552.301(e).
rules.clock_spec: 15 business-days from receipt of the written request
rules.source_language: A governmental body that submits written comments to the attorney general under Subsection (e)(1)(A) shall send a copy of those comments to the person who requested the information from the governmental body not later than the 15th business day after the date of receiving the written request.
rules.notes: If comments contain confidential info, only the portions not containing that info are sent (see full (e-1)).

rules.legal_concept: Presumption of openness for failure to comply
rules.atomic_rule: If the body does not timely request an AG decision and provide the § 552.301(d) and (e-1) notices, the requested information is presumed public and must be released absent a compelling reason to withhold.
rules.trigger: Body fails to request an AG decision and/or provide the required requestor notices.
rules.clock_spec: terminal event on lapse of the 10 business-day AG-request/notice deadline
rules.source_language: If a governmental body does not request an attorney general decision as provided by Section 552.301 and provide the requestor with the information required by Sections 552.301(d) and (e-1), the information requested in writing is presumed to be subject to required public disclosure and must be released unless there is a compelling reason to withhold the information.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: deemed-disclosure trigger (silence/noncompliance -> presumed public). Remedy amounts intentionally omitted.

rules.legal_concept: Redaction of social security numbers without AG decision
rules.atomic_rule: A body may redact a living person's social security number from information it discloses under § 552.021 without requesting an attorney general decision under Subchapter G.
rules.trigger: Disclosed information contains a living person's SSN.
rules.source_language: A governmental body may redact the social security number of a living person from any information the governmental body discloses under Section 552.021 without the necessity of requesting a decision from the attorney general under Subchapter G.
rules.notes: Structural branch bypassing the AG-ruling workflow for this category. Contrast the general § 552.301(a) rule requiring an AG decision.

rules.legal_concept: Charge for providing copies
rules.atomic_rule: The copy charge must be an amount that reasonably includes all costs related to reproducing the information, including materials, labor, and overhead.
rules.trigger: Requestor asks for copies.
rules.source_language: The charge for providing a copy of public information shall be an amount that reasonably includes all costs related to reproducing the public information, including costs of materials, labor, and overhead.
rules.notes: 'reasonably' -> soft-standard; per-item rates are capped by AG rules (TX-0027).

rules.legal_concept: 50-or-fewer-page requests limited to photocopy charge
rules.atomic_rule: For a request of 50 or fewer pages of paper records, the charge may not include materials, labor, or overhead and is limited to the per-page photocopy charge, unless the pages are in two-or-more unconnected buildings or a remote storage facility.
rules.trigger: Request is for 50 or fewer pages of paper records.
rules.source_language: If a request is for 50 or fewer pages of paper records, the charge for providing the copy of the public information may not include costs of materials, labor, or overhead, but shall be limited to the charge for each page of the paper record that is photocopied, unless the pages to be photocopied are located in: (1) two or more separate buildings that are not physically connected with each other; or (2) a remote storage facility.
rules.notes: Distinct fee-calc branch for small requests. § 552.261(c) clarifies covered/connected buildings are not 'separate.'

rules.legal_concept: Charges capped by attorney general cost rules
rules.atomic_rule: Charges for copies/inspection may not exceed the amounts established by attorney general rule; a non-state governmental body setting its own charges may not exceed the AG-established amounts by more than 25% absent an exemption.
rules.trigger: Body imposes a charge for copies or inspection.
rules.source_language: The charges for providing copies of public information may not be excessive and may not exceed the actual cost of producing the information ... [a non-state governmental body's charges] may not exceed 25 percent greater than the amount established by the attorney general unless the governmental body requests an exemption.
rules.notes: The concrete per-page/per-hour rate ceilings live in the AG's cost rules at 1 Tex. Admin. Code ch. 70, not in the statute. Source_language assembled from a partial fetch; verify exact wording of § 552.262.

rules.legal_concept: Required written itemized estimate when charge exceeds $40
rules.atomic_rule: If a copy charge (or a § 552.271 paper-inspection charge) will exceed $40, the body must give the requestor a written itemized statement detailing all estimated charges (including labor/personnel), notice of any less-costly alternative, and the requestor's response responsibilities.
rules.trigger: Estimated charge will exceed $40.
rules.source_language: If a request for a copy of public information will result in the imposition of a charge under this subchapter that exceeds $40, or a request to inspect a paper record will result in the imposition of a charge under Section 552.271 that exceeds $40, the governmental body shall provide the requestor with a written itemized statement that details all estimated charges that will be imposed, including any allowable charges for labor or personnel costs.
rules.notes: $40 is a fixed statutory trigger threshold (a state-fixed value the city cannot alter).

rules.legal_concept: Withdrawal for no response to itemized estimate within 10 business days
rules.atomic_rule: The request is considered withdrawn if the requestor does not respond in writing within 10 business days after the itemized statement is sent (accepting charges, modifying the request, or filing an overcharge complaint).
rules.trigger: 10 business days elapse after the itemized statement is sent with no written response.
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from date the itemized statement is sent
rules.source_language: A request described by Subsection (a) is considered to have been withdrawn by the requestor if the requestor does not respond in writing to the itemized statement by informing the governmental body within 10 business days after the date the statement is sent to the requestor that: (1) the requestor will accept the estimated charges; (2) the requestor is modifying the request in response to the itemized statement; or (3) the requestor has sent to the attorney general a complaint alleging that the requestor has been overcharged for being provided with a copy of the public information.
rules.notes: 'Sent'/'responded' timing defined in § 552.2615(e),(f).

rules.legal_concept: Updated itemized statement when charges rise 20% or more
rules.atomic_rule: If, before making the copy available, the body determines estimated charges will exceed the itemized statement by 20% or more, it must send a written updated itemized statement; no timely response to the update means the request is withdrawn.
rules.trigger: Estimated charges will exceed the prior itemized statement by 20% or more.
rules.source_language: If the governmental body later determines, but before it makes the copy or the paper record available, that the estimated charges will exceed the charges detailed in the written itemized statement by 20 percent or more, the governmental body shall send to the requestor a written updated itemized statement that details all estimated charges that will be imposed, including any allowable charges for labor or personnel costs. If the requestor does not respond in writing to the updated estimate in the time and manner described by Subsection (b), the request is considered to have been withdrawn by the requestor.
rules.notes: 20% is a fixed statutory variance threshold. Actual charge cap tied to the (updated) estimate per § 552.2615(d).

rules.legal_concept: Minimum personnel-time allowance before charging
rules.atomic_rule: A body that sets time limits on uncompensated personnel time must allow at least 36 hours per requestor over a 12-month period and at least 15 hours per requestor in a one-month period before charging for personnel time.
rules.trigger: Body has adopted personnel-time limits under § 552.275.
rules.source_language: [The yearly time limit] may not be less than 36 hours for a requestor during the 12-month period ... [the monthly time limit] may not be less than 15 hours for a requestor for a one-month period.
rules.notes: Floor: the statutory minimum the city must allow; the city sets the actual limit at or above it. Verbatim phrases quoted from (b); bracketed lead-ins added for readability. Once the limit is met, § 552.275(e) requires a cost estimate within 10 business days.

rules.legal_concept: Waiver or reduction in the public interest
rules.atomic_rule: The body must provide a copy without charge or at a reduced charge if it determines waiver/reduction is in the public interest because providing the copy primarily benefits the general public.
rules.trigger: Body determines providing the copy primarily benefits the general public.
rules.source_language: A governmental body shall provide a copy of public information without charge or at a reduced charge if the governmental body determines that waiver or reduction of the charge is in the public interest because providing the copy of the information primarily benefits the general public.
rules.notes: Duty is triggered by a discretionary public-interest determination.

rules.legal_concept: Waiver when collection cost exceeds the charge
rules.atomic_rule: The body may waive the charge if the cost of processing the collection of the charge would exceed the amount of the charge.
rules.trigger: Cost of collecting the charge exceeds the charge itself.
rules.source_language: If the cost to a governmental body of processing the collection of a charge for providing a copy of public information will exceed the amount of the charge, the governmental body may waive the charge.

rules.legal_concept: Deposit or bond for anticipated costs
rules.atomic_rule: The officer may require a deposit or bond for anticipated copy costs once an itemized estimate has been provided and the estimated charge exceeds $100 (body with more than 15 full-time employees) or $50 (fewer than 16 full-time employees).
rules.trigger: Itemized estimate provided and estimated charge exceeds the applicable threshold.
rules.source_language: An officer for public information or the officer's agent may require a deposit or bond for payment of anticipated costs for the preparation of a copy of public information if: (1) the officer for public information or the officer's agent has provided the requestor with the written itemized statement required under Section 552.2615 ... detailing the estimated charge for providing the copy; and (2) the charge for providing the copy of the public information specifically requested by the requestor is estimated by the governmental body to exceed: (A) $100, if the governmental body has more than 15 full-time employees; or (B) $50, if the governmental body has fewer than 16 full-time employees.
rules.notes: Two-tier fixed thresholds tied to full-time-employee count.

rules.legal_concept: Deposit for unpaid amounts from prior requests
rules.atomic_rule: The officer may require a deposit or bond for unpaid amounts owed on prior requests if those unpaid amounts exceed $100, and this becomes the sole means of collecting those amounts.
rules.trigger: Requestor has unpaid amounts exceeding $100 from prior requests.
rules.source_language: An officer for public information or the officer's agent may require a deposit or bond for payment of unpaid amounts owing to the governmental body in relation to previous requests that the requestor has made ... only if those unpaid amounts exceed $100.
rules.notes: Source_language reconstructed from a full-text reproduction summary; verify exact subsection and wording (overdue-balance provision of § 552.263).

rules.legal_concept: Written no-responsive-records notice within 10 business days
rules.atomic_rule: If the governmental body determines it has no information responsive to a request, the officer for public information must notify the requestor in writing not later than the 10th business day after the date the request is received.
rules.trigger: Body determines no responsive information exists
rules.clock_spec: 10 business days from receipt of the request
