rules.source_language: If the governmental body determines it has no information responsive to a request for information, the officer for public information shall notify the requestor in writing not later than the 10th business day after the date the request is received.
rules.source_authority: Tex. Gov't Code § 552.221(f) (added by HB 4219, 89th Leg., eff. 9/1/2025)
rules.notes: ADDED 2026-07-26 via desktop-research recency cross-check; verified verbatim against enrolled HB 4219. Before 9/1/2025 no-records letters were practice, not statute. Post-HB 4219 the 10-bd checkpoint has five exits (produce / certify later date / no-records notice / previous-determination notice / AG-ruling request) - no request may silently close.

rules.legal_concept: Written notice identifying the specific previous determination relied on to withhold
rules.atomic_rule: If the body withholds based on a previous determination, the officer for public information must, not later than the 10th business day after receipt, notify the requestor in writing that the information is being withheld and identify the specific previous determination relied on.
rules.trigger: Body relies on a previous determination to withhold instead of requesting a new AG ruling
rules.clock_spec: 10 business days from receipt of the request
rules.source_language: If a governmental body determines the requested information is subject to a previous determination that permits or requires the governmental body to withhold the requested information, the officer for public information shall, not later than the 10th business day after the date the request is received: (1) notify the requestor in writing that the information is being withheld; and (2) identify in the notice the specific previous determination the governmental body is relying on to withhold the requested information.
rules.source_authority: Tex. Gov't Code § 552.221(g) (added by HB 4219, 89th Leg., eff. 9/1/2025)
rules.notes: ADDED 2026-07-26 via desktop-research recency cross-check; verified verbatim against enrolled HB 4219. Pairs with restored TX-0017 (previous-determination exception to the AG-ruling requirement): the exception now carries an affirmative notice duty.

rules.legal_concept: AG-ruling request must state the specific exceptions claimed (wording update to TX-0018)
rules.atomic_rule: The governmental body must ask for the attorney general's decision and state the specific exceptions that apply within a reasonable time but not later than the 10th business day after the date of receiving the written request.
rules.trigger: Body wishes to withhold information not covered by a previous determination
rules.clock_spec: 10 business days from receipt of the request (hard; miss = information presumed public under § 552.302)
rules.source_language: The governmental body must ask for the attorney general's decision and state the specific exceptions that apply within a reasonable time but not later than the 10th business day after the date of receiving the written request.
rules.source_authority: Tex. Gov't Code § 552.301(b) (as amended by HB 4219, 89th Leg., eff. 9/1/2025)
rules.notes: ADDED 2026-07-26. SUPERSEDES the wording of restored TX-0018 (pre-amendment text said 'the applicable exceptions'; HB 4219 requires 'the specific exceptions'). Kept as its own rule so the frozen wave text stays untouched.

rules.legal_concept: Catastrophe suspension of PIA duties (7 days + one 7-day extension, max 14 calendar days)
rules.atomic_rule: A body currently significantly impacted by a catastrophe may suspend PIA requirements for an initial period of up to 7 consecutive days (once per catastrophe, after submitting notice to the AG on the prescribed form), extendable once by up to 7 more consecutive days; the combined suspension may not exceed 14 consecutive calendar days per catastrophe. Requests received during a suspension are considered received on the first business day after the suspension ends, and pre-suspension requests are tolled until that day.
rules.trigger: Catastrophe significantly impacting the body; catastrophe notice submitted to the AG (remote-work-only situations excluded)
rules.clock_spec: Up to 7 consecutive days + one 7-day extension (max 14 calendar days per catastrophe); requests during suspension deemed received the first business day after it ends; pending-request clocks tolled
rules.source_language: The initial suspension period may not exceed seven consecutive days ... The initial suspension period may be extended one time for not more than seven consecutive days that begin on the day following the day the initial suspension period ends. ... The combined suspension period for a governmental body filing under Subsections (d) and (e) may not exceed a total of 14 consecutive calendar days with respect to any single catastrophe. ... a request for public information received by a governmental body during a suspension period determined by the governmental body is considered to have been received by the governmental body on the first business day after the date the suspension period ends.
rules.source_authority: Tex. Gov't Code § 552.233 (formerly § 552.2325; as amended by SB 1225, 87th Leg., 2021)
rules.notes: ADDED 2026-07-26 via desktop-research recency cross-check; verified against enrolled SB 1225 (composite of subsections (d), (e), (g), (i) - ellipses join clauses, each clause verbatim). Desktop research cited the pre-2021 number 552.2325; current codification is 552.233. Clock-matrix design input: a state-gated global pause timer, not a per-request timer.

material_negatives.note: Texas imposes NO fixed statutory acknowledgment or final-response day-count. The only response duty is to 'promptly produce' (soft standard, § 552.221(a)-(b)); the sole hard 10-business-day event is a certification duty when records cannot be produced in that time (§ 552.221(d)), not a decision/production deadline. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

There is no requestor-initiated administrative appeal of a denial. The Act instead compels the governmental body to seek an AG ruling to withhold (§ 552.301); a requestor's recourse for noncompliance is a complaint to the AG or a mandamus suit under § 552.321 (external litigation, excluded).

No statewide per-page copy rate is fixed in the statute itself; the concrete rates/ceilings are set by attorney general cost rules (1 Tex. Admin. Code ch. 70), which were not opened this pass. § 552.262 only supplies the ceiling mechanism. Verify the current TAC rate schedule in a later pass.

The Act repeatedly uses 'business day' but a general statutory definition/holiday-exclusion rule for computing the PIA clocks was not separately captured this pass; confirm how 'business day' and skip-days are defined for §§ 552.221/552.301.

Preservation/litigation-hold triggered by the request itself: no distinct PIA preservation-hold provision was located this pass (routine retention schedules are out of scope); flag for the retention/records-authority pass.

structural_branches.description: Requests from incarcerated/confined individuals (or their non-attorney agents) may be declined — a routing/decline branch the engine must express (§ 552.028).
To withhold under a Subchapter C exception the body must proactively obtain an attorney general decision; there is no requestor-initiated administrative appeal (§ 552.301(a)).
A 'previous determination' short-circuits the AG-decision requirement — a branch that skips the § 552.301 workflow (§ 552.301(a)).
Failure to timely seek an AG decision / give the required notices flips the request into a 'presumed public, must release' terminal state (§ 552.302).
A good-faith clarification request tolls the 10-business-day AG-request clock until the requestor responds (City of Dallas v. Abbott).
SSNs may be redacted without invoking the AG-decision workflow — a redaction path parallel to, and bypassing, § 552.301 (§ 552.147(b)).
Charges over $40 route through a mandatory itemized-estimate / requestor-response / updated-estimate flow that can terminate the request by withdrawal (§ 552.2615).
Requests of 50 or fewer pages follow a distinct fee-calc path (photocopy charge only, no labor/materials/overhead) unless multi-building/remote (§ 552.261(a)).
A discretionary public-interest determination routes the request into free/reduced-charge production (§ 552.267(a)).

rules.legal_concept: Right to inspect a public record free of charge
rules.atomic_rule: Any person has the right to inspect a public record free of charge and to take a copy during normal working hours, subject to the fee and response sections.
rules.trigger: None stated (any person)
rules.source_language: Except as provided in Subsection (1)(b), a person has the right to inspect a public record free of charge, and the right to take a copy of a public record during normal working hours, subject to Sections 63G-2-203 and 63G-2-204.
rules.notes: Config_home marked parameter only to satisfy schema; substantively this is the universal-access grant. Exceptions in 201(1)(b): already-provided copies, non-fillable requests under 7(a)(v), and non-segregable electronic files.

rules.legal_concept: No residency/citizenship condition on access
rules.atomic_rule: The right of access runs to 'a person' with no residency or citizenship qualification imposed by GRAMA.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: GRAMA grants the right of inspection and copying to 'a person' (§ 63G-2-201(1)(a)) and § 63G-2-204(1)(a) enumerates the required contents of a request without any residency or citizenship element; no provision conditions access on residency.
rules.notes: is_paraphrase=true: GRAMA has no explicit no-residency clause; this is the universal-access symmetry fact stated from the affirmative 'a person' grant and the absence of a residency element in the request-content list. Requires manual verification.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A requester need not state a reason or purpose; purpose is not among the required contents of a records request.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: The required contents of a written request under § 63G-2-204(1)(a) are the requester's name, mailing address, email address (if applicable), daytime telephone number, and a description of the record with reasonable specificity; no statement of purpose is required (purpose is relevant only to optional expedited response and fee waivers).
rules.notes: is_paraphrase=true: inferred from the absence of purpose in the mandatory request-content list. Note purpose IS optionally relevant to expedited-response benefit (204(4)-(5)) and fee waivers (203(4)); those are separate rules. Requires manual verification.

rules.legal_concept: Written request required
rules.atomic_rule: A person requesting a record must submit a written request to the governmental entity that retains the record.
rules.trigger: Person seeks a record
rules.source_language: A person making a request for a record shall submit to the governmental entity that retains the record a written request containing: (i) the person's: (A) name; (B) mailing address; (C) email address, if the person has an email address and is willing to accept communications by email relating to the person's records request; and (D) daytime telephone number; and (ii) a description of the record requested that identifies the record with reasonable specificity.
rules.notes: Enumerated required fields: name, mailing address, email (if applicable), daytime telephone, and reasonably-specific description. Split into UT-0005 (specificity standard).

rules.legal_concept: One request may not span multiple entities
rules.atomic_rule: A single record request may not be submitted to multiple governmental entities (though identical separate requests to each entity are allowed).
rules.trigger: Request submitted
rules.source_language: (i) A single record request may not be submitted to multiple governmental entities. (ii) Subsection (1)(b)(i) may not be construed to prevent a person from submitting a separate record request to each of multiple governmental entities, even if each of the separate requests seeks access to the same record.

rules.legal_concept: Entity may specify where requests are directed
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity may make rules specifying where and to whom requests for access must be directed.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may make rules in accordance with Title 63G, Chapter 3, Utah Administrative Rulemaking Act, specifying where and to whom requests for access shall be directed.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: drives routing / custodian designation.

rules.legal_concept: Prompt forwarding of misdirected request; clock start
rules.atomic_rule: If a request goes to the wrong office, that office must promptly forward it to the appropriate office; if promptly forwarded, the response clock starts when the correct office receives it.
rules.trigger: Request submitted to office other than the one specified by rule
rules.clock_spec: response time limit begins when request is received by the office specified by rule
rules.source_language: (a) If a request for access is submitted to an office of a governmental entity other than that specified by rule in accordance with Subsection (3), the office shall promptly forward the request to the appropriate office. (b) If the request is forwarded promptly, the time limit for response begins when the request is received by the office specified by rule.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver #1 (routing). Clock-start rule for the 10/5-business-day response window.

rules.legal_concept: Time for responding to a records request
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity must respond (approve/provide, deny, disclaim custody, or claim extraordinary circumstances) as soon as reasonably possible but no later than 10 business days after receiving a written request.
rules.trigger: Receipt of written request
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 10 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: After receiving a request for a record, a governmental entity shall: ... (b) as soon as reasonably possible, but no later than 10 business days after receiving a written request, or five business days after receiving a written request if the requester demonstrates that expedited response to the record request benefits the public rather than the person: (i) approve the request and provide a copy of the record; (ii) deny the request in accordance with the procedures and requirements of Section 63G-2-205; (iii) notify the requester that it does not maintain the record requested and provide, if known, the name and address of the governmental entity that does maintain the record; or (iv) notify the requester that because of one of the extraordinary circumstances listed in Subsection (6), it cannot immediately approve or deny the request...
rules.notes: 'as soon as reasonably possible' is a soft floor on top of the 10-business-day hard ceiling. Political subdivisions may set different response times under § 63G-2-701(4)(b) if resources are insufficient (see UT-0049).

rules.legal_concept: Expedited (5-business-day) response
rules.atomic_rule: If the requester demonstrates that an expedited response benefits the public rather than the person, the entity must respond no later than 5 business days after receiving the request.
rules.trigger: Requester demonstrates expedited response benefits the public rather than the person
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 5 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: or five business days after receiving a written request if the requester demonstrates that expedited response to the record request benefits the public rather than the person

rules.legal_concept: Notice that expedited treatment is denied
rules.atomic_rule: For a request seeking expedited response, the entity must review it and, within 5 business days, notify any requester who has not demonstrated public benefit that the response will not be expedited.
rules.trigger: Request seeks expedited response but public benefit not demonstrated
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 5 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: After receiving a request for a record, a governmental entity shall: (a) review each request that seeks an expedited response and notify, within five business days after receiving the request, each requester that has not demonstrated that their record request benefits the public rather than the person that their response will not be expedited;

rules.legal_concept: Notice that entity does not maintain the record
rules.atomic_rule: If the entity does not maintain the requested record, it must, within the response window, notify the requester and provide (if known) the name and address of the entity that does maintain it.
rules.trigger: Entity does not maintain the requested record
rules.source_language: notify the requester that it does not maintain the record requested and provide, if known, the name and address of the governmental entity that does maintain the record;
rules.notes: Routing/referral outcome; occurs within the UT-0009 window.

rules.legal_concept: Extraordinary-circumstances delay notice
rules.atomic_rule: If extraordinary circumstances prevent immediate approval or denial, the entity must, within the response window, notify the requester with a description of the circumstances and the date the records will be available.
rules.trigger: One of the enumerated extraordinary circumstances applies
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: extension period per Subsection (7), stated as a 'date when the records will be available'
rules.source_language: notify the requester that because of one of the extraordinary circumstances listed in Subsection (6), it cannot immediately approve or deny the request, and include with the notice: (A) a description of the circumstances that constitute the extraordinary circumstances; and (B) the date when the records will be available, consistent with the requirements of Subsection (7).
rules.notes: Structural branch: the request enters an extended-processing state. Extension length depends on which ground applies (UT-0015..UT-0018).

rules.legal_concept: Extension for legal-counsel analysis
rules.atomic_rule: Where the delay is due to legal-issue analysis requiring counsel, the entity must approve or deny within 5 business days after the original response time expired.
rules.trigger: Extraordinary circumstance under 204(6)(f)
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 5 business-days after the original response time expires
rules.source_language: for claims under Subsection (6)(f), the governmental entity shall either approve or deny the request within five business days after the response time specified for the original request has expired;

rules.legal_concept: Extension for extensive editing to segregate
rules.atomic_rule: Where segregating disclosable from non-disclosable information requires extensive editing, the entity must fulfill the request within 15 business days from the date of the original request.
rules.trigger: Extraordinary circumstance under 204(6)(g)
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 15 business-days from date of original request
rules.source_language: for claims under Subsection (6)(g), the governmental entity shall fulfill the request within 15 business days from the date of the original request; or

rules.legal_concept: Soft 'as soon as reasonably possible' extension for volume/programming grounds
rules.atomic_rule: For voluminous/high-volume/locate-review grounds and for grounds requiring computer programming, the entity must disclose located records the requester may inspect, give an estimate of time to finish, and complete and disclose as soon as reasonably possible.
rules.trigger: Extraordinary circumstance under 204(6)(c),(d),(e), or (h)
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "as soon as reasonably possible" from the extraordinary-circumstances notice
rules.source_language: for claims under Subsections (6)(c), (d), and (e), the governmental entity shall: (i) disclose the records that it has located which the requester is entitled to inspect; (ii) provide the requester with an estimate of the amount of time it will take to finish the work required to respond to the request; (iii) complete the work and disclose those records that the requester is entitled to inspect as soon as reasonably possible; ... (f) for claims under Subsection (6)(h), the governmental entity shall complete its programming and disclose the requested records as soon as reasonably possible.
rules.notes: Soft standard -> config_home structural per contract. Includes a duty to provide a time estimate.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to conduct a reasonable search
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity must conduct a reasonable search for a requested record.
rules.trigger: Record request received
rules.source_language: A governmental entity shall conduct a reasonable search for a requested record.
rules.notes: 'Reasonable' is an undefined soft standard; not a numeric parameter.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to create, compile, or reformat records
rules.atomic_rule: In responding, an entity is not required to create a record; compile/format/manipulate/package/summarize/tailor information; or provide a record in a format, medium, or program not currently maintained.
rules.trigger: Request would require creation/compilation/reformatting
rules.source_language: In response to a request, a governmental entity is not required to: (i) create a record; (ii) compile, format, manipulate, package, summarize, or tailor information; (iii) provide a record in a particular format, medium, or program not currently maintained by the governmental entity;
rules.notes: Entity MAY optionally do so under 201(8), and may charge for it under § 63G-2-203.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to fulfill unreasonably duplicative requests
rules.atomic_rule: An entity is not required to fulfill a request that unreasonably duplicates prior records requests from that same person.
rules.trigger: Request unreasonably duplicates prior requests from the same person
rules.source_language: fulfill a person's records request if the request unreasonably duplicates prior records requests from that person;

rules.legal_concept: No duty to fill request for records already publicly available
rules.atomic_rule: An entity need not fill a request where the record is publicly accessible online or in a public publication/product, provided the entity specifies where it is accessible or provides the publication and specifies where the record is found.
rules.trigger: Requested record is publicly accessible online or in a public publication
rules.source_language: fill a person's records request if: (A) the record requested is: (I) publicly accessible online; or (II) included in a public publication or product produced by the governmental entity receiving the request; and (B) the governmental entity: (I) specifies to the person requesting the record where the record is accessible online; or (II) provides the person requesting the record with the public publication or product and specifies where the record can be found...
rules.notes: Routing/refusal outcome conditioned on the entity pointing the requester to the source.

rules.legal_concept: Electronic copy in lieu of paper
rules.atomic_rule: An entity must provide an electronic copy in lieu of paper if the requester prefers electronic, the entity currently maintains a reproducible electronic format providable without reformatting/conversion, and the copy does not disclose exempt records or can be segregated without undue expenditure.
rules.trigger: Requester requests/prefers electronic copy and conditions met
rules.source_language: Subject to the requirements of Subsection (7), a governmental entity shall provide access to an electronic copy of a record in lieu of providing access to its paper equivalent if: (a) the person making the request requests or states a preference for an electronic copy; (b) the governmental entity currently maintains the record in an electronic format that is reproducible and may be provided without reformatting or conversion; and (c) the electronic copy of the record: (i) does not disclose other records that are exempt from disclosure; or (ii) may be segregated to protect private, protected, or controlled information from disclosure without the undue expenditure of public resources or funds.

rules.legal_concept: Physical form may not be used to deny access
rules.atomic_rule: An entity may not use the physical form (electronic or otherwise) in which a record is stored to deny or unreasonably hinder inspection or copying.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may not use the physical form, electronic or otherwise, in which a record is stored to deny, or unreasonably hinder the rights of a person to inspect and receive a copy of a record under this chapter.

rules.legal_concept: Requester self-copying for large requests
rules.atomic_rule: For a request of more than 50 pages, an entity may allow the requester to make the copies (using entity facilities or the requester's own) where the files contain no exempt records or can be segregated and reasonable safeguards are provided.
rules.trigger: Request exceeds 50 pages and segregability/safeguard conditions met
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may allow a person requesting more than 50 pages of records to copy the records if: (i) the records are contained in files that do not contain records that are exempt from disclosure, or the records may be segregated to remove private, protected, or controlled information from disclosure; and (ii) the governmental entity provides reasonable safeguards to protect the public from the potential for loss of a public record.
rules.notes: 50-page threshold (floor: 'more than 50 pages'). If requester uses own facilities on-site, entity waives copying fees. Cross-referenced by extraordinary-circumstances handling in 204(7)(c)(iv).

rules.legal_concept: Certified copy of a record
rules.atomic_rule: An entity must provide a certified copy of a record if the person has a right to inspect it, identifies it with reasonable specificity, and pays the lawful fees.
rules.trigger: Requester with inspection right requests certified copy and pays fees
rules.source_language: A governmental entity shall provide a person with a certified copy of a record if: (a) the person requesting the record has a right to inspect it; (b) the person identifies the record with reasonable specificity; and (c) the person pays the lawful fees.

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable fee to cover actual cost
rules.atomic_rule: An entity may charge a reasonable fee to cover its actual cost of providing a record; the fee must be approved by the entity's executive officer.
rules.trigger: Entity provides a record
rules.source_language: (a) Subject to Subsection (5), a governmental entity may charge a reasonable fee to cover the governmental entity's actual cost of providing a record. (b) A fee under Subsection (1)(a) shall be approved by the governmental entity's executive officer.
rules.notes: Ceiling = actual cost; also bounded by the soft 'reasonable' standard. Executive-officer approval is a structural sub-requirement (UT-0030).

rules.legal_concept: Actual-cost components for compiled records
rules.atomic_rule: When compiling a record in a form other than normally maintained, actual costs may include staff time for compiling/formatting/tailoring, staff time for search/retrieval and direct administrative costs, and (for non-word-processing computer output) actual incremental cost plus a reasonable portion of formatting/administrative costs.
rules.trigger: Entity compiles a record in a form other than normally maintained
rules.source_language: When a governmental entity compiles a record in a form other than that normally maintained by the governmental entity, the actual costs under this section may include the following: (i) the cost of staff time for compiling, formatting, manipulating, packaging, summarizing, or tailoring the record...; (ii) the cost of staff time for search, retrieval, and other direct administrative costs for complying with a request; and (iii) in the case of fees for a record that is the result of computer output other than word processing, the actual incremental cost of providing the electronic services and products together with a reasonable portion of the costs associated with formatting or interfacing the information for particular users, and the administrative costs...

rules.legal_concept: Hourly charge capped at lowest-paid qualified employee
rules.atomic_rule: An hourly staff-time charge may not exceed the salary of the lowest paid employee who has the necessary skill and training to perform the request.
rules.trigger: Entity charges staff-time hourly fee
rules.source_language: An hourly charge under Subsection (2)(a) may not exceed the salary of the lowest paid employee who, in the discretion of the custodian of records, has the necessary skill and training to perform the request.

rules.legal_concept: Political subdivisions set fees by ordinance/policy
rules.atomic_rule: Political subdivisions must establish records fees by ordinance or written formal policy adopted by the governing body.
rules.trigger: Political subdivision establishes fees
rules.source_language: Political subdivisions shall establish fees by ordinance or written formal policy adopted by the governing body.
rules.notes: The municipal hook: the CITY supplies the actual fee schedule under the state's actual-cost ceiling (UT-0028).

rules.legal_concept: Discretionary fee waiver
rules.atomic_rule: An entity may (and is encouraged to) fulfill a request without charge if release primarily benefits the public, the requester is the subject of/specified in the record, or the requester's legal rights are directly implicated and the requester is impecunious.
rules.trigger: One of the enumerated benefit/subject/impecunious conditions
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may fulfill a record request without charge and is encouraged to do so if it determines that: (a) releasing the record primarily benefits the public rather than a person; (b) the individual requesting the record is the subject of the record, or an individual specified in Subsection 63G-2-202(1) or (2); or (c) the requester's legal rights are directly implicated by the information in the record, and the requester is impecunious.
rules.notes: Denial of a fee waiver is separately appealable (UT-0040) and reviewed de novo (§ 63G-2-203(6)).

rules.legal_concept: No fee for reviewing a record for disclosability
rules.atomic_rule: An entity may not charge a fee for reviewing a record to determine whether it is subject to disclosure, except as permitted for search/retrieval staff time under 203(2)(a)(ii).
rules.trigger: Entity reviews record for disclosability
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may not charge a fee for: (i) reviewing a record to determine whether it is subject to disclosure, except as permitted by Subsection (2)(a)(ii);

rules.legal_concept: First quarter hour of staff time free
rules.atomic_rule: An entity may not charge a fee for the first quarter hour of staff time spent responding to a request.
rules.trigger: Entity responds to a request under § 63G-2-204
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may not charge a fee for: ... (iii) the first quarter hour of staff time spent in responding to a request under Section 63G-2-204.
rules.notes: Fixed free allotment of 15 minutes. Exception in UT-0036.

rules.legal_concept: Exception to free first quarter hour for repeat non-media requesters
rules.atomic_rule: The free first quarter hour does not apply if the requester is not a Utah media representative AND previously submitted a separate request within the 10-day period immediately before the current request.
rules.trigger: Non-media requester filed a separate request within prior 10 days
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding Subsection (5)(b)(iii), a governmental entity is not prevented from charging a fee for the first quarter hour of staff time spent in responding to a request under Section 63G-2-204 if the person who submits the request: (i) is not a Utah media representative; and (ii) previously submitted a separate request within the 10-day period immediately before the date of the request to which the governmental entity is responding.
rules.notes: 'Media representative' here (203(5)(a)) excludes blog/podcast/social-media requesters, unlike the broader publication/broadcast presumption in 204(5).

rules.legal_concept: Advance payment before processing
rules.atomic_rule: An entity may require payment of past fees and future estimated fees before beginning to process a request.
rules.trigger: Fees expected to exceed $50, or prior invoiced fees unpaid
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: processing withheld until prepayment received ('before beginning to process a request')
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may require payment of past fees and future estimated fees before beginning to process a request if: (i) fees are expected to exceed $50; or (ii) after the government entity has sent an invoice, the requester has not paid fees from a previous request.
rules.notes: Prepayment gate; the request enters a hold state until paid. Threshold value in UT-0038.

rules.legal_concept: $50 prepayment threshold
rules.atomic_rule: Prepayment may be required when fees are expected to exceed $50.
rules.trigger: Estimated fees exceed $50
rules.source_language: fees are expected to exceed $50;
rules.notes: Fixed statutory threshold.

rules.legal_concept: Refund of excess prepayment
rules.atomic_rule: Any prepaid amount in excess of fees due must be returned to the requester.
rules.trigger: Prepaid amount exceeds fees actually due
rules.source_language: Any prepaid amount in excess of fees due shall be returned to the requester.

rules.legal_concept: Segregation of disclosable from non-disclosable information
rules.atomic_rule: If a record contains both disclosable and non-disclosable information and the disclosable portion is intelligible, the entity must allow access to the disclosable information and may deny the exempt information by issuing a notice of denial.
rules.trigger: Record contains both entitled and non-entitled information
rules.source_language: if a governmental entity receives a request for access to a record that contains both information that the requester is entitled to inspect and information that the requester is not entitled to inspect under this chapter, and, if the information the requester is entitled to inspect is intelligible, the governmental entity: (1) shall, except as provided in Subsection 63G-2-201(1)(b)(iii), allow access to information in the record that the requester is entitled to inspect under this chapter; and (2) may deny access to information in the record if the information is exempt from disclosure to the requester, issuing a notice of denial as provided in Section 63G-2-205.
rules.notes: Partial-denial of segregated portions triggers the denial-notice machinery (UT-0044).

rules.legal_concept: Notice of denial
rules.atomic_rule: If the entity denies a request in whole or part, it must provide a notice of denial to the requester either in person or by sending it to the requester's address.
rules.trigger: Request denied in whole or part
rules.source_language: If the governmental entity denies the request in whole or part, it shall provide a notice of denial to the requester either in person or by sending the notice to the requester's address.

rules.legal_concept: Required contents of denial notice
rules.atomic_rule: The notice of denial must contain a description of the denied record/portions, citations to the exempting provisions, a statement of the right to appeal to the chief administrative officer, and the appeal time limits plus the CAO's name and business address.
rules.trigger: Notice of denial issued
rules.source_language: The notice of denial shall contain the following information: (a) a description of the record or portions of the record to which access was denied...; (b) citations to the provisions of this chapter, court rule or order, another state statute, federal statute, or federal regulation that exempt the record or portions of the record from disclosure...; (c) a statement that the requester has the right to appeal the denial to the chief administrative officer of the governmental entity; and (d) the time limits for filing an appeal, and the name and business address of the chief administrative officer of the governmental entity.

rules.legal_concept: Mandatory denial of shared records with source referral
rules.atomic_rule: An entity may not provide a record it received as a shared record under § 63G-2-206; it must deny the request and inform the requester of the identity of the entity from which the shared record was received.
rules.trigger: Requested record was received as a shared record under § 63G-2-206
rules.source_language: (a) In response to a request for a record, a governmental entity may not provide a record that it has received under Section 63G-2-206 as a shared record. (b) If a governmental entity is prohibited from providing a record under Subsection (2)(a), the governmental entity shall: (i) deny the records request; and (ii) inform the person making the request of the identity of the governmental entity from which the shared record was received.
rules.notes: Routing: requester must be redirected to the originating entity.

rules.legal_concept: Classification deferred until access requested
rules.atomic_rule: An entity is not required to classify a particular record, record series, or information until access to the record is requested.
rules.trigger: Access to a record is requested
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may classify a particular record, record series, or information within a record at any time, but is not required to classify a particular record, record series, or information until access to the record is requested.
rules.notes: Drives when the classification step runs during request handling.

rules.legal_concept: Limited duty to respond to incarcerated/parolee requesters
rules.atomic_rule: An entity is not required to respond to a request by or on behalf of an individual on parole or confined in a correctional facility, except for the first five requests per calendar year seeking only records referencing that individual, or a request submitted by the individual's attorney.
rules.trigger: Requester is on parole or confined following conviction
rules.source_language: (a) Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, and subject to Subsection (9)(b), a governmental entity is not required to respond to, or provide a record in response to, a record request if the request is submitted by or in behalf of an individual who is on parole or confined in a jail or other correctional facility following the individual's conviction. (b) Subsection (9)(a) does not apply to: (i) the first five record requests submitted to the governmental entity by or in behalf of an individual described in Subsection (9)(a) during any calendar year requesting only a record that contains a specific reference to the individual; or (ii) a record request that is submitted by an attorney of an individual described in Subsection (9)(a).
rules.notes: Alters processing/routing for a requester class. Threshold: 5 requests/calendar year (floor of guaranteed responses).

rules.legal_concept: Business confidentiality claim submission
rules.atomic_rule: A person who provides a record they believe should be protected as a trade secret/commercial information under 63G-2-305(1)/(2) must provide, with or within a reasonable time after the record, a written claim of business confidentiality and a concise statement of supporting reasons.
rules.trigger: Person submits a record believed protectable under § 63G-2-305(1) or (2)
rules.source_language: Any person who provides to a governmental entity a record that the person believes should be protected under Subsection 63G-2-305(1) or (2) or both Subsections 63G-2-305(1) and (2) shall provide with the record, or within a reasonable amount of time after providing the record: (A) a written claim of business confidentiality; and (B) a concise statement of reasons supporting the claim of business confidentiality.
rules.notes: Creates a distinct redaction/notice workflow; the claim triggers appeal-notice duties (UT-0062) and a disclosure hold (UT-0064).

rules.legal_concept: Production and notice of compliance after director order
rules.atomic_rule: If the director orders production and no appeal is filed (or production is required as a result of appeal), the governmental entity must produce the record and file a notice of compliance with the director.
rules.trigger: Director orders production and no notice of intent to appeal is filed
rules.source_language: If the director orders the governmental entity to produce a record and no appeal is filed, or if, as a result of the appeal, the governmental entity is required to produce a record, the governmental entity shall: (i) produce the record; and (ii) file a notice of compliance with the director.
rules.notes: Post-order production step. Failure to comply or appeal can draw a civil penalty of up to $500/day (403(15)(d)) — remedy amount excluded per inclusion test.

rules.legal_concept: Political subdivisions may set different response/appeal timeframes
rules.atomic_rule: In its records ordinance/policy, a political subdivision may establish reasonable response times and appeal time limits different from those in § 63G-2-204 and Part 4 if it determines its resources are insufficient to meet those sections.
rules.trigger: Political subdivision adopts a records ordinance/policy and finds insufficient resources
rules.source_language: (a) Each ordinance or policy shall establish access criteria, procedures, and response times for requests to inspect, obtain, or amend records of the political subdivision, and time limits for appeals consistent with this chapter. (b) In establishing response times for access requests and time limits for appeals, the political subdivision may establish reasonable time frames different than those set out in Section 63G-2-204 and Part 4, Appeals, if it determines that the resources of the political subdivision are insufficient to meet the requirements of those sections.
rules.notes: Critical municipal-config fork: a city's actual response/appeal deadlines may differ from the statutory defaults (UT-0009, UT-0010, UT-0040, UT-0041, UT-0056). A political subdivision that adopts no ordinance/policy is fully subject to this chapter (701(2)(c)); regardless of any ordinance it remains subject to Parts 1 & 3 and §§ 201, 202, 205, 206, 601, 602 (701(2)(d)).

material_negatives.note: GRAMA sets no separate acknowledgment/receipt-confirmation deadline distinct from the substantive 10/5-business-day response window in § 63G-2-204(4). No found rule requiring an interim acknowledgment.

No explicit clarification clock or nonresponse-abandonment/withdrawal procedure found. A request must be reasonably specific (§ 63G-2-204(1)(a)(ii)) but GRAMA does not codify a tolling clarification exchange or deem an unclarified request abandoned. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

Chapter 2 contains no codified Saturday/Sunday/holiday day-counting rule. Guidance (Utah State Archives / ombudsman) states business days exclude weekends and legal holidays and that periods over 11 days are counted as calendar days, but this was not located in the statute itself this pass — flagged for an administrative-rule / guidance pass.

No statewide per-page copy rate. Fees are actual-cost-based (§ 63G-2-203) and set by each political subdivision by ordinance/policy (§ 63G-2-203(3)(c)); the per-page value is a city-supplied parameter, not a state number.
No fixed deposit percentage; prepayment is of past plus estimated future fees in full, gated by the $50 threshold (§ 63G-2-203(8)). No partial-deposit formula found.

Related caveat: GRAMA has no explicit anti-purpose-discrimination clause in current § 63G-2-201; the no-purpose fact (UT-0003) is inferred from the request-content list. An older/handbook statement that access cannot be restricted based on the reason for the request should be verified against statute/case law in a later pass.

structural_branches.description: Request enters an extended-processing state on an extraordinary-circumstances claim (UT-0014/0015), with ground-specific extension deadlines (UT-0016 5-day legal review; UT-0017 15-day editing; UT-0018 soft ASAP for volume/programming).
Prepayment gate (UT-0037/0038): the request is held before processing when estimated fees exceed $50 or prior fees are unpaid.

Municipal fork (UT-0057): a political subdivision may create a 3-member local appeals board; if it does, the second-stage appeal of a CAO decision goes to that board rather than to the director of the Government Records Office.

State-level second-stage appeal to the director of the Government Records Office (UT-0056/0059/0060), a distinct adjudicative body with its own hearing scheduling (16-64 day) and a 73-calendar-day deemed-denial backstop.

Ombudsman-mediation branch (UT-0058): submitting a § 63A-12-204 mediation request tolls both the director-appeal and judicial-review filing windows until the ombudsman certifies conclusion or non-occurrence.

Vexatious-requester adjudication before the director (UT-0051/0052/0053): an entity can petition to be relieved (up to one year) of the duty to fulfill a person's requests; such blocked requests are not appealable under Part 4.
Business-confidentiality workflow (UT-0062/0063/0064): a submitter's trade-secret claim triggers claimant notice on appeal (3-day / 7-day) and a disclosure hold pending appeal.

Municipal timeframe fork (UT-0049): a city's ordinance may set response and appeal deadlines different from the statutory defaults where resources are insufficient — the operative per-request deadlines can be city-specific.
Deemed-denial state transition (UT-0019): silence past the response window becomes an appealable denial. Parallel deemed outcomes exist at the CAO stage (UT-0042) and director stage (UT-0060).

rules.legal_concept: Records open to citizens of the Commonwealth and in-state media
rules.atomic_rule: Public records are open only to citizens of the Commonwealth and to representatives of newspapers/magazines with circulation in, and radio/TV stations broadcasting in or into, the Commonwealth; the engine may restrict standing to these requester classes.
rules.trigger: Any records request
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise specifically provided by law, all public records shall be open to citizens of the Commonwealth, representatives of newspapers and magazines with circulation in the Commonwealth, and representatives of radio and television stations broadcasting in or into the Commonwealth during the regular office hours of the custodian of such records.
rules.notes: Virginia is one of the few states with a requester-residency limitation (upheld in McBurney v. Young, 569 U.S. 221 (2013)). Do NOT map to eligibility.any_person or eligibility.no_residency_requirement — VFOIA affirmatively restricts standing.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A requester need not state a purpose or reason to obtain public records; the custodian may require only the requester's name and legal address.
rules.trigger: Any records request
rules.source_language: The custodian may require the requester to provide his name and legal address.
rules.notes: Emitted as a rule with the shared eligibility key per universal-access symmetry. is_paraphrase=true because 'no purpose required' is an inference from the enumerated permission (name + legal address only); VFOIA states no purpose condition affirmatively.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian may require name and legal address
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may require the requester to provide his name and legal address.
rules.trigger: Request received
rules.source_language: The custodian may require the requester to provide his name and legal address.

rules.legal_concept: Request must identify records with reasonable specificity
rules.atomic_rule: A request for public records shall identify the requested records with reasonable specificity.
rules.trigger: Request submitted
rules.source_language: A request for public records shall identify the requested records with reasonable specificity.
rules.notes: 'Reasonable specificity' is an undefined soft standard the engine applies at intake; not a numeric threshold.

rules.legal_concept: Request need not reference the chapter
rules.atomic_rule: A request need not reference VFOIA to invoke the chapter's provisions or to impose the response time limits on the public body.
rules.trigger: Request submitted
rules.source_language: The request need not make reference to this chapter in order to invoke the provisions of this chapter or to impose the time limits for response by a public body.

rules.legal_concept: Five-working-day response deadline
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian shall, promptly but in all cases within five working days of receiving a request, provide the records or make one of four written responses.
rules.trigger: Public body receives a request
rules.clock_spec: fixed: 5 working days from receipt of request
rules.source_language: Any public body that is subject to this chapter and that is the custodian of the requested records shall promptly, but in all cases within five working days of receiving a request, provide the requested records to the requester or make one of the following responses in writing:

rules.legal_concept: Additional seven work days when response not practically possible
rules.atomic_rule: If, within the five-work-day period, the body responds in writing that it is not practically possible to provide the records or determine availability and specifies the conditions making a response impossible, it gets an additional seven work days to make one of the four responses.
rules.trigger: Body determines it is not practically possible to respond within 5 working days and says so in writing within that period
rules.clock_spec: fixed: additional 7 work days from the original 5-working-day response
rules.source_language: It is not practically possible to provide the requested records or to determine whether they are available within the five-work-day period. Such response shall specify the conditions that make a response impossible. If the response is made within five working days, the public body shall have an additional seven work days ... in which to provide one of the four preceding responses.

rules.legal_concept: Sixty work days for criminal investigative files
rules.atomic_rule: For a request for criminal investigative files under § 2.2-3706.1, the additional extension when a response is not practically possible is 60 work days rather than seven.
rules.trigger: Not-practically-possible response to a request for criminal investigative files under § 2.2-3706.1
rules.clock_spec: fixed: 60 work days (in lieu of 7) from the original 5-working-day response
rules.source_language: the public body shall have an additional seven work days or, in the case of a request for criminal investigative files pursuant to § 2.2-3706.1, 60 work days in which to provide one of the four preceding responses.

rules.legal_concept: Petition court for additional time — extraordinary volume/search
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may petition the appropriate court for additional time to respond when the request is for an extraordinary volume of records or requires an extraordinarily lengthy search that would prevent it from meeting operational responsibilities, but must first make reasonable efforts to reach agreement with the requester.
rules.trigger: Request for extraordinary volume or requiring extraordinarily lengthy search
rules.source_language: Any public body may petition the appropriate court for additional time to respond to a request for records when the request is for an extraordinary volume of records or requires an extraordinarily lengthy search, and a response by the public body within the time required by this chapter will prevent the public body from meeting its operational responsibilities. Before proceeding with the petition, however, the public body shall make reasonable efforts to reach an agreement with the requester concerning the production of the records requested.
rules.notes: Structural fork: an external court-extension path with an antecedent duty to attempt agreement; no fixed day-count set.

rules.legal_concept: Entire-withholding response requirements
rules.atomic_rule: A response withholding records entirely shall identify with reasonable particularity the volume and subject matter of withheld records and cite, as to each category, the specific Code section authorizing the withholding.
rules.trigger: Records withheld in their entirety
rules.source_language: The requested records are being entirely withheld. Such response shall identify with reasonable particularity the volume and subject matter of withheld records, and cite, as to each category of withheld records, the specific Code section that authorizes the withholding of the records.

rules.legal_concept: Partial provide/withhold response requirements
rules.atomic_rule: A response providing records in part and withholding in part shall identify with reasonable particularity the subject matter of withheld portions and cite, as to each category, the specific Code section authorizing the withholding.
rules.trigger: Records provided in part and withheld in part
rules.source_language: The requested records are being provided in part and are being withheld in part. Such response shall identify with reasonable particularity the subject matter of withheld portions, and cite, as to each category of withheld records, the specific Code section that authorizes the withholding of the records.

rules.legal_concept: Records could not be found or do not exist — referral
rules.atomic_rule: If records could not be found or do not exist, the response says so; and if the receiving body knows another public body has the records, the response shall include contact information for that other public body.
rules.trigger: Records not found or nonexistent; receiving body knows another body holds them
rules.source_language: The requested records could not be found or do not exist. However, if the public body that received the request knows that another public body has the requested records, the response shall include contact information for the other public body.
rules.notes: Routing keeper-sliver: obligates a referral hand-off to the correct custodian.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to create a new record
rules.atomic_rule: No public body is required to create a new record that does not already exist, but it may abstract or summarize information under terms agreed with the requester.
rules.trigger: Requested record does not already exist
rules.source_language: Subject to the provisions of subsection G, no public body shall be required to create a new record if the record does not already exist. However, a public body may abstract or summarize information under such terms and conditions as agreed between the requester and the public body.

rules.legal_concept: Failure to respond is a deemed denial and violation
rules.atomic_rule: Failure to respond to a request within the statutory period is deemed a denial of the request and constitutes a violation of the chapter.
rules.trigger: No response made within the applicable response deadline
rules.clock_spec: terminal: expiry of the 5-working-day (or extended) response window with no response = deemed denial
rules.source_language: Failure to respond to a request for records shall be deemed a denial of the request and shall constitute a violation of this chapter.
rules.notes: Deemed-denial keeper-sliver: the terminal trigger only; the remedy/penalty amount is excluded.

rules.legal_concept: Access to records in an electronic database
rules.atomic_rule: Records maintained in an electronic data processing system or database shall be made available at a reasonable cost not exceeding actual cost; where databases combine exempt and nonexempt records, the body shall provide access to the nonexempt records.
rules.trigger: Requested records held in an electronic database or structured data collection
rules.source_language: Public records maintained by a public body in an electronic data processing system, computer database, or any other structured collection of data shall be made available to a requester at a reasonable cost, not to exceed the actual cost in accordance with subsection F. When electronic or other databases are combined or contain exempt and nonexempt records, the public body may provide access to the exempt records if not otherwise prohibited by law, but shall provide access to the nonexempt records as provided by this chapter.

rules.legal_concept: Production in any tangible medium identified by requester
rules.atomic_rule: The body shall produce nonexempt database records in any tangible medium identified by the requester — including, where it has the capability, posting on a website or delivery to a requester-provided email address — if that medium is used in the regular course of business.
rules.trigger: Requester identifies a tangible medium for production
rules.source_language: Public bodies shall produce nonexempt records maintained in an electronic database in any tangible medium identified by the requester, including, where the public body has the capability, the option of posting the records on a website or delivering the records through an electronic mail address provided by the requester, if that medium is used by the public body in the regular course of business.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to produce in a format not regularly used
rules.atomic_rule: No public body is required to produce records from an electronic database in a format not regularly used by it, but it shall make reasonable efforts to provide records in any format under terms agreed with the requester, including payment of reasonable costs.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for a format the body does not regularly use
rules.source_language: No public body shall be required to produce records from an electronic database in a format not regularly used by the public body. However, the public body shall make reasonable efforts to provide records in any format under such terms and conditions as agreed between the requester and public body, including the payment of reasonable costs.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to redact and disclose nonexempt portions
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may not withhold an entire record because some portion is excluded; a record may be withheld in full only where an exclusion applies to its entire content, otherwise only the excluded portions are withheld and all nonexcluded portions shall be disclosed.
rules.trigger: Record contains both excluded and nonexcluded information
rules.source_language: No provision of this chapter is intended, nor shall it be construed or applied, to authorize a public body to withhold a public record in its entirety on the grounds that some portion of the public record is excluded from disclosure by this chapter or by any other provision of law. A public record may be withheld from disclosure in its entirety only to the extent that an exclusion from disclosure under this chapter or other provision of law applies to the entire content of the public record. Otherwise, only those portions of the public record containing information subject to an exclusion under this chapter or other provision of law may be withheld, and all portions of the public record that are not so excluded shall be disclosed.

rules.legal_concept: Charges not to exceed actual cost incurred
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may make reasonable charges not to exceed its actual cost incurred in accessing, duplicating, supplying, or searching for the requested records.
rules.trigger: Body incurs cost in responding
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost incurred in accessing/duplicating/supplying/searching
rules.source_language: a public body may make reasonable charges not to exceed its actual cost incurred in accessing, duplicating, supplying, or searching for the requested records and shall make all reasonable efforts to supply the requested records at the lowest possible cost.
rules.notes: State sets a ceiling (actual cost); the city sets its actual per-request charge under it. No statewide fixed per-page rate exists.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to supply at lowest possible cost
rules.atomic_rule: The body shall make all reasonable efforts to supply the requested records at the lowest possible cost.
rules.trigger: Body sets charges for a request
rules.clock_spec: soft-standard: 'lowest possible cost'
rules.source_language: and shall make all reasonable efforts to supply the requested records at the lowest possible cost.

rules.legal_concept: No extraneous/intermediary/surplus fees
rules.atomic_rule: No public body shall impose extraneous, intermediary, or surplus fees or expenses to recoup the general costs of creating or maintaining records or transacting the general business of the public body.
rules.trigger: Body assesses charges
rules.source_language: No public body shall impose any extraneous, intermediary, or surplus fees or expenses to recoup the general costs associated with creating or maintaining records or transacting the general business of the public body.

rules.legal_concept: Duplicating fee not to exceed actual cost of duplication
rules.atomic_rule: Any duplicating fee charged by a public body shall not exceed the actual cost of duplication.
rules.trigger: Body charges a duplicating fee
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost of duplication
rules.source_language: Any duplicating fee charged by a public body shall not exceed the actual cost of duplication.

rules.legal_concept: Pre-search written notice of possible charges
rules.atomic_rule: Prior to conducting a search for records, the body shall notify the requester in writing that it may make reasonable charges not to exceed actual cost and inquire whether the requester would like a cost estimate in advance.
rules.trigger: Before conducting a search for records
rules.source_language: Prior to conducting a search for records, the public body shall notify the requester in writing that the public body may make reasonable charges not to exceed its actual cost incurred in accessing, duplicating, supplying, or searching for requested records and inquire of the requester whether he would like to request a cost estimate in advance of the supplying of the requested records.

rules.legal_concept: Cost estimate provided on request
rules.atomic_rule: The public body shall provide the requester with a cost estimate if requested.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for a cost estimate
rules.source_language: The public body shall provide the requester with a cost estimate if requested.

rules.legal_concept: Response period tolled pending requester's estimate response
rules.atomic_rule: The response period is tolled for the amount of time that elapses between the public body's notice of the cost estimate and the requester's response.
rules.trigger: Cost estimate sent; awaiting requester's response
rules.clock_spec: tolls: from notice of cost estimate until requester responds
rules.source_language: The period within which the public body shall respond under this section shall be tolled for the amount of time that elapses between notice of the cost estimate and the response of the requester.

rules.legal_concept: Request deemed withdrawn after 30 days' silence on cost estimate
rules.atomic_rule: If the public body receives no response from the requester within 30 days of sending the cost estimate, the request is deemed withdrawn.
rules.trigger: No requester response within 30 days of the cost estimate being sent
rules.clock_spec: fixed terminal: 30 days from sending the cost estimate = deemed withdrawn
rules.source_language: If the public body receives no response from the requester within 30 days of sending the cost estimate, the request shall be deemed to be withdrawn.

rules.legal_concept: Estimating cost credited toward overall charges
rules.atomic_rule: Any costs incurred by the public body in estimating the cost of supplying the records shall be applied toward the overall charges to be paid by the requester.
rules.trigger: Body incurs cost preparing a cost estimate
rules.source_language: Any costs incurred by the public body in estimating the cost of supplying the requested records shall be applied toward the overall charges to be paid by the requester for the supplying of such requested records.

rules.legal_concept: Local body may offer an electronic method of payment
rules.atomic_rule: Any local public body that charges for producing records may provide an electronic method of payment (noncash, non-paper-check — credit/debit cards, direct deposit/debit, electronic checks, telephonic payment).
rules.trigger: Local public body charges for record production
rules.source_language: Any local public body that charges for the production of records pursuant to this section may provide an electronic method of payment through which all payments for the production of such records to such locality may be made.

rules.legal_concept: Advance deposit when charges likely to exceed $200
rules.atomic_rule: Where a public body determines in advance that charges are likely to exceed $200, it may, before continuing to process the request, require the requester to pay a deposit not to exceed the amount of the advance determination.
rules.trigger: Advance determination that charges are likely to exceed $200
rules.clock_spec: fixed threshold: $200; deposit ceiling = the advance-determination amount
rules.source_language: In any case where a public body determines in advance that charges for producing the requested records are likely to exceed $200, the public body may, before continuing to process the request, require the requester to pay a deposit not to exceed the amount of the advance determination.
rules.notes: $200 is a state-fixed trigger threshold; the deposit itself is capped at the body's advance determination (a ceiling).

rules.legal_concept: Response period tolled pending advance-determination response
rules.atomic_rule: The response period is tolled for the amount of time that elapses between notice of the advance determination and the requester's response.
rules.trigger: Advance determination (deposit demand) sent; awaiting requester's response
rules.clock_spec: tolls: from notice of advance determination until requester responds
rules.source_language: The period within which the public body shall respond under this section shall be tolled for the amount of time that elapses between notice of the advance determination and the response of the requester.

rules.legal_concept: No charge for FERPA scholastic records to parent/guardian/eligible student
rules.atomic_rule: The reasonable-charge fee provisions do not apply to scholastic records that must be made available under FERPA when requested by a parent or legal guardian of a minor student or by a student who is 18 or older.
rules.trigger: Request for scholastic records under § 2.2-3705.4(A)(1) by parent/guardian or student 18+
rules.source_language: Except with regard to scholastic records requested pursuant to subdivision A 1 of § 2.2-3705.4 that must be made available for inspection pursuant to the federal Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (20 U.S.C. § 1232g) and such requests for scholastic records by a parent or legal guardian of a minor student or by a student who is 18 years of age or older, a public body may make reasonable charges ...
rules.notes: Special-record fee treatment: carves this class out of the § 2.2-3704(F) charge regime.

rules.legal_concept: Charge for GIS records to non-owner; topo map pro rata
rules.atomic_rule: A body may make a reasonable charge, not exceeding actual cost, for records produced from a geographic information system at the request of anyone other than the owner of the subject land, except that it may charge on a pro rata per-acre basis for topographical maps it developed that encompass a contiguous area greater than 50 acres.
rules.trigger: Request for GIS-produced records by a non-owner of the subject land
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost; exception — pro rata per-acre for body-developed topo maps over 50 contiguous acres
rules.source_language: The public body may also make a reasonable charge for the cost incurred in supplying records produced from a geographic information system at the request of anyone other than the owner of the land that is the subject of the request. However, such charges shall not exceed the actual cost to the public body in supplying such records, except that the public body may charge, on a pro rata per acre basis, for the cost of creating topographical maps developed by the public body, for such maps or portions thereof, which encompass a contiguous area greater than 50 acres.
rules.notes: Special-record fee treatment (GIS/topo).

rules.legal_concept: Designation of a FOIA officer as point of contact
rules.atomic_rule: All state, local, and regional public bodies subject to the chapter shall designate and publicly identify one or more FOIA officers to serve as the point of contact for records requests and to coordinate the body's FOIA compliance.
rules.trigger: Body is subject to VFOIA
rules.source_language: All state public bodies, including state authorities, that are subject to the provisions of this chapter and all local public bodies and regional public bodies that are subject to the provisions of this chapter shall designate and publicly identify one or more Freedom of Information Act officers (FOIA officer) whose responsibility is to serve as a point of contact for members of the public in requesting public records and to coordinate the public body's compliance with the provisions of this chapter.
rules.notes: Custodian-designation keeper-sliver: anchors intake routing to the designated FOIA officer.

material_negatives.note: VFOIA has no acknowledgment step distinct from the substantive response. The five-working-day response IS the first required communication (§ 2.2-3704(B)); there is no separate 'we received your request' clock. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

VFOIA provides NO internal administrative appeal and no binding agency/AG review of a denial. The only formal remedy is the judicial mandamus/injunction petition (§ 2.2-3713). The Virginia FOIA Advisory Council (§ 30-179) issues only nonbinding advisory opinions. Emit no appeal.administrative.* rule for Virginia.
No statewide fixed or ceiling per-page copy rate. Fees are bounded only by the 'actual cost' ceiling (VA-0021, VA-0024); the per-page amount, if any, is set by each locality under that ceiling.

VFOIA draws no commercial-vs-noncommercial requester distinction and authorizes no commercial-purpose fee surcharge; 'commercial purpose' is not a defined term in § 2.2-3701. Charges turn on actual cost regardless of requester purpose.

Deliberately NOT emitted as a rule: Virginia does not grant universal any-person access. Standing is restricted to citizens of the Commonwealth plus in-state media (see VA-0001). Emitting the shared any_person/no_residency key here would misjoin Virginia with open-access states.
No statutory classification for multi-record, recurring, or subscription requests, and no distinct processing track for them. Each request runs the single § 2.2-3704 pipeline.

No VFOIA provision imposes a preservation/litigation hold triggered by the request or by an enforcement petition. Records retention runs under the separate Public Records Act (Title 42.1) on routine schedules, which are out of scope. No request-triggered hold rule found.

VFOIA prescribes no mandatory submission channel (no required form, portal, or writing). A request need not even cite the chapter (VA-0006); the statute is silent on medium, so no channel rule is emitted.

structural_branches.description: The § 2.2-3704(B) response is a four-way branch the engine must express within the 5-day clock: (1) provide records, (2) withhold entirely with citation, (3) provide/withhold in part with citation, (4) records not found/not practically possible. Each leg has its own required notice content (VA-0011/0012/0013) and the (4) leg opens the extension path.

§ 2.2-3704(C) court-petition-for-additional-time is a state-specific external fork (extraordinary volume / lengthy search) gated by a prior duty to attempt agreement with the requester; it produces no fixed day-count (VA-0010).
A request enters a terminal 'deemed withdrawn' state after 30 days of requester silence following a cost estimate (VA-0028) — a distinct end-state separate from denial or fulfillment.

The statutory clock pauses (tolls) in two payment-negotiation states: awaiting the requester's answer to a cost estimate (VA-0027) and awaiting the requester's answer to a >$200 advance-deposit determination (VA-0032). The request sits in a paused-for-payment state, resuming on requester response.

§ 2.2-3704.2 requires a designated, publicly-identified FOIA officer as the intake point of contact (VA-0035); routing anchors to that officer, and a not-found response must hand off to a known alternate custodian (VA-0013).

Virginia's only formal denial-review path is judicial — a mandamus/injunction petition (VA-0036) with a 7-day expedited hearing (VA-0037), burden on the public body (VA-0038), and docket precedence (VA-0039). There is no administrative-appeal stage to model.

rules.legal_concept: Availability to any person
rules.atomic_rule: Upon request for identifiable public records, the agency shall make them promptly available to any person.
rules.trigger: Any person submits a request for identifiable public records.
rules.source_language: Public records shall be available for inspection and copying, and agencies shall, upon request for identifiable public records, make them promptly available to any person including, if applicable, on a partial or installment basis as records that are part of a larger set of requested records are assembled or made ready for inspection or disclosure.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule per the shared eligibility key.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A requester shall not be required to provide the purpose of the request, except to establish whether disclosure would violate the commercial-purpose list prohibition or another statute restricting disclosure to certain persons.
rules.trigger: Any records request; purpose may be asked only to test a commercial-purpose or person-specific prohibition.
rules.source_language: Agencies shall not distinguish among persons requesting records, and such persons shall not be required to provide information as to the purpose for the request except to establish whether inspection and copying would violate RCW 42.56.070(8) or 42.56.240(14), or other statute which exempts or prohibits disclosure of specific information or records to certain persons.
rules.notes: The purpose-inquiry exception is the branch that connects to the commercial-purpose list prohibition (WA-0030).

rules.legal_concept: No distinction among requesters
rules.atomic_rule: An agency shall not distinguish among persons requesting records.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional).
rules.source_language: Agencies shall not distinguish among persons requesting records, and such persons shall not be required to provide information as to the purpose for the request except to establish whether inspection and copying would violate RCW 42.56.070(8) or 42.56.240(14), or other statute which exempts or prohibits disclosure of specific information or records to certain persons.
rules.notes: Same sentence as WA-0002; split as a distinct concept (equal treatment) from the no-purpose concept.

rules.legal_concept: No residency requirement
rules.atomic_rule: Records must be made available to any person with no residency or citizenship qualification.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional).
rules.source_language: agencies shall, upon request for identifiable public records, make them promptly available to any person
rules.notes: Washington states 'any person' with no residency clause; residency-neutrality derives from that phrase and is confirmed by the AG model rules (WAC 44-14). Emitted as the shared eligibility key per universal-access symmetry rule.

rules.legal_concept: No official request format required
rules.atomic_rule: No official format is required to make a records request, though an agency may recommend a form or web page.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: No official format is required for making a records request; however, agencies may recommend that requestors submit requests using an agency provided form or web page.

rules.legal_concept: Accepted request channels
rules.atomic_rule: An agency shall honor requests for identifiable public records received in person during normal office hours, or by mail or email, unless exempted by the chapter.
rules.trigger: Request received in person, by mail, or by email.
rules.source_language: Agencies shall honor requests received in person during an agency's normal office hours, or by mail or email, for identifiable public records unless exempted by provisions of this chapter.
rules.notes: RCW 42.56.100 separately confirms mail requests must be honored.

rules.legal_concept: Identifiable records requirement
rules.atomic_rule: A request must be for identifiable records; a request for all or substantially all of an agency's records is not valid, but a request for all records on a particular topic, keyword, or name is not treated as a request for all records.
rules.trigger: Request is evaluated for validity at intake.
rules.source_language: A public records request must be for identifiable records. A request for all or substantially all records prepared, owned, used, or retained by an agency is not a valid request for identifiable records under this chapter, provided that a request for all records regarding a particular topic or containing a particular keyword or name shall not be considered a request for all of an agency's records.
rules.notes: Gates whether a submission is a valid request the engine must process.

rules.legal_concept: Overbreadth not a sole basis for denial
rules.atomic_rule: An agency shall not deny a request for identifiable public records solely because the request is overbroad.
rules.trigger: Request is identifiable but broad.
rules.source_language: Agencies shall not deny a request for identifiable public records solely on the basis that the request is overbroad.

rules.legal_concept: Bot request denial
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may deny a bot request that is one of multiple requests from the same requester within a 24-hour period if it establishes that responding would cause excessive interference with other essential functions.
rules.trigger: Multiple computer-generated (bot) requests from one requester within a 24-hour period that would cause excessive interference.
